AME-208.title: Computational Methods in Engineering
AME-208.description: Common tools for Aerospace and Mechanical engineers: vectors, matrices, fundamentals of python, data manipulation and analysis, statistics, data presentation, optimization, large data sets.

AME-291.description: Analysis, design, fabrication, and evaluation of devices intended for entry in local and national design competitions. Intended for lower division students or those with little prior project experience. Graded CR/NC.

AME-301.title: Dynamics
AME-301.description: Reference frames and coordinate systems; relationships between forces, moments, power, linear/angular momentum, and energy for particles and rigid bodies; particle and rigid body systems.

AME-302A.title: Modeling and Analysis of Dynamic Systems
AME-302A.description: Mathematical modeling of constrained mechanical systems, transfer function formulation, state-space models, block diagram representation, time-domain open-loop systems response analysis; application to electrical circuits.
AME-302A.prereqText:
Prerequisite: MATH 245
Recommended preparation: PHYS 151, AME 301
Duplicates credit: former AME 302

AME-302B.title: Modeling and Analysis of Dynamic Systems
AME-302B.description: Modeling and analysis of mechanical and combined dynamic systems; simple mechanisms; design-oriented approach to dynamic systems; system stability; approximation with lower-order systems, engineering applications.
AME-302B.prereqText:
Prerequisite: AME 302A; MATH 245
Recommended preparation: PHYS 152L

AME-308.title: Computer-Aided Engineering
AME-308.description: Introduction to the finite element method; practical application of computer analysis tools for structural analysis and design.
AME-308.prereqText:

Corequisite: AME 301
Recommended preparation: Familiarity with CAD tools on the level of AME 101, AME 105 or ASTE 101

AME-309.title: Dynamics of Fluids
AME-309.description: Fluid statics; conservation of mass, momentum, and energy in integral and differential form; applications. Laminar and turbulent pipe flow; compressible flow; potential flow over bodies.
AME-309.prereqText:
Prerequisite: AME 201
Corequisite: MATH 245
Recommended preparation: AME 310

AME-310.title: Engineering Thermodynamics I

AME-310.prereqText: Prerequisite: PHYS 151; MATH 125 or MATH 126 or MATH 129 or MATH 226 or MATH 229

AME-341B.title: Mechoptronics Laboratory
AME-341B.description: Coordinated laboratory and lecture sequence on aeromechanical instrumentation, test and measurement, integration of mechanical, optical and electronic components and technical communication.

AME-409.title: Senior Design Project

AME-409.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Senior

AME-415.title: Turbine Design and Analysis
AME-415.description: Physics of turbine operation; design and analysis for the development of turbine hardware for propulsion and power generation.
AME-415.prereqText: Recommended preparation: Basic thermodynamics and mechanics such as AME 310, familiarity with MATLAB to the level of TAC 168.

AME-420.title: Engineering Vibrations I
AME-420.description: The theory of free and forced vibrations with and without damping; systems with single and multiple degrees of freedom; solution methods; introduction to continuous systems.

AME-431.title: Heat Transfer
AME-431.description: General principles underlying heat transfer by conduction, convection, and radiation; steady and transient conditions; heat exchangers.
AME-431.prereqText:
Prerequisite: AME 310
Corequisite: AME 309
Duplicates credit: former AME 331

AME-436.description: Analysis of combustion engines: reciprocating-piston, gas turbines, rockets. Tradeoffs compared to non-combustion sources. Ideal and non-ideal cycle analysis and performance evaluation; pollutant formation and remediation.

AME-441A.title: Senior Projects Laboratory
AME-441A.description: Team engineering design project to model, construct and test a physical principle or system. Complete industrial research project including proposal, design review, presentation, technical report.

AME-441B.title: Senior Projects Laboratory
AME-441B.description: Individual engineering projects designed and constructed to model and test a physical principle or system.

AME-443.title: Control Systems Laboratory
AME-443.description: Practical measurement, analysis, and control of dynamic systems; system identification; linear control system design; simulation and verification of control system performance; and experimental controller implementation.
AME-443.prereqText:
Recommended preparation: AME 302ab, AME 420, and MATH 245
Duplicates credit: former AME 442bL.

AME-451.title: Linear Control Systems I
AME-451.description: Transform methods, block diagrams; transfer functions; stability; root-locus and frequency domain analysis and design; application to flight control, state space and multiloop systems.

AME-455.title: Introduction to Microelectromechanical Systems
AME-455.description: Introduction to micro-electro-mechanical systems (MEMS); scaling effects; materials and structures in MEMS; MEMS sensing and actuation principles; microfabrication.
AME-455.prereqText: Recommended preparation: Mechanics of materials on the level of AME 204 or CE 225, Dynamics on the level of AME 301

AME-460.title: Aerodynamic Theory
AME-460.description: Basic relations describing the inviscid flow field about bodies and wings moving at subsonic and supersonic speeds.

AME-481.title: Aircraft Design
AME-481.description: Aircraft design and analysis, design requirements and specifications; integration of structure, propulsion, control system, and aerodynamic configuration; performance analysis and prediction.

AME-503.prereqText: Recommended preparation: Engineering Design and Principles on the level of AME 410

AME-504.prereqText:

AME-508.prereqText:
Prerequisite: AME 525
Recommended preparation: Basic familiarity with Python/Matlab

AME-509.title: Applied Elasticity
AME-509.description: Cartesian tensors; kinematics of deformation, balance laws, and constitutive equations; variational principles; finite elasticity; plates and cylindrical shells; viscoelasticity; analytical and numerical solutions for elasticity.

AME-510.description: Study concepts behind computational representations, algorithms and mathematical foundations, and their applications in computer-aided design and manufacturing. Develop hands-on computational skills in team projects.

AME-513B.title: Fundamentals and Applications of Combustion

AME-513B.prereqText:
Prerequisite: AME 513A

AME-521.description: Multi-degree of freedom systems; continuous systems; modal analysis. Beams, rods, membranes, plates, shells. Approximate methods; Galerkin, Rayleigh Ritz; assumed-mode, finite elements.

AME-522.title: Nonlinear Dynamical Systems, Vibrations, and Chaos

AME-526.title: Partial Differential Equations for Engineering Applications
AME-526.description: Solving linear heat, wave, Laplace and Poisson equations, separation of variables and Fourier series, special functions, Fourier and Laplace transforms, characteristics, Greens functions, similarity solutions.

AME-529.title: Aircraft Structures Analysis

AME-535B.title: Introduction to Computational Fluid Mechanics

AME-544.title: Computer Control of Mechanical Systems
AME-544.description: Computer control as applied to machine tools, mechanical manipulators, and other mechanical machinery; discrete time controller design; microprocessor implementation of motion and force control servos.

AME-549.title: Systems Architecting
AME-549.description: Introduction to systems architecture in aerospace, electrical, computer, and manufacturing systems emphasizing the conceptual and acceptance phases and using heuristics.

AME-552.description: Phase plane, describing function, applications to mechanical and aerospace systems. Lyapunov stability theory. Popov theorem. Circle criterion. Lyapunov redesign. Sliding mode control. Backstepping. Passivity.
AME-552.prereqText:
Recommended preparation: Background in dynamics and classical control system
Duplicates credit: EE 587

AME-554.title: Additive Manufacturing Technologies
AME-554.description: Overview and working principles of commonly used additive manufacturing processes; process models; process and material selection; cost estimation methods; current applications and future directions.

AME-560.title: Fatigue and Fracture
AME-560.description: Behavior of materials under cyclic and static fatigue; plastic instability; life-time predictions; brittle and ductile fracture; crack propagation and plastic blunting.

AME-577.description: Power production includes conventional fossil fuels, synthetic fuels, hydroelectric, solar, wind, geothermal, biomass and nuclear. The environmental consequences of various energy sources are discussed.

AME-580.prereqText: Recommended preparation: Linear algebra at the level of AME 525, partial differential equations at the level of AME 526, and exposure to Python programming at the level of AME 508.

AME-585.description: Finite element analysis of aerospace structures including heat transfer, joints, bellows, pressure vessels, flexible dynamics, random vibrations, repairs, buckling, fatigue/fracture and stress concentrations.
AME-585.prereqText: Recommended preparation: An undergraduate background in aerospace or mechanical engineering.

AMST-200.title: Introduction to American Studies and Ethnicity
AMST-200.description: Introduction to American studies and ethnic studies. Provides an overview of major theories, concepts, and issues.

AMST-204.title: Introduction to Native Studies
AMST-204.description: Overview of Native American studies, including Indigenous intellectualism and resistance through language revitalization, film-making, and the recognition of one another.

AMST-205.title: Introduction to American Popular Culture
AMST-205.description: Examines the relation between U.S. national culture, race, and popular culture.

AMST-211.title: Sex in America
AMST-211.description: Explores how the proliferation of sexual cultures, identities, politics shape everyday lives in the United States and beyond.

AMST-250.title: The African Diaspora
AMST-250.description: History, political-economy and aesthetics of the African Diaspora with emphasis on Latin America, the Caribbean, Europe and Africa.

AMST-301.title: America, the Frontier, and the New West
AMST-301.description: Introduction to an interdisciplinary study of American political, cultural and social life with a particular emphasis on the Western United States as a region. Recommended preparation: HIST 200, ENGL 263

AMST-312.title: Documenting Latinx Los Angeles Food Cultures
AMST-312.description: Explores Latinx food in Los Angeles through an anthropological lens. Students experience, document and analyze local food knowledge and traditions through active field study.

AMST-325.title: The Middle East in Hollywood
AMST-325.description: An examination of how Hollywood representations of the Middle East have changed over the last 100 years, focusing on how representations influence perceptions and policies.

AMST-336.title: Re-Viewing Religion in Asian America
AMST-336.description: Interdisciplinary analysis of the religions traditions, institutions, and experiences of Asians and Pacific Islanders in the U.S.

AMST-340.title: Latina/o LA
AMST-340.description: Examination of spatial and social patterns of the Latino population in Los Angeles. Emphasis on economic, demographic and cultural processes. Duplicates credit in the former GEOG-340.

AMST-345.title: Law and American Indian Studies
AMST-345.description: Examines indigenous sovereignties and the historical andcontemporary legal histories and cases which inform them.

AMST-348.title: Race and the Environment
AMST-348.description: Relationships between environmentalism, environmental problems and racial-ethnic minorities. Rise of environmental justice movement. Assessment of social science methods used to investigate these relationships. Duplicates credit in the former GEOG-350.

AMST-350.title: Junior Seminar in American Studies and Ethnicity: Theories and Methods
AMST-350.description: Advanced study in interdisciplinary theories and methods for analyzing race and ethnicity in the United Stes, including a comparative study of topics such as inequality, gender, and class.

AMST-364.title: African American Art
AMST-364.description: A survey of the fine arts produced by people of African descent in the United States from the nation's inception in the late 18th century until the contemporary moment.

AMST-376.title: Contemporary Issues in Asian American Communities
AMST-376.description: Survey of current social and political issues facing Asian American communities with emphasis on Los Angeles region; design and implementation of community-based research projects.

AMST-389.title: Carceral Geographies
AMST-389.description: Focusing on California, interdisciplinary research teams will study why there are so many new US prisons. What is their relationship to shopping malls, gated communities, globalization?

AMST-406.title: Social Media Storytelling for Latinx Audiences
AMST-406.description: Create native journalistic content for current social media and emerging platforms with an emphasis on engaging content for Latinx audiences and underrepresented communities.

AMST-445.title: African American Anthropology
AMST-445.description: An examination of anthropological research on race and African American culture, from the 18th century to the present.

AMST-449.title: Asian American Literature
AMST-449.description: Survey of Asian American literature from the earliest time to the present; development of prose, poetry, and novel.

AMST-452.title: Race, Gender and Sexuality
AMST-452.description: Examination of sexual discourses in the United States in the context of slavery, empire, sex work, labor markets, schools and prisons.

AMST-458.title: Race and Ethnicity in Entertainment and the Arts
AMST-458.description: Examines how race and ethnicity as social categories are shaped by communication media; focuses on how race and ethnicity sustain entertainment and media industries.

Recommended preparation: COMM 206
Class standing: not open to Freshman, Sophomore

AMST-464.title: Latino News Media in the United States
AMST-464.description: History and growing importance of Latino print and broadcast news media in covering immigration, discrimination, culture, social differences and other aspects of U.S. Latino life.

AMST-498.description: Capstone course for majors, highlighting interdisciplinary study of race and ethnicity in a comparative context.

AMST-520.description: Graduate seminar covering critical themes in the interdisciplinary field of Asian American Studies, including perspectives from anthropology, literature, sociology, history, political science, religious studies, cultural studies, women/gender studies, and psychology.

AMST-599.title: Special Topics

AMST-610.description: Exploration of issues involved in conducting research in the interdisciplinary field of Chicano/Latino Studies and guides students through the design and completion of a journal-quality research paper.

AMST-635.title: Critical Spatial Methods
AMST-635.description: An overview of key methodological and theoretical approaches to the study of race and space.

AMST-701.title: Contemporary Theories of American Studies and Ethnicity

ANST-501.title: Advanced Pharmacology of Anesthesia Practice I
ANST-501.description: Pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic principles, uptake and distribution of inhalational anesthetics, and pharmacology of respiratory and cardiovascular drugs. Application of pharmacologic principles to anesthetic management.
ANST-501.prereqText: Major: open only to Nurse Anesthesia

ANST-502.title: Principles of Nurse Anesthesia Practice
ANST-502.description: Basic theory of anesthesia administration, preanesthetic assessment, physical examination, monitoring. Case management including airway and blood/fluid management, anesthesia machine, and postoperative pain. Lecture/case study format.
ANST-502.prereqText: Major: open only to Nurse Anesthesia

ANST-601.title: Professional Integration to the Clinical Environment
ANST-601.description: Correlation of techniques of anesthesia administration with application of scientific and pharmacologic theory in the clinical environment with observation and supervised clinical instruction.
ANST-601.prereqText: Major: open only to Nurse Anesthesia

ANST-615.title: Clinical Residency in Nurse Anesthesia II
ANST-615.description: Correlation of techniques of anesthesia administration with application of scientific and pharmacologic theory in the clinical setting with observation and supervised clinical residency.

ANST-616.title: Advanced Clinical Residency in Nurse Anesthesia I
ANST-616.description: Correlating techniques of anesthesia administration with application of scientific and pharmacologic theory expanded to geriatric, obstetrical, and pediatric anesthesia; anesthetic management includes medically compromised patients.
ANST-616.prereqText:
Prerequisite: ANST 614; ANST 615
Major: open only to Nurse Anesthesia

ANST-619.title: Advanced Clinical Residency in Nurse Anesthesia IV
ANST-619.description: Correlation of techniques of anesthesia administration with application of scientific and pharmacologic theory expanded to neuroanesthesia, cardiac anesthesia, trauma anesthesia, critical care and pain management.
ANST-619.prereqText:
Prerequisite: ANST 614; ANST 615; ANST 616; ANST 617; ANST 618
Major: open only to Nurse Anesthesia

ANST-632.title: Clinical Synthesis II
ANST-632.description: Part two of a four-semester curriculum promoting synthesis and mastery of topics integral to the art and science of nurse anesthesia planning, management and delivery.
ANST-632.prereqText:
Prerequisite: ANST 631
Major: open only to Nurse Anesthesia   
Duplicates credit: ANST 621b and former ANST 621a

ANST-652.title: PeriOperative Evaluation and Management II
ANST-652.description: Continuation of ANST-651 with an emphasis on differential diagnosis, illness management, and perioperative optimization in patients with multiple health alterations.
ANST-652.prereqText:
Prerequisite: ANST 651
Concurrent enrollment: ANST 501, ANST 502
Recommended preparation: Two years of direct patient care in a critical care setting
Major: open only to Nurse Anesthesia

Major: open only to Nurse Anesthesia

ANTH-105.title: Culture, Medicine and Politics
ANTH-105.description: Survey of the impact of public institutions, private interests and cultural practices on health and the delivery of health care.

ANTH-123.title: Forms of Folklore
ANTH-123.description: Introduction to folklore as a discipline, including folklore research methods and theory. Core course for the minor in Folklore and Popular Culture.

ANTH-124.title: Archaeology of the Americas
ANTH-124.description: A comparative survey of archaeological cultures, Indigenous systems of belief, the complex histories, and deep relationships to landscapes across the Americas. Critically explores anthropological questions.

ANTH-180.title: Anthropology of Capitalism
ANTH-180.description: Uses anthropological frameworks and ethnographic case studies to explore key themes in contemporary capitalism (labor, commodification, markets, finance, entrepreneurship, resistance, authoritarian capitalism).

ANTH-200.title: The Human Animal
ANTH-200.description: Foundations of the human species. Examination of scientific evidence from Darwinian theory, primate behavior, fossils, and the behavior of modern people. Laboratory. Duplicates credit in former ANTH 200Lg.

ANTH-202.title: Archaeology: Our Human Past
ANTH-202.description: Archaeology as the means of investigating our shared human past, from the origins of humanity to the foundations of current civilization.

ANTH-203.title: Global Media
ANTH-203.description: An anthropological approach to examine social and cultural practices of media production, circulation and consumption, engaging with a variety of multimedia.

ANTH-205.title: Introduction to Global Studies and Cross-cultural Research
ANTH-205.description: The effects of globalization on social life in diverse communities, approaching related issues from an ethnographic perspective. Gateway course for the Global Studies Major.

ANTH-220.title: Anthropology of the Environment
ANTH-220.description: Introduces students to anthropological inquiry into human relationships with the environment and provides foundational training in qualitative research methods to investigate environmental issues.

ANTH-255.title: Culture, Performance and Personal Narrative
ANTH-255.description: Explore personal narratives: Stories people tell about their own lives and experiences as objects of artistic expression and sites for formation of individual and social identity.

ANTH-263.title: Exploring Culture through Film
ANTH-263.description: Concepts of social anthropology, using filmic representations of societies throughout the world. Gateway course for the Anthropology major.

ANTH-270.title: Ethnographic Film Past and Present
ANTH-270.description: A selective survey of ethnographic film from the 1890s to 2020s exploring the practice, theory and contemporary relevance of the genre.

ANTH-274.title: Posthuman Anthropology
ANTH-274.description: Examines how posthumanism is reshaping our understanding of humankind, including the ways in which "vernacular posthumanisms" are increasingly enacted in our everyday lives.
ANTH-274.prereqText:
Recommended preparation: Introductory courses in Anthropology and/or Philosophy
Duplicates credit: former ANTH 474

ANTH-312.title: Documenting Latinx Los Angeles Food Cultures
ANTH-312.description: Explores Latinx food in Los Angeles through an anthropological lens. Students experience, document and analyze local food knowledge and traditions through active field study.

ANTH-314.title: The Nature of Maya Civilization
ANTH-314.description: A seminar forum on Maya culture from the earliest form to thepresent; problems of origins, classic florescence, systemscollapse, conquests, persistance, and transformation today.

ANTH-315.title: Native North Americans
ANTH-315.description: Indigenous peoples of North America: major cultural themes, contemporary issues, language revitalization, native sovereignty, environmental issues, decolonization.

ANTH-325.title: Mixed Methods Research for Global and Cross-Cultural Studies
ANTH-325.description: Project-based research practicum emphasizing qualitative methods for cross-cultural analysis. Collecting and interpreting scholarly, ethnographic and archival materials.
ANTH-325.prereqText: Recommended preparation: Introductory coursework in Global Studies (GLOS), Anthropology (ANTH), or comparable fields within the humanistic social sciences.

ANTH-326.title: European Folklore and Ethnology
ANTH-326.description: Investigates the folklore of Europe, viewing European cultures and societies through an anthropological lens with a focus on shared, expressive cultural traditions.

ANTH-343.title: Heritage Archaeology
ANTH-343.description: An introduction to the field of heritage studies as it is practiced today, examining archaeological, ethnohistorical and ethnographic theory and methodologies, mixed-methods approaches and research.

ANTH-357.title: Cultures of Genocide, Cultures of Care
ANTH-357.description: The comparative analysis of genocide in different cultures and historical moments as well as different cultural responses to it, including human rights and humanitarianism.

ANTH-371.title: Cross-Cultural Research on Urban Gangs
ANTH-371.description: Youth gang dynamics and their effects on institutions. Comparative analysis of Asian, African, and Mexican American gangs.

ANTH-373.title: Magic, Witchcraft and Healing
ANTH-373.description: Analysis of the practices of witches and witch doctors, priests, diviners and traditional healers in Western and non-Western societies, relating their practices to religion and medicine.

ANTH-405.title: Evolutionary Medicine
ANTH-405.description: Evolutionary, cultural, and environmental factors in the emergence and existence of diseases; a Darwinian examination of illness in the human species.

Prerequisite: BISC 220 or BISC 221
Recommended preparation: HBIO 200Lg

ANTH-505.description: Introduction to philosophical, anthropological and sociological considerations of intersubjectivity and experience; narrative approaches to intersubjectivity and relational self-making focusing, especially on clinical encounters.
ANTH-505.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student, Master Student, Professional Year 1, Senior (Fifth Year)

ANTH-550.title: Global Black Thought
ANTH-550.description: Examines Black intellectual genealogies across a variety of sites and historical periods, with a thematic emphasis on the traffic of ideas and political forms.

ANTH-563.description: Writing proposals is an essential skill for anthropologists in academia and beyond. Provides familiarity with research grant proposals.

ANTH-570.description: A hands-on approach to contemporary topics in ethnographic media arts and creative nonfiction cinema.

ANTH-790.description: Research leading to the doctorate. Maximum number of units which may be applied to the degree to be determined by the department. Graded CR/NC.

ARCH-106.description: Introduction to the ways architecture is created and understood, for minors and non-majors. Hands-on discussion and laboratory session with some drawing and model building. Not available for credit to architecture majors.

ARCH-108.title: Idea to Reality
ARCH-108.description: Examines the entrepreneurial process of taking a product from idea to marketplace, including innovation, concepts of feasibility, design, prototyping, getting investors and marketing.

ARCH-109.title: Design Foundation Workshop
ARCH-109.description: Introduction to concepts and principles that are the distinguishing attributes of the architectural discourse and to the range of skills essential to the design process.
ARCH-109.prereqText:

ARCH-202B.title: Architectural Design II
ARCH-202B.description: Continuing development of principles and processes: sequence of projects selected to broaden awareness of design issues at various scales in the urban context. Prerequisite: 102abL.

ARCH-205B.title: Building Science I
ARCH-205B.description: The process and communication of building design: physical building shell, systems for structure, enclosure, and space ordering.

ARCH-211.title: Materials and Methods of Building Construction
ARCH-211.description: Basic considerations and design implications of the problem of determination of the materials and the construction details and processes for buildings.

ARCH-213B.title: Building Structures and Seismic Design

ARCH-228.title: Social Environments
ARCH-228.description: Exploration of the intersection between the urban form and the social life of cities, looking at systemic problems of urban societies and potential design solutions.

ARCH-303.title: Principles of Spatial Design I

ARCH-305B.title: Building Science II
ARCH-305B.description: The design of a building as a complex of interacting systems; relations of subsystems; influences of production and marketing on design.

ARCH-315.title: Design for the Luminous and Sonic Environment
ARCH-315.description: Ideas, problems, and computations related to the design of buildings in response to the luminous and sonic environment.

ARCH-316.title: Place and Culture
ARCH-316.description: (Study abroad programs only) Study of the relationships between places and culture through readings, lectures, discussion and weekly field trips.

ARCH-329.description: Students are required to have an architecture-related internship. Students reflect on the nature of their internships and the practice in general through readings and assignments.

ARCH-404.title: Topics in Modern Architecture in Southern California

ARCH-405B.title: Building Science III

ARCH-406.title: Global Studies: Topics in                        Architecture, Urbanism, History and Art
ARCH-406.description: Offered for particular geographic areas of study. Required prerequisite for all full semester undergraduate global programs. Also intended for general interest in focused study on particular geographic area.
ARCH-406.prereqText: Prerequisite: ARCH 304 or ARCH 214a and ARCH 214b

ARCH-411.title: Architectural Technology
ARCH-411.description: Architectural design considered as a technological problem; influence of technology on design; buildings as integrated sets of subsystems.

ARCH-412.prereqText:
Prerequisite: ARCH 403 or RED 425
Corequisite: SSCI 381 or SSCI 382

ARCH-421.title: Digital Architectural Photography
ARCH-421.description: Perceiving and documenting the built environment through the perspective and frame of the digital camera. Mastering the basic principles of the digital image through an understanding of frame, light, exposure, color correction and printing output.

ARCH-424.title: Field Studies in Architecture
ARCH-424.description: Field studies using direct observation, site recordings/documentation, analysis and evaluation supplemented by discussions and readings in architecture. Departmental approval. Recommended preparation: core curriculum

ARCH-425.title: Field Studies in Urbanism

ARCH-426.title: Field Studies in Tectonics
ARCH-426.description: Field studies using direct observation, site recordings/documentation, analysis and evaluation supplemented by discussions and readings in tectonics. Departmental approval. Recommended preparation: core curriculum

ARCH-431.title: Nonconventional Materials for the Built Environment
ARCH-431.description: An exploration of materials science topics relevant to the application of nonconventional materials in architecture, design, and engineering, addressing a broad range of materials, from the experimental to the vernacular.

ARCH-499.title: Special Topics
ARCH-499.description: Selected topics in various specialty areas of architecture.

ARCH-502A.title: Architectural Design V
ARCH-502A.description: The final architectural project under the guidance of a faculty adviser to demonstrate architectural knowledge, skills, and professional interests and goals.
ARCH-502A.prereqText:
Prerequisite: ARCH 500A; ARCH 501
Class standing: open only to Senior (Fifth Year)
Major: open only to Architecture
School: open only to School of Architecture

ARCH-505B.title: Graduate Architecture Design I
ARCH-505B.description: A general introduction to architectural principles, intended to develop design and critical thinking skills and proficiency to communicate those ideas effectively. Open to graduate architecture majors only.
ARCH-505B.prereqText:
Prerequisite: ARCH 505a
Major: open only to Architecture

ARCH-507.title: Theories of Computer Technology
ARCH-507.description: Fundamental theories and meanings of computation as a technique in architectural design.

ARCH-514B.title: Global History of Architecture
ARCH-514B.description: A historical survey of global architecture, analyzed as a product of social, cultural, religious and political forces.a: 4500 BCE to 1500 CE; b: 1500 CE to present.

ARCH-517.title: Current Topics in Building Science
ARCH-517.description: Critical studies in building science ranging from sustainability, lighting, acoustics, materials and methods, structures, energy issues, digital media, and fabrication. Students focus on minimum of two topics.

ARCH-519.title: Sustainability in the Environment:               Infrastructures, Urban Landscapes, and Buildings
ARCH-519.description: Methodologies and exercises on contextual design and environmentally sound technologies (EST's) applications for the sustainability of urban infrastructures, operative landscapes, and building integration in the urban system.

ARCH-523A.title: Structural Design and Analysis
ARCH-523A.description: a. Introduction to behavior and analysis of building structures. Structural loading, materials, and element types will be explored to understand the basic building blocks of buildings. b. Investigation and design of building structural systems for gravity, wind and seismic loading. Comprehensive design exploration of framing type, materials, detailing, layout, form and integration. Recommended preparation: One-semester college-level course in physics or calculus.

ARCH-525.title: Professional Practice: Pre-Design, Project and   Office Administration
ARCH-525.description: Design methodology, typology programming, site analysis, budget formulation and pro-forma procedures. Office management, emphasizing professional service and professional ethics as well as project management focusing on the architect's responsibilities during construction.

ARCH-526.title: Professional Practice: Legal and Economic        Context, Project Documentation
ARCH-526.description: The laws and regulations that affect architecture as well as building economics and financing. Development of comprehensive project documentation, detailing, specifications, drawing formats and organizations.

ARCH-527.title: Case Studies: The Development of Urban Housing
ARCH-527.description: An exploration of the various elements and stages of the housing development process. Recommended preparation: a preliminary understanding of real estate or housing.

ARCH-529.title: Urban Housing: Programs, Precedents, and Recent Case Studies
ARCH-529.description: Historical overview of the major domestic and international housing developments and innovations since the early 20th century case study format examining a wide range of issues that determine the form of urban housing in various cultures. Major emphasis on the detail analysis of social, technical, and design factors affecting recent housing developments. Recommended preparation: two years of undergraduate architectural studies.

ARCH-534.title: Landscape Construction: Topographic Design
ARCH-534.description: Techniques, strategies, materials, and standards to topographic design and construction in landscape architecture. In-class labs practice basic grading, drainage design, and stormwater management.

ARCH-535.title: Landscape Construction: Performance Approaches
ARCH-535.description: Develop tools and knowledge to expand the performative boundaries of landscape architecture beyond common typologies. Topics range from ecological infrastructure to design with weather patterns. A systematic approach to case studies, landscape technologies, and field trips seeds the knowledge base and representational methods necessary to design and build these complex landscape performances.

ARCH-537.title: Plant Ecology + Identification
ARCH-537.description: Principles and concepts of plant ecology and regional plant identification; introduction to California native plant species and communities with field trips and case studies.

ARCH-541B.title: Landscape Architecture Design
ARCH-541B.description: Projects in urban settings with emphasis on landscape continuities as well as development of integrative schematic proposals and detailed open space design.

ARCH-542B.title: Landscape Architecture Design
ARCH-542B.description: Projects for the public realm with emphasis on urbanity and connectivity, place and meaning.

ARCH-544.title: Landscape as Urbanism: Case Studies
ARCH-544.description: Cities predominantly in the Global South are studied in relationship to landscape systems. Focus on historic and future urbanization at the interface of natural systems and climate dynamics.

ARCH-545.title: Contemporary Theories of Landscape Architecture
ARCH-545.description: Explores contemporary landscape architecture theories, propositions and projects in the context of cities. The exploration methodology includes the study of epochal projects and theoretical texts.

ARCH-547.title: Advanced Topics in Urban Ecology
ARCH-547.description: Builds on knowledge related to the impacts of anthropocentrism on our current environmental/landscape condition - stresses on biodiversity, urban heat island, sea-level rise, etc, and strategies at mitigating these conditions - urban forestry, building soils, etc.

ARCH-548.title: Media for Landscape Architecture: 3D Design
ARCH-548.description: Developing and communicating landscape architecture design intent using visualization tools for three-dimensional studies.

ARCH-549.title: Fundamentals of Heritage Conservation
ARCH-549.description: Concepts and strategies for conservation of significant elements of the built environment: buildings, sites and communities as revealed by readings, site visits, and case studies.

ARCH-550.title: Heritage Conservation Policy and Planning
ARCH-550.description: Conservation practice within an economic, political, and cultural context looking at the regulatory environment, public advocacy and policy, real estate development, heritage tourism, environmental sustainability, cultural diversity, and interpretation. Recommended Preparation: ARCH-549.

ARCH-551.title: Conservation Methods and Materials
ARCH-551.description: Concepts and techniques for building conservation including identification of treatments, recordation and research, material properties and behavior, building forensics, and project implementation. Recommended preparation: ARCH-549.

ARCH-554.title: Heritage Conservation Practicum  Advanced Documentation
ARCH-554.description: Heritage conservation practicum utilizing in-depth documentation methodology to explore the historic built environment of greater Los Angeles. Topics will vary from year to year; may be repeated for credit when subject matter is different.

ARCH-555.title: Global Perspectives in Heritage Conservation
ARCH-555.description: In-depth analysis of international heritage conservation practice with a focus on a single country, continent, or world region outside the United States. Topics will vary from year to year; may be repeated for credit when subject matter is different.

ARCH-557.title: Sustainable Conservation of the Historic Built Environment
ARCH-557.description: Analysis of the intersection between green building and historic resources with an emphasis on stewardship and sustainability.

ARCH-560.title: A History of Architectural Theory: 1400-1914
ARCH-560.description: A seminar on architectural history from Alberti to Scott, reviewing primary texts and subsequent criticisms.

ARCH-561.title: Urbanism Themes and Case Studies
ARCH-561.description: Examines urbanism through case studies in theory and design to understand the impacts of globalization, technology, and sustainability on the contemporary city.

ARCH-563.title: Contemporary Architectural Theory
ARCH-563.description: Investigates, compares, and critiques modern and contemporary theories of the designed and built environment by focusing on key figures, movements, and texts.

ARCH-573.title: Seismic Design
ARCH-573.description: Theory, design methodology and practice of how seismicity affects architecture and structural system selection required for robust earthquake performance and seismic sustainability.
ARCH-573.prereqText: Recommended preparation: Basic knowledge of physics and/or exposure to architectural design. Two semesters of building structures required for M.Arch students

ARCH-574.title: Parametric Design
ARCH-574.description: An in depth and critical look into the reasons and uses for parametric design and its relationship to contemporary form, fabrication, and construction of the built environment.

ARCH-575B.title: Systems
ARCH-575B.description: The fundamental scientific principles governing light and sound in the built environment will be examined in the context of human physiological, psychological and biological needs.
ARCH-575B.prereqText:
Prerequisite: ARCH 575A
Recommended preparation: ARCH 505a, ARCH 505b

ARCH-576.title: Sustainable Design for Healthy Indoor Environments
ARCH-576.description: Course outlines the building design and its performance diagnostic processes required to assure indoor environmental quality and the building occupants environmental health, productivity, and physiological comfort.

ARCH-577.title: Lighting Design
ARCH-577.description: The physics, technical knowledge, professional knowledge, design, and documentation processes used in architectural lighting design, including first principles, manual calculations and computer simulations..

ARCH-578.title: Engineering Design: Industrialized and Modular Construction
ARCH-578.description: Integration of architecture, engineering and construction practices through the development of a construction project.

ARCH-580.title: Field Studies
ARCH-580.description: Off-campus field studies using direct observation, site recordings/documentation, analysis and evaluation supplemented by discussions and readings.

ARCH-581.title: Techniques in Digital Fabrication
ARCH-581.description: A practical introduction to digital fabrication. Covered topics include 3D surface milling, thermoforming, materials, casting and shop technology as applied to repeatable surfaces in architecture.

ARCH-585.title: Visual Storytelling and Entrepreneurship in Media
ARCH-585.description: Investigating visual stories as an active tool to critically explore and express design ideas; positions social media and crowdfunding as a foundation for creative action. Not open to Freshmen and Sophomores.
ARCH-585.prereqText: Class standing: not open to Freshman, Sophomore

ARCH-587.title: Light the Night...or Not?
ARCH-587.description: Explores principles and applications of exterior lighting design through lectures, demonstrations and experiments. Emphasizes perception, impact, integration of light with architectural forms and the environment.
ARCH-587.prereqText: Recommended preparation: Proficiency in presentation software (Powerpoint, Google slides, Keynote, InDesign, etc)

ARCH-590.title: Directed Research
ARCH-590.description: Research leading to the master's degree. Maximum units which may be applied to the degree to be determined by the department. Graded CR/NC.

ARCH-605B.title: Graduate Architecture Design- Comprehensive
ARCH-605B.description: b. Comprehensive project emphasizing the interaction between general principles and local sites, building technologies and total building design. Open only to Architecture majors.
ARCH-605B.prereqText:
Prerequisite: ARCH 605a
Major: open only to Architecture

ARCH-606.title: Advanced Architectural Theory
ARCH-606.description: Interrogates the architectural and cultural landscape of our contemporary cities through a combination of lectures and seminars on theories of place, identity, aesthetics, and technology.

ARCH-607.title: Advanced Computation
ARCH-607.description: Introduction to a range of new technologies and techniques examining their technical and theoretical implications including advanced computational design techniques and geospatial design tools.

ARCH-608.title: Urban Theory: Los Angeles Case Study
ARCH-608.description: Critically investigates the urban condition of Los Angeles through lectures, readings, and field visits. Aims to heighten awareness of the entwinement of environment, culture, architecture and the contemporary city.

ARCH-609.title: Advanced Digital Fabrication
ARCH-609.description: Introduction to a range of new technologies and techniques examining technical and theoretical implications including a range of digital fabrication technologies, robotics and film-making techniques.

ARCH-611.title: Advanced Building Systems Integration
ARCH-611.description: Design criteria development, material and construction process methods, occupancy based load profiles, performance/material life-cycle-mandates, durability for advanced building systems including integrity in sustainable urban systems.

ARCH-615.title: Seminar: Environmental Systems Research
ARCH-615.description: A detailed examination of current issues in the thermal, acoustical and radiant environment; recent developments in criteria, systems, controls, design tools and simulations; an understanding of the relationships between environmental factors, economics, and architectural goals.

ARCH-672.title: Future Building Skins: Advanced Applications in Architecture
ARCH-672.description: Focuses on the development of novel facade solutions that respond to shortcomings of contemporary facades applications in both new and existing buildings.

ARCH-691A.title: Heritage Conservation Thesis Preparation and Thesis
ARCH-691A.description: Introduction to, and exploration of, topics leading to the development of a thesis prospectus and directed research towards the completion of the master's thesis in heritage conservation.
ARCH-691A.prereqText:
Prerequisite: ARCH 549
Class standing: open only to Master Student
Major: open only to Heritage Conservation, Heritage Conservation/Planning

ARCH-691B.title: Heritage Conservation Thesis Preparation and Thesis
ARCH-691B.description: Introduction to, and exploration of, topics leading to the development of a thesis prospectus and directed research towards the completion of the master's thesis in heritage conservation.
ARCH-691B.prereqText:
Prerequisite: ARCH 549
Class standing: open only to Master Student
Major: open only to Heritage Conservation, Heritage Conservation/Planning

ARCH-692B.title: Building Science Thesis
ARCH-692B.description: Research and thesis for the Master of Building Science degree.
ARCH-692B.prereqText:
Prerequisite: ARCH 692A
Class standing: open only to Master Student
Major: open only to Building Science
School: open only to School of Architecture

ARCH-694.title: Research Publication Methods for Building Science
ARCH-694.description: Technical documentation, graphic representation, and verbal presentation for writing and presenting journal articles and conference presentations in building science.
ARCH-694.prereqText:
Class standing: open only to Master Student
Major: open only to Building Science
School: open only to School of Architecture

ARCH-698B.title: Advanced Design-Research
ARCH-698B.description: Directed research option for the MLArch degree.
ARCH-698B.prereqText:
Prerequisite: ARCH 698A
Class standing: open only to Master Student
Major: open only to Landscape Architecture, Planning/Landscape Architecture

ARCH-790.title: Doctoral Research
ARCH-790.description: Research leading to the doctorate. Maximum units which may be applied to the degree to be determined by the School of Architecture. Graded CR/NC.

ARCH-793B.title: Architecture Directed Design Research Option I
ARCH-793B.description: Directed Design Research option for graduate level architecture degree. Credit on acceptance of research project. Open only to Architecture majors. Graded IP/CR/NC.
ARCH-793B.prereqText:
Prerequisite: ARCH 793a
Major: open only to Architecture

ART-105.title: Art and Design Studio I
ART-105.description: Introduction to the fundamental elements in art making, design creation and thinking, including key principles of process and critical analysis.

ART-106.title: Art and Design Studio II
ART-106.description: Introduction to the fundamental elements in art making, design creation and thinking, including the key principles of process and critical analysis.

ART-110.title: Drawing for Art and Design
ART-110.description: An introduction to drawing, both skill and perception oriented, as the basic tool for all the visual arts and design.

ART-120.title: Painting I
ART-120.description: Practical introduction to oil and acrylic pigments, painting tools, mediums, processes and contemporary concepts. Primary experience in: color, composition and perception through representational and abstract painting.

ART-130.title: Ceramics I
ART-130.description: Practical and theoretical exploration of the nature of surface, form, volume and mass as fundamental elements of clay sculpture and the ceramic object.

ART-131.title: Wheel Throwing
ART-131.description: An introductory course using wheel throwing techniques for ceramics to explore a variety of forms through three-dimensional exercises.
ART-131.prereqText: Duplicates credit: former ART 230 and former FACE 212

ART-140.title: Sculpture I
ART-140.description: Practical and theoretical introduction to sculpture as dimensional manipulation. Primary exploration of form, mass, gravity, surface, structure and associative recognition in three-dimensional art.

ART-141.title: Creating and Understanding Visuals
ART-141.description: Lecture-studio course on the theory and history behind contemporary art, design, and visual communication; students also create work, informed by ideas from the lecture.

ART-149.title: Black and White Film and Darkroom Photography
ART-149.description: Introduces film cameras, development, and darkroom techniques, photographic history, theory and practice within an art context.

ART-150.title: Introduction to Photography: Process and Concept
ART-150.description: Digital photography as a medium of contemporary art. Includes concept development, DSLR cameras, lighting, digital workflow, software, large format printing and installation.

ART-205.title: Foundation Studio Intensive
ART-205.description: Cohort building studio intensive that ensures incoming transfers have foundational concepts and skill sets for intermediate and advanced studio courses.
ART-205.prereqText:
Major: open only to Art, Design, Fine Arts
School: open only to Roski School of Art and Design

ART-207A.title: Two-Dimensional Art Workshop
ART-207A.description: Studio practice to develop drawing fundamentals for game designers, animators and narrative artists.

ART-207B.title: Two-Dimensional Art Workshop
ART-207B.prereqText:
Prerequisite: ART 207A
Duplicates credit: former FA 207b

ART-260.title: Introduction to Video: Projection and Virtual Worlds in Art
ART-260.description: An introductory course exploring contemporary processes and practices of video experimentation in art including the camera, editing, digital manipulation and spatial and virtual platforms.

ART-280.title: Studio Critique I
ART-280.description: Interdisciplinary forum where students develop research skills, learn how to best articulate their artistic production, discuss materials related to their research interests, and critique the work of their peers.
ART-280.prereqText:
Class standing: open only to Sophomore
Major: open only to Art, Fine Arts
School: open only to Roski School of Art and Design

ART-310.title: Drawing II
ART-310.description: Directed examination of personal approaches to drawing with emphasis on making visual and artistic decisions and developing additional skills and sources of inspiration. Individual expression will be encouraged.
ART-310.prereqText:
Prerequisite: ART 110 or FADW 101
Duplicates credit: former FADW 301

ART-312.title: Comics Project
ART-312.description: All aspects of comics will be covered, from writing and composition to inking and marketing through the production of an individual multi-page comic creation.
ART-312.prereqText: Recommended preparation: Any drawing, graphic design or creative writing course

ART-314.title: Illustration for Art and Design
ART-314.description: Illustration techniques and professional practices across the range of fine art, comics, editorial illustration, narrative arts, visual development and others. Digital and hybrid approaches.
ART-314.prereqText: Recommended preparation: ART 110, ART 120, or any graphic design course

ART-330.title: Ceramics II
ART-330.description: Directed examination of aesthetic concepts and investigation into personal ideas as they relate to the development of a creative visual language in ceramics.
ART-330.prereqText:
Prerequisite: ART 130 or FACE 112
Duplicates credit: former FACE 312

ART-340.title: Sculpture II
ART-340.description: Directed examination of three-dimensional aesthetic concepts; development of an individual creative vision.
ART-340.prereqText:
Prerequisite: ART 140
Duplicates credit: former FASC 306

ART-362.title: Ideas in Intermedia
ART-362.description: An examination of the impact of digital media on contemporary culture, with attention to a particular, changing topic each semester.

ART-370.title: Printmaking
ART-370.description: Introductory course in various printmaking techniques; necessary skills and inherent expressive qualities of different printmaking methods are explored.

ART-380.title: Studio Critique II
ART-380.description: A continuation of ART 280 for third-year students, providing an interdisciplinary forum for artistic practice and a deepening critique of one's work and the work of peers.
ART-380.prereqText:
Prerequisite: ART 280
Class standing: open only to Junior
Major: open only to Art, Fine Arts
School: open only to Roski School of Art and Design

ART-412.title: Advanced Comics Project
ART-412.description: Creation of an advanced comic/chapter of a graphic novel of meaningful content, development of the student voice and to learn professional practices for careers in Comics.

ART-415.title: Studies in Drawing and Painting
ART-415.description: A studio examination of rotating topics in drawing/painting, either media-based or content-driven, with individual and collaborative projects; topics change each semester.
ART-415.prereqText:
Recommended preparation: ART 310; ART 320; or permission of instructor
Duplicates credit: former FADW 331 and former ART 315

ART-417.title: Digital Painting Studio
ART-417.description: Create a portfolio of images reflecting student interests, voice and sensibilities, through digital painting/drawing and using the software and hardware of their choice.

ART-418.title: Independent Studies in Studio Arts
ART-418.description: Independent research of specific topics under the direction of a faculty member. Administrative and faculty approval required.
ART-418.prereqText:
Recommended preparation: appropriate 300-level course work
Duplicates credit: former FA 418

ART-419.title: Professional Internship in the Arts
ART-419.description: An experiential/academic opportunity in a museum, gallery, community cultural center or related facility. Lectures, seminars, written analysis and working internship.

ART-420.title: Topics in Advanced Painting
ART-420.description: Examination of personal approaches and professional careers in painting and 2D art making, emphasis on making a body of work with creative freedom in committed studio space.
ART-420.prereqText:
Prerequisite: ART 320 or FAPT 305
Duplicates credit: former FAPT 405

ART-430.title: Topics in Advanced Ceramics
ART-430.description: Continued directed examination of aesthetic concepts and investigation into personal ideas as they relate to the development of a creative visual language in ceramics.
ART-430.prereqText:
Prerequisite: ART 330 or FACE 312
Duplicates credit: former FACE 412

ART-443.title: Woodworking
ART-443.description: Exploration of the essential skills in woodworking through lecture, demonstration and hands-on training. Includes instruction in joinery and relevant machinery and hand tools.

ART-444.title: Modeling and Mold Making
ART-444.description: Introduction to plaster mold making using clay and wax for both ceramics and sculpture. Exploration of various casting materials.
ART-444.prereqText: Duplicates credit: former FASC 136 and former ART 142

ART-445.title: Metal
ART-445.description: Introduction to metal in fine art. Emphasis on technical proficiencies and effective solutions working in a variety of metals.
ART-445.prereqText:
Recommended preparation: ART 140
Duplicates credit: former FASC 236 and former ART 242

ART-450.title: Topics in Advanced Photography
ART-450.description: In-depth exploration of photographic and artistic concepts as they apply to the articulation of personal work.
ART-450.prereqText:
Prerequisite: ART 350 or FAPH 309B
Duplicates credit: former FAPH 409

ART-452.title: Cut and Paste: Photo Collage Analog and Digital
ART-452.description: Exploration of methods with working photographically through collage.

ART-461.title: Motion Graphics for Art and Video
ART-461.description: An intensive investigation of the mechanics and methodology of contemporary software for video art. Recommended to be taken concurrently with ART 260.

ART-470.title: Topics in Advanced Printmaking
ART-470.description: Directed examination of specific printmaking media in relation to personal aesthetic goals and expressive concepts.
ART-470.prereqText:
Prerequisite: FAPR 311 or ART 370
Duplicates credit: former FAPR 411

ART-484.title: Contemporary Issues in Art
ART-484.description: An advanced studio and discussion course aims to expand a students relationship to, and understanding of, contemporary artistic dissemination, discourse, and display via a series of rotating topics.
ART-484.prereqText: Recommended preparation: junior status or permission of instructor

ART-485.title: Studio Capstone
ART-485.description: A faculty-mentored course supporting advanced conceptual exploration and the development of an ambitious, self-defined series or body of work; may culminate in a group exhibition or individual project.
ART-485.prereqText:
Class standing: open only to Senior
Major: open only to Art, Fine Arts
School: open only to Roski School of Art and Design

ART-494A.title: Senior Thesis
ART-494A.description: Individual research under guidance of faculty member for senior-level BFA students, leading to a substantial paper or other project.
ART-494A.prereqText:
Class standing: open only to Senior
Major: open only to Fine Arts
School: open only to Roski School of Art and Design

ART-515.description: Lecture and discussion course in the professional practice of art featuring formal presentations by visiting artists and scholars. (Duplicates credit in FA 515)

ART-520.title: Individual Studies
ART-520.description: Investigation of creative problems through various media. Course may be repeated. (Duplicates credit in former FA 520)

ART-525.title: Making and Curating Art: Pedagogy and Praxis
ART-525.description: Provides students with a foundation in the history and theory of studio art and curatorial education and develops their teaching skills in these areas.

ART-535.title: Group Critique
ART-535.description: Presentation and critique which builds students' skills in presenting and contextualizing their artwork for peer review; analytic discussion regarding directions in contemporary art.

ART-590.description: Research leading to graduate degree. Maximum units which may be applied to degree determined by department. Graded CR/NC. (Duplicates credit in former FA 590)

ART-594A.description: Credit on acceptance of Thesis. Open only to master students. Graded CR/NC. (Duplicates credit in former FA 594a)

ART-594B.description: Credit on acceptance of Thesis. Open only to master students. Graded CR/NC. (Duplicates credit in former FA 594b)
ART-594B.prereqText:

Class standing: open only to Master Student

ART-594Z.prereqText:
Prerequisite: ART 594b
Class standing: open only to Master Student

ARTL-502.title: Issues in the Arts and the Contemporary World
ARTL-502.description: Examination of major environmental trends including changing demographics, new business models, rapidly developing technology and globalization, and understanding their implications for the arts.

ARTL-504.title: Arts and the Community: Current Practice and New Visions
ARTL-504.description: Exploration of a range of ideas, ideologies and strategies that have historically been used to connect arts organizations to their communities.

ARTL-510.title: Arts Leadership Practicum
ARTL-510.description: Year-long practicum which puts ideas and concepts into practice. Each student will conceptualize, develop, and complete an arts project of his/her own choosing.

ARTL-590.title: Directed Research
ARTL-590.description: Research leading to the master's degree. Maximum units which maybe applied to the degree to be determined by the department.Graded CR/NC.

ARTL-598.title: Internship for Arts Leadership
ARTL-598.description: Practical work experience in the student's field of study, at an off-campus location. Students are individually supervised by faculty.

ARTL-790.title: Research
ARTL-790.description: Research leading to the doctorate. Maximum units which may be applied to the degree to be determined by the department. Graded CR/NC.

ASCJ-200.title: Navigating Media and News in the Digital Age
ASCJ-200.description: Students will be engaged as discriminating media/news consumers and contributors. Emphasis on critical skills needed to understand, employ, enjoy and help shape our media landscape.

ASCJ-210.title: Contours of Change in Media and Communication
ASCJ-210.description: Provides an introduction to cultivating a curious, critical, and proactive approach to the challenges of social change. Students will be encouraged to develop an expansive and critical definition and understanding of change as it relates to the role of media and communication in producing and responding to political and cultural transformations that shape our status as citizens and our ideas of citizenship.

ASCJ-420.title: Annenberg Collaboratory
ASCJ-420.description: Collaborative, cutting-edge, experimental, experiential, interdisciplinary, results-based classes taught in new ways and places. Recommended Preparation: ASCJ-220.

Class standing: open only to Freshman, Sophomore, Junior, Senior, Senior (Fifth Year)
School: open only to ASCJ

School: open only to ASCJ

ASTE-280.title: Foundations of Astronautical Engineering
ASTE-280.description: Coordinate systems and transformations. Spherical trigonometry. Filtering and estimation. Spacecraft orbits and orbital maneuvers. Rocket propulsion, spacecraft attitude dynamics, spacecraft communications, and space environment.
ASTE-280.prereqText:
Prerequisite: MATH 226; PHYS 152
Recommended preparation: Skill in MATLAB programming.

ASTE-291.title: Team Projects I
ASTE-291.description: Participation in ASTE undergraduate student team projects. Intended for lower-division students or those with little prior project experience. Departmental approval.

ASTE-305.title: Astronautical Gas Dynamics
ASTE-305.description: Introduction to compressible and rarefied gas flows with applications to rocket propulsion and the dynamics of supersonic and hypersonic vehicles and spacecraft; ionized gases and plasmas.
ASTE-305.prereqText:
Prerequisite: PHYS 153 or PHYS 163; AME 310
Corequisite: MATH 245

ASTE-421.title: Mission Systems Design
ASTE-421.description: Space systems engineering process: requirements definition; trade studies; system integration; technical reviews; cost and schedule development; case studies; ethics. Capstone design experience.
ASTE-421.prereqText:
Prerequisite: ASTE 331 or ASTE 331A
Class standing: open only to Senior

ASTE-490.title: Directed Research
ASTE-490.description: Individual research and readings. Not available for graduate credit.
ASTE-490.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Junior, Senior

ASTE-491.title: Team Projects II
ASTE-491.description: Participation in ASTE undergraduate student team projects. Intended for students with prior project experience. Departmental approval.

ASTE-523.title: Design of Low Cost Space Missions
ASTE-523.description: Reviews all aspects of space mission design for practical approaches to reducing cost. Examines "LightSat" mission experience and potential applicability to large scale missions. Graduate standing in engineering or science. Recommended preparation: ASTE 520 or some experience in space engineering.
ASTE-523.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student, Master Student

ASTE-535.title: Space Environments and Spacecraft Interactions
ASTE-535.description: Space environments and interactions with space systems. Vacuum, neutral and ionized species, plasma, radiation, micrometeoroids. Phenomena important for spacecraft operations.

ASTE-562.title: Spacecraft Life Support Systems
ASTE-562.description: Engineering fundamentals of spacecraft systems design and analysis to support human life in the space environment.
ASTE-562.prereqText:
Prerequisite: ASTE 524
Recommended preparation: Students should be able to perform numerical solutions to

ASTE-570.title: Liquid Rocket Propulsion
ASTE-570.description: Liquid-propelled rocket propulsion systems. Capillary devices for gas-free liquid acquisition in zero gravity. Ground and in-orbit operations. Propellant life predictions and spacecraft end-of-life de-orbiting strategies.

ASTE-572.title: Advanced Spacecraft Propulsion
ASTE-572.description: Nuclear, electric, sails, and far-term propulsion systems. Overviews of nozzles, heat transfer, electromagnetics, rarefied gases, and plasma physics. Analysis of electrothermal, electrostatic and electromagnetic thrusters. Graduate standing in engineering or science.

ASTE-575.title: Rocket and Spacecraft Propulsion
ASTE-575.description: Space missions, rocket dynamics, and propulsion requirements. Thermodynamics and combustion; compressible gas dynamics in nozzles. Liquid- and solid-propellant rockets; launch systems. Advanced propulsion.

ASTE-586.description: Dynamics of systems of particles and rigid bodies; spacecraft attitude systems; attitude maneuvers (spin, precession, nutation, etc.); attitude stabilization and attitude determination; simulation methods.

ASTR-100.description: Survey of the universe: planets, satellites, comets, stars, nebulae, galaxies. Practical component includes planetary observations and dark-sky field trip. Not available for major credit.

ASTR-104.description: Laboratory component for ASTR 100Lxg for transfer students with equivalent lecture credit from another institution. For transfer students only. Departmental approval. Graded CR/NC.

ASTR-110.description: Introduction to the physical characteristics and structure of the Universe, with detailed discussions and labs emphasizing the underlying physics and mathematics.

Major: open only to Astronomy

ASTR-200.title: Life in the Universe
ASTR-200.description: Survey of the prospects for life in our solar system and beyond, based on the evolution of life on Earth.

ASTR-350.title: Astrophysics I
ASTR-350.description: Introduction to astrophysics including stellar parameters, evolution, end states (white dwarfs, supernovae, black holes) and extrasolar planetary systems; emphasis on physical processes and cosmic significance.

ASTR-422.title: Galaxies and Large-Scale Structures in the Universe
ASTR-422.description: Galaxies and clusters of galaxies: their content, structure, dynamics, distribution, and motions; the cosmic microwave background: theory and observation; elements of observational cosmology. Prerequisite: PHYS-153L or PHYS-163L.

ASTR-490.description: Individual research and readings. Not available for graduate credit.
ASTR-490.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Junior, Senior

ASTR-540.title: Advanced Cosmology
ASTR-540.description: The Universe: its content and thermal history. Density anisotropies: initial conditions, linear and non-linear evolution. Observables, current and future data, theory-observations comparison.
ASTR-540.prereqText: Prerequisite: PHYS 504 or PHYS 508a or PHYS 508b or PHYS 510 or PHYS 518

BAEP-450.title: Fundamentals of Entrepreneurship
BAEP-450.description: Starting and managing one's own business: developing a viable concept, organizing the enterprise, market and financial planning, and controlling the organization. (Duplicates credit in BAEP 451)

BAEP-452.title: Feasibility Analysis
BAEP-452.description: Students develop, analyze, and validate entrepreneurial concepts (including marketing, operational, and financial considerations) using customer feedback and risk assessment to conclude worthiness to pursue.
BAEP-452.prereqText: Prerequisite: BAEP 423 or BAEP 450 or BAEP 451 or BUAD 301

BAEP-453.title: Venture Management
BAEP-453.description: Design and application of organization structures and systems in management of new ventures.
BAEP-453.prereqText: Prerequisite: BAEP 423 or BAEP 450 or BAEP 451 or BUAD 301

BAEP-454.title: Venture Initiation: Launching and Scaling Your Startup
BAEP-454.description: Learn to build a startup from concept to reality. Focus on real-world entrepreneurial action and execution. Prerequisite: BAEP 452.

BAEP-455.title: Founder's Dilemmas
BAEP-455.description: Prepares potential founders, hires, and investors for the decisions they will face both before and during their involvement with new ventures.

BAEP-460.title: Seminar in Entrepreneurship
BAEP-460.description: Perspectives into the art and science of entrepreneurship under the guidance of a master instructor. Specific topics vary.

BAEP-470.title: The Entrepreneurial Mindset- Taking the Leap
BAEP-470.description: A deeper insight into the entrepreneurial mind, how it approaches opportunities and challenges and gives leadership to an organization.

BAEP-473.title: Sales Mindset for Entrepreneurs
BAEP-473.description: The sales planning decisions that entrepreneurs make, including how to accelerate startup revenue, what metrics drive success and how to build great sales teams.

BAEP-475.title: Entertainment Entrepreneurship
BAEP-475.description: Explore the current entrepreneurial trends and opportunities in the entertainment industry and uncover the key success factors for entrepreneurs in this industry.
BAEP-475.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Sophomore, Junior, Senior, Senior (Fifth Year)

BAEP-480.description: Explores the dynamics of family and privately held businesses. Exploring generational and extended family issues, opportunities and obstacles faced in today's environment.
BAEP-480.prereqText: Class standing: not open to Freshman

BAEP-495.title: Practicum in Business Issues (Internship)
BAEP-495.description: Combined classroom discussion and field application of business theories and practices; part-time internship employment. Project to be jointly defined by student, employer and professor. Graded CR/NC.

BAEP-497.description: Individual or team projects solving real problems for an enterprise. Situation analyses; research proposal composition; field research techniques; statistical analysis; oral and written presentations. Open only to Juniors and Seniors. Graded Credit/No Credit.
