BISC-102.title: Humans and Their Environment
BISC-102.description: An examination of the physical and biological laws that influence agriculture, pollution, population dynamics (including humans), climate, biodiversity and ecosystem structure and function. Not available for major credit.

BISC-103.title: General Biology for the Environment and Life
BISC-103.description: Study of common skills in biology, including basics of evolution, systematics, ecology, genetics, biochemistry and molecular biology, physiology, and anatomy.

BISC-108.title: Special Laboratory I
BISC-108.description: Laboratory component for BISC 120 for entering freshmen or transfer students with advanced placement or equivalent lecture credit from another institution.

BISC-109.title: Special Laboratory II
BISC-109.description: Laboratory component for BISC 220 for entering freshmen or transfer students with advanced placement or equivalent lecture credit from another institution.

BISC-110.title: Good Genes, Bad Genes
BISC-110.description: Introduction to the scientific method; basic instruction in molecular biology with emphasis on how biological research advancement has impacted medicine, commerce and society in general.

BISC-115.title: The Biology of Food
BISC-115.description: Exploration of molecular biology, biochemistry, microbiology, nutrition and the history of biology through the study of food, focusing on food's relationship to the biological world.

BISC-120.title: General Biology: Organismal Biology and Evolution
BISC-120.description: In-depth survey of key topics related to advances in our knowledge of the diversity of life and evolution; origin of life; eukaryotes/prokaryotes; ecology.

BISC-180.title: Evolution
BISC-180.description: Changes in the physical and biological universe over time; origins of life, dinosaurs, human evolution. Implications of evolutionary mechanisms and mass extinctions for human survival.

BISC-194.title: Introduction to Research II
BISC-194.description: A series of lectures and discussions at which faculty of the department introduce their research activities to students entering biology and related majors.
BISC-194.prereqText: Recommended preparation: At least one introductory biology course or equivalent AP credit in biology

BISC-199.title: Neuroscience Colloquium
BISC-199.description: Introduction to research activities conducted by Neuroscience faculty at USC.

BISC-220.title: General Biology: Cell Biology and Physiology
BISC-220.description: In-depth survey of key topics related to advances in our knowledge of cellular biology and physiology; cell composition/metabolism; gene action; organism structure and function. Recommended preparation: high school chemistry; BISC 120L or BISC 121L.

BISC-221.title: Advanced General Biology: Cell Biology and Physiology
BISC-221.description: Equivalent to 220L, but taught at a higher level for exceptionally well-prepared students. Admission to the course by departmental approval only.
BISC-221.prereqText:
Prerequisite: BISC 120 or BISC 121
Corequisite: CHEM 105b or CHEM 115b

BISC-230.title: The Biology of the Brain
BISC-230.description: Exploration of the unique properties of brain cells that allow complex perceptions and behaviors; examination of structure and activity of brain cells that underlie function.

BISC-290.title: Introduction to Biological Research
BISC-290.description: Experience in basic techniques through supervised research in the research laboratory of a departmental faculty member.
BISC-290.prereqText: Prerequisite: BISC 120 or BISC 121; BISC 220 or BISC 221; CHEM 105B or CHEM 108 or CHEM 115B

BISC-300.title: Microbiology
BISC-300.description: Comparative approach to bacteria, Archaea and viruses; their structure, life cycles, geochemical activity, ecology and nutrition. Fundamentals of metabolism and microbial genetics.
BISC-300.prereqText:
Prerequisite: BISC 120 or BISC 121 or BISC 320
Recommended preparation: BISC 312 or BISC 330 or CHEM 330 or CHEM 350

BISC-307.title: General Physiology
BISC-307.description: Physiological functions of the circulatory, digestive, endocrine, integuementary, musculoskeletal, nervous, respiratory, and urogenital systems in animals. Lecture, 3 hours; Laboratory, 3 hours.

BISC-312.title: Molecular Biochemistry
BISC-312.description: Structure and function of biological macromolecules; major metabolic pathways including glycolysis and photosynthesis. DNA replication, repair, and recombination; gene expression, regulation and epigenetics.

BISC-313.title: Evolution and Population Genetics
BISC-313.description: History of evolutionary thought; molecular basis for evolution; dynamics of genes in populations; specialization and macroevolution; patterns of evolution. Recommended preparation: BISC-320, BISC-325, and familiarity with algebra, basic chemistry, and basic physics.
BISC-313.prereqText: Prerequisite: BISC 220 or BISC 221; BISC 120 or BISC 121

BISC-321.title: Multidisciplinary Seminar: Science, Technology and Society
BISC-321.description: Builds upon a basic science background to provide students with an awareness of cutting edge scientific research, its technological applications and its societal ramifications.
BISC-321.prereqText:
Prerequisite: BISC 120 or BISC 121 or BISC 220 or BISC 221; CHEM 105A or CHEM 107 or CHEM 115A; PHYS 135A or PHYS 151
Duplicates credit: former MDA 321

BISC-330.title: Biochemistry
BISC-330.description: Basic biochemical principles; classes of molecules - structure and function; cellular energetics.
BISC-330.prereqText:
Prerequisite: CHEM 322A or CHEM 325A
Duplicates credit: former BISC 316

BISC-363.title: Mammalogy
BISC-363.description: Introduction to the morphology, classification, distribution and physiology of mammals; study of major mammalian groups worldwide and identification and field study of local species.

BISC-364.title: Advanced Techniques in Field Mammalogy
BISC-364.description: Application of modern field techniques to monitor mammalian biodiversity; quantification of biodiversity using museum-based collections and geospatial data; multi-day field trips.

BISC-380.title: Stem Cells: Fact and Fiction
BISC-380.description: Exploring how stem cells and regenerative medicine are portrayed in culture, the scientific underpinnings of what is currently possible, and visions into the future.
BISC-380.prereqText:
Recommended preparation: basic cell biology
Duplicates credit: former MEDS 380

BISC-401.title: Introduction to Computational Analysis of Biological Data
BISC-401.description: A project-based course integrating biology, computer science, and statistics through the analysis of genomic datasets available publicly or collected and sequenced during the semester.

BISC-402.title: RNA Biology and Biotechnology
BISC-402.description: Fundamental concepts of RNA biology and state-of-the-art biotechnologies using RNA for medical and industrial applications; CRISPR/Cas genome editing; therapeutic advances exploiting RNA biology.
BISC-402.prereqText:
Prerequisite: BISC 312 or BISC 320; BISC 325
Recommended preparation: BISC 330

BISC-407.title: Cellular and Molecular Neuroscience
BISC-407.description: An examination of individual nerve cell development, target location, and establishment of functional synapses; how dysfunction in these processes contributes to neurological and neuropsychiatric diseases.

BISC-408.title: Systems Neuroscience: From Synapses to Perception
BISC-408.description: Sensory and motor systems to illustrate concepts regarding the functional organization of the brain, from microcircuitry of neural circuits to global processes such as perception. Prerequisite: BISC 421.

BISC-410.title: Applications of Molecular Biology to Medicine
BISC-410.description: Advances and trends in the understanding, diagnosis and treatment of human diseases.
BISC-410.prereqText:
Prerequisite: BISC 312 or BISC 330 or CHEM 350
Class standing: open only to Senior

BISC-411.title: Advanced Cell Biology
BISC-411.description: The synthesis, transport and assembly of the complex structures that mediate eukaryotic cellular function. Electrical and biochemical mechanisms underlying intercellular communication.

BISC-412.title: Oceans, Climate, and the Environment
BISC-412.description: A comprehensive survey of climate, including ocean, atmospheric and continental environments with a California sustainability focus. Methods in climate, oceanography and paleoclimate and independent research.
BISC-412.prereqText:
Recommended preparation: GEOL 107Lg or GEOL 150Lg or GEOL 160Lg
Class standing: not open to Freshman

BISC-423.title: Epilepsy to Ecstasy: Biological Basis of Neurological Disord
BISC-423.description: Examination of various neurological disorders originating from developmental signaling and/or anatomical abnormalities.

BISC-424.title: Brain Architecture
BISC-424.description: How the parts of the brain are interconnected to form a complex biological computer, from historical, evolutionary and developmental perspectives.

BISC-427.title: The Global Environment
BISC-427.description: Earth's development as a habitable planet, from origin to human impacts on global biogeochemical cycles in the ocean, land, atmosphere. Discussion of environmental alternatives.
BISC-427.prereqText:
Prerequisite: BISC 103 or BISC 120 or BISC 121; CHEM 103 or CHEM 105B or CHEM 108 or CHEM 115B
Major: open only to Biological Sciences, Environmental Science and Health, Environmental Studies, Geological Sciences

BISC-431.title: Aquatic Microbiology
BISC-431.description: Introduction to the habitat, phylogenetic, physiological and metabolic diversity of microbial life in aquatic environments.
BISC-431.prereqText:
Prerequisite: BISC 103 or BISC 120 or BISC 121
Duplicates credit: BISC 419L

BISC-435.title: Advanced Biochemistry
BISC-435.description: Macromolecular structure and function; enzymology; metabolic regulation. Lecture, 3 hours; discussion, 2 hours.

BISC-440.title: Biodemography of Aging
BISC-440.description: Consideration of the biological and social-cultural factors that govern the evolution of life spans and the life of humans and selected animal models

BISC-445.title: Fundamentals of Vertebrate Biology
BISC-445.description: Evolution and comparative anatomy of vertebrates.
BISC-445.prereqText:
Prerequisite: BISC 120 or BISC 121

BKN-610.description: Introduction of topics related to assessments of athlete performance on the field or in the sports setting. BKN-611.description: Introduction to the physiological assessment of athlete performance. Focus on understanding, performing and interpreting physiological assessments such as metabolic testing (VO2max), hydration, oxygen saturation, body composition, lactate threshold, heart rate, core body temperature.

BME-201.description: Examination of the technical and practical challenges involved in the development of medical devices, including neural implants, in industry and the clinical setting. Recommended preparation: BME 101.

BME-210.description: Computational methods for simulation of circulatory, respiratory, pharmacokinetic, and neural models. Quadrature, differential equations, systems of linear equations, simulation languages, experimental statistics.

COH-705.title: Research and Biostatistics in Healthcare
COH-705.description: Introduction to research processes; emphasizes methods and designs frequently used to study health and health care delivery.

COH-706.title: Foundations and Strategies in Health Education
COH-706.description: Examines the impact of education in community oral health, identifying strategies to engage and empower the members of the community to achieve health and wellness.

COH-710.title: Health Assessment
COH-710.description: The importance of health assessment; identification of strategies to understand the needs and priorities of a healthy community.

COH-712.title: Practicum 2
COH-712.description: Incorporates a service learning approach involving a partnership between the student, community organization and designated faculty or research team members.

COH-717.title: Practicum 3
COH-717.description: Participation in a multidisciplinary team; collection of community health data to build a plan for sustainability and maintenance.

COLT-102.title: On Location: The Place of Literature in Global Cultures
COLT-102.description: Comparative study of works from a broad range of cultural traditions that originate from, and provide insight into, vital global locations outside the Western sphere.

COLT-255.title: Southeast Asian Literature and Film
COLT-255.description: Comparative approach and general introduction to literature and cinema from selected countries in the Association for Southeast Asian Nations.

COLT-264.title: Asian Aesthetic and Literary Traditions
COLT-264.description: A comparative study of the Asian aesthetic heritage of poetry, painting, music, and drama; of literary themes, trends, and myths.

COLT-303.title: Globalization: Culture, Change, Resistance
COLT-303.description: Cultural dimensions of issues in globalization: migration, diaspora, terrorism, communications, climate change, collectives, production and technology, money and exchange.

COLT-346.title: Fictions of the First Person
COLT-346.description: Study of prose fiction in the first person as a model of fiction in general and as a reflection of the fictional structure of selfhood.

COLT-347.title: Modern Arab Culture and Literature
COLT-347.description: Examines contemporary Arab state-society relations using literature to illustrate how people construct meanings and portray issues of national, social, and cultural significance.

COLT-374.title: Women Writers in Europe and America
COLT-374.description: Introduction to works of major women writers from the Middle Ages to the 20th century in their literary, social and cultural contexts.

COLT-377.title: Gender and Sexuality in Literary Theory
COLT-377.description: Literary representations and theories of gender difference. Examines questions of gendered voice in writing and the cultural construction of gender in various periods and cultures.

COLT-379.title: Nationalism and Postcolonialism in Southeast Asian Cinema
COLT-379.description: Cinema from Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, and Vietnam in local and global cultural contexts.

COLT-426.title: Utopias
COLT-426.description: Examination of selected utopias in their historical context as "no places" whose projections of alternate cultures always comment on their own.

COLT-487.title: Critical Image
COLT-487.description: Introduction to critical reflection on the image. Analysis of criticism, fiction, film, and visual artifacts.

COLT-490.title: Directed Research
COLT-490.description: Individual research and readings. Not available for graduate credit.
COLT-490.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Junior, Senior

COLT-495.title: Senior Honors Thesis
COLT-495.description: Writing of an honors thesis under individual faculty supervision.
COLT-495.prereqText:
Class standing: open only to Senior
Major: open only to Comparative Literature

COLT-511.title: Translating Race
COLT-511.description: Contemporary notions of racial, cultural, and religious difference across languages and history.
COLT-511.prereqText:
Recommended preparation: COLT 510
Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student, Master Student

COLT-620.title: Seminar in Literature, Culture and Thought
COLT-620.description: Varying focus on social and political thought, psychoanalysis, and philosophy in relation to literary and cultural analysis.

COMM-200.title: Communication and Social Science
COMM-200.description: Social scientific inquiry into human communication; core theories of message production and reception in interpersonal, group and organizational contexts.

COMM-204.title: Public Speaking
COMM-204.description: Principles and practices of effective oral communication; analysis of the speaking-listening process; selection and organization of speech materials; use of new presentation technologies.

COMM-205.title: Communication Practicum
COMM-205.description: Students address communication issues in a field setting. They will evaluate communication practices using appropriate methodology. Projects are jointly evaluated by internship supervisor and professor. Sophomore standing. Graded: CR/NC. Not for major credit for Communication majors.
COMM-205.prereqText: Class standing: not open to Freshman

COMM-206.title: Communication and Culture
COMM-206.description: Examines cultural institutions, ideologies, artifacts, and productions; role of culture in everyday life; cultural studies as methodology; culture and power.

COMM-209.title: Communication and Media Economics
COMM-209.description: Economic and political economic principles for the analysis of communication and media industries including broadcasting, newspapers, motion pictures, music, video games, advertising and public relations.

COMM-300.title: Entertainment, Communication and Society
COMM-300.description: Theoretical foundation for understanding the construction, consumption, and consequences of entertainment from classical to contemporary times; situates entertainment within the ecology of information and communication.

COMM-301.title: Empirical Research in Communication
COMM-301.description: Experimental and survey methods for communication study; basic statistical concepts, procedures, and tests.

COMM-302.title: Persuasion
COMM-302.description: Theories and research in social influence; strategies and tactics of persuasive communications in such settings as politics, public relations, advertising, business.

COMM-305.title: Understanding Social Science Research
COMM-305.description: Students learn to be consumers rather than creators of social science research. Examines the challenges and opportunities of communicating research through mass media.

COMM-307.title: Sound Clash: Popular Music and American Culture
COMM-307.description: Music as inter-cultural communication and method for exploring race and ethnicity in the constitution of American culture and American self; role of music industry.

COMM-309.title: Communication and Technology
COMM-309.description: Cultural, social, political, and economic dynamics of communication technologies, including internet architecture, social media, participatory cultures, privacy, surveillance, networked journalism, big data, algorithms, online activism.

COMM-310.title: Media and Society
COMM-310.description: Interplay between media and society, including family and children's socialization, inter-group relations and community, pornography and violence, gender and race, media ethics, conduct of politics.

COMM-311.title: Communication and Publics
COMM-311.description: Forms of civic life; opportunities and obstacles in forming, participating in, and disrupting community; issues of knowledge, power, identity; theories/methods of rhetorical analysis and production.

COMM-313.title: Screen time: How Media Shapes Us
COMM-313.description: Investigate medias role in daily activities. Examine usage trends, research methods and industry analytics. Analyze media impacts, policy issues and research-informed strategies.

COMM-315.title: Health Communication
COMM-315.description: Behavioral approaches to health communication; communication competencies in health care settings, theories of risky behaviors and behavioral change programs.

COMM-321.title: Communication and Social Media
COMM-321.description: Social media within the broader social, political, and historical contexts; key themes include labor, Web 2.0, self-branding, celebrity, participation, privacy, online shaming, and activism.

COMM-322.title: Argumentation and Advocacy
COMM-322.description: Basic argumentation theory including analysis. Research and evidence, case construction, refutation; discursive and visual argument; diverse fields of advocacy including law, politics, organizations, interpersonal relations.

COMM-324.title: Intercultural Communication
COMM-324.description: Cultural variables and social psychological processes that influence intercultural interaction; relationship between communication and culture in diverse settings including business, medicine, and education.

COMM-339.title: Communication Technology and Culture
COMM-339.description: This course examines philosophies and popular representations of technology from the origins of western culture to the present and identifies the complex attitudes toward technology.

COMM-340.title: The Cultures of New Media
COMM-340.description: Cultural implications of computer-mediated communication and related media. Ideological responses to media innovation; debates over artificial intelligence, virtual communities, and virtual reality. Recommended preparation: COMM 339.

COMM-355.title: Advertising and Communication
COMM-355.description: Advertising as a mode of communication; US advertising history and institutions; economic and policy contexts (domestic and global); critical analysis of advertising texts

COMM-360.title: Los Angeles: Communication and Culture
COMM-360.description: Representations of Los Angeles communicated in diverse media; the city as a rhetorical text; analysis of cultural identities, art, architecture and representations in popular culture.

COMM-363.title: Media Consumption
COMM-363.description: Theoretical approaches to the study of media consumption and audiences; examines international media and consumption practices; explores new media's impact on consumption.

COMM-365.title: The Rhetoric of London
COMM-365.description: Examination of the modern city as a communicative text with London as the case study.

COMM-373.title: Media Technologies and Free Speech
COMM-373.description: Exploration of how freedom of speech has been adapted and applied to "new media" from film to computer algorithms and video games.

COMM-375.title: Business and Professional Communication
COMM-375.description: Oral and written communication skills demanded in the workplace including informative and persuasive speeches; interviewing; team communication; and training material preparation. Recommended preparation: COMM 204

COMM-380.title: Forensics Laboratory
COMM-380.description: Directed individual research studies of contemporary problems. Supervised laboratory experience. Open only to members of the University debate squad.

COMM-382.title: Sports, Business and Media in Today's Society
COMM-382.description: An inside look at the important stories, topical issues, trends and historical developments related to the growing influence of business and media on college and professional sports; identifying the key components and meeting the influencers in class that help shape the business side of sports, while recognizing the role the media plays in providing daily coverage across multiple platforms.

COMM-383.title: Sports, Communication and Culture
COMM-383.description: Rhetorical and critical approaches to sports and public discourse; application to sports organizations, the news and popular media; representations of gender and race in sports.

COMM-384.title: Interpreting Popular Culture
COMM-384.description: Popular culture as an indicator of cultural values, a producer and reflection of cultural meaning, and a means of communication; theory and case studies.

COMM-385.title: Organizational Communication
COMM-385.description: How communication processes both create organizations and are constrained by them. Theory and research into topics such as culture, technology, power, leadership and decision-making in a variety of organizational contexts.

COMM-387.title: Sports and Social Change
COMM-387.description: Application of critical, sociological and rhetorical theories to sports events and sport media; examination of the role of sports in enacting social change.

COMM-388.title: Ethics in Human Communication
COMM-388.description: Value perspectives on communication in varied settings: interpersonal, organizational, and public. Issues of truth and responsibility in family and social interactions, advertising, and governmental communication.

COMM-391.title: Made in Italy: The Marketing of an Ideal
COMM-391.description: Examines case studies on important Italian companies, ranging from the transportation to the luxury goods industries from both an economical and business point of view.
COMM-391.prereqText: Major: open only to Communication, Journalism, Public Relations

COMM-392.title: Media and Migration in Times of European Crisis
COMM-392.description: Investigates the implications of the perceptual process of mass media generated immigration discourse in Europe.
COMM-392.prereqText: Major: open only to Communication, Journalism, Public Relations

COMM-393.title: The Rhetoric of Rome
COMM-393.description: Examination of the modern city as a communicative text with Rome as the case study.
COMM-393.prereqText: Major: open only to Communication, Journalism, Public Relations

COMM-395.title: Gender, Media and Communication
COMM-395.description: Issues of gender in communication, including: mediarepresentations of femininity and masculinity; and gender's rolein communication at the interpersonal, public, and cultural levels.

COMM-400.title: Seminar in Communication
COMM-400.description: Advanced readings in communication theory and research (broadly defined); specialized interest areas of individual faculty on the frontiers of knowledge; seminar topics change each semester.
COMM-400.prereqText: Class standing: not open to Freshman, Sophomore

COMM-406.title: Communicating About Sex
COMM-406.description: Communicating with partners, friends, parents and health care professionals about sexual behavior; interpersonal and mediated contexts; understanding of sexual scripts; current theory and research.
COMM-406.prereqText:
Class standing: not open to Freshman, Sophomore
Duplicates credit: former COMM 336

COMM-412.title: Communication and Social Movements
COMM-412.description: Social and political movements as rhetorical phenomena; ideology, organization, and influence of such movements as civil rights, "New Left," feminism, "New Right," environmentalism.
COMM-412.prereqText: Class standing: not open to Freshman, Sophomore

COMM-429.title: The Internet, Economy and Society
COMM-429.description: Examines the effects of the Internet on communication industries, the economy, economic policy, and on social, political and cultural practices.
COMM-429.prereqText: Class standing: not open to Freshman, Sophomore

COMM-434.title: Italian Media: Popes, Politicians, and Popular Culture
COMM-434.description: Provides an overview of 2,000 years of Italian-style communications, from Julius Caesar to Machiavelli, Mussolini and the Mafia.

COMM-441.title: Podcasting: Origin Stories
COMM-441.description: A foundational understanding of the historic, cultural and theoretical underpinning of the podcast medium with an emphasis on critical listening.

COMM-444.title: Critical Theories of Sport
COMM-444.description: Focuses on critical theories that examine social and political roles of sport in society and how these roles play out in media and broadcast platforms.
COMM-444.prereqText: Class standing: not open to Freshman, Sophomore

COMM-451.title: Visual Communication and Social Change
COMM-451.description: Analysis of photography's evolution; new strategies for the photographic image, photo documentary work and global social issues; analysis of images on blogs and Websites.
COMM-451.prereqText: Class standing: not open to Freshman, Sophomore

COMM-456.title: Entertainment, Marketing and Culture
COMM-456.description: Explores blurring of entertainment, marketing and culture in advanced information economies; intersections of culture and media and their social ramifications.
COMM-456.prereqText: Class standing: not open to Freshman, Sophomore

COMM-458.title: Race and Ethnicity in Entertainment and the Arts
COMM-458.description: Examines how race and ethnicity as social categories are shaped by communication media; focuses on how race and ethnicity sustain entertainment and media industries.
COMM-458.prereqText:
Recommended preparation: COMM 206
Class standing: not open to Freshman, Sophomore

COMM-467.title: Gender and the News Media
COMM-467.description: Gender and news media evolving images of women and men in print and electronic media. Impact of gender in content and style of news, television and cinema. Open to non-majors.

COMM-473.title: Advanced Issues in Communication and Technology
COMM-473.description: Advanced level readings into human-computer interfaces; social interaction with artifacts; concept of presence, and emerging social and psychological issues of new communication and computer technologies.
COMM-473.prereqText:
Prerequisite: COMM 301
Class standing: not open to Freshman, Sophomore

COMM-489.title: Campaign Communication
COMM-489.description: Problems in political communication: creating an informed electorate, use of mass media, factors in voter persuasion. Guest experts in political analysis, opinion polling, communication evaluation.
COMM-489.prereqText: Class standing: not open to Freshman, Sophomore

COMM-490.title: Directed Research
COMM-490.description: Individual research and readings. Not available for graduatecredit. Available to juniors and seniors only.
COMM-490.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Junior, Senior

COMM-494.title: Research Practicum
COMM-494.description: Students gain research experience in the design, implementation, analysis, and reporting of communication research. Students serve as research assistants to faculty members. Not available for graduate credit.

COMM-497.description: Writing of the honors thesis. Not available for graduate credit.

COMM-526.description: Overview of humanistic and social scientific approaches to the study of communication; emphasis on macro and micro social scientific, symbolic, and structural perspectives. Not open to M.A. in Communication Management majors,

COMM-569.title: Seminar in Science and Technology Studies
COMM-569.description: Introduction to key concepts and theories in the interdisciplinary field of Science and Technology Studies.

COMM-586.description: A culmination of foundational training in communication, data science and machine learning. Building AI solutions for digital media and product development.
COMM-586.prereqText:

Recommended preparation: Proficiency in Python programming and machine learning fundamentals.
Major: open only to Communication Data Science, Communication Data Science

COMM-597.description: Conduct research, design and produce a group-based research report and website to assess disruption within Global Media Industries over the past year or two.

School: open only to Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism

COMM-620.title: Studies in Communication Theory
COMM-620.description: Current problems in communication theory and research; advanced, specialized interest areas of individual faculty on the frontiers of knowledge.

COMM-636.title: Interpretive and Cultural Approaches in Organizational Communication
COMM-636.description: Interpretive, critical and cultural research in organizational communication; emphasis on narrative approaches to ethnographic studies, critical essays, and quantitative intercultural research in organizational communication.

COMM-645.title: Communication Networks
COMM-645.description: Conceptual and analytic issues in network perspectives; emphasis on communication patterns, processes, content, influences and impacts.

COMM-647.title: Network Society
COMM-647.description: Advanced research seminar examining the interaction between communication technology, society, economy, politics, and culture from interdisciplinary and cross-cultural perspectives. Not available for degree credit for M.A. in Communication Management students. Not available for Communication Management M.A. students.

COMM-650.description: Principles of survey construction and validation; format selection, sampling, question wording, adaptation for international audiences, response option formats, order, and avoiding acquiesence bias and breakoffs.

COMM-675.title: Independent Study
COMM-675.description: A supervised course tailored to specific student interests. The professor and student develop a syllabus that permits exploration of advanced or specialized topics. Graded CR/NC.

COMM-694.title: Preliminary Research Paper
COMM-694.description: Independent research designed to demonstrate the student's ability to conceptualize, conduct, and present scholarly research. Parallel to COMM 794. Graded CR/NC.

CORE-101.title: Symbols and Conceptual Systems: Thematic Option Honors Progr
CORE-101.description: Study of the structures through which we shape our experience in religion, philosophy, literature, music, and the visual arts, and of competing theories of interpretation. Students may not take this course on a P/NP basis.

CORE-103.title: The Process of Change in Science: Thematic Option Honors Pro
CORE-103.description: Critical problems in the development of scientific thought, studied as vehicles for understanding the content and structure of the sciences. Specific subject matter in selected scientific disciplines will be presented. Students may not take this course on a P/NP basis.

CORE-104.title: Change and the Future: Thematic Option Honors Program
CORE-104.description: Analysis of historical change; social and political theory and revolutionary thought; introduction to competing images of future states of affairs; the continuing process of change. Students may not take this course on a P/NP basis.

CORE-112.title: Writing Seminar II: Thematic Option Honors Program
CORE-112.description: Instruction on analytic writing that integrates methods of research, identifying and addressing specific audiences and presenting ideas publicly. Readings examine modernity and postmodernity.

CORE-200.title: Liberal Arts Reading Salon
CORE-200.description: Critical readings of a series of texts in the liberal arts designed to promote discussion of important themes, theoretical approaches, research directions, and interdisciplinary connections. Graded CR/NC.

CORE-301.title: Modes of Inquiry
CORE-301.description: Modern tools of cultural and discursive analysis which seek to demystify "the natural," as it appears in the formation of cultures, their institutions, and individuals.

CORE-499.title: Special Topics
CORE-499.description: Intensive interdisciplinary exploration of a selected theme, problem, process, or period.

CORE-601.title: Teaching Analytical Writing through Readings in the Humanities
CORE-601.description: Theories and practices in university-level teaching of close-reading and analytical writing, using texts central to Western tradition. Graduate student professionalization throught topical workshops and discussions. Open to assistant lecturers and teaching assistants only. Graded CR/NC.
CORE-601.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student, Master Student

CRIT-150.title: Histories of Art, Design and Visual Culture
CRIT-150.description: A loosely chronological, thematic survey of art, visual culture, design, and critical theory from the early modern period through modernism (1500 1950).

CRIT-160.title: Critical Theory in Art, Design and Visual Culture
CRIT-160.description: An issues-based introduction to critical theory in the twentieth and twenty-first centuries, especially as it relates to philosophy, art, design, and visual culture.
CRIT-160.prereqText:
Recommended preparation: CRIT 150
Major: open only to Art, Fine Arts
School: open only to Roski School of Art and Design

CRIT-350.title: Global Art, Design and Visual Culture since 1960
CRIT-350.description: A critical history of art, design, visual culture, and visual theory since 1960, addressing through a postcolonial/decolonial lens the concepts and practices of "global" art.
CRIT-350.prereqText:
Recommended preparation: CRIT 150 and CRIT 160
Major: open only to Art, Fine Arts
School: open only to Roski School of Art and Design
Duplicates credit: former FA 350

CRIT-425.title: Identity and Visual Representation
CRIT-425.description: A critical study of the relationship between identity or coalitional politics and specific practices, meanings, and sitings of contemporary art and design.
CRIT-425.prereqText: Recommended preparation: CRIT 150, CRIT 160, CRIT 350 or permission of instructor

CRIT-515.title: Visiting Artist and Scholar Seminar
CRIT-515.description: Lecture and discussion course in the professional practice of art featuring formal presentations by visiting artists and scholars. (Duplicates credit in FA 515)

CRIT-525.title: Making and Curating Art: Pedagogy and Praxis
CRIT-525.description: Provides students with a foundation in the history and theory of studio art and curatorial education and develops their teaching skills in these areas.

CRIT-555.title: Methods of Curating: Introduction to Curatorial Practicum
CRIT-555.description: First in a sequence of three courses on history/theory of curatorial methods, with practical experience necessary to mounting exhibitions and devising interfaces with the public. (Duplicates credit in former PAS 555a)

CRIT-557.title: Curatorial Practicum: Group Project Summation
CRIT-557.description: Third in a sequence of three courses on history/theory of curatorial methods, with practical experience necessary to mounting exhibitions and devising interfaces with the public. Prerequisite: CRIT 556. (Duplicates credit in former PAS 555c)

CRIT-590.title: Directed Research
CRIT-590.description: Research leading to the master's degree. Maximum units which may be applied to the degree to be determined by the department. Graded CR/NC. (Duplicates credit in former PAS 590)

CRIT-591.title: Field Internship Experience
CRIT-591.description: Supervised internship in an art institution or an art agency, or with an independent curator or artist, on projects and research specific to public space. Recommended preparation: Completion of first year of courses. Graded CR/NC. (Duplicates credit in former PAS 591)

CRIT-594A.title: Master's Thesis
CRIT-594A.description: Credit on acceptance of thesis. Graded IP/CR/NC. (Duplicates credit in former PAS 594a)

CRIT-594B.title: Master's Thesis
CRIT-594B.description: Credit on acceptance of thesis. Recommended preparation: 28 units of coursework. Graded IP/CR/NC. (Duplicates credit in former PAS 594b)

CRIT-594Z.title: Master's Thesis
CRIT-594Z.description: Credit on acceptance of thesis. Recommended preparation: 28 units of coursework. Graded IP/CR/NC. (Duplicates credit in former PAS 594z)

CSCI-102.title: Introduction to Programming
CSCI-102.description: Fundamental concepts of algorithmic thinking as a primer to programming. Introduction to C++.

CSCI-103.title: Object Oriented Programming
CSCI-103.description: Basic datatypes, assignments, control statements (if, switch, for, while), input/output (printf, scanf, cin, cout), functions, arrays, structures, recursion, dynamic memory, file handling. Programming in C/C++.

CSCI-104.title: Data Structures
CSCI-104.description: Data structures including linked lists, balanced search trees, heaps, hash tables; probability and number theory applicable to the analysis of randomized data structures.

CSCI-113.title: Programming Fundamentals for Computing
CSCI-113.description: Introduction to Python and C++ with examples from various domains in computational science; intended for students without prior programming experience.
CSCI-113.prereqText: Major: not open to Computer Engineering & Computer Science, Computer Science/Business Administration, Computer Science, Computer Science Games

CSCI-114.title: Programming for Applications of Computing
CSCI-114.description: Solutions to computational science problems using Python and C++; data structures; searching and sorting algorithms; computational efficiency.
CSCI-114.prereqText:
Prerequisite: CSCI 103 or CSCI 113 or TAC 216 or TAC 265 or ITP 216 or ITP 265
Major: not open to Computer Engineering & Computer Science, Computer Science/Business Administration, Computer Science, Computer Science Games

CSCI-170.title: Discrete Methods in Computer Science
CSCI-170.description: Boolean algebra, propositional and first-order logic, proof techniques. Sets, functions, series, summations. Big-O notation; algorithm analysis. Recursion; basic sorting algorithms. Graphs and basic graph algorithms.

CSCI-201.title: Principles of Software Development
CSCI-201.description: Object-Oriented Programming in Java; using Java threads, Web Services and SQL to write client/server applications; team project; vibe coding with AI tools.

CSCI-270.title: Introduction to Algorithms and Theory of Computing
CSCI-270.description: Algorithm analysis. Greedy algorithms, divide and conquer, dynamic programming, graph algorithms. NP-completeness and basic recursion theory and undecidability. Sorting lower bounds. Number-theory based cryptography.
CSCI-270.prereqText:
Prerequisite: CSCI 104 or CSCI 114; CSCI 170
Duplicates credit: former CSCI 303

CSCI-310.title: Software Engineering
CSCI-310.description: Introduction to the software engineering process and software lifecycle. Covers project management, requirements, architecture, design, implementation, testing, and maintenance phase activities in team based projects. Prerequisites: CSCI 201. Duplicates credit in former CSCI 377.
CSCI-310.prereqText:
Prerequisite: CSCI 201
Duplicates credit: former CSCI 377

CSCI-350.title: Fundamentals of Operating Systems
CSCI-350.description: Basic issues in concurrency, deadlock control, synchronization scheduling, memory management, protection and access control, inter-process communication, and structured design. Laboratory experiences with Unix-like operating system.
CSCI-350.prereqText:
Prerequisite: CSCI 356 or EE 354; CSCI 201 or EE 250
Duplicates credit: CSCI 402

CSCI-353.title: Internetworking
CSCI-353.description: Global Internet: design principles, layering, protocol design/analysis. Networked applications, Internet structure/architecture, Protocols for transport/congestion control, network layer/routing, link layer/MAC. Network security.
CSCI-353.prereqText:
Prerequisite: CSCI 201
Recommended preparation: Familiarity with C and C++.
Duplicates credit: EE 450

CSCI-356.title: Computer Systems
CSCI-356.description: Computer organization; entity abstraction and representation; program execution; code optimization; memory usage; exception handling; processing control; computer performance; hands-on work done in C and assembly.
CSCI-356.prereqText:
Prerequisite: CSCI 104
Duplicates credit: former EE 352 and EE 457

CSCI-360.title: Artificial Intelligence: Principles and Foundations
CSCI-360.description: Concepts and algorithms underlying the understanding and construction of intelligent systems. Agents, problem solving, search, representation, reasoning, planning, machine learning.
CSCI-360.prereqText:
Prerequisite: CSCI 104 or CSCI 114; CSCI 170
Duplicates credit: former CSCI 460

CSCI-368.title: Cross-Platform App Development with Flutter
CSCI-368.description: Programming applications with dynamic graphical user interfaces. Topics include events, controls, resources, data bindings, styles and user experience.
CSCI-368.prereqText:
Prerequisite: TAC 265 or ITP 265 or CSCI 103
Duplicates credit: former ITP 368

CSCI-380.title: Video Game Programming
CSCI-380.description: Underlying concepts and principles required for programming video games (topics include vectors, transformations, 3-D math, geometric primitives, matrices).
CSCI-380.prereqText:
Prerequisite: CSCI 104 or TAC 365 or ITP 365
Duplicates credit: former ITP 380

CSCI-401.title: Capstone: Design and Construction of Large       Software Systems
CSCI-401.description: Group project with an outside stakeholder to develop real-world software solutions to large-scale problems. Topics include software engineering, professional preparation, and recent computer science research. Duplicates credit in CSCI 477a and CSCI 477b.

CSCI-402.title: Operating Systems
CSCI-402.description: Concurrency, deadlock control, synchronization, process and thread scheduling, memory management, file systems, security and access control, communication and networking, distributed file systems, data management. Duplicates credit in CSCI 350.
CSCI-402.prereqText:
Recommended preparation: CSCI 201 or CSCI 455; CSCI 356 or EE 352
Duplicates credit: CSCI 350

CSCI-420.title: Computer Graphics
CSCI-420.description: Computer graphics, OpenGL, 2D and 3D transformations, Bzier splines, computer animation, rendering including ray tracing, shading and lighting, artistic rendering, virtual reality, visualization.
CSCI-420.prereqText:
Prerequisite: CSCI 104; MATH 225 or EE 141 and MATH 126 or EE 141 and MATH 127 or EE 141 and MATH 129
Class standing: not open to Freshman, Sophomore

CSCI-430.title: Computer and Network Security
CSCI-430.description: A broad overview of security threats and defenses, security systems and functionalities. Includes homeworks and in-class exercises to provide practical experience working with such systems. Prerequisite: CSCI 104.

CSCI-435.title: Professional C++
CSCI-435.description: Applications of advanced concepts in C++ including lambda expressions, templates, secure coding, parallel programming, writing performant code, CMake and continuous integration.
CSCI-435.prereqText:
Prerequisite: CSCI 104 or TAC 365 or ITP 365
Duplicates credit: former ITP 435

CSCI-444.title: Language Models in Natural Language Processing
CSCI-444.description: Natural language processing; language modeling; deep neural networks for language processing; language technologies and their socioeconomic and societal impacts.
CSCI-444.prereqText:
Prerequisite: CSCI 170; CSCI 104 or CSCI 114; MATH 225 or EE 141; EE 364 or MATH 407 or BUAD 310 or BUAD 312 or ISE 225
Recommended preparation: Fluency with Python programming on the level of ITP 216 or TAC 216

CSCI-445.title: Foundations of Robotics
CSCI-445.description: Designing and programming mobile robots; sensors, effectors, basic control theory, control architectures, planning, some advanced topics, illustrations of state-of-the-art. Weekly robot programming labs; final project.
CSCI-445.prereqText:
Prerequisite: CSCI 104 or CSCI 114 or EE 355
Class standing: open only to Junior, Senior

CSCI-450.title: Foundations of Computer Networks
CSCI-450.description: Network architectures; layered protocols, network service interface; local, wide area, wireless networks; Internet protocols; link protocols; addressing; routing; flow control; software defined network; multimedia networks.
CSCI-450.prereqText:
Class standing: not open to Freshman, Sophomore
Duplicates credit: CSCI 353

CSCI-455.title: Introduction to Programming Systems Design
CSCI-455.description: Intensive introduction to programming principles, discrete mathematics for computing, software design and software engineering concepts. Not available for credit to computer sciencemajors, graduate or undergraduate.

CSCI-457.title: Computer Systems Organization
CSCI-457.description: Register Transfer level machine organization; performance; arithmetic; pipelined processors; exceptions, out-of-order and speculative execution, cache, virtual memory, multi-core multi-threaded processors, cache coherence.

CSCI-458.title: Numerical Methods
CSCI-458.description: Rounding errors in digital computation; solution of linear algebraic systems; Newton's method for nonlinear systems; matrix eigenvalues; polynomial approximation; numerical integration; numerical solution of ordinary differential equations.
CSCI-458.prereqText:
Prerequisite: MATH 225 or MATH 235 or MATH 245
Recommended preparation: MATH 226 or MATH 227 or MATH 229

CSCI-467.title: Foundations of Machine Learning
CSCI-467.description: Algorithms for learning behavior from data, including both mathematical underpinnings and practical techniques. Covers supervised learning, deep learning, unsupervised learning and reinforcement learning.
CSCI-467.prereqText:
Prerequisite: CSCI 170; CSCI 104 or CSCI 114; MATH 225 or EE 141; EE 364 or MATH 407 or BUAD 310 or BUAD 312 or ISE 225
Recommended preparation: CSCI 360, comfortable with mathematical derivations, such as those in MATH 225; comfortable with manipulating vectors and matrices
Duplicates credit: EE 460

CSCI-475.title: Theory of Computation
CSCI-475.description: History of the theory of computing, foundational theorems and theoretical frameworks of computer science, solvable and unsolvable problems.

CSCI-476.title: Cryptography: Secure Communication and Computation
CSCI-476.description: Introduction to modern Cryptography; Mathematical/algorithmic studies of methods for protecting information in computer and communication systems: Public-Key Cryptosystems, zero-knowledge proofs, data privacy. Prerequisites: CSCI 270.

CSCI-487.title: Programming Game Engines
CSCI-487.description: Building the core components of a modern 3D game engine including shaders, animation, collision detection, artificial intelligence algorithms, multithreading and profiling.

CSCI-490.title: Directed Research
CSCI-490.description: Individual research and readings. Not available for graduate credit.
CSCI-490.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Junior, Senior

CSCI-491B.title: Advanced Game Project
CSCI-491B.description: The practice of design in various areas of game production, iterative stage two prototyping and development of refined videogame.
CSCI-491B.prereqText:
Prerequisite: CSCI 491A
Recommended preparation: Knowledge of game design at the level of CTIN 489L

CSCI-495.title: Senior Project
CSCI-495.description: An original project will be constructed applying computer technology (in either hardware or software) to produce a result useful in the physics classroom or laboratory.

CSCI-501.title: Numerical Analysis and Computation
CSCI-501.description: Linear equations and matrices, Gauss elimination, error estimates, iteration techniques; contractive mappings, Newton's method; matrix eigenvalue problems; least-squares approximation, Newton-Cotes and Gaussian quadratures; finite difference methods. Prerequisite: linear algebra and calculus.

CSCI-505B.title: Applied Probability
CSCI-505B.description: Markov processes in discrete or continuous time; renewal processes; martingales; brownian motion and diffusion theory; random walks, inventory models, population growth, queuing models, shot noise.

CSCI-507.title: Games as a Service and Live Operations: Foundations
CSCI-507.description: Fundamentals of free-to-play game development and live operations; creation of original prototypes; and measurement of player engagement.
CSCI-507.prereqText: Recommended preparation: Introductory games coursework on the level of CTIN 458, CTIN 488, or CTIN 489 is helpful but not required.

CSCI-509.title: Games as a Service and Live Operations: Launch
CSCI-509.description: Take a Live Operations game from Alpha through beta versions to a polished launch candidate; iterative usability testing and player metrics; plan post-launch operations.
CSCI-509.prereqText: Recommended preparation: Foundational and developmental games coursework on the level of CSCI-507 and CSCI-508.

CSCI-520.title: Computer Animation and Simulation
CSCI-520.description: Fundamental techniques of computer animation and simulation, knowledge and/or experience in the design, scripting, production and post-production stages of computer animation. Prerequisite: CSCI-420 or CSCI-580. Recommendedpreparation: Familiarity with calculus, linear algebra, and numerical computation; C/C++ programming skills.

CSCI-522.title: Game Engine Development
CSCI-522.description: The principles of developing game engines targeted at modern PC and game console hardware.

CSCI-526.title: Advanced Mobile Devices and Game Consoles
CSCI-526.description: Explore the complex engineering process required to design and build a real-time graphics engine to support physical realism on mobile devices. Recommended preparation: CSCI 420 or CSCI 580 or an equivalent course in graphics.

CSCI-529B.title: Graduate Advanced Game Project
CSCI-529B.description: The practice of design in various areas of game production, iterative stage two prototyping and development of a refined videogame.
CSCI-529B.prereqText:
Prerequisite: CSCI 529A
Recommended preparation: Knowledge of interactive design and production at the level of CTIN 532L

CSCI-530.title: Security Systems
CSCI-530.description: Protecting computer networks and systems using cryptography, authentication, authorization, intrusion detection and response. Includes lab to provide practical experience working with such systems.

CSCI-531.title: Applied Cryptography
CSCI-531.description: Intensive overview of cryptography for practitioners, historical perspective on early systems, number theoretic foundations of modern day cryptosystems and basic cryptanalysis.

CSCI-532.title: Innovation for Defense Applications
CSCI-532.description: Development of problem statements and innovative software prototypes for defense, intelligence and homeland security applications; team projects; hands-on experience.
CSCI-532.prereqText: Recommended preparation: An introductory programming class such as CSCI 103 and the ability to write short programs or scripts to manipulate data.

CSCI-533.title: Algebraic Combinatorics
CSCI-533.description: Combinatorics motivated by Representation Theory and Algebraic Geometry. Topics may include: representations of the symmetric group, symmetric functions, Young tableaux and plane partitions, permutation enumeration.

CSCI-538.title: Augmented, Virtual and Mixed Reality
CSCI-538.description: Technical design and implementation of immersive environments; visual simulations, interactive 3D graphics and games.

CSCI-544.title: Applied Natural Language Processing
CSCI-544.description: Introduction to key components of human language technologies, including: information extraction, sentiment analysis, question answering, machine translation.

CSCI-545.title: Robotics
CSCI-545.description: Fundamental skills for modeling and controlling of dynamic systems for robotic applications and graphics animations; control theory; kinematics; dynamics; sensor processing; real-time operating systems; robot labs. Recommended preparation: Basic knowledge in linear algebra (matrices and vectors), calculus, programming in C/C++ or any another language or permission of the instructor.

CSCI-546.title: Distributed Systems
CSCI-546.description: The theory and practice of distributed systems. Topics include: distributed storage systems, fault tolerance, consensus, consistency, transactions, distributed data processing and efficient cloud computing.
CSCI-546.prereqText: Recommended preparation: Knowledge of operating systems at the level of CSCI 350 and computer systems at the level of CSCI 356. Strong C++ experience is highly recommended.

CSCI-551.title: Computer Networking
CSCI-551.description: Protocol design for computer communication networks, network routing, transport protocols, internetworking.
CSCI-551.prereqText:
Prerequisite: CSCI 353 or EE 450; CSCI 350 or CSCI 402
Recommended preparation: C-language programming
Duplicates credit: CSCI 651

CSCI-557.title: Computer Systems Architecture
CSCI-557.description: Computer architecture from a design perspective: Pipelined processors, speculative execution, VLIW, vector processors, GPU/GPGPU, memory technology and systems, interconnection networks, shared-memory and message-passing multiprocessors, chip multiprocessors.

CSCI-559.title: Machine Learning I: Supervised Methods
CSCI-559.description: Distribution-free and probabilistic methods for supervised classification and regression; learning algorithms; optimization techniques; feature-space transformations; parametric and nonparametric methods; Bayes decision theory; artificial neural networks.
CSCI-559.prereqText:
Corequisite: EE 503; EE 510
Recommended preparation: knowledge of Python at the level of EE 541 (A Computational Introduction to Deep Learning); knowledge of multivariate calculus.

CSCI-561.title: Foundations of Artificial Intelligence
CSCI-561.description: Foundations of symbolic intelligent systems, search, logic, knowledge representation, planning, learning.

CSCI-566.title: Deep Learning and Its Applications
CSCI-566.description: Deep learning research in computer vision, natural language processing and robotics; neural networks; deep learning algorithms, tools and software.
CSCI-566.prereqText:
Recommended preparation: CSCI 567, Python programming, calculus, linear algebra, probability and statistics, knowledge of machine learning
Duplicates credit: CSCI 527

CSCI-567.title: Machine Learning
CSCI-567.description: Statistical methods for building intelligent and adaptive systems that improve performance from experiences; Focus on theoretical understanding of these methods and their computational implications. Recommended preparation: Undergraduate level training or coursework in linear algebra, multivariate calculus, basic probability and statistics; an undergraduate level course in Artificial Intelligence may be helpful but is not required.

CSCI-570.title: Analysis of Algorithms
CSCI-570.description: Explores fundamental techniques such as recursion, Fourier transform ordering, dynamic programming for efficient algorithm construction. Examples include arithmetic, algebraic, graph, pattern matching, sorting, searching algorithms.

CSCI-571.title: Web Technologies
CSCI-571.description: Study of client-side and server-side Web programming languages, including HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Python, Java, Kotlin. Vibe coding with IDEs, AI Assistants and LLMs.
CSCI-571.prereqText: Recommended preparation: knowledge of at least two programming languages.

CSCI-572.title: Information Retrieval and Web Search Engines
CSCI-572.description: Examines key aspects of information retrieval as they apply to search engines; web crawling, indexing, querying and quality of results are studied.
CSCI-572.prereqText: Recommended preparation: Familiarity in programming in multiple languages, C, C++, and/or Java and experience with a database

CSCI-573.title: Probabilistic Reasoning
CSCI-573.description: Reasoning under uncertainty, statistical directed and undirected graphical models, temporal modeling, inference in graphical models, parameter learning, decisions under uncertainty. Recommended preparation: An undergraduate level course in probability theory.

CSCI-575.title: Quantum Computing and Quantum Cryptography
CSCI-575.description: Introduction to quantum computing and quantum cryptography; quantum Fourier sampling with applications to factoring, quantum search, quantum key distribution.
CSCI-575.prereqText: Recommended preparation: CSCI 570 and knowledge of linear algebra at the level of EE 510 (preferred) or MATH 225

CSCI-579.title: Embodied Intelligence
CSCI-579.description: Advanced topics in embodied intelligence: multi-view reconstruction, visual reasoning, visual centric manipulation and locomotion, 3D deep learning for robotics.
CSCI-579.prereqText: Recommended preparation: Familiarity with recent deep learning techniques at the level of CSCI 566 and basic robotic algorithms at the level of CSCI 545.

CSCI-580.title: 3-D Graphics and Rendering
CSCI-580.description: Course outlines the process of creating images from 3D models. Includes transformations, shading, lighting, rastorization, texturing, and other topics.

CSCI-584.title: Advanced Game Project Pre-Production
CSCI-584.description: Pre-production processes for team projects intended to address the multifaceted technical and creative challenges that are inherent to comprehensive game development.

CSCI-585.title: Database Systems
CSCI-585.description: Database system architecture; conceptual database models; semantic, object-oriented, logic-based, and relational databases; user and program interfaces; database system implementation; integrity, security, concurrency and recovery. Recommended Preparation: Knowledge of relational databases, SQL, relational algebra and physical database design is required. Open only to graduate students.
CSCI-585.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student, Master Student

CSCI-587.title: Geospatial Data Analysis
CSCI-587.description: Techniques to efficiently store, manipulate, index, query and analyze geospatial information in support of real-world geographical and decision-making applications.
CSCI-587.prereqText: Recommended preparation: Knowledge of database management at the level of CSCI 485 and machine learning at the level of CSCI 467

CSCI-590.title: Directed Research
CSCI-590.description: Research leading to the master's degree. Maximum units which may be applied to the degree to be determined by the department. Graded CR/NC.

CSCI-591.title: Computer Science Research Colloquium
CSCI-591.description: Exploration and critical assessment of research activities in computer science. Course will serve as a forum for current research presentations from academia and industry. Graded CR/NC.

CSCI-594A.title: Master's Thesis
CSCI-594A.description: Credit on acceptance of thesis. Graded IP/CR/NC.

CSCI-594B.title: Master's Thesis
CSCI-594B.description: Credit on acceptance of thesis. Graded IP/CR/NC.

CSCI-594Z.title: Master's Thesis
CSCI-594Z.description: Credit on acceptance of thesis. Graded IP/CR/NC.

CSCI-617.title: Machine Learning for/with Mixed-Integer Optimization
CSCI-617.description: Using mixed-integer optimization (MIO) to solve problems in artificial intelligence (Al) and machine learning (ML). Leveraging Al/ML to improve MIO solvers.
CSCI-617.prereqText:
Recommended preparation: Optimization (at the level of CSCI 675, ISE 630, or ISE 631); machine learning (at the level of CSCI 567, ISE 568, CSCI 467, EE 460, ISE 529, or CSCI 559) using Python
Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student, Master Student

CSCI-619.title: End-to-End Learning and Optimization
CSCI-619.description: End-to-end learning models and algorithms from operations research and machine learning perspectives. Computational considerations and performance guarantees. Energy, healthcare and supply chain applications.
CSCI-619.prereqText: Recommended preparation: Basic optimization (at the level of CSCI 675, ISE 630, or ISE 631). Basic machine learning (at the level of CSCI 567, ISE 568, CSCI 467, EE 460, ISE 529, or CSCI 559) using Python.

CSCI-625.title: Program Synthesis and Computer-Aided Verification
CSCI-625.description: Introduction to the principles and practices of software verification and program synthesis.
CSCI-625.prereqText: Recommended preparation: Knowledge of discrete math and algorithm design. Background in systems and software engineering.

CSCI-644.title: Natural Language Dialogue Systems
CSCI-644.description: Computational models of natural language dialogue; conversational interfaces to artificial systems; dialogue system architectures and applications; Reinforcement learning of dialogue policies.

CSCI-651.title: Advanced Computer Networking
CSCI-651.description: Computer communication protocols and systems, including classic and contemporary literature. The emphasis is on conceptual issues in the design and implementation of computer internetworks.
CSCI-651.prereqText:
Prerequisite: CSCI 353 or EE 450; CSCI 350 or CSCI 402
Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student
Major: open only to Computer Science
Duplicates credit: CSCI 551

CSCI-654.title: Crafting a Research Agenda
CSCI-654.description: Formulation of a computer science research agenda, examination of trends within sub-areas of computer science and identification of fruitful and problematic research directions.
CSCI-654.prereqText: Recommended preparation: At least one year of graduate-level research experience.

CSCI-656.title: Networked Systems in Cloud Computing
CSCI-656.description: Systems and network design and protocols in cloud computing and data centers networks.

CSCI-658.title: Diagnosis and Design of Reliable Digital Systems
CSCI-658.description: Fault models; test generation; fault simulation; self-checking and self-testing circuits; design for testability; fault tolerant design techniques; case studies; search techniques; memory testing.

CSCI-670.title: Advanced Analysis of Algorithms
CSCI-670.description: Fundamental techniques for design and analysis of algorithms. Dynamic programming; network flows; theory of NP-completeness; linear programming; approximation, randomized, and online algorithms; basic cryptography. Prerequisite: CSCI 570. Recommended preparation: familiarity with algorithms and discrete mathematics. Open only to doctoral students.
CSCI-670.prereqText:
Prerequisite: CSCI 570
Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student

CSCI-672.title: Approximation Algorithms
CSCI-672.description: Algorithmic techniques include combinatorial algorithms and rounding of linear and semi-definite programs. Applications include network design, graph cuts, covering problems, and approximation hardness.

CSCI-697.title: Seminar in Computer Science Research
CSCI-697.description: Introduction of Ph.D. students to the broad range of computer science research. Two semesters registration required. Open to Computer Science doctoral students only. Graded CR/NC. Duplicates credit in former CSCI 597.
CSCI-697.prereqText:
Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student
Major: open only to Computer Science

CSCI-698.title: Practicum in Teaching Computer Science
CSCI-698.description: Practical principles for the long-term development of effective teaching in Computer Science. Intended for teaching assistants for classes offered by the Computer Science department. Graded CR/NC. Open only to Computer Science doctoral students.
CSCI-698.prereqText:
Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student
Major: open only to Computer Science

CSCI-699.title: Special Topics
CSCI-699.description: Course content to be selected each semester from recent developments in computer science.
CSCI-699.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student

CSCI-790.title: Research
CSCI-790.description: Research leading to the doctorate. Maximum units which may be applied to the degree to be determined by the department. Graded CR/NC.

CSCI-794A.title: Doctoral Dissertation
CSCI-794A.description: Credit on acceptance of Dissertation. Graded CR/NC.
CSCI-794A.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student

CSCI-794B.description: Credit on acceptance of Dissertation. Graded CR/NC.

Prerequisite: CSCI 794a
Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student

CSCI-794C.description: Credit on acceptance of Dissertation. Graded CR/NC.
CSCI-794C.prereqText:
Prerequisite: CSCI 794b
Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student

CSCI-794D.title: Doctoral Dissertation
CSCI-794D.description: Credit on acceptance of Dissertation. Graded CR/NC.
CSCI-794D.prereqText:
Prerequisite: CSCI 794c
Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student

CSCI-794Z.title: Doctoral Dissertation
CSCI-794Z.description: Credit on acceptance of Dissertation. Graded CR/NC.
CSCI-794Z.prereqText:
Prerequisite: CSCI 794d
Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student

CSLC-503.title: Introduction to Comparative Studies in Culture
CSLC-503.description: Examination of culture as an instrument of discursive practice that shapes social formations in Asia, Europe, North and Latin America.

CSLC-511.title: Translating Race
CSLC-511.description: Contemporary notions of racial, cultural, and religious difference across languages and history.
CSLC-511.prereqText:
Recommended preparation: COLT 510
Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student, Master Student

CSLC-590.title: Directed Research
CSLC-590.description: Research leading to the master's degree. Graded CR/NC. Duplicates credit in former COLT 590.

CSLC-596.title: Internship for Curricular Practical Training
CSLC-596.description: Part-time or full-time practical work experience in the student's field of study. The internship must be located at an off-campus facility. Students are individually supervised by faculty. May not be taken until the student has completed at least on semester of enrollment in the graduate program.
CSLC-596.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student

CSLC-620.title: Seminar in Literature, Culture and Thought
CSLC-620.description: Varying focus on social and political thought, psychoanalysis, and philosophy in relation to literary and cultural analysis.

CSLC-702.title: Professional Development IV: Applying for Academic Positions
CSLC-702.description: Designed to familiarize students in the Comparative Studies in Literature and Culture doctoral program with the process of seeking an academic position.

CSLC-790.title: Research
CSLC-790.description: Research leading to the doctorate. Maximum units that may be applied to the degree to be determined by the department. Graded CR/NC.

CSLC-794A.title: Doctoral Dissertation
CSLC-794A.description: Credit on acceptance of dissertation. Graded IP/CR/NC.

CSLC-794B.description: Credit on acceptance of dissertation. Graded IP/CR/NC.

CSLC-794D.description: Credit on acceptance of dissertation. Graded IP/CR/NC.

CSLC-794Z.title: Doctoral Dissertation
CSLC-794Z.description: Credit on acceptance of dissertation. Graded IP/CR/NC.

CTAN-102.title: Introduction to the Art of Movement
CTAN-102.description: Theory and practice of animation with a focus on movement, gesture, timing and performance. Open to freshman in Animation and Digital Arts majors only.
CTAN-102.prereqText:
Prerequisite: CTAN 101
Class standing: open only to Freshman
Major: open only to Animation and Digital Arts

CTAN-110.title: Design Fundamentals for Animation I
CTAN-110.description: Developing skills in design, composition, shape language, image-making, and visual thinking to create more sophisticated style frames and imagery for animation practice.
CTAN-110.prereqText: Major: open only to Animation and Digital Arts

CTAN-200.title: The Rise of Digital Hollywood
CTAN-200.description: An overview of the evolution of computer graphics in modern media.

CTAN-201.title: Intermediate Animation Production
CTAN-201.description: Tools, skills and procedures used in animation production with a focus on professional execution of independent and collaborative productions. Prerequisite: CTAN 102. Open to sophomore animation majors only.
CTAN-201.prereqText:
Prerequisite: CTAN 102
Class standing: open only to Sophomore
School: open only to School of Cinematic Arts

CTAN-202.title: Introduction to 3-D Character Animation
CTAN-202.description: 3-D animation performance utilizing preset rigs and virtual characters. Emphasis on timing, gesture, and performance.
CTAN-202.prereqText:
Class standing: open only to Sophomore
Major: open only to Animation and Digital Arts

CTAN-336.title: Ideation and Pre-Production
CTAN-336.description: Emphasis on lateral thinking working across boundaries to find underlying principles in terms of ideation: the act of becoming an agent of ideas.
CTAN-336.prereqText:
Prerequisite: CTAN 301
Class standing: open only to Junior
School: open only to School of Cinematic Arts

CTAN-401B.title: Senior Project
CTAN-401B.description: b: Completion and exhibition of the short animated film to demonstrate understanding and further examination of the possibilities of animation time based graphic media. Open to senior animation majors only.
CTAN-401B.prereqText:
Prerequisite: CTAN 401a
Class standing: open only to Senior
School: open only to School of Cinematic Arts

CTAN-420.title: Concept Design for Animation
CTAN-420.description: Creating characters and environments for animation, live action, and video games.

CTAN-425.title: Studio Careers: Story to Screen
CTAN-425.description: Seminar featuring guest speakers from major animation studios to provide an overview of a feature animation pipeline from development to pre-production, production and post-production.

CTAN-432.title: The World of Visual Effects
CTAN-432.description: Introduction to the expanding field of visual effects; topics include integration for cinematic storytelling and the study of digital productions employing the latest visual effects.

CTAN-436.title: Writing for Animation
CTAN-436.description: Workshop exploring concept and structure of long and short form animated films through practical writing exercises.

CTAN-452.title: Introduction to 3-D Computer Animation
CTAN-452.description: Lecture and laboratory in computer animation: geometric modeling, motion specification, lighting, texture mapping, rendering, compositing, production techniques, systems for computer-synthesized animation using Maya software.

CTAN-454.title: Real-Time Animation
CTAN-454.description: The fundamentals of lighting and rendering in real-time. Creating complex, compelling and dynamic scenes and manipulating them in real-time using Unreal Engine.

CTAN-460.title: Character Design Workshop
CTAN-460.description: The basics of character design for animation: anatomy, poses, facial expressions, silhouettes, and anthropomorphism. Development of a portfolio.

CTAN-462.title: Visual Effects
CTAN-462.description: Survey of contemporary concepts and approaches to production in the current state of film and video effects work. Digital and traditional methodologies will be covered, with a concentration on digital exercises illustrating modern techniques.

CTAN-465.title: Digital Effects Animation
CTAN-465.description: All aspects of digital effects animation, including particles, dynamics, and fluids. Creating water, fire, explosions, and destruction in film.

CTAN-480.title: Advanced Character Animation for Games
CTAN-480.description: Advanced techniques for animating 3-D creature characters in games. An emphasis on unique non-human fantasy characters.

CTAN-495.title: Visual Music
CTAN-495.description: Creating visual music animation in a variety of forms and styles. Exploring the relationship between music, movement, and visual expression. Freshmen and sophomores not eligible.
CTAN-495.prereqText: Class standing: not open to Freshman, Sophomore

CTAN-496.title: Directed Studies
CTAN-496.prereqText: Major: open only to Animation and Digital Arts

CTAN-497.title: Procedural Animation
CTAN-497.description: Introduction to software packages and practices exploring current animation techniques that leverage simulation systems. Artificial intelligence as a tool for animation.

CTAN-503.title: Storyboarding for Animation
CTAN-503.description: Focus on film grammar, perspective, and layout, staging and acting as it relates to storyboarding for animation.

CTAN-504.title: Creative Production in Virtual Reality
CTAN-504.description: A creative studio course in producing both a linear cinematic virtual reality short film and associated real-time immersive experience.

CTAN-508.title: Compositing and the Art of Creating Visual Styles
CTAN-508.description: A comprehensive overview of compositing techniques to effectively create film looks in 3D/2D animations and visual effects.

CTAN-509.title: Environment Modeling
CTAN-509.description: Create 3D models for environments for urban and natural settings and props including vehicles, rocks, trees and furniture.

CTAN-510.title: Inside Story: Creative Development for Animation
CTAN-510.description: A creative development workshop for animated pitch storytelling, supported by an introduction to character development and story structure fundamentals.

CTAN-535.title: Fundamentals of 3-D Character Animation

Class standing: open only to Master Student

CTCS-190.title: Introduction to Cinema

CTCS-402.title: Practicum in Film/Television Criticism

CTCS-403.title: Studies in National and Regional Media

CTCS-467.title: Television Symposium

CTCS-468.title: Media Industry Studies

CTCS-469.title: Film and/or Television Style Analysis

CTCS-473.title: Topics in Cinema and Media Theory
CTCS-473.description: Advanced seminar on particular influential ideas and theoretical approaches that have shaped the making and study of media.

CTCS-487.title: Critical Image
CTCS-487.description: Introduction to critical reflection on the image. Analysis of criticism, fiction, film, and visual artifacts.

CTCS-501.title: World Cinema Before 1945

CTCS-503.title: Survey History of the United States Sound Film
CTCS-503.description: Survey history of the United States film from 1927 to the present, with emphasis upon film as art form, economic institution, technology, and cultural product.

CTCS-505.title: Survey of Interactive Media
CTCS-505.description: A survey course exploring the historical, cultural, business, creative, and technological aspects of the new interactive media.

CTCS-510.title: National/Regional Media
CTCS-510.description: Seminar on media's impact in defining nation and/or region in specific cultural contexts. Also addresses issues of exile, diaspora, transnationalism and globalism.

CTCS-517.title: Topics in Cultural Studies
CTCS-517.description: Introduction to central concepts, key theories and leading figures in cultural studies, particularly as they relate to issues of popular culture and visual media.

CTCS-521.title: Media Archiving: History and Practice

CTCS-587.title: Seminar in Television Theory
CTCS-587.description: Detailed investigation and discussion of various aspects of television, including genre, textual analysis, production and distribution systems and audience studies.

CTCS-673.title: Topics in Theory

CTCS-677.title: Cultural Theory
CTCS-677.description: Seminar in theoretical approaches to cultural studies; focus on interdisciplinary research of media and audiences, covering a range of methods and theoretical frameworks; concentration varies.

CTCS-790.title: Research
CTCS-790.description: Research leading to the doctorate. Maximum units which may be applied to the degree to be determined by the department.

CTIN-252.title: Themed Concept Development: Creativity, Research, Ideation
CTIN-252.description: Processes used in the themed entertainment industry to research concepts, develop concepts and deliver creative product.

CTIN-290.title: Digital Media Workshop
CTIN-290.description: Exploration of a variety of moving image aesthetics and methodologies in order to highlight how the language of cinema shapes contemporary digital and interactive media practices.

CTIN-291.description: Hands-on creating experiences for students who want to work as crew on an advanced game project.

CTIN-295.title: Themed Entertainment Project Crew
CTIN-295.description: An introduction to building for themed entertainment and the experience of live operating a ride or exhibit.

CTIN-391.title: Fundamentals of User Research and Experience
CTIN-391.description: An introduction to games user research, interface design and user experience, covering both theory and practice.

CTIN-396.title: Miniature Golf Production

CTIN-406.title: Sound Design for Games

CTIN-486.title: Alternative Control Workshop

CTIN-591.description: Students from many disciplines work in large teams to create an innovative, large-scale interactive media or game project.

Prerequisite: CTIN 594a

Prerequisite: CTIN 594B

CTPR-438.title: Practicum in Producing

CTPR-506.title: Visual Expression

Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student, Master Student
School: open only to School of Cinematic Arts

Prerequisite: CTPR 507; CTWR 505
Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student, Master Student

CTPR-514.title: Realtime CG Filmmaking

CTPR-524.title: Virtual Production

Prerequisite: CTPR 514 or CTAN 454 or CTAN 564 or CTIN 534
Duplicates credit: former CTPR 446
