CTPR-537.prereqText:
Prerequisite: CTPR 508 or CTAN 547
Major: open only to Cinematic Arts, Film and Television Production
School: open only to School of Cinematic Arts

CTPR-554.title: Advanced Sound
CTPR-554.description: Study of the technical and aesthetic elements of sound design at the professional level. Intended for those contemplating a career in the field of audio. Prerequisite: CTPR 540 or CTPR 546 or CTPR 547.
CTPR-554.prereqText: Prerequisite: CTPR 540 or CTPR 546 or CTPR 547

CTPR-556.title: Advanced Professional Editing Tools and Software
CTPR-556.description: Advanced editing tools for picture editors, picture editing assistants, DIT, post supervisors and VFX editors, including AVID, After Effects, Photoshop, Scriptsync, Davinci Resolve and more.
CTPR-556.prereqText: Prerequisite: CTPR 421 or CTPR 535 or CTPR 480 or CTPR 484 or CTPR 486 or CTPR 546 or CTPR 547

CTPR-557.title: Advanced Cinematography
CTPR-557.description: Advanced camera and lighting techniques for those considering a professional career in cinematography.
CTPR-557.prereqText:
Prerequisite: CTPR 424 or CTPR 537
Major: open only to Cinematic Arts, Film and Television Production
School: open only to School of Cinematic Arts

CTPR-558.title: Advanced Producing
CTPR-558.description: Defines and examines the role of the Executive/Feature Producer through the preproduction, production and post production phases. Prerequisites: CTPR-538 or one of the following in equivalent crew position: CTPR 486, CTPR 546, CTPR 547.
CTPR-558.prereqText: Prerequisite: CTPR 486 or CTPR 538 or CTPR 546 or CTPR 547

CTPR-566.title: The Pitch Class: Film and TV
CTPR-566.description: Developing, pitching and selling your feature motion picture and TV projects.
CTPR-566.prereqText:
Class standing: open only to Master Student, Senior
School: open only to School of Cinematic Arts

CTPR-573.title: Developing and Producing the Advanced Project
CTPR-573.description: An advanced preproduction workshop in which students complete the development and production planning of an advanced project to be executed in CTPR 581, CTPR 582 or CTPR 587a.
CTPR-573.prereqText:
Prerequisite: CTPR 508
Recommended preparation: submission of script required
Duplicates credit: former CTPR 553

CTPR-581A.description: Individual experimental projects involving the creative use of visuals (live action or animated) and sound. Qualifying courses: CTPR 532 (for directors); CTPR 558 (for producers). Graded IP/Letter.
CTPR-581A.prereqText:

Major: open only to Cinematic Arts, Film and Television Production

CTPR-582A.description: Advanced individual film or video projects under the guidance of a faculty mentor, without benefit of university equipment or resources. Qualifying courses: CTPR 532 (for directors); CTPR 558 (for producers). Graded IP/Letter.
CTPR-582A.prereqText:
Prerequisite: CTPR 573; CTPR 484 or CTPR 486 or CTPR 546 or CTPR 547
Major: open only to Cinematic Arts, Film and Television Production

CTPR-582B.description: Advanced individual film or video projects under the guidance of a faculty mentor, without benefit of university equipment or resources. Graded IP/Letter.
CTPR-582B.prereqText:

CTPR-582Z.description: Advanced individual film or video projects under the guidance of a faculty mentor, without benefit of university equipment or resources. Open to Production students only.
CTPR-582Z.prereqText:
Prerequisite: CTPR 582B
Major: open only to Cinematic Arts, Film and Television Production

CTPR-585A.description: Supervised, individual study leading to the creation of a producer's package. The package will include script, schedule, budget, finance and marketing plan. Graded IP/Letter.

Corequisite: CTPR 558 or CTPR 572

CTPR-587A.description: Advanced group project involving the creative use of visuals (live action or animated) and sound specifically designed for students who want to work in pairs. Qualifying courses: CTPR 532 (for directors); CTPR 558 (for producers).
CTPR-587A.prereqText:

CTPR-587B.description: Advanced group project involving the creative use of visuals (live action or animated) and sound specifically designed for students who want to work in pairs.

CTWR-206B.title: Writing the Screenplay
CTWR-206B.description: Writing a feature-length screenplay based on treatment developed in CTWR 206a. Includes a first draft and a polish.
CTWR-206B.prereqText:
Prerequisite: CTWR 206a
Major: open only to Writing for Screen and Television

CTWR-211.title: The Television Writer: An Agent of Change
CTWR-211.description: The television writer as an agent of change across current social issues including, but not limited to: race, gender, and class.

CTWR-250.title: Breaking the Story
CTWR-250.description: Examination of the fundamental elements of a good story, and how to use those elements to develop new screenplay ideas. Recommended preparation: CTWR 106b.

CTWR-321.title: Breaking the Hour-Long Television Series
CTWR-321.description: Introduction to hour-long television staff writing. Breaking of a complete season and writing episodes. Special attention to season construction, pitching, character and story engine.
CTWR-321.prereqText: Prerequisite: CTWR 100 or CTWR 402 or CTWR 409 or CTWR 413

CTWR-324.title: Breaking the Half-Hour Television Series
CTWR-324.description: The fundamentals of writing for half-hour television. Writing an episode of an existing half-hour television series, with emphasis on conception, pitching, characterization and structure.
CTWR-324.prereqText:
Prerequisite: CTWR 409 or CTWR 413
Recommended preparation: CTWR 404

CTWR-400.title: Is This A Joke: Mechanics of Comedy Writing
CTWR-400.description: Intensive fundamental writing class for all forms of comedy writing including joke construction, late night, sketches, scene work, and stand-up.

CTWR-403.title: Writing the Narrative Podcast Series
CTWR-403.description: Development of an original narrative podcast. Emphasis on dramatic elements of auditory storytelling and character development.

CTWR-406.title: Why The Long Face: Writing Comedy & the Human Experience
CTWR-406.description: Lectures in Comedy Writing through an interdisciplinary exploration of human experience and expression in the genre.

CTWR-409.title: Fundamentals of Screenwriting: Character, Conflict and Story
CTWR-409.description: Introduction to writing compelling scenes, creating authentic characters, three-act structure and feature film outlining.

CTWR-411.title: Television Script Analysis
CTWR-411.description: In-depth analysis of the craft of writing prime-time episodic television. Examination of situation comedies and dramas through weekly screenings and lectures.

CTWR-413.title: Writing the Short Script I
CTWR-413.description: Preparation of scripts for short films: form, structure, planning. Open only to Cinematic Arts Film and Television Production majors.
CTWR-413.prereqText: Major: open only to Cinematic Arts, Film and Television Production

CTWR-414.title: The Screenplay
CTWR-414.description: Students study story structure and develop several story outlines, write a short script for possible production, a feature film outline and first act. Recommended preparation: CTWR-416. Open only to Cinematic Arts Film and Television Production majors.
CTWR-414.prereqText:
Prerequisite: CTWR 413
Major: open only to Cinematic Arts, Film and Television Production, Cinema-Television

CTWR-417.title: Script Coverage and Story Analysis
CTWR-417.description: Evaluation of completed scripts prior to their production. Coverage and analysis of scripts as potential properties from the perspective of a production company.

CTWR-418B.title: Senior Thesis
CTWR-418B.description: b: Completion and revision of Senior Thesis project and introduction to motion picture industry procedures and practices through interaction with industry representatives. Open to B.F.A. Writing for Screen and Television students only.
CTWR-418B.prereqText:
Prerequisite: CTWR 418A
Major: open only to Writing for Screen and Television

CTWR-419B.title: Senior Thesis in Dramatic Television
CTWR-419B.description: Revision of original pilot script, writing of mid-season episode, and completion of bible for original dramatic series developed in first semester.
CTWR-419B.prereqText:
Prerequisite: CTWR 419a
Major: open only to Writing for Screen and Television

CTWR-422.title: Creating the Dramatic Television Series
CTWR-422.description: Examination and creation of the world, characters, and concept for an original hour-long dramatic series. Writing an outline for an original dramatic pilot.

CTWR-423.title: Writing the Screenplay
CTWR-423.description: Introduction to formal elements of the screenplay through lectures and the workshopping of a complete first draft of a feature-length script.
CTWR-423.prereqText:
Prerequisite: CTWR 409 or CTWR 413
Recommended preparation: CTWR 416
Duplicates credit: CTWR 415a, CTWR 415b

CTWR-430.title: Comedy Writers and Their Work
CTWR-430.description: Detailed investigation of specific comedy writers, comedy genres, and the works they've influenced. Lectures include screenings and visiting screenwriters.

CTWR-431.title: Screenwriters and Their Work
CTWR-431.description: Detailed investigation of a specific screenwriter's style and the works they've influenced. Lectures include screenings and visiting screenwriters.

CTWR-432.title: Television Writers and Their Work
CTWR-432.description: Detailed investigation of various television writers' styles, the worlds they have created, and the works they've influenced. Lectures include screenings and visiting television writers.

CTWR-437.title: Writing the Original Situation Comedy Pilot
CTWR-437.description: Advanced workshop for writing an original half-hour comedy series, including a pilot script, summary of characters and story lines for first season.
CTWR-437.prereqText:
Prerequisite: CTWR 321 or CTWR 324
Recommended preparation: CTWR 316 or CTWR 411

CTWR-439.title: Writing the Original Dramatic Series Pilot
CTWR-439.description: Advanced workshop in creation of an original dramatic series, including a first draft of the pilot and a summary of characters and storylines.
CTWR-439.prereqText:
Prerequisite: CTWR 321 or CTWR 324
Recommended preparation: CTWR 316 or CTWR 411

CTWR-446.title: Narrative Design of the Contained Story
CTWR-446.description: Analysis and practice of storytelling techniques when faced with imposed story limitations. Weekly screenings and lectures of classic and contemporary works.

CTWR-449.title: Rewriting the Original Dramatic Series Pilot
CTWR-449.description: An advanced workshop in which an original hour-long television pilot will be rewritten with emphasis on character, world creation and future story lines. Prerequisite(s): CTWR 439. Recommended preparation: CTWR 411.

CTWR-453.title: Advanced Feature Rewriting
CTWR-453.description: An advanced workshop in which a feature length screenplay will be rewritten using a specific methodology that focuses on a macro to micro approach to revision.

CTWR-457.title: Writing the Comedy Screenplay
CTWR-457.description: Writing a comedy feature length screenplay. Special attention to creating comedic characters and premise. Outline and first draft.
CTWR-457.prereqText:
Prerequisite: CTWR 206B or CTWR 409 or CTWR 512
Recommended preparation: CTWR 416

CTWR-459A.title: Entertainment Industry Seminar
CTWR-459A.description: Examination and analysis of various topics, issues, and resources pertaining to creative, legal, and business perspectives for writers in the entertainment industry.

CTWR-505.title: Creating the Short Film
CTWR-505.description: Strengthening and deepening the ability to conceive and develop ideas that will lead to compelling, authentic, and personally meaningful films. Duplicates credit in CTWR 528.

CTWR-510.title: Fundamentals of Storytelling for Animation
CTWR-510.description: Introduction to the fundamentals of storytelling with techniques and practices that work best for animated stories.

CTWR-514B.title: Basic Dramatic Screenwriting
CTWR-514B.description: Dramaturgy for the fiction and nonfiction work. Techniques for creating the original or adapted theatrical script. Open to graduate screenwriting majors (CTWR) and dramatic writing (Theatre) majors only. Development of an outline and feature-length original script.
CTWR-514B.prereqText:
Prerequisite: CTWR 514A
Class standing: open only to Master Student
Major: open only to Theatre (Dramatic Writing), Writing for Screen and Television

CTWR-515B.title: Practicum in Screenwriting
CTWR-515B.description: Comprehensive re-writing of second and third drafts of a feature screenplay leading to a polished and professional piece.

CTWR-516.title: Advanced Motion Picture Script Analysis
CTWR-516.description: Critical analysis of the structure of films from the classics to current award winners. Students will learn how to identify key story concepts and break down three act structure in finished films and scripts.

CTWR-517B.title: Thesis in Half-Hour Television Comedy
CTWR-517B.description: The re-write, casting, and performance stages of television comedy development. The completion of a final draft of the pilot script and series bible. Open only to Writing for Screen and Television master students.
CTWR-517B.prereqText:
Prerequisite: CTWR 517a
Class standing: open only to Master Student
Major: open only to Writing for Screen and Television

CTWR-519B.title: Thesis in Television Drama
CTWR-519B.description: Part B -- writing the series bible and mid-season episode -- is part two of the television thesis course. Students develop their original series further by writing the bible for the series and the mid-season episode which is reflective of storylines, characters and settings developed in part A of the course. Open to M.F.A. Writing for Screen and Television students only.
CTWR-519B.prereqText:
Prerequisite: CTWR 519A
Major: open only to Writing for Screen and Television

CTWR-520.title: Advanced Scene Writing Workshop
CTWR-520.description: Intensive workshop oriented specifically to writing and rewriting the most effective and telling dramatic scenes to heighten audience participation and greater story impact.

CTWR-523.title: Introduction to the Screenplay
CTWR-523.description: Introduction to formal elements of the screenplay through lectures and the workshopping of a complete first draft of a feature-length script. Prerequisite: CTAN 536 or CTWR 505 or CTWR 518. Recommended preparation: CTWR 516.
CTWR-523.prereqText: Prerequisite: CTAN 536 or CTWR 505 or CTWR 518

CTWR-529.title: Intermediate Screenwriting
CTWR-529.description: Emphasizes structural elements crucial to the feature film. Techniques for creating an original or adapted theatrical-length script.

CTWR-533.title: Rewriting the Feature Screenplay
CTWR-533.description: Rewriting the feature-length screenplay. Focus on macro to micro approach to revision.
CTWR-533.prereqText:
Prerequisite: CTWR 523
Recommended preparation: CTWR 516
Duplicates credit: former CTWR 533ab

CTWR-537.title: Advanced Half-Hour Comedy Series Pilot
CTWR-537.description: Development of an original half-hour comedy series; writing of the pilot episode and series bible.

CTWR-539.title: Advanced Hour-Long Drama Series Pilot
CTWR-539.description: Development of an original one hour drama series; writing of the pilot episode and series bible.

CTWR-541.title: Dreams, the Brain, and Storytelling
CTWR-541.description: Examination of the links between the brain, creativity, neuroscience and storytelling. Through lectures, screenings, and readings, students will log dreams for use in creative exercises.

CTWR-555.title: Pitching for Film and Television
CTWR-555.description: Development and pitching of ideas for motion pictures, episodic, and television pilots. Reducing ideas to basic components enhancing verbal presentation skills.
CTWR-555.prereqText: Prerequisite: CTWR 305 or CTWR 423 or CTWR 514B or CTWR 533

CTWR-585.title: Advanced Genre Writing
CTWR-585.description: Development and execution of writing in various genres of film, television, or new media scripts. Prerequisite: CTWR 514b.

CTXA-591.title: Expanded Animation Pre-Thesis
CTXA-591.description: Research and development of the thesis project in expanded animation. Presentation of the thesis proposal at the end of the semester.

CXPT-501.title: Biomedical Data Sciences
CXPT-501.description: Basics concept of code-based biomedical data analysis and visualization. Introduction to rigorous and reproducible analytical tools, including Python-based interactive notebooks. Appropriate use of statistical analysis.

CXPT-590.title: Directed Research
CXPT-590.description: Research leading to the master's degree. Maximum units which may be applied to the degree to be determined by the department.

CXPT-594A.title: Master's Thesis
CXPT-594A.description: Credit on acceptance of Master's thesis.
CXPT-594A.prereqText: Recommended preparation: Completion of all required coursework for MS degree

CXPT-594B.title: Master's Thesis
CXPT-594B.description: Credit on acceptance of master's thesis.

CXPT-594Z.title: Master's Thesis
CXPT-594Z.description: Credit on acceptance of Masters thesis.

CXPT-790.title: Research
CXPT-790.description: Research-based course for students enrolled in the CXPT PhD program who are preparing for their written and oral qualifying examination.

CXPT-794A.title: Doctoral Dissertation
CXPT-794A.description: Independent research course for students enrolled in the CXPT PhD program who have passed their written and oral qualifying examination and advanced to PhD candidacy.

CXPT-794B.title: Doctoral Dissertation
CXPT-794B.description: Independent research course for students enrolled in the CXPT PhD program who have passed their written and oral qualifying examination and advanced to PhD candidacy.

CXPT-794C.title: Doctoral Dissertation
CXPT-794C.description: Independent research course for students enrolled in the CXPT PhD program who have passed their written and oral qualifying examination and advanced to PhD candidacy.

CXPT-794D.title: Doctoral Dissertation
CXPT-794D.description: Independent research course for students enrolled in the CXPT PhD program who have passed their written and oral qualifying examination and advanced to PhD candidacy.

CXPT-794Z.title: Doctoral Dissertation
CXPT-794Z.description: Independent research course for students enrolled in the CXPT PhD program who have passed their written and oral qualifying examination and advanced to PhD candidacy.

DANC-101.title: Colloquium I: Joining the Creative Community
DANC-101.description: Introduction to a vibrant creative community. Students will explore university resources, engage with faculty, guest artists and staff, and establish goals for sustainability and growth.

DANC-110.title: Dance Technique I
DANC-110.description: Fundamental technique studies in a studio setting. Concentration on classical ballet, hip hop and its derivatives, partnering and contemporary techniques essential to the dancers' development.
DANC-110.prereqText:
Concurrent enrollment: DANC 120
Major: open only to Dance

DANC-120.title: Repertory and Performance I
DANC-120.description: Study and guided practice of choreographic repertory. Emphasis in choreographic intention, stylistic approaches and performance technique.
DANC-120.prereqText:
Concurrent enrollment: DANC 110
Major: open only to Dance
School: open only to Glorya Kaufman School of Dance

DANC-131.title: Composition: Movement Invention and Syntax
DANC-131.description: Applying improvisational tools to the development of set choreography and/or the development of functional improvisational structures for spontaneous composition in performance.
DANC-131.prereqText:
Prerequisite: DANC 130
Major: open only to Dance

DANC-181A.title: Contemporary Dance
DANC-181A.description: An introduction to methods developed from modern and post-modern dance techniques, including the study of the rebellious, individualistic, and democratic nature of dance in the 20th and 21st centuries.

DANC-181B.title: Contemporary Dance
DANC-181B.description: Continued study in the fusion of modern, post-modern dance and classical ballet techniques encompassing the study of the democratic nature of dance and choreographic composition in the 20th and 21st centuries.
DANC-181B.prereqText:
Prerequisite: DANC 181A
Duplicates credit: former THTR 181b

DANC-183A.title: Ballet
DANC-183A.description: An introduction to Classical Ballet technique with beginning-level barre and center work, focusing on correct body alignment and musicality. Development of a basic knowledge of ballet history and terminology.

DANC-183B.title: Ballet
DANC-183B.description: Continued study of Classical Ballet technique with intermediate-level barre and center work, focusing on developing greater clarity, coordination, musicality, and knowledge of ballet history and terminology.
DANC-183B.prereqText:
Prerequisite: DANC 183A
Duplicates credit: former THTR 183b

DANC-183C.title: Ballet
DANC-183C.description: Intermediate/advanced study of Classical Ballet technique with emphasis on clarity, precision, musicality, movement quality, and artistic expression. Introduction of beats, tours, advanced adagio and allegro combinations, and optional pointe work.
DANC-183C.prereqText:
Prerequisite: DANC 183B
Duplicates credit: former THTR 183c

DANC-184A.title: Jazz Dance
DANC-184A.description: An introduction to Jazz Dance technique, focusing on African and Latin based diaspora dances with European influences, improvisation, and strength/stretching series.

DANC-184B.title: Jazz Dance
DANC-184B.description: Continued study of Jazz Dance technique at the intermediate level, focusing on African and Latin based diaspora dances with European influences, improvisation, center work, performance techniques, and strength/stretching series.
DANC-184B.prereqText:
Prerequisite: DANC 184A
Duplicates credit: former THTR 184b

DANC-185A.title: Hip Hop Dance
DANC-185A.description: An introduction to elements of Hip Hop Dance, including technique, movement, musical rhythm, tempo, and phrasing, as well as the historical context required to develop the skills needed to practice and perform this popular dance form.
DANC-185A.prereqText: Duplicates credit: former THTR 185 and former DANC 185

DANC-185B.title: Hip Hop Dance
DANC-185B.description: Continued study of Hip Hop Dance elements on an intermediate level, augmenting the historical context, technique, fluidity, and musicality required to execute the form with greater movement acuity.

DANC-187.title: Bollywood Dance
DANC-187.description: An introduction to basic and intermediate Bollywood Dance, including technique, movement fundamentals, musical rhythm, choreography and historical context. Inspired by the eclectic and energetic music from the Hindi-language film industry of India, Bollywood is a highly expressive dance style that combines Indian folk and classical dances with Hip Hop, Jazz, Latin and popular forms.

DANC-188A.title: International Style Ballroom Dance
DANC-188A.description: Introduction to International Standard, International Latin, and American Style ballroom dances. Designed to introduce students to the fundamentals of ballroom dance, emphasizing partner connection, communication, and creativity, with the practical application of dance within a social setting.

DANC-188B.title: International Style Ballroom Dance
DANC-188B.description: Continued study in International Standard, International Latin, and American Style ballroom dances. Designed for advanced knowledge in ballroom styles, emphasizing rhythmic sequences, partnering techniques, complex patterns, and performance quality.
DANC-188B.prereqText:
Prerequisite: DANC 188A
Duplicates credit: former THTR 188b

DANC-189A.title: Tap Dance
DANC-189A.description: An introduction to basic Tap Dance technique, rhythms, syncopation, and musicality, developing into complex steps and elementary dances with progressive understanding of weight change, improvisation, and combinations of sound.

DANC-189B.title: Tap Dance
DANC-189B.description: Continued study of Tap Dance technique, focusing on more complex rhythmic patterns and combinations and introducing advanced steps and combinations, all with continued emphasis on improvisation and musicality.
DANC-189B.prereqText:
Prerequisite: DANC 189A
Duplicates credit: former THTR 189b

DANC-195.title: Kaufman in the Community
DANC-195.description: Practice-based community engagement through dance, pedagogy and program development.

DANC-201.title: Colloquium II: Investing in the Collaboratory
DANC-201.description: Continued investment in the creative community, with a focus on best practices for sharing work, soliciting feedback and establishing healthy relationships with fellow creators.
DANC-201.prereqText:
Prerequisite: DANC 101
Major: open only to Dance

DANC-210.title: Dance Technique II
DANC-210.description: Intermediate technique studies in a studio setting. Concentration on classical ballet, hip hop and its derivatives, partnering and contemporary techniques essential to the dancers' development.
DANC-210.prereqText:
Prerequisite: DANC 110
Major: open only to Dance

DANC-212.title: Dance in Popular Culture
DANC-212.description: Examination of the role of dance in popular culture in a classroom setting. Studies of dance styles and their evolution in recreational and professional contexts through research, observation, and practice.

DANC-218.title: Introduction to Dance Media Composition
DANC-218.description: Effective navigation and utilization of digital technologies to create dance-based media compositions and online portfolios.

DANC-220.title: Repertory and Performance II
DANC-220.description: Continued studies and guided practice of choreographic repertory. Investigation of choreographic vocabulary, intention, stylistic approaches, and performance technique for group work.
DANC-220.prereqText:
Prerequisite: DANC 120
Concurrent enrollment: DANC 210
Major: open only to Dance

DANC-231.title: Composition: Collaborative Creation
DANC-231.description: Continued integration of interdisciplinary design elements resulting in the more fully realized production and presentation of choreographic work.
DANC-231.prereqText:
Prerequisite: DANC 230
Major: open only to Dance

DANC-280.title: Introduction to Dance as an Art Form
DANC-280.description: Gateway to the minor in dance. An interdisciplinary overview of dance relating to the aesthetic and art in various subjects. Applications of the elements of dance studies, art criticism, and viewing productions to explore topic such as architecture, photography, poetry, technology, cinematic arts, sports, medicine, and more.

DANC-301.title: Colloquium III: Clarifying Personal Pathways
DANC-301.description: Clarification of long-term goals, establishment of a unique artistic identity, and contextualization of creative work within broader social, political and cultural contexts.
DANC-301.prereqText:
Prerequisite: DANC 201
Major: open only to Dance

DANC-302.title: Hip Hop Don't Stop: Black Social Dance Culture and Media
DANC-302.description: Introduction to the history and practice of Urban Folk Dance including hip hop, freestyle, street dance and the relevant social dances of the 20th century.

DANC-305.title: Dance Science: Analysis of Dance Movement
DANC-305.description: A broad overview of the scientific principles of exercise physiology, functional anatomy, kinesiology, and bio-mechanics with applications to dance.

DANC-310.title: Dance Technique III
DANC-310.description: Advanced technique studies in a studio setting. Concentration on classical ballet, hip hop and its derivatives, partnering and contemporary techniques essential to the dancers' development.
DANC-310.prereqText:
Prerequisite: DANC 210
Major: open only to Dance

DANC-312.title: African American Dance
DANC-312.description: Exploration of the discursive foundations, political motivations, and aesthetic strategies of dance writers and artists whose works have enabled the category of "black dance."

DANC-320.title: Repertory and Performance III
DANC-320.description: Study and guided practice of new works and developing roles. Emphasis on the dancer as collaborator in the creative process.
DANC-320.prereqText:
Prerequisite: DANC 220
Concurrent enrollment: DANC 310
Major: open only to Dance

DANC-333.title: Origins of Jazz Dance
DANC-333.description: Examining the role that vernacular dance and music play in the creation of Jazz Dance, taught in lecture format; practical studies in Jazz Dance, from recreational to professional settings.

DANC-342.title: International and Historical Perspectives on Dance
DANC-342.description: Exploration of dance as an art form in its artistic, political, and socio-cultural climate. Studies of the continuum of dance within its historical context.

DANC-350.title: Advanced Composition
DANC-350.description: Explore a variety of compositional forms and methods to develop a personalized choreographic approach.
DANC-350.prereqText: Duplicates credit: former DANC 330 and former DANC 430

DANC-355.title: Performance Lab

Recommended preparation: A basic understanding of engineering and/or technology is recommended.

EALC-101.title: Conversational Chinese and Intercultural Communication
EALC-101.description: Basic Mandarin conversational skills for effective communication in familiar, everyday Chinese contexts and better understanding of intercultural communication through content-based language acquisition. Graded CR/NC. Not available for credit to East Asian Area Studies, East Asian Languages and Cultures, and East Asian Studies majors and minors.

EALC-102.title: Language, Art and Culture: Calligraphy
EALC-102.description: This course introduces students to the origin of the basic components of Chinese scripts and the basic principles and styles of calligraphy.

EALC-104.title: Chinese I
EALC-104.description: The sound system of modern Chinese; aural comprehension, oral expression, basic patterns, and writing system.

EALC-106.title: Chinese II
EALC-106.description: Dialogue practice and conversation; reading of simple stories and essays; comparison of Chinese and English grammar; writing of paragraphs.

EALC-109.title: Extensive Reading in Chinese
EALC-109.description: Develops reading fluency in Chinese through the Extensive Reading method, emphasizing large-volume reading with minimal unfamiliar vocabulary to build comprehension and enjoyment.

EALC-115.title: Korean I
EALC-115.description: Basic Korean conversation practice, aural comprehension, basic grammar and building proficiency of reading and writing with Hangul (Korean alphabet).

EALC-117.title: Korean II
EALC-117.description: Continuation of EALC 115, basic conversation practice, aural comprehension, basic grammar and building proficiency of reading and writing.

EALC-120.title: Japanese I
EALC-120.description: Basic Japanese conversation practice, basic grammar and building proficiency of reading and writing Hiragana and Katakana (Japanese alphabetical systems) and some basic kanji (Chinese characters).

EALC-121.title: Extensive Reading in Japanese I
EALC-121.description: Development of reading skill in Japanese for elementary level students through short stories written for learners of Japanese and authentic materials written for native Japanese speakers.

EALC-122.title: Japanese II
EALC-122.description: Continuation of EALC 120. Basic Japanese conversation practice, basic grammar and building proficiency of reading and writing Hiragana and Katakana and basic kanji.

EALC-125.title: Introduction to Contemporary East Asian Cinema and Culture
EALC-125.description: An introduction to and overview of the contemporary cinemas of East Asia: China (Hong Kong, the People's Republic, and Taiwan), Japan, and Korea.

EALC-130.title: Introduction to East Asian Ethical Thought
EALC-130.description: Foundations of East Asian ethical and philosophical thought and how they apply to modern ethical issues, such as the death penalty, abortion or climate change.

EALC-204.title: Chinese III
EALC-204.description: Conversational practice: reading of stories and essays; writing of short essays.

EALC-206.title: Chinese IV
EALC-206.description: Continuation of 204, with emphasis on reading and writing, frequent interaction with native speakers.

EALC-215.title: Korean III
EALC-215.description: Drill to increase proficiency in dialogue, reading, and writing; intermediate level readings.

EALC-217.title: Korean IV
EALC-217.description: Advanced level reading of modern Korean and exercises in written composition.

EALC-220.title: Japanese III
EALC-220.description: Continuation of EALC 122. Conversation practice, basic to intermediate grammar, and building proficiency of reading and writing Hiragana and Katakana with additional kanji.

EALC-221.title: Extensive Reading in Japanese II
EALC-221.description: Development of reading skills in Japanese for intermediate level students through short stories written for learners of Japanese and authentic materials written for native speakers.

EALC-222.title: Japanese IV
EALC-222.description: Continuation of EALC 220. More sophisticated grammar and vocabulary for natural conversation. Enhancing fundamental reading and writing skills, expanding the knowledge of kanji.

EALC-250.title: Nation, Culture and Power in East Asia
EALC-250.description: Analyzes political power, nationalism and cultural identity in East Asia. Topics addressed include multiculturalism, migration and ethnic politics, in addition to theories of nationalism.

EALC-255.title: Southeast Asian Literature and Film
EALC-255.description: Comparative approach and general introduction to literature and cinema from selected countries in the Association for Southeast Asian Nations.

EALC-264.title: Asian Aesthetic and Literary Traditions
EALC-264.description: A comparative study of the Asian aesthetic heritage of poetry, painting, music, and drama; of literary themes, trends, and myths.

EALC-304.title: Advanced Modern Chinese I
EALC-304.description: Reading selections from different styles of modern Chinese writings, analysis of stylistic techniques and syntactic structure, composition, and translation.

EALC-306.title: Advanced Modern Chinese II
EALC-306.description: Continuation of 304; composition exercises in different styles of writing.

EALC-317.title: Advanced Korean II
EALC-317.description: Continuation of EALC 315, with emphasis on the use of Chinese characters, translation, and composition exercises.

EALC-320.title: Advanced Japanese I
EALC-320.description: Strengthen intermediate Japanese language proficiency. Oral/aural communication skills as well as reading and writing skills. Promote an understanding of the present-day Japanese culture.

EALC-322.title: Advanced Japanese II
EALC-322.description: Continuation of EALC 320. Improve and strengthen abilities to speak, listen, read and write, coping with more involved materials and situation.

EALC-331.title: Encountering Japanese Religions
EALC-331.description: The development of religious thought and practice in the Japanese islands, with Buddhism and Shinto being the most prominent.

EALC-333.title: Introduction to Korean Film
EALC-333.description: Survey of Korean film, the film industry and critical issues from the colonial period to the present.

EALC-358.title: Transnational Chinese Literature and Culture
EALC-358.description: An introduction to Sinophone literatures and cultures (in English translation) from the Asia-Pacific region, including Taiwan, Hong Kong, Tibet, Southeast Asia, and North America.

EALC-366.title: Chinese Professional Internship: Communication and Culture
EALC-366.description: Combined classroom discussion and supervised internship at companies. Practical experience in applying communication and cultural knowledge in a professional, "real world" employment context.

EALC-383.title: Later Chinese Art
EALC-383.description: A survey of Chinese painting from 900 to the present, emphasizing the role of painting within the context of Chinese intellectual history.

EALC-407.title: News and Web Chinese
EALC-407.description: Reading selections from newspaper articles and online reports to further develop proficiency in advanced Chinese and understanding of the society and culture.

EALC-420.title: Advanced Oral Communication in Japanese
EALC-420.description: Development of advanced oral communication skills in Japanese, fostering cultural understanding and practical communication for diverse academic, professional, and social contexts.

EALC-432.title: Premodern Korean Literature and Storytelling
EALC-432.description: Development of Korean literature from ancient times to the nineteenth century, including major canonical works. Conducted in English.

EALC-455.title: Japanese Fiction
EALC-455.description: Japanese fiction from early to modern times; literary, philosophical, and social aspects of tales and novels. Conducted in English.

EALC-465.title: Topics in Korean Visual and Cultural Studies
EALC-465.description: Examination of dominant and emergent critical issues in the study of modern and contemporary Korean visual culture.

EALC-483.title: East Asian Garden and Designed Landscape
EALC-483.description: Explores the transmigration of Japanese art and aesthetics and the politics of their adaptation and assimilation in Los Angeles.

EALC-485.title: Material Culture of the Silk Road
EALC-485.description: Introduction to the history and material culture of the Silk Road with emphasis on the arts of Dunhuang and Kucha.

ECON-101.title: Free People, Free Thought and Free Markets
ECON-101.description: The philosophical foundations of modern political and economic thought, including economic rationality, neoclassical economics, free-market vs. socialist economies and behavioral economics.

ECON-203.title: Principles of Microeconomics
ECON-203.description: Behavior of firms and consumers, functions of the price system, competition and monopoly, labor markets, poverty, government regulation, international trade, and the environment.

ECON-205.title: Principles of Macroeconomics
ECON-205.description: Unemployment, inflation and output determination and links.Effects of government taxation and spending on growth, investment,saving, consumption, and trade.

ECON-303.title: Intermediate Microeconomic Theory
ECON-303.description: Decision-making by business firms, consumer preferences and behavior, uncertainty, competition, monopoly, labor and resource markets, efficient resource allocation, externalities, and government policy.

ECON-305.title: Intermediate Macroeconomic Theory
ECON-305.description: The determinants of aggregate income, employment, and inflation; economic fluctuations; fiscal and monetary policy; financial markets; the national debt.
ECON-305.prereqText: Prerequisite: ECON 203; ECON 205; MATH 118 or MATH 125

ECON-317.title: Introduction to Statistics for Economists
ECON-317.description: Introduction to statistical methods appropriate for analyzing economic data: probability theory, random variables and probability distributions, sampling, estimation, statistical inference.

ECON-318.title: Introduction to Econometrics
ECON-318.description: Application of statistical methods to economic data: estimating economic relationships using regression analysis, testing hypotheses involving economic behavior, forecasting economic variables.
ECON-318.prereqText:
Prerequisite: ECON 317
Duplicates credit: former ECON 414

ECON-333.title: Innovation Economics and Business: Beer, AI and Video Games
ECON-333.description: Analyze varied industries using legal, business, and economic principles. Emphasis is on how these forces shape marketing strategies.
ECON-333.prereqText: Prerequisite: ECON 203 or ECON 351 or BUAD 351

ECON-339.title: Philosophy of Economics
ECON-339.description: Central topics in the philosophy of economics, including models of economic rationality, the aggregation of preferences and the conditions in which markets yield undesirable outcomes.

ECON-340.title: Economics of Less Developed Countries
ECON-340.description: Causes of economic underdevelopment: historical, institutional, structural, ideological, technological, cultural. Patterns and theories of development. Role of government, international trade, and education in economic growth.

ECON-346.title: Economics of Transition and Development: China
ECON-346.description: A focus on the Chinese economy, its reform and transition to a market economy, its relation with East Asian countries and integration into the world economy.

ECON-351.title: Microeconomics for Business
ECON-351.description: Development and business applications of: theory of the firm; theory of the consumer; inter-temporaldecisions; decisions under risk; market failures; industrial and enterprise structure. Prerequisites: MATH 118 or MATH 125 or MATH 126 or MATH 226. Not for major credit for: Economics, Economics/Mathematics, Social Sciences (Economics). Duplicates credit in BUAD 351.
ECON-351.prereqText:
Prerequisite: MATH 118 or MATH 125 or MATH 126 or MATH 226
Duplicates credit: BUAD 351

ECON-352.title: Macroeconomics for Business
ECON-352.description: Theoretical development and significance to business and markets of economic growth; inflation;unemployment; monetary and fiscal policy; business cycles; savings and investment; exchange rates. Corequisite: ECON 351. Recommended preparation: introductory economics course, high school math, and algebra. Not for major credit for: Economics, Economics/Mathematics, Social Sciences (Economics). Duplicates credit in BUAD 352.

ECON-357.title: Money, Credit, and Banking
ECON-357.description: The money, bond, stock, and other financial markets; portfolio choice; determinants of asset prices and interest rates; inflation; interactions between financial markets and government policies.

ECON-361.title: Understanding Financial Crises
ECON-361.description: Key facts and basic mechanisms concerning financial crises and related topics (bank runs, sovereign default decision, currency collapse).

ECON-379.title: Economic Policy Analysis
ECON-379.description: Main frameworks, theories, practices of applied economics policy in real-world settings; creating competencies for elected officials, central bank personnel, public administrators, regulators, nonprofit executives, implementers and evaluators.

ECON-395.title: Economic Policy Issues
ECON-395.description: Selected policy dilemmas in economics. Topics vary.

ECON-405.title: Neuroeconomics
ECON-405.description: Introduction to the methodology used in experimental neuroeconomics and discussion of neural correlates of decision-making. Prerequisite: ECON 303.

ECON-415.title: Behavioral Economics
ECON-415.description: Examination of the traditional and behavioral theories of decision-making and the state of the art in the field. Prerequisite: ECON 303.

ECON-451.title: The Politics of International Trade
ECON-451.description: Economic approaches and political processes are used to explain observed international trade policy choices. Topics covered include globalization, regionalism, labor standards, the environment and sanctions. Recommended preparation: Micro- and Macroeconomics.

ECON-457.title: Financial Markets
ECON-457.description: General equilibrium analysis of economics with financial markets; decision making under uncertainty; methods of risk reduction; portfolio theory and valuation of securities; efficiency of security markets.

ECON-460.title: Economic Applications of Machine Learning
ECON-460.description: A capstone course that introduces state-of-the-art estimation methods for high-dimensional data.
ECON-460.prereqText:
Prerequisite: ECON 303; ECON 318; MATH 225; DSCI 250
Corequisite: CSCI 103
Recommended preparation: MATH 226g

ECON-464.title: The Principles of Market Design
ECON-464.description: Fundamental principles in designing successful market mechanisms to allocate resources.

ECON-474.title: Economic Consulting and Applied Managerial Economics
ECON-474.description: Economic consulting and managerial economic methods applied in real world problems. Economic methods to analyze issues of intellectual property, environmental damage, trademark infringement, brand value, and consumer demand.

ECON-480.title: Economics of Industrial Organization
ECON-480.description: Pricing and resource allocation in imperfectly competitive markets; monopoly regulation, collusion, cartels, mergers and antitrust; patents and development incentives; industry case studies.

ECON-487.title: Resource and Environmental Economics
ECON-487.description: Management and extraction of renewable and non-renewable natural resources; environmental externalities and regulation of air, water, and land pollution; market incentives versus direct regulation.

ECON-490.title: Directed Research
ECON-490.description: Supervised individual research. Not available for graduate credit. Requires departmental approval.
ECON-490.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Junior, Senior

ECON-495.title: Honors Thesis
ECON-495.description: Individual research supervised by a faculty advisor. Successful completion required for departmental honors degree.

ECON-499.title: Special Topics
ECON-499.description: Selected topics in economic theory, history, or policy.

ECON-500.title: Microeconomic Analysis and Policy
ECON-500.description: Theories of the household and the firm; product and factor markets; perfect and imperfect competition; welfare criteria.

ECON-501.title: Macroeconomic Analysis and Policy
ECON-501.description: Theories of aggregate economic activity; design and use of macroeconometric models; stabilization and control of inflation, unemployment, and growth.

ECON-504.title: Game Theory with Economic and Financial Applications
ECON-504.description: Applying game theory to economic and financial markets and interactions in a diverse set of examples like reputation, herding, bubbles and crashes, auctions, strategic information revelation and information accumulation in markets. Witnessing the wide range of applications that is amenable to game theoretical analysis.

ECON-513.title: Practice of Econometrics
ECON-513.description: Application of econometric tools using standard econometric software packages for microcomputers; empirical applications to selected economic problems of estimation and inference.

ECON-515.title: Time Series Analysis
ECON-515.description: Understanding and implementing models commonly used in time series econometrics. Emphasis is placed on intuition and application. Assists students understanding how to use time series data to test hypotheses and serve as an introduction to the ideas and techniques of forecasting.

ECON-521.title: International Macroeconomics and Financial Policy
ECON-521.description: The balance of payments, macroeconomic policy in an open economy, exchange rate determination, exchange rate systems, currency crises, international financial arrangements and monetary history.

ECON-550.title: Applied Trade Policy
ECON-550.description: Introduction and exploration of quantitative methods and data sources used for applied trade policy analysis.

ECON-555.title: Topics in Asset Pricing Theory
ECON-555.description: How do investors evaluate risks? With what information? How do they form their beliefs? Via empirical evidence and theoretical works, this course addresses these questions.
ECON-555.prereqText: Recommended preparation: ECON 508 and ECON 514 and ECON 606

ECON-569.title: Cryptoeconomics and Blockchain Mechanisms
ECON-569.description: Introduction to the economics of decentralized blockchain systems; explores how mechanism design and cryptography are used in combination to build secure, trustless, consensus-driven blockchains

ECON-571.title: Economics of Digital Platforms
ECON-571.description: Introduces the novel business model and important features associated with digital platforms and analyzes firms various competitive behavior and anticompetitive conducts in the digital space.

ECON-577.title: Foundations of Financial Economics
ECON-577.description: Broad training in theoretical and empirical finance. Choice under uncertainty; equilibrium asset pricing; static portfolio choice; factor pricing models, asset allocation; the Black-Scholes-Merton Formula.

ECON-580.title: Antitrust Economics and Competition Policy
ECON-580.description: Efficiency, market failure, government regulation, some basics for antitrust economics, competition policy analysis and collusion and agreements among competitors.

ECON-584.title: Economic Consulting and Applied Econometrics
ECON-584.description: Economic methods to analyze issues of intellectual property, environmental damage, trademark infringement, brand value and consumer demand, using an applied econometric approach.

ECON-590.description: Research leading to the master's degree. Maximum units which may be applied to the degree to be determined by the department. Graded CR/NC.

ECON-596.title: Internship for Curricular Practical Training
ECON-596.description: Part-time or full-time, practical work experience in the student's field of study. Students must have a specific job/internship offer. Job must be related to students major. The internship must be located at an off-campus facility. Students are individually supervised by faculty. Students must have been in F-1 student status for at least one academic year in a degree-seeking program before they can apply for CPT, with a cumulative 3.0 GPA. Course does not apply to degree credit. Open only to graduate students.

ECON-603.title: Microeconomic Theory II
ECON-603.description: General equilibrium theory; existence, uniqueness, and stability; welfare economics; social choice; dynamic models and uncertainty; special topics. Prerequisite: ECON-601.

ECON-605.title: Macroeconomic Theory II
ECON-605.description: Macroeconomic theory based on the concepts of optimal growth and intertemporal equilibrium; overlapping generations models; recent developments in macroeconomic theory. Prerequisites: ECON-601 and ECON-602.

ECON-609.title: Econometric Methods
ECON-609.description: Review of statistical methods of estimation and inference, linear regression with multicollinearity and serial correlation; multivariate regression and simultaneous equations. Prerequisite: ECON 611. Duplicates credit in former ECON 511.

ECON-616.title: Experimental Economics
ECON-616.description: Laboratory methods for testing economic theory; experimental comparison of alternative market and non-market institutions; identification of behavioral responses to alternative regulations.

ECON-641.title: Empirical Analysis of Economic Development
ECON-641.description: Theory and empirics of the sources of and barriers to economic development and the micro underpinnings of macroeconomic dynamics of growth, inequality, and productivity. Prerequisites: ECON 601 and ECON 609.

ECON-661.title: Topics in Macroeconomics
ECON-661.description: Current areas of research in macroeconomics: Structural Change; Inequality and Macroeconomics.

ECON-681.title: Economics of Regulated Industries
ECON-681.description: Theories and methods of government regulation; effects of regulation on various industries; behavior of regulatory agencies. Prerequisites: ECON-500 or ECON-601.

ECON-686B.title: Empirical Methods in Economics
ECON-686B.description: Think about and design empirical studies in economics using cutting-edge approaches to causal inference -- structural and discrete choice models, micro-macro models and historical data models.
ECON-686B.prereqText:

ECON-694.description: Topics in dynamic economics involving business fluctuations, economic growth and development, microeconomic adjustments and market mechanisms; related quantitative and qualitative methods; empirical research involving economic change. Graded CR/NC.

EDHP-560.description: History of feminist theory and major perspectives of current feminist theory: liberal feminism, socialist/Marxist feminism, radical feminism, psychological feminism, spiritual feminism, and ecological feminism.

EDHP-580.title: The Community College

EE-105.title: Introduction to Electrical Engineering

EE-109.title: Introduction to Embedded Systems

EE-109.prereqText: Prerequisite: EE 155 or CSCI 102 or CSCI 113

EE-141.title: Applied Linear Algebra for Engineering
EE-141.description: Introduction to linear algebra with engineering applications. Weekly laboratory exercises using MATLAB.

EE-155.title: Introduction to Computer Programming for         Electrical Engineers
EE-155.description: Introduction to solving engineering problems using computational methods. Survey of various programming languages and their strengths and weaknesses. Program structure, input/output, conditionals, loops, functions, arrays.

EE-202.title: Linear Circuits
EE-202.description: Lumped circuit elements; network equations; zero-input and zerostate responses; sinusoidal steady-state analysis; impedance; resonance; network functions; power concepts; transformers; Laplace transforms.

EE-250.title: Distributed Systems for the Internet of Things
EE-250.description: Introduction to hardware, operating systems, signal processing and control, network protocols, mobile applications, databases, cloud computing, machine learning and security for the Internet of Things.
EE-250.prereqText:
Prerequisite: EE 109
Recommended preparation: Experience with DIY electronics, Linux and programming in a distributed, networked environment
Class standing: not open to Freshman

EE-355.title: Software Design for Electrical Engineers
EE-355.description: Object-oriented programming techniques, basic data structures and elementary complexity analysis for the modeling, simulation and solution of engineering problems.

EE-364.title: Probability and Statistics for Engineers and Computer Scient
EE-364.description: Introduction to concepts of randomness and uncertainty: probability, random variables, statistics. Applications to digital communications, signal processing, automatic control, computer engineering and computer science.

EE-370.title: Electromagnetics for Engineering Systems
EE-370.description: Electromagnetic plane-wave propagation and interactions with simple media, transmission/reception of wireless signals in complex environments. Optimization design methods for system applications.

EE-415.title: Introduction to Microelectromechanical Systems
EE-415.description: Introduction to micro-electro-mechanical systems (MEMS); scaling effects; materials and structures in MEMS; MEMS sensing and actuation principles; microfabrication.
EE-415.prereqText: Recommended preparation: Mechanics of materials on the level of AME 204 or CE 225, Dynamics on the level of AME 301

EE-443.title: Power Systems

Prerequisite: CSCI 104 or CSCI 114 or EE 355
Class standing: open only to Junior, Senior

Class standing: not open to Freshman, Sophomore

Prerequisite: EE 155 or TAC 168 or ITP 115 or ITP 165 or ITP 168 or BME 210 or CE 108 or CHE 305 or CSCI 103 or CSCI 113 or ISE 150 or TAC 115 or TAC 165; EE 141 or MATH 225 or MATH 235

EE-496.prereqText: Prerequisite: EE 354 or EE 348 or EE 460 or EE 483

EE-501.title: Solid State
EE-501.description: Atomic electronic states, molecular bonding, crystal structures, diffraction, reciprocal lattice, Brillouin zones, crystal binding, lattice vibrations, specific heat, anharmonic effects, energy bands, metals, conductivity.
EE-501.prereqText: Recommended preparation: Quantum Mechanics (EE 471 or EE 539 or PHYS 438a or equivalent). Vector analysis, linear algebra, complex variables, transforms, ordinary and partial second order differential equations (MATH 445).

EE-503.title: Probability for Electrical and Computer Engineers
EE-503.description: Rigorous coverage of probability, discrete and continuous random variables, functions of multiple random variables, covariance, correlation, random sequences, Markov chains, estimation, and introduction to statistics. Duplicates credit in former EE 464 and EE 465.

EE-506.title: Semiconductor Physics
EE-506.description: Semiconductor bonds, crystallography, band structure assumptions, group theory, band structure results, k.p. method, quantum wells, wires and dots, superlattices, amorphous, organic semiconductors, defects, statistics, surfaces.
EE-506.prereqText: Recommended preparation: Undergraduate differential calculus, linear algebra, statistics, programming, Newtonian mechanics, waves, Maxwells equations

EE-508.title: Hardware Foundations of Machine Learning
EE-508.description: Introduction to ML accelerators; memory access kernels; parallelization approaches to the design of scalable ML systems; distributed ML; privacy in machine learning.
EE-508.prereqText: Recommended preparation: Matrix algebraic algorithms on the level of EE141L; Gradient descent, PyTorch, Tensorflow or similar parallel  programming experience on the level of EE451; Memory systems of CPUs and GPUs on the level of EE457

EE-510.title: Linear Algebra for Engineering
EE-510.description: Introduction to linear algebra and matrix theory and their underlying concepts; applications to engineering problems; mathematically rigorous and foundational to other classes in communication, control, and signal processing.
EE-510.prereqText: Recommended preparation: EE 141 and MATH 445 or equivalent (calculus, undergraduate linear algebra, matrix theory)

EE-512.title: Stochastic Processes for Financial Engineering
EE-512.description: Theory and applications of stochastic processes relevant to financial engineering. Stochastic processes, Brownian motion, martingales, stochastic calculus, Monte Carlo Simulations with financial application examples.
EE-512.prereqText: Prerequisite: EE 503; EE 441 or EE 510 or EE 518

EE-515.title: Quantum Sensing: Machine Learning, Inference and Information
EE-515.description: Basics of quantum mechanics, quantum sensing, quantum theory of inference, information and machine learning.
EE-515.prereqText: Recommended preparation: Basic quantum mechanics on the level of EE 539. Linear algebra on the level of EE 141.  Probability on the level of EE 364.

EE-518.title: Mathematics and Tools for Financial Engineering
EE-518.description: Students will build a mathematical background for studying Financial Engineering. Emphasis is on analysis, proofs and examples. Mathworks Financial toolbox will be introduced.

EE-519.title: Speech Recognition and Processing for Multimedia
EE-519.description: Speech production, acoustics, perception, synthesis, compression, recognition, transmission. Coding for speech, music, and CD-quality. Feature extraction. Echo cancellation. Audio, visual synchronization. Multimedia, Internet use.

EE-521.title: Power Systems Analysis and Design
EE-521.description: Power system planning, studies, and design; time-domain modeling and analysis of power-system networks; power flow, stability, fault, and economic dispatch analysis; symmetrical components.

EE-522.title: Spatial Audio for Real and Virtual Spaces
EE-522.description: Fundamentals of audio signal processing, acoustics and human perception to understand sound in the real world and create compelling virtual auditory worlds.
EE-522.prereqText: Recommended preparation: MATLAB experience is useful but not required

EE-523.title: Advanced Biomedical Imaging
EE-523.description: Advanced scientific and engineering principles of biomedical imaging including magnetic resonance, X-ray computed tomography, ultrasound and single photon and positron emission tomography.
EE-523.prereqText: Recommended preparation: BME 513 or EE 483 or previous/concurrent exposure to linear systems and signals, Fourier Transform, and signal processing in the frequency domain

EE-524.title: Complex Digital ASIC System Design
EE-524.description: Complex digital/mixed-signal ASICs from algorithm to chip tapeout including synthesis, hardware accelerators, RTL design, physical design, specialization, verification, post-fabrication experiments. Project-based.
EE-524.prereqText: Recommended preparation: Digital circuits on the level of EE 354L; computer systems organization on the level of EE 457; VLSI circuit design on the level of EE 477; VLSI system design on the level of EE 577a/b.

EE-526.title: Renewable Energy in Power Systems
EE-526.description: Renewable energy sources and their integration in electrical networks. Power-flow control from highly variable resources. Cost analysis and planning.

EE-528.title: Power Electronics
EE-528.description: Fundamentals of switched-mode power converters operating under steadystate and transient conditions. Feedback control systems. Magnetic circuit design.

EE-531.title: Nonlinear Optics
EE-531.description: Theory of nonlinear optical susceptibility and application to self-focusing, harmonic generation, and parametric interactions. Raman and Brillouin scattering. Coherent spectroscopy.
EE-531.prereqText: Recommended preparation: Maxwell's equations and Fourier transforms on the level of EE 572

EE-533.title: Network Processor Design and Programming
EE-533.description: Design, implementation, and programming of a custom multi-core RISC-V-based network processor and hardware accelerators using reconfigurable hardware in a SmartNIC in a realistic network testbed.

EE-535.title: Wireless Communications
EE-535.description: The mobile communication channel; techniques used to combat the channel; cellular communications; multiple-access techniques; example mobile communication systems.
EE-535.prereqText:
Corequisite: EE 503
Recommended preparation: Basic electromagnetic theory, digital communications systems; EE 510

EE-538.title: Computing Principles for Electrical Engineers
EE-538.description: Survey of computing principles and practice of software design: object-oriented and non object-oriented, testing, template libraries, time-space complexity, data structures, algorithms, and dynamic programming.
EE-538.prereqText: Recommended preparation: Exposure to computer programming

EE-541.title: A Computational Introduction to Deep Learning
EE-541.description: Deep learning frameworks for training multilayer perceptrons, convolutional and recurrent neural networks; Python, virtual environments, linux and shell scripting, cloud computing, including GPUs and datasets.
EE-541.prereqText:
Corequisite: EE 503; EE 510
Recommended preparation: Graduate standing and a typical undergraduate ECE background including the equivalent of EE 105 and EE 155 and some exposure to a high-level scripting language such as Python or Matlab.

EE-545.title: Robotics
EE-545.description: Fundamental skills for modeling and controlling of dynamic systems for robotic applications and graphics animations; control theory; kinematics; dynamics; sensor processing; real-time operating systems; robot labs. Recommended preparation: Basic knowledge in linear algebra (matrices and vectors), calculus, programming in C/C++ or any another language or permission of the instructor.

EE-547.title: Applied and Cloud Computing for Electrical Engineers
EE-547.description: Introduction to cloud applications; software development and deployment within cloud platforms; interactive user-facing interfaces; API development; databases, virtualization, asynchronous execution, testing and scalability.

EE-549.title: Nanotechnology for Materials, Electronics, and Circuits
EE-549.description: Nanotechnology for advanced nanomaterials, nanoelectronics devices, and circuits, including the rigorous treatment of electronic band structures of carbon nanotubes, graphene, and two-dimensional materials.

EE-557.title: Computer Systems Architecture
EE-557.description: Computer architecture from a design perspective: Pipelined processors, speculative execution, VLIW, vector processors, GPU/GPGPU, memory technology and systems, interconnection networks, shared-memory and message-passing multiprocessors, chip multiprocessors.

EE-559.title: Machine Learning I: Supervised Methods
EE-559.description: Distribution-free and probabilistic methods for supervised classification and regression; learning algorithms; optimization techniques; feature-space transformations; parametric and nonparametric methods; Bayes decision theory; artificial neural networks.
EE-559.prereqText:
Corequisite: EE 503; EE 510
Recommended preparation: knowledge of Python at the level of EE 541 (A Computational Introduction to Deep Learning); knowledge of multivariate calculus.

EE-561.title: Foundations of Artificial Intelligence
EE-561.description: Foundations of symbolic intelligent systems, search, logic, knowledge representation, planning, learning.

EE-562.title: Random Processes in Engineering
EE-562.description: Probability Axioms. Random vectors and processes, their convergence and limit theorems. Stationary processes, Markov chains, Martingales, Gaussian processes. Basic calculus of random processes. Wiener filtering.
EE-562.prereqText:
Prerequisite: EE 503; EE 441 or EE 510
Duplicates credit: former EE 562a

EE-563.title: Inference and Estimation: Theory and Algorithms
EE-563.description: Bayesian and non-Bayesian hypothesis testing and estimation, sufficient statistics, exponential families, expectation-maximization, approximations, Kalman filtering and smoothing, recursive Bayesian tracking.

EE-569.title: Introduction to Digital Image Processing
EE-569.description: Image sampling, 2-D image transform, image enhancement, geometric image modification, morphologic processing, edge detection, texture analysis, image filtering and restoration.

EE-570A.title: Advanced Electromagnetic Theory
EE-570A.description: Classical electromagnetic field theory and its usage in understanding and analytically modelling advanced applied electrical engineering devices.

EE-576.title: Integrated Memory Devices and Technologies
EE-576.description: Fundamental device physics, integration technology and cutting-edge innovations in integrated microelectronic memory devices and systems, and their applications in data storage and emerging beyond-von-Neumann computing.
EE-576.prereqText: Recommended preparation: Understanding of basic semiconductor device physics and fabrication technology is useful, but not required

EE-577A.title: VLSI System Design
EE-577A.description: MOS logic; system design; memory design; datapath subsystem design; circuit simulation; basic device physics; simple device layout: structured chip design; timing; project chip; silicon compilers.

EE-577B.title: VLSI System Design
EE-577B.description: Semi-custom ASIC VLSI design flow; RTL coding, logic synthesis, automatic placement & routing, memory and interface design, signal integrity solutions, hardware acceleration and approximation

EE-587.title: Nonlinear Control Systems
EE-587.description: State-space Models. Equilibrium points. Limit Cycles. Linearization. Nonlinear Phenomena. Lyapunov Stability. Analysis and Design of Nonlinear Systems. Passivity. Backstepping. Feedback and Input-Output Linearization.
EE-587.prereqText:
Recommended preparation: EE 585
Duplicates credit: AME 552

EE-590.description: Research leading to the master's degree. Maximum units which may be applied to the degree to be determined by the department. Graded CR/NC.

EE-597.description: Introduction to wireless networking technologies; fundamental architectural and design principles used at all protocol layers; optimization, performance evaluation and implementation using mathematical analysis, simulations, and experiments.

Recommended preparation: EE 467 or equivalent; familiarity with Matlab and C programming

EE-607.title: Microelectromechanical Systems
EE-607.description: Exploration of the technology methods and physical principles of MEMS, and survey various MEMS of current interest.
EE-607.prereqText: Recommended preparation: Knowledge of microfabrication, electromagnetic fields and waves, and mechanics

EE-613.title: Quantum Optimization Algorithms
EE-613.description: Introduction to quantum computing; analysis of quantum algorithms; matrix manipulation, gradient computation and optimization.
EE-613.prereqText:
Recommended preparation: Linear algebra on the level of MATH 471, mathematical optimization on the level of ISE 630 or ISE 631. Prior knowledge of quantum mechanics is not assumed.
Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student, Master Student

EE-626.title: Survey of Energy and Power for a Sustainable Future
EE-626.description: Power production includes conventional fossil fuels, synthetic fuels, hydroelectric, solar, wind, geothermal, biomass and nuclear. The environmental consequences of various energy sources are discussed.
EE-626.prereqText:
Recommended preparation: Graduate standing in Engineering, Physics, or Chemistry
Duplicates credit: CHE 510

EE-631.title: Mixed-Signal Integrated Circuits
EE-631.description: Fundamentals of sampling and discrete-time signals; analog to digital converters; digital to analog converters; switched-capacitor circuits.

EE-632A.title: Integrated Communication Systems
EE-632A.description: System- and transistor-level analysis and design of integrated circuits for wireless communications. Wireless communication concepts; radiofrequency transceiver architectures; low-noise amplifiers; mixers; oscillators; power amplifiers.
EE-632A.prereqText:
Prerequisite: EE 536A
Duplicates credit: former EE 632

EE-658.title: Diagnosis and Design of Reliable Digital Systems
EE-658.description: Fault models; test generation; fault simulation; self-checking and self-testing circuits; design for testability; fault tolerant design techniques; case studies; search techniques; memory testing.

EE-690.title: Directed Research
EE-690.description: Laboratory study of specific problems by candidates for the degree Engineer in Electrical Engineering. Graded CR/NC.

EIS-103.description: Analyze misinformation and disinformation on digital platforms using library research methodologies and applying information literacy principles. Examine how technology creates and disseminates information in society.

EIS-370.title: Ethical Issues in Artificial Intelligence
EIS-370.description: Ethical issues in artificial intelligence including algorithmic bias and interpretability, data privacy and control, autonomous systems and relationships with AI entities.

EIS-499.title: Special Topics

EIS-503.description: Academic and professional presentation skills for PhD students. Preparation for qualifying exams, conference paper presentations and other forms of oral communication. Use of visual aids and poster displays included. Graded CR/NC. Not available for degree credit to master's students.

EM-500.title: Principles of Emergency Management
EM-500.description: Explores the historical development of emergency management as a distinct discipline in the United States and abroad, including theories, terminology and international coordination.

Class standing: open only to Master Student
Major: open only to Emergency Management
School: open only to BOV

EM-505.title: Emergency Management Policies and Regulations
EM-505.description: Examines policies, regulations, politics and budgets that impact emergency management domestically and internationally in the government, non-profit and private sectors.

Major: open only to Emergency Management

EM-510.title: Social and Cultural Competency in Emergency Management
EM-510.description: Explores how emergency management practices and community interactions can help address social, economic and cultural inequities while building increased resilience.

EM-515.description: Examines the administrative functions of an emergency manager, including project management, policy implementation, acquisition of funding and managing diverse teams.

Major: open only to Emergency Management

EM-520.title: Critical Decision-Making in Emergency Management
EM-520.description: Explores how to manage and assess information to limit risk and make ethical, critical decisions under both steady-state and crisis situations.

Major: open only to Emergency Management

EM-525.title: Emergency Management and Disaster Planning
EM-525.description: Examines the necessary components of deliberate and crisis action plans that are used to prepare for, respond to, and recover from disasters.
EM-525.prereqText:

School: open only to BOV

EM-530.title: Operational Coordination in Emergency Management
EM-530.description: Focuses on the complexity of post-disaster immediate and long-term response and recovery challenges in local, state, federal and international jurisdictions.
EM-530.prereqText:

EM-535.title: Critical Infrastructure in Emergency Management
EM-535.description: Examines the wide spectrum of security threats to critical infrastructure and how to strengthen infrastructure protection and resilience through collaborative partnerships across sectors.
EM-535.prereqText:
Class standing: open only to Master Student
Major: open only to Emergency Management
School: open only to BOV

EM-550.title: Resilience in Emergency Management
EM-550.description: Examines resilience in emergency management as it pertains to areas such as planning, mitigation, disaster logistics and supply chains.

ENE-200.title: Environmental Engineering Principles
ENE-200.description: Analysis of water, air and land pollution, including hazardous waste; engineering of mitigation measures; water and wastewater treatment systems.
ENE-200.prereqText:
Prerequisite: CHEM 105A or CHEM 115A; MATH 126 or MATH 129; PHYS 151 or PHYS 161
Recommended preparation: CE 110

ENE-300.title: Contaminant Transport in the Environment
ENE-300.description: Fundamentals of the physical mechanisms controlling solute transport in environmental flows.
ENE-300.prereqText: Recommended preparation: Knowledge of environmental engineering principles on the level of ENE 200

ENE-426.title: Particulate Air Pollutants: Properties/Behavior/Measurement
ENE-426.description: Particulate air pollutants, their measurement and instrumentation methods and their effects on the environment and human health; optical properties and visibility degradation.
ENE-426.prereqText:
Prerequisite: ENE 200
Duplicates credit: former ENE 526

ENE-428.title: Air Pollution Fundamentals
ENE-428.description: Quantitative overview of air pollution and the physical and chemical processes that describe its behavior.
ENE-428.prereqText:
Prerequisite: MATH 245; PHYS 151; CHEM 105A or CHEM 115A
Recommended preparation: Environmental engineering principles on the level of ENE 200

ENE-465.title: Water Supply and Sewerage System Design
ENE-465.description: Design of water supply systems, storm drains, sanitary sewers, and lift stations.

ENE-512.title: Environmental Fluid Mechanics
ENE-512.description: Application of the fundamentals on the physical laws governing fluid flow and analyzing transport of contaminant in the environment and the risks involved.
ENE-512.prereqText: Recommended preparation: Undergraduate fluid mechanics on the level of CE 309 or AME 309.

ENE-523.title: Physiochemical Processes in Environmental Engineering
ENE-523.description: Concepts and applications of physicochemical processes in engineered systems, including coagulation, sedimentation, filtration, adsorption and membrane processes.
ENE-523.prereqText:
Prerequisite: CE 453
Recommended preparation: CE 363 and CE 485

ENE-562.title: Aquatic Chemistry
ENE-562.description: Quantitative prediction of chemical speciation in aquatic systems, including acid-base chemistry, precipitation/dissolution, complexation, oxidation/reduction and phase partitioning of organics. Applications to water treatment.
ENE-562.prereqText: Recommended preparation: General chemistry (CHEM 105aLg and CHEM 105bL); differential and integral calculus (MATH 125 and MATH 129); linear algebra (MATH 245); basic mechanics and conservation of energy (PHYS 151).
