ENGL-105.title: Creative Writing for Non-Majors
ENGL-105.description: Introductory workshop in writing poetry, short fiction and nonfiction for love of the written and spoken word. Not for English major credit. Not for English major or English (Creative Writing) major credit.

ENGL-172.title: The Art of Poetry
ENGL-172.description: Introduction to the pleasures and power of poetry, exploring elements drawn from high-points of English poetry, and the lives and works of major poets. (Duplicates credit in ARLT 101g)

ENGL-174.title: Reading the Heart: Emotional Intelligence and the Humanities
ENGL-174.description: A study of emotional intelligence through literature, history and the arts with a focus on anger, happiness, love and empathy.

ENGL-230.title: Shakespeare and His Times
ENGL-230.description: Close study of Shakespeare's plays and poems to introduce his language, stagecraft, literary "genius," social and literary contexts, precursors and rivals, and legacy.

ENGL-240.title: Literary Arts
ENGL-240.description: Introduction to theory and practice of literary study.

ENGL-250.title: The African Diaspora
ENGL-250.description: History, political-economy and aesthetics of the African Diaspora with emphasis on Latin America, the Caribbean, Europe and Africa.

ENGL-261.title: English Literature to 1800
ENGL-261.description: Intensive reading of major writers to 1800.

ENGL-270.title: Studying Narrative
ENGL-270.description: Introduction to major forms, styles and theories of narrative, with attention to characterization, plot, genres, ethics, empathy, perspective, audience and social conditions.

ENGL-280.title: Introduction to Narrative Medicine
ENGL-280.description: Study of literary modes of narrative and their uses in medical understanding, character formation, social identity, and relations between mind and body.

ENGL-297.title: Introduction to the Genre of Nonfiction
ENGL-297.description: Study of forms of nonfiction writing, focusing on craft and process: how it works and how to read, write and write about it.

ENGL-300.title: The Art and Craft of the Essay
ENGL-300.description: Intensive practice in crafting literary essays.

ENGL-302.title: Writing Narrative
ENGL-302.description: Introduction to the techniques and practice of writing narrative in fiction and literary non-fiction

ENGL-303.title: Introduction to Fiction Writing
ENGL-303.description: Introduction to the techniques and practice of writing prose fiction.

ENGL-304.title: Introduction to Poetry Writing
ENGL-304.description: Introduction to the techniques and practice of writing poetry.

ENGL-325.title: Pre-Modern Wonders: Magic, Monsters and Marvels
ENGL-325.description: A study of literature and literary theory through the themes and theories of wonder, magic and the uncanny in English literature before 1800.

ENGL-344.title: Sexual/Textual Diversity
ENGL-344.description: Questions of gay and lesbian identity, expression and experience in a variety of literary and cultural forms; emphasis on sexual politics, equality and difference.

ENGL-350.title: Literature of California
ENGL-350.description: Novels, stories, essays, poems, and plays written in and about California from the Gold Rush to the present.

ENGL-352.title: Bookpacking
ENGL-352.description: Literary travel using novels to explore regional culture and unify the study of literature, history, geography, politics and social studies.

ENGL-360.title: Modern Poetry
ENGL-360.description: Study of poetry written in English from 1900 to 1945, with special emphasis on American modernists of the first two decades.
ENGL-360.prereqText:
Recommended preparation: ENGL 262, ENGL 263
Duplicates credit: former ENGL 452

ENGL-361.title: Contemporary Prose
ENGL-361.description: Study of prose written in English since 1945, principally fiction of the past two decades.

ENGL-362.title: Contemporary Poetry
ENGL-362.description: Study of poetry written in English since 1945, with special emphasis on the last two decades.

ENGL-371.title: Literary Genres and Film
ENGL-371.description: Literary studies in the relationship between fiction and drama and their adaptation as films.

ENGL-373.title: Literature and Society
ENGL-373.description: Theoretical and applied studies of literature in English as social activity and cultural production; its expression of, and influence upon, social values, concepts, and behavior.

ENGL-375.title: Science Fiction
ENGL-375.description: Investigation of the scope and possibilities of British and American science fiction as a genre, with some attention to its historical development.

ENGL-405.title: Fiction Writing
ENGL-405.description: A practical course in composition of prose fiction.

ENGL-406.title: Poetry Writing
ENGL-406.description: A practical course in poetry writing.

ENGL-407.title: Advanced Fiction Writing
ENGL-407.description: Prerequisite: English 405 and/or consent of instructor.

ENGL-408.title: Advanced Poetry Writing
ENGL-408.description: Prerequisite: Acceptance of manuscript by instructor.

ENGL-424.title: English Literature of the Romantic Age (1800-1832)
ENGL-424.description: Selected studies of major writers, including Blake, Austen, Wordsworth, Coleridge, Byron, Mary Shelley, P.B. Shelley, and Keats.

ENGL-430.title: Shakespeare
ENGL-430.description: Major history plays, comedies, and tragedies.

ENGL-449.title: Asian American Literature
ENGL-449.description: Survey of Asian American literature from the earliest time to the present; development of prose, poetry, and novel.

ENGL-490.title: Directed Research
ENGL-490.description: Individual research and readings. Not available for graduate credit.
ENGL-490.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Junior, Senior

ENGL-491.title: Senior Seminar in Literary Studies
ENGL-491.description: Selected problems in literary history and criticism.

ENGL-492.title: Narrative Studies Capstone Seminar
ENGL-492.description: Individual research, reading, writing and project development as a senior capstone experience in the study of narrative.
ENGL-492.prereqText:
Class standing: open only to Senior
Major: open only to Narrative Studies

ENGL-496.title: Senior Honors Thesis
ENGL-496.description: Seminar in workshop form to accompany completion of Senior HonorsThesis. Bi-weekly meetings to complete thesis according to contract.

ENGL-499.title: Special Topics
ENGL-499.description: Studies in the works of one or more authors, or in the development of a theme or genre.

ENGL-520.title: Renaissance English Literatures and Cultures
ENGL-520.description: Studies in poetry and patronage, the popular tradition in literature and drama, the social and sexual dynamics of comedy, historical and cultural uses of genres, among other topics.

ENGL-563.title: Poetry and Prose into Drama
ENGL-563.description: Plays for the stage shall be written using public-domain poetry and prose as inspiration and source material, complemented with exploring poetry, prose, and varied dramas as context for the student writer. Students should be well-versed in literature, and have written in one or more genres.
ENGL-563.prereqText: Recommended preparation: reading poetry and novels

ENGL-602.title: Writers in the World: Text and Context
ENGL-602.description: Editing and publishing within the tradition of literary and cultural influences upon a wide range of authors, readers and genres.

ENGL-606B.title: The Literary Landscape: Digital Toolkit
ENGL-606B.description: Research and identification of internships; preparation of application materials for submission to in-person and remote internship opportunities.
ENGL-606B.prereqText:

Concurrent enrollment: ENGL 602

FBE-596.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student, Master Student

FBE-621.title: Research Forum
FBE-621.description: Seminar. Review and discuss current research in Finance and Business Economics. Presentations by faculty, visiting researchers, and advanced students. Open only to Marshall PhD students.
FBE-621.prereqText:
Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student
Major: open only to Business Administration

FBE-630.title: Fundamentals of Corporate Finance
FBE-630.description: Core theory and empirical evidence in corporate finance.
FBE-630.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student

FBE-633.title: Fundamentals of Asset Pricing
FBE-633.description: Financial Economics course that focuses on core theory and empirical evidence in asset pricing.
FBE-633.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student

FBE-670.title: Selected Topics in Finance Research
FBE-670.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student

FDN-430.title: Materiality and Construction
FDN-430.description: Exploration of textiles and materials in the creation of garments and other forms of wearable designs.

FDN-513.title: Visiting Fashion Speaker Series
FDN-513.description: The professional practices of fashion design featuring formal presentations by visiting fashion designers, artists and professionals.

FDN-520.title: Individual Studies
FDN-520.description: Investigation of creative problems through various fashion media.

FREN-012.title: French 120 Language Practicum
FREN-012.description: English grammar as it relates to French in order to improve students' French language skills; explicit pronunciation and intonation practice. Requires concurrent enrollment in either FREN 120 French I or MPVA 261 French Language and Diction.

FREN-015.title: French 150 Language Practicum
FREN-015.description: English grammar as it relates to French in order to improve students French language skills; explicit pronunciation and intonation practice.

FREN-120.title: French I
FREN-120.description: Introduction to current French. Oral practice, listening and reading comprehension; grammar necessary for simple spoken and written expression.

FREN-175.title: Accelerated French for Speakers of Spanish and   Other Romance Languages
FREN-175.description: Accelerated introduction to written and spoken French for students with a high level of proficiency in Spanish or another Romance Language. Students completing this course may enroll in the third semester of the basic language sequence FREN 220.
FREN-175.prereqText: Prerequisite: ITAL 220 or PORT 220 or SPAN 220

FREN-220.title: French III
FREN-220.description: Continuation of FREN 150. Review of structural patterns of French; selected cultural and literary readings; conversation and composition.

FREN-235.title: Intermediate Conversational French
FREN-235.description: Designed for non-majors/minors interested in maintaining and developing French language competency. Builds vocabulary, ease of communication, and cultural knowledge through discussion of contemporary topics. Graded Credit/No Credit. Not available for credit to French majors. Not open to French majors.
FREN-235.prereqText:
Prerequisite: FREN 202 or FREN 220
Major: not open to French

FREN-250.title: French IV
FREN-250.description: Introduction to French literature through the study of texts and audiovisuals organized around a central theme; develops close-reading techniques and discursive skills; reviews French grammar.

FREN-275.title: Plants, Animals and other Non-Humans
FREN-275.description: Exploration of phenomena such as climate change, predators and viruses, using ecological and interspecies perspectives provided by French philosophers, ecofeminists and thinkers in science and technology studies.

FREN-300.title: French Grammar and Composition
FREN-300.description: Grammatical structure and vocabulary building with practical application to written composition. Prerequisites: FREN 250.

FREN-320.title: The French New Wave and its Legacy
FREN-320.description: Film-making in France from the earliest experiments to current trends. Emphasis on the political, social, historical context of French films. Taught in English. Reading knowledge of French recommended.

FREN-330.title: Critical Writing in French
FREN-330.description: Advanced composition through critical reading of literary texts; comprehensive analysis of difficult grammatical structures and stylistics. Prerequisite: FREN 300.

FREN-347.title: Race, Gender and Power in Francophone Literature
FREN-347.description: Study of post-colonialism as a ferment for literary creation in the literature of French expression from Africa, the Caribbean and Canada. Conducted in French.

FREN-370.title: Equality and Difference around the Enlightenment
FREN-370.description: 18th- and 20th-century debates around the idea of equality and the notion of difference. Relevance of the Enlightenment to contemporary discussions of identity, citizenship, and human rights. Conducted in English.

FREN-375.title: Global Narratives of Illness and Disability
FREN-375.description: Study of difference as represented through French, Francophone and related narratives of disability and illness, with attention to race and gender. Conducted in English.

FREN-402.title: Modernity and Modernism
FREN-402.description: Study and analysis of representative works and major intellectual, cultural, and artistic trends from the modern period (post-1789).

FREN-440.title: Reading in Real Time: Experiencing the French Literary Scene
FREN-440.description: Exploration and experience of the workings of the literary and artistic production in France and Francophone countries in the 21st century.

FREN-490.title: Directed Research
FREN-490.description: Individual research and readings. Not available for graduate credit.
FREN-490.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Junior, Senior

FREN-503.title: Modernities
FREN-503.description: An intellectual genealogy of French modernity and modernism through the examination of canonical literary texts and theories.

FREN-590.title: Directed Research
FREN-590.description: Research leading to the master's degree. Maximum units which may be applied to the degree to be determined by the department. Graded CR/NC.

FSEM-100.title: Freshman Seminar
FSEM-100.description: A seven-to-eleven week course offered for incoming freshmen; limited to 18 students. Graded CR/NC. A combined maximum of 4 units of FSEM 100 and FSEM 101 may be applied to the degree.
FSEM-100.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Freshman

GDEN-712C.title: Capstone Research Project for GDEN Students
GDEN-712C.description: Production and defense of a research plan that demonstrates significant understanding of a topic in geriatric dentistry.

GDEN-725.title: Epidemiology, Nutrition and Aging for Dental Residents
GDEN-725.description: Seminars on the various mucosal, cutaneous, gingival and salivary diseases and lesions in the oral and maxillofacial region.

GEOL-107.title: Oceanography
GEOL-107.description: Physical, chemical, and geological character of the oceans andocean basins. Origin of the oceans. Ocean processes and agents.Economic value of the oceans. Lecture, 3 hours; laboratory, 2 hours. One all-day field trip required.

GEOL-108.title: Natural Disasters and Their Global Impact
GEOL-108.description: The science behind natural disasters and their impacts on society, focusing on earthquakes, tsunamis, volcanic eruptions, landslides, floods, hurricanes, tornadoes and wildfires, often through Southern California-based examples.

GEOL-126.title: The History of Life on Earth: A View from the Museum
GEOL-126.description: Topically-driven exploration of evolution, environmental change, and the history of life on Earth via the fossil record with the Natural History Museum of Los Angeles as a laboratory. How the changing Earth and life co-evolved through time.

GEOL-150.title: Climate Change
GEOL-150.description: Exploration of factors that influence climate and the scientific basis for concern about rising greenhouse gases, the threat to human society know as global warming.

GEOL-241.title: Energy Systems
GEOL-241.description: Energy resources from a global perspective, including fossil fuels, nuclear, and renewable energy.

GEOL-290.title: Special Laboratory
GEOL-290.description: Laboratory component for GEOL 105Lg, 107Lxg, 108Lg, 125Lxg, 130Lxg, 150Lxg, or 240Lxg for students with equivalent lecture credit from another institution.

GEOL-316.title: Igneous and Metamorphic Petrology
GEOL-316.description: The dynamic processes which produce igneous and metamorphic rocks; descriptions/analyses of the rock mineralogies, textures and chemistries used to quantify these processes.

GEOL-321.title: Structural Geology and Tectonics
GEOL-321.description: Field and theorectical aspects of rock deformation, analysis of structural systems, and stress and strain; orogenic belts and plate tectonics; introduction to field techniques and construction of geologic maps. Recommended preparation: GEOL 320L

GEOL-387A.title: Undergraduate Team Research
GEOL-387A.description: Introduction to scientific inquiry, field research opportunities, and history of physical sciences; strategies, research methodologies, and writing skills for proposals, abstracts, papers, and professional development. Duplicates credit in the former GEOL-385. Recommended preparation: A GE course in Earth Science.

GEOL-412.title: Oceans, Climate, and the Environment
GEOL-412.description: A comprehensive survey of climate, including ocean, atmospheric and continental environments with a California sustainability focus. Methods in climate, oceanography and paleoclimate and independent research.
GEOL-412.prereqText:
Recommended preparation: GEOL 107Lg or GEOL 150Lg or GEOL 160Lg
Class standing: not open to Freshman

GEOL-427.title: The Global Environment
GEOL-427.description: Earth's development as a habitable planet, from origin to human impacts on global biogeochemical cycles in the ocean, land, atmosphere. Discussion of environmental alternatives.
GEOL-427.prereqText:
Prerequisite: BISC 103 or BISC 120 or BISC 121; CHEM 103 or CHEM 105B or CHEM 108 or CHEM 115B
Major: open only to Biological Sciences, Environmental Science and Health, Environmental Studies, Geological Sciences

GEOL-465.title: Field Geology
GEOL-465.description: GEOL 465 Field Geology (4, SmSp)Ten days to four weeks of field study in an area of geological complexity, with preparatory instruction.

GEOL-483.title: Geobiology and Astrobiology
GEOL-483.description: Relationships between microbiota and the earth environment including the hydrosphere, lithosphere and atmosphere, with consideration of the potential for life on other planets.
GEOL-483.prereqText: Prerequisite: BISC 120 or BISC 121; CHEM 105B or CHEM 108

GEOL-490.title: Directed Research
GEOL-490.description: Individual research and readings. Not available for graduate credit.
GEOL-490.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Junior, Senior

GEOL-491.title: Earth Sciences Internship
GEOL-491.description: Local, national, and international internships providing earth sciences experience in a professional setting. Not available for graduate credit. Department permission required.

GEOL-494.title: Senior Thesis
GEOL-494.description: Writing of a thesis under individual faculty supervision. Not available for graduate credit.

GEOL-553.title: Physics of Earthquakes
GEOL-553.description: Basic physics of earthquakes and seismicity. Continuum elasticity; fracture mechanics; laboratory friction; damage rheology; physics of critical phenomena; spatio-temporal seismicity patterns; analysis of complex data sets. Recommended preparation: GEOL 537 and/or GEOL 551

GEOL-556.title: Active Tectonics
GEOL-556.description: Aspects of deformation and associated seismicity at active plate margins around the world. Includes review of plate tectonics, seismology, geodesy, paleomagnetism, geodynamics, Quaternary dating techniques, tectonic geomorphology, paleoseismology, and seismic hazard assessment. Two weekend field trips required. Recommended preparation: GEOL 530, GEOL 531

GEOL-590.title: Directed Research
GEOL-590.description: Research leading to the master's degree. Maximum units which may be applied to the degree to be determined by the department. Graded CR/NC.

GEOL-599.description: Special topics in the geological sciences. Field trip required when appropriate to the topic.

GEOL-600.title: Earth Sciences Colloquium
GEOL-600.description: Exploration of prominent topics at the frontiers of research in the geosciences, through weekly talks presented by leading researchers in the field. Specific topics vary by semester.

GEOL-601.title: Seminar in Sedimentary Geology
GEOL-601.description: Analysis and discussion of current topics in sedimentary geology; topics will be chosen by students and faculty to focus on areas of recent advances.

GERM-101.title: German I
GERM-101.description: Introduction to modern German. Oral practice, listening and reading comprehension. Basic structures necessary for simple spoken and written expression.

GERM-102.title: German II
GERM-102.description: Continuation of German I. Introduction to German culture. Prerequisite: 101.

GERM-201.title: German III, Conversation and Composition
GERM-201.description: Intermediate German. Increasing emphasis on listening and speaking skills and a review of basic structures of German. Discussion of cultural aspects. Prerequisite: 101 and 102.

GERM-221.title: Conversational German IV
GERM-221.description: Conversational German in a variety of topical settings and vocabulary domains. Prerequisite: 3rd semester German or equivalent.

GERO-200.title: Gerontology: The Science of Adult Development
GERO-200.description: Introduction to adult development through the lifespan; biological, psychological, and social processes; gerontology as a career for the future.

GERO-310.title: Physiology of Aging
GERO-310.description: Effects of normative aging processes on homeostatic mechanisms and how these changes relate to development of disorder and disease in later life.

GERO-315.title: A Journey into the Mind
GERO-315.description: Introduction to the brain and mind. A unique multimedia approach to stress how knowledge about the mind is gained from scientific and clinical investigations.

GERO-320.title: Psychology of Adult Development
GERO-320.description: How psychologists study thinking, memory, emotions, personality, and behavior, and how people change in these throughout adulthood to old age.

GERO-321.title: Introduction to Psychology and Aging
GERO-321.description: An introduction to the core curriculum in the study of Gerontology. Research perspectives on adult development and aging; methodological issues; personality and relationship issues; general mental and emotional components of aging; research methods.

GERO-340.title: Policy, Values, and Power in an Aging Society
GERO-340.description: How Americans' political values affect public policy. Studies of landmark legislation to explore the social contract between generations and role of governments in social welfare.

GERO-380.title: Diversity in Aging
GERO-380.description: Exploring diversity in the older population and variability in the human aging process.

GERO-411.title: Physiology, Nutrition, and Aging
GERO-411.description: Explores nutritional needs and the physiological, psychological, and sociological relationships to nutrition. Laboratory experiments in assessment and evaluation.

GERO-412.title: Exercise and Aging: Principles and Programs
GERO-412.description: Physiological, psychological, and sociological aspects of exercise. Laboratory involvement in assessment and evaluation of fitness.

GERO-414.title: Neurobiology of Aging
GERO-414.description: Age-related changes in nervous system structure and function; relationship of brain changes to changes in cognitive function and perception; Alzheimer's and Parkinson's diseases.

GERO-415.title: Neuroaffective Disorders of Aging
GERO-415.description: Methods of studying, evaluating, and treating cognitive, psychiatric, and behavioral problems associated with medical conditions of old age.

GERO-416.title: Health Issues in Adulthood
GERO-416.description: Physiological, psychological, and social health problems of adults as they are impacted by health choices throughout life.

GERO-418.title: Aging Brain Interventions
GERO-418.description: Design and write up a proposal for a behavioral intervention with older adults that examines the effects of the intervention on the aging brain.
GERO-418.prereqText: Prerequisite: GERO 315 or GERO 414 or BISC 408 or BISC 424 or BISC 421

GERO-435.title: Women and Aging: Psychological, Social, and      Political Implications
GERO-435.description: Problems and resources of the middle-aged and older woman in a changing society; including discrimination, stereotypes, employment, social interaction, etc.

GERO-437.title: Social and Psychological Aspects of Death and Dying
GERO-437.description: Introduction and critical survey of the current issues, concepts, and research of the social and psychological aspects of death and dying.

GERO-440.title: Biodemography of Aging
GERO-440.description: Consideration of the biological and social-cultural factors that govern the evolution of life spans and the life of humans and selected animal models

GERO-452.title: Economic Issues and the Aged
GERO-452.description: Analysis of economic factors associated with the aged; implications for individuals, society, and the economy; life-cycle economics, retirement, income maintenance, and social security.

GERO-461.title: Seminar in Molecular and Computational Biology
GERO-461.description: Topical seminar in molecular and computational biology. Junior, senior or graduate standing.
GERO-461.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student, Master Student, Junior, Senior

GERO-484.title: Food History, Culture and Society
GERO-484.description: Examines historical, cultural, economic, social and wellness roles of food in society and introduces dietary practices that support healthy aging and longevity.

GERO-489.title: Finding the Key to a Long, Happy Life in the     Worlds Blue Zones
GERO-489.description: Immersion into lifestyles shown to improve quality of life and extend lifespan by studying populations in "Blue Zone" communities throughout the world.

GERO-490.title: Directed Research
GERO-490.description: Individual research and readings. Not available for graduate credit.
GERO-490.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Junior, Senior

GERO-491.title: Practicum
GERO-491.description: Supervised experience in one or more community agencies. Graded CR/NC.

GERO-492.title: Senior Seminar
GERO-492.description: An in-depth integration of major research and professional themes in the study of human development and aging.

GERO-493.title: Longevity and Death among Ancient and Modern European Popula
GERO-493.description: The discoveries of ancient humans and bodies that have been preserved illuminate the connection between diet, health and disease.

GERO-495.title: Practicum in Geriatric Care
GERO-495.description: Supervised experience in a geriatric health care setting which allows students to put theories and ideas into practive. Graded CR/NC. Lecture, discussion, and fieldwork.

GERO-497A.title: Honors Seminar
GERO-497A.description: Advanced study of empirical approaches in gerontology. Preparation, progress, presentation, and evaluation of Senior Honors Thesis research. Standing in Gerontology Honors Program and departmental approval.

GERO-497B.title: Honors Seminar
GERO-497B.description: Advanced study of empirical approaches in gerontology. Preparation, progress, presentation, and evaluation of Senior Honors Thesis research. Standing in Gerontology Honors Program and departmental approval.
GERO-497B.prereqText:
Prerequisite: GERO 497A
Major: open only to Gerontology

GERO-497C.title: Honors Seminar
GERO-497C.description: Advanced study of empirical approaches in gerontology. Preparation, progress, presentation, and evaluation of Senior Honors Thesis research. Standing in Gerontology Honors Program and departmental approval.
GERO-497C.prereqText:
Prerequisite: GERO 497B
Major: open only to Gerontology

GERO-498.title: Nutrition, Genes, Longevity and Diseases
GERO-498.description: Examines role of nutrition and genes and the impact each has on longevity and diseases, particularly diseases related to aging.Offered in Genoa, Italy.

GERO-499.title: Special Topics
GERO-499.description: Examination of special topics in the area of gerontology.

GERO-500.title: Perspectives on a Changing Society: An Introduction to Aging
GERO-500.description: A web based course analyzing physical, mental, and social age-related changes as well as implications of population aging trends for individuals and society.

GERO-502.title: Marketing and Shifts in Consumer Decision Making
GERO-502.description: Branding, marketing, and consumer behavior through examination of established, transitioning and emerging aging services and organizations.

GERO-504.title: Current Issues in Aging Services Management
GERO-504.description: Basic skills needed for an executive working in an aging services environment. Recommended for entry level administrators and managers.

GERO-505.title: Housing and Community Policies and Programs
GERO-505.description: Examination of the behavioral and social consequences of design and the environment to create a more satisfying physical environment for both frail and active older adults.

GERO-506.title: Technological Innovations in Aging (Gerontechnology)
GERO-506.description: Reflections on shifts in preferences for aging in place and the market ramifications of innovations in science and technology on older consumers and service provider.

GERO-508.title: The Mind and Body Connection through the Lifespan
GERO-508.description: An introduction to mind-body processes involved in healthy aging. Examines the interplay of emotions, beliefs, and behaviors in shaping health-relevant biological processes.

GERO-510.title: Physiology of Development and Aging
GERO-510.description: Examination of lifespan physiology of human development, growth, and aging; major emphasis in the physiology of the later years and implications for health maintenance.

GERO-516.title: Introduction to Genomic Science for Biologists
GERO-516.description: Broad introduction to genomics for students with a biology background, including overviews of 'wet' genomics techniques, available public databases and useful analytical tools.

GERO-517.title: Advanced Therapeutic Nutrition
GERO-517.description: Application of nutrition science, physiology, biochemistry, and metabolism to evaluate critically ill patients and plan nutrition intervention and monitoring. Open only to graduate students.
GERO-517.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student, Graduate Visitor, Master Student

GERO-520.title: Life Span Developmental Psychology
GERO-520.description: Behavior from adulthood to old age; study of major components of behavior such as perception, cognitive processes, personality, intergenerational relationships, sexuality, and life styles.

GERO-530.title: Life Span Developmental Sociology
GERO-530.description: Life-span perspective on the sociological theories of marriage and the family, intergenerational relationships, work and retirement, and other forms of social organization.

GERO-540.title: Social Policy and Aging
GERO-540.description: Major legislation and programs; examination and analysis of policy-making and political processes affecting development and implementation of programs for older persons.

GERO-550.title: Administration and System Management in Programs for Older Adults
GERO-550.description: Application of theories of administration and system management to public and volunteer programs and services for older adults including residential institutions and community programs.

GERO-551.title: Applied Policy Skills in Aging
GERO-551.description: An overview and application of techniques and approaches used in the definition and analysis of policy problems in aging.

GERO-552.title: Human Resources and Aging
GERO-552.description: Addresses legal issues and liability arising out of the employer-employee relationship, and how to identify and act proactively to minimize such risk.
GERO-552.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student, Master Student

GERO-555.title: Integrating Gerontology: A Multidisciplinary Approach
GERO-555.description: Aging (commonalities and distinctions) as addressed by biologists,psychologists, and sociologists. Topics include researchperspectives, normative agings, functional decline and disability,and aging and society.

GERO-560.title: Fundamentals of Nutrition: Micronutrients
GERO-560.description: Explore the role of micronutrients, vitamins, minerals and phytonutrients in human nutrition, including digestion, absorption, metabolism, and major biological, physiological and metabolic roles.
GERO-560.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student, Graduate Visitor, Master Student

GERO-561.title: Introduction to Aging and Normal Changes with Aging
GERO-561.description: Introduces medical and health care professionals to the interdisciplinary field of gerontology. Examines the worlds changing demography; effects of aging on physical, psychological and social changes; aging process, ethical issues, aging stereotypes.

GERO-563.title: Geropsychology
GERO-563.description: Understanding geropsychology and cognition in advanced age; psychosocial theories of aging and psychodynamic models.

GERO-565.title: Novel Technologies in Aging and Assisted Living
GERO-565.description: Focuses on the understanding of technology use with older adults. Examines telemedicine and e-health technologies as well as ethical considerations.

GERO-566.title: Cognitive Decline: Alzheimer's Disease and Dementia and Adva
GERO-566.description: Covers cognitive decline for people with Alzheimers Disease or other forms of dementia. Imaging technology to identify and find treatment options.

GERO-575.title: Marketing Senior Living
GERO-575.description: Current practices in marketing senior living and associated services. Examines behaviors and preferences of older adults and their families. Explores new media platforms.

GERO-577.title: Food Service and Senior Living
GERO-577.description: Addresses the food services components of senior living. Covers pricing, menu design and nutrition.

GERO-579.title: Branding Senior Living
GERO-579.description: Marketing models aimed to provide services for senior living. Analyze various institutions models for marketing, communicating and technological influence to brand a facility.

GERO-587.title: Interprofessional Education and Collaboration for Geriatrics
GERO-587.description: Students from multiple health professions learn about aging and collaborative team care through a combination of didactic and experiential learning working in a community-based setting.
GERO-587.prereqText: School: open only to Ostrow School of Dentistry, Leonard Davis School of Gerontology, Dana and David Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences, Keck School of Medicine, Suzanne Dworak-Peck School of Social Work

GERO-589.title: Case Studies in Leadership and Change Management
GERO-589.description: Examination of case studies of issues affecting the aging services industries and the role industry leaders play in reacting to change.

GERO-590.title: Directed Research
GERO-590.description: Research leading to the master's degree. Maximum units which may be applied to the degree to be determined by the department. Graded CR/NC.

GERO-591.title: Field Practicum
GERO-591.description: Supervised experiential learning in one or more organizations that serve older adults; includes a regularly scheduled seminar. Graded CR/NC.

GERO-592.title: Multidisciplinary Research Seminar in Aging
GERO-592.description: Multidisciplinary perspectives on current research in Gerontology including physiology, neurobiology, health and medicine, psychology, sociology and public policy. Topics will change each semester.

GERO-593.title: Research Methods
GERO-593.description: An introduction to research methods and their application to gerontology including problem formation, research design, data collection, descriptive and analytical statistics, interpretation, and report preparation.

GERO-594A.title: Master's Thesis
GERO-594A.description: Credit on acceptance of Thesis. Graded CR/NC.
GERO-594A.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Master Student

GERO-601.title: Molecular Genetics of Aging
GERO-601.description: Explores concepts of molecular and genetic regulation of healthy aging, lifespan, and age-related diseases.

GERO-602B.title: Seminar on Discoveries of Biogerontology
GERO-602B.description: Critical analyses of primary scientific data and interpretations presented in the literature. (Duplicates credit in former GERO 602)

GERO-605.title: Research and Journal Club Presentation Workshop
GERO-605.description: Intensive training in journal club and research talk presentations for graduate students in the Biology of Aging Ph.D. program.

GERO-614.description: Mandatory organized laboratory rotation. Allows students to participate in laboratory activities. Designed to help select dissertation advisor and research.
GERO-614.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student

GERO-620.title: Psychology of Aging
GERO-620.description: Overview of topics in the psychology of aging. Includes research and theory bearing on cognitive, personality, adaptive, and social processes throughout the adult life span. Recommended preparation: Undergraduate coursework in psychology. Open only to doctoral students.
GERO-620.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student

GERO-641.title: Practical Data Science and Stats for Geroscience Research
GERO-641.description: Holistic training in Geroscience including solid bases in statistics, data analysis and data science for reporting reproducible and robust research results.
GERO-641.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student

GESM-110.title: Seminar in the Arts
GESM-110.description: The multifaceted history of the creative act, its analysis, production, and context as a representation of human experience. (Satisfies GE-A, The Arts) Open only to Freshmen. Duplicates credit in GESM 111.
GESM-110.prereqText:
Class standing: open only to Freshman, Sophomore

GESM-111.title: Seminar in the Arts
