INTD-600.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student

INTD-620.title: Medical Students Elective Program
INTD-620.description: Opportunities for Medical students as preceptors, in research laboratories or in field medical services under guidance of sponsors approved by faculty committees. Graded CR/NC.

INTD-622.title: Pre-clinical System Block for Health, Technology and Engineering
INTD-622.description: A three-to-nine week block of lectures and laboratories focused on particular body system (e.g. Cardiovascular, Renal, etc.). Open only to Health, Technology and Engineering students.

INTD-623.title: Interprofessional Education and Collaboration for Geriatrics
INTD-623.description: Students from multiple health professions learn about aging and collaborative team care through a combination of didactic and experiential learning working in a community-based setting.
INTD-623.prereqText: School: open only to Ostrow School of Dentistry, Leonard Davis School of Gerontology, Dana and David Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences, Keck School of Medicine, Suzanne Dworak-Peck School of Social Work

INTD-790.title: Research
INTD-790.description: Research leading to the doctorate. Maximum units which may be applied to the degree to be determined by the department. Open only to doctoral students. Graded CR/NC.
INTD-790.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student

IR-101.title: International Relations
IR-101.description: Basic concepts of world affairs for non-majors. Development ofcompetency to understand and critically evaluate global relationsand international events, stressing empirical approaches. Not available for major credit.

IR-150.title: Environmental Issues in Society
IR-150.description: Exploration of the major social, political, economic, religious, and philosophical disagreements that exist between scholars, leaders, and citizens concerning today's most serious environmental issues and problems. Not available for credit to environmental studies majors and minors.

IR-210.title: International Relations: Introductory Analysis
IR-210.description: Comprehensive introduction to contending theoretical and analytical approaches; development of critical, evaluative, cognitive, and analytical competencies regarding historical and contemporary issues.

IR-211.title: International Relations: Approaches to Research
IR-211.description: Introduction to theoretically oriented research approaches and designs; emphasis on the logic of argumentation.

IR-213.title: The Global Economy
IR-213.description: Economic and political concepts necessary to the understanding of the modern global economy. Topics include international trade, foreign investment and migration.

IR-303.title: Leadership and Diplomacy
IR-303.description: The role of leaders, diplomatic leadership and creativity in statecraft, providing a deep understanding of the theoretical and practical dimensions of diplomacy.

IR-304.title: National Intelligence and the Shaping of Policy
IR-304.description: The focus is intelligence to improve the making of policy, with attention to collection; overt and covert, operations; domestic intelligence; and oversight in democracies.

IR-305.title: Managing New Global Challenges
IR-305.description: Examines the strategies for managing global issues in the post Cold War period. Explores ways that international institutions, national governments and non-state actors work separately and together to provide order and control over complex international issues areas. Issues that will receive attention could include financial and monetary relations, trade and foreign investment, preservation of the environment, the spread of weapons of mass destruction, population and migration, terrori

IR-306.title: International Organizations
IR-306.description: The emergence of international organizations as a permanent feature in world politics; role of the United Nations Organization as well as regional international organizations.

IR-308.title: Economic Globalization
IR-308.description: Globalization makes national borders and regulations increasingly obsolete. Analyzes the economic foundation of globalization, its consequences and efforts to manage it.

IR-310.title: Peace and Conflict Studies
IR-310.description: Interdisciplinary study of the pursuit of peace, including causes of wars, arms races, conflict resolution, peace movements, nonviolent resistance, and peace with justice.

IR-313.title: Religions and Political Violence
IR-313.description: An introduction to debates about the intersection of religion and conflict in politics and international affairs; theoretical, classical, and contemporary issues.

IR-321.title: Civil War, Peace Building and International Intervention
IR-321.description: Examination of the causes of civil war, the dynamics and consequences of civil war and how peace is or is not built.

IR-323.title: Politics of Global Environment
IR-323.description: Examines the politics of managing the global environment. The nature of ecosystems, commons problems, population and resource utilization problems along with biodiversity and global governance are emphasized.

IR-325.title: North-South Relations in the Global Economy
IR-325.description: Analysis of inequality in relations between developed and developing states; contending views on the causes and legacies of imperialism; development strategies and aid.

IR-329.title: The Global Finance and Monetary Regime
IR-329.description: The international financial and monetary regime, its evolution and the problems facing it today

IR-330.title: Politics of the World Economy
IR-330.description: Exploration of questions and concepts in international economics and politics, especially as they relate to flows of trade, capital, people, and problems across borders.

IR-343.title: U.S. Foreign Policy Since World War II
IR-343.description: Analysis of U.S. foreign policy since 1945 as a basis for understanding significant new trends. Explanation of contemporary issues in U.S. relations with other nations.

IR-344.title: The Global South in World Politics
IR-344.description: Origin, concepts, realities and ideals of the non-aligned movement, focusing on the role of the United States in the developing world.

IR-345.title: Russian and Post-Soviet Foreign Policy
IR-345.description: Overview of Tsarist and Soviet experience as background to detailed examination of the political, economic and ideological forces behind contemporary Russian foreign policy.

IR-357.title: Urban Politics in the Global South
IR-357.description: Examination of social and economic justice in the questions of urban governance facing cities in the developing world.

IR-362.title: The International Relations of the Contemporary Middle East
IR-362.description: Introduction to problems and issues in the Middle East today: religio-ethnic rivalries, conflicting nationalisms and ideologies, the Arab-Israeli conflict, Middle East oil.

IR-364.title: The Political Economy of Latin American Development
IR-364.description: The main economic development themes and strategies in Latin America over the past century. The interplay between domestic and international variables, and the resulting dynamic changes.

IR-365.title: Politics and Democracy in Latin America
IR-365.description: Examines Latin America's experience with democracy emphasizing events since the 1980s. Analyzes the roles of interest groups, ideology, domestic politics, bureaucratic processes, perceptions and analogical reasoning.

IR-371.title: Global Civil Society: Non-State Actors in World Politics
IR-371.description: Examination of diplomatic and moral relationships between sovereign states and transnational non-state actors, both benevolent (humanitarian groups and philanthropies) and malevolent (mercenaries, pirates and terrorists).

IR-381.title: Introduction to International Security
IR-381.description: Key concepts in international security studies; historical evolution of international warfare and diplomacy; contemporary international security issues.

IR-386.title: Terrorism and Counterterrorism
IR-386.description: Examination of terrorism and responses to terrorism, including how societies understand and deal with terrorism; focus on ethical and normative issues.

IR-391.title: Directed International Relations Field Study
IR-391.description: Intensive internship experience in international relations professional areas with academic research component (may be repeated for credit different semesters)

IR-397.title: Field Research in Human Rights
IR-397.description: Conducting human rights research and policy work in the field
IR-397.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Sophomore, Junior, Senior

IR-402.title: Theories of War
IR-402.description: Causes of war; means of prevention and consequences of war.

IR-413.title: Applied Data Science for International Relations 2
IR-413.description: Intermediate statistical computing and data visualization in R. Focus the on graphical presentation of complex statistical relationships. Students create publication-ready figures for actual faculty research projects.

IR-420.title: Political Economy of Corruption
IR-420.description: Examines causes, consequences and how to combat corruption as an economic, political and social problem.

IR-425.title: The New Triangle: China, the U.S. and Latin America
IR-425.description: China's rise in the international political economy raises policy research questions, including an analysis of how this trend relates to U.S and Latin American relations. Recommended preparation: Micro and macro economics

IR-427.title: Seminar on Economics and Security
IR-427.description: Introduction to important economic issue areas that are understood as security-related in the contemporary world: population, food, trade, debt, etc.

IR-430.title: The Politics of International Trade
IR-430.description: Economic approaches and political processes are used to explain observed international trade policy choices. Topics covered include globalization, regionalism, labor standards, the environment and sanctions. Recommended preparation: Micro- and Macroeconomics.

IR-490.title: Directed Research
IR-490.description: Individual research and readings. Not available for graduate credit.
IR-490.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Junior, Senior

IR-499.title: Special Topics
IR-499.description: Selected topics in various special areas within international relations, which may vary from semester to semester or within semesters.

IRAN-150.title: Persian II
IRAN-150.description: Continuation of Persian I. Prerequisite: IRAN 120. (Duplicates credit in former MDES 150)

IRAN-250.title: Persian IV
IRAN-250.description: Continuing Intermediate Persian (Farsi). Building conversational skills, listening and reading comprehension, grammar and vocabulary necessary for intermediate level spoken and written expression. Prerequisite: IRAN 220. (Duplicates credit in former MDES 250)

IRAN-350.title: Advanced Persian II
IRAN-350.description: Continuation of Advanced Persian I. Prerequisite: IRAN 320. (Duplicates credit in former MDES 350)

ISE-150.title: Solving Engineering Problems using Python
ISE-150.description: Engineering examples are used as a platform to introduce computer programming skills for problem solving; critical thinking skills.

ISE-220.title: Foundations of Probability Modeling
ISE-220.description: Techniques for modeling uncertainty: discrete and continuous random variables, probability distributions, expectations and conditional probability; Poisson processes, Markov chains and queuing decision models.

ISE-225.title: Foundations of Data Analysis
ISE-225.description: Sampling distributions; confidence intervals and hypothesis testing; analysis of variance; regression; data aggregation; prediction and classification.

ISE-315.title: Engineering Project Management
ISE-315.description: Managing a project intended to create an engineered system. Methods, processes, tools. Lessons-learned from actual practice. Case studies from real projects. Presentations by student teams.

ISE-330.title: Optimization
ISE-330.description: Modeling, solution analysis and applications of complex decision problems using linear, dynamic and integer optimization.
ISE-330.prereqText: Prerequisite: MATH 225 or EE 141 and MATH 126 or EE 141 and MATH 129

ISE-349.title: Enterprise Data Analytics
ISE-349.description: Methodology to store, organize, cleanse, harmonize and stage enterprise data for analytics. Report, visualize, slice and dice, forecast and predict trends.
ISE-349.prereqText:
Prerequisite: TAC 249 or TAC 320 or ITP 249 or ITP 320 or DSCI 351
Duplicates credit: former ITP 487 and former ITP 349

ISE-350.title: Principles and Practices of Systems Engineering
ISE-350.description: Systems as complex collaborative ensembles of interconnected components. Theory and practice of requirements, design, implementation, testing, deployment, operation and disposal. Case studies from real projects.

ISE-370.title: Human Factors in Work and Systems Design
ISE-370.description: Role of humans in technological systems; human-systems integration; ergonomics; anthropometry and workstation design; work methods and measurement; human error, safety and accident analysis.

ISE-382.title: Database Systems: Storage and Retrieval using SQL
ISE-382.description: Data models for industry applications. Modeling and designing robust databases. Implementing and querying databases with SQL. Innovations in database applications.

ISE-410.title: Planning and Scheduling for Production and Supply Chains
ISE-410.description: Production, resource and service planning, forecasting, scheduling, vendor and location selection, inventory; integrated decision systems for the control of production, services and supply chains.

ISE-435.title: Discrete Systems Simulation
ISE-435.description: Modeling of complex discrete event systems, input and output analysis, system evaluation via experimentation on the simulation model, applications to industrial and systems engineering problems.

ISE-440.title: Socio-Technical Systems and Work Organizations
ISE-440.description: Design, modeling and analysis of complex systems, challenges they present and methods for resolving those challenges. Impact of technology on work and organizational design.
ISE-440.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Junior, Senior

ISE-460.title: Engineering Decisions, Economics and Ethics
ISE-460.description: Principles of economic analysis and decision analysis for engineering systems, including applications in financing, developing and comparing new technologies.

ISE-490.title: Directed Research
ISE-490.description: Individual research and readings. Not available for graduate credit.
ISE-490.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Junior, Senior

ISE-495A.title: Senior Design Project
ISE-495A.description: Investigate client organization operations, evaluate alternative designs to meet client needs, complete preliminary design review.
ISE-495A.prereqText:
Prerequisite: ISE 225; ISE 382
Class standing: open only to Junior, Senior
Major: open only to Industrial and Systems Engineering

ISE-495B.title: Senior Design Project
ISE-495B.description: Develop the detailed design including countermeasures for risks, complete critical design review, implement the project plan, close-out the project.
ISE-495B.prereqText:
Prerequisite: ISE 315; ISE 370; ISE 435; ISE 495A
Class standing: open only to Junior, Senior
Major: open only to Industrial and Systems Engineering

ISE-501.title: Innovative Conceptual Design for New Product Development
ISE-501.description: A logic-based framework for conceptual design, including systematic concept generation and improvement, in innovative product developments.
ISE-501.prereqText: Recommended preparation: Bachelor's degree in engineering or physical sciences

ISE-506.title: Lean Operations
ISE-506.description: Study of various aspects of integrated manufacturing and service enterprises including management, design and production functions, interfaces and related resources and information systems.

ISE-509.title: Practicum in Health Care Systems
ISE-509.description: Application of performance and efficiency tools to streamline hospital operations. Group projects collaborating with hospital staff.
ISE-509.prereqText: Recommended preparation: Engineering statistics at the level of ISE 225

ISE-513.title: Logistics and Inventory Systems
ISE-513.description: Practice in inventory management, computerized procedures, materials requirements planning. Deterministic and stochastic demand systems with static/dynamic models.

ISE-515.title: Engineering Project Management
ISE-515.description: Methods, processes and tools for managing projects to create engineered systems. Project management; engineering economics; risk management. Industry-drawn large-scale engineering case studies. Team project presentations.

ISE-516.title: Stochastic Processes for Financial Engineering
ISE-516.description: Theory and applications of stochastic processes relevant to financial engineering. Stochastic processes, Brownian motion, martingales, stochastic calculus, Monte Carlo Simulations with financial application examples.
ISE-516.prereqText: Prerequisite: EE 503; EE 441 or EE 510 or EE 518

ISE-519.title: Engineering Management of Systems Integration
ISE-519.description: Foundations of systems integration; advanced topics in systems integration including generative artificial intelligence (AI); data analytics for predicting and supporting engineering decisions.
ISE-519.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student, Master Student

ISE-521.title: Foundations of Analytics
ISE-521.description: Foundational tools, technologies and methodologies for analytics. The statistical basis of analytics. Understanding and preparing data. Python, SQL and exploratory data analysis.

ISE-529.title: Predictive Analytics
ISE-529.description: Supervised learning. Linear regression, cross validation, ridge and lasso regression, logistic regression, k-nearest-neighbors, decision trees, random forest and gradient-boosting models, support vector machines, neural networks.
ISE-529.prereqText: Recommended preparation: Undergraduate statistics on the level of ISE 225; working knowledge of a programming language on the level of ISE 150

ISE-530.title: Optimization Methods for Analytics
ISE-530.description: Fundamentals of Linear Programming, Integer Programming, quadratic and nonlinear programming for analytics and data science problems.
ISE-530.prereqText: Recommended preparation: Multivariable calculus on the level of MATH 229, linear algebra on the level of MATH 245, computer programming on the level of ISE 150

ISE-534.title: Data Analytics Consulting
ISE-534.description: Consulting project concepts, frameworks, analytical tools and managerial skills with a focus on the use of data analytics, design thinking and insight-driven frameworks.
ISE-534.prereqText:
Prerequisite: ISE 529
Recommended preparation: Statistics and statistical modeling on the level of ISE 225

ISE-535.title: Data Mining
ISE-535.description: Data preprocessing, data cleaning, data summarization, dimension reduction, data visualization, anomaly detection, classification and clustering. Modeling dependencies using association rules.
ISE-535.prereqText: Recommended preparation: Engineering statistics at the level of ISE 225; working knowledge of a programming language on the level of ISE 150.

ISE-537.title: Financial Analytics
ISE-537.description: Modern portfolio theory and optimal decision-making problems in finance. Market microstructure and high-frequency trading. Machine learning models for quantitative finance.
ISE-537.prereqText: Recommended preparation: Engineering statistics on the level of ISE 225; working knowledge of a programming language on the level of ISE 150.

ISE-543.title: Enterprise Cloud Analytics
ISE-543.description: Project-based course covers developing scalable analytics solutions using major cloud platforms, focusing on data management, machine learning and enterprise applications.

ISE-544.title: Leading and Managing Engineering Teams
ISE-544.description: Design and management of engineering teams. Group decision-making, motivation, leadership, infrastructure requirements, performance measurement, team diversity, conflict and integration.

ISE-547.title: Applied Generative Artificial Intelligence for Enterprises
ISE-547.description: Foundational concepts and methods in large language models and generative artificial intelligence; fine-tuning and pre-training strategies; applications in dialogue systems and text generation.

ISE-560.title: Analysis of Algorithms
ISE-560.description: Explores fundamental techniques such as recursion, Fourier transform ordering, dynamic programming for efficient algorithm construction. Examples include arithmetic, algebraic, graph, pattern matching, sorting, searching algorithms.

ISE-561.title: Economic Analysis of Engineering Projects
ISE-561.description: Economic evaluations of engineering systems for both government and private industry; quantitative techniques for evaluating non-monetary consequences; formal treatment of risk and uncertainty.
ISE-561.prereqText: Recommended preparation: undergraduate engineering economics on the level of ISE 460

ISE-562.title: Decision Analysis
ISE-562.description: Decisions under uncertainty; utility theory; multiattribute utility; probability elicitation; conjugate distributions; decision analysis applications, framing, modeling using spreadsheets or software; cognitive biases, behavioral decision theory.

ISE-563.title: Financial Engineering
ISE-563.description: Concepts underlying the economic analysis of engineering projects; applications to call and put options; utility theory and mathematical optimizations models; simulation.
ISE-563.prereqText: Recommended preparation: Probability on the level of ISE 220.

ISE-568.title: Machine Learning
ISE-568.description: Statistical methods for building intelligent and adaptive systems that improve performance from experiences; Focus on theoretical understanding of these methods and their computational implications. Recommended preparation: Undergraduate level training or coursework in linear algebra, multivariate calculus, basic probability and statistics; an undergraduate level course in Artificial Intelligence may be helpful but is not required.

ISE-574.title: Probabilistic Reasoning
ISE-574.description: Reasoning under uncertainty, statistical directed and undirected graphical models, temporal modeling, inference in graphical models, parameter learning, decisions under uncertainty. Recommended preparation: An undergraduate level course in probability theory.

ISE-583.title: Enterprise Wide Information Systems
ISE-583.description: The role enterprise resource planning systems (ERPs) play in organization; integrating and coordinating the many business processes such as demand planning, procurement, production and sales.

ISE-585.title: Strategic Management of Technology and Innovation
ISE-585.description: Examine principles, strategies, practices and case studies where new technology and innovation are transforming the traditional business paradigms to identify best practices in real-world implementation.

ISE-590.title: Directed Research
ISE-590.description: Research leading to the master's degree; maximum units which may be applied to the degree to be determined by the department. Graded CR/NC.

ISE-610.title: Advanced Design of Experiments and Quality Engineering
ISE-610.description: Methodologies of planning, conducting, analyzing and interpreting controlled physical or computational experiments for causal inference with broad data science and engineering applications.
ISE-610.prereqText: Recommended preparation: Engineering statistics (including distributions, confidence intervals, ANOVA, and regression) on the level of ISE 225.

ISE-612.title: Quantum Optimization Algorithms
ISE-612.description: Introduction to quantum computing; analysis of quantum algorithms; matrix manipulation, gradient computation and optimization.
ISE-612.prereqText:
Recommended preparation: Linear algebra on the level of MATH 471, mathematical optimization on the level of ISE 630 or ISE 631. Prior knowledge of quantum mechanics is not assumed.
Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student, Master Student

ISE-615.title: Reinforcement Learning and Control Theory
ISE-615.description: Modern stochastic control theory, recent developments in reinforcement learning theory, game theory, mean-field analysis and reinforcement learning in practice.
ISE-615.prereqText:
Recommended preparation: Linear algebra on the level of MATH 225; optimization methods on the level of ISE 630; probability and statistics on the level of ISE 220 and ISE 225; programming on the level of ITP 115 or ISE 150. Knowledge of machine learning and advanced optimization methods is useful but not required.
Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student

ISE-617.title: Machine Learning for/with Mixed-Integer Optimization
ISE-617.description: Using mixed-integer optimization (MIO) to solve problems in artificial intelligence (Al) and machine learning (ML). Leveraging Al/ML to improve MIO solvers.
ISE-617.prereqText:
Recommended preparation: Optimization (at the level of CSCI 675, ISE 630, or ISE 631); machine learning (at the level of CSCI 567, ISE 568, CSCI 467, EE 460, ISE 529, or CSCI 559) using Python
Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student, Master Student

ISE-619.title: End-to-End Learning and Optimization
ISE-619.description: End-to-end learning models and algorithms from operations research and machine learning perspectives. Computational considerations and performance guarantees. Energy, healthcare and supply chain applications.
ISE-619.prereqText: Recommended preparation: Basic optimization (at the level of CSCI 675, ISE 630, or ISE 631). Basic machine learning (at the level of CSCI 567, ISE 568, CSCI 467, EE 460, ISE 529, or CSCI 559) using Python.

ISE-626.title: Advanced Topics in Applied Stochastic Models
ISE-626.description: Stochastic processes, reversed continuous-time Markov chains, coupling, martingales, random walks, Brownian motion, stochastic order relations and probability inequalities.
ISE-626.prereqText:
Prerequisite: ISE 620
Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student

ISE-630.title: Foundations of Optimization
ISE-630.description: Convex sets, convex functions, structures of optimization problems, Lagrangian and conjugate duality. First and second order optimality conditions; applications in engineering and statistics.
ISE-630.prereqText: Recommended preparation: Multivariable calculus on the level of MATH 229; linear algebra on the level of MATH 225 or MATH 245.

ISE-632.title: Network Flows and Combinatorial Optimization
ISE-632.description: Combinatorial optimization, particularly graph problems. Shortest paths, max flow, minimum cost flows, Spanning trees, matroids, submodular functions. Bipartite and general matchings, Polyhedral combinatorics, total unimodularity.

ISE-651.title: Seminar in Industrial and Systems Engineering
ISE-651.description: Current research, guest speakers in the field; review papers; guidance in preparing research proposals and special projects.
ISE-651.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student, Master Student

ISE-662.title: Advanced Decision Theory
ISE-662.description: Rational decision making; value and utility functions; distribution theory; invariance relations; copulas; value of information and control; multiattribute utility; decision and game theory; behavioral research.
ISE-662.prereqText:
Recommended preparation: Multivariate calculus on the level of MATH 226; linear algebra on the level of MATH 225; probability and statistics on the level of ISE 500.
Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student

ISE-670.title: Advanced Analysis of Algorithms
ISE-670.description: Fundamental techniques for design and analysis of algorithms. Dynamic programming; network flows; theory of NP-completeness; linear programming; approximation, randomized, and online algorithms; basic cryptography. Prerequisite: CSCI 570. Recommended preparation: familiarity with algorithms and discrete mathematics. Open only to doctoral students.
ISE-670.prereqText:
Prerequisite: CSCI 570
Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student

ISE-790.title: Research
ISE-790.description: Research leading to the doctorate. Maximum units which may be applied to the degree to be determined by the department. Graded CR/NC.

ISE-794A.title: Doctoral Dissertation
ISE-794A.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student

ISE-794B.title: Doctoral Dissertation
ISE-794B.prereqText:
Prerequisite: ISE 794A
Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student

ISE-794C.title: Doctoral Dissertation
ISE-794C.prereqText:
Prerequisite: ISE 794B
Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student

ISE-794D.title: Doctoral Dissertation
ISE-794D.prereqText:
Prerequisite: ISE 794C
Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student

ISE-794Z.title: Doctoral Dissertation
ISE-794Z.prereqText:
Prerequisite: ISE 794D
Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student

ITAL-120.title: Italian I
ITAL-120.description: Introduction to current Italian. Oral practice, hearing and reading comprehension; grammar necessary for simple spoken and written expression. Lecture, classroom drill, laboratory drill.

ITAL-175.title: Accelerated Italian for Speakers of Spanish and  Other Romance Languages
ITAL-175.description: Accelerated introduction to written and spoken Italian for students with a high level of proficiency in Spanish or another Romance Language. Students completing this course may enroll in the third semester of the basic language sequence ITAL 220.
ITAL-175.prereqText:
Prerequisite: SPAN 220 or FREN 220 or PORT 220
Duplicates credit: ITAL 120, ITAL 150

ITAL-220.title: Italian III
ITAL-220.description: Continuation of Italian II. Review of structure of the language, drill in aural and reading comprehension, practice in oral expression.

ITAL-222.title: Italian Professional Internship: Communication and Culture
ITAL-222.description: Combined classroom discussion and supervised internship at companies. Practical experience in applying communication and cultural knowledge in a professional employment context.

ITAL-240.title: Italian IV
ITAL-240.description: Continuation of Italian III. Review and expand upon abilities to create with the language in concrete exchanges, descriptions, comparisons, questions and discussions relevant to current issues and topics.
ITAL-240.prereqText:
Prerequisite: ITAL 220
Duplicates credit: In former ITAL 224

ITAL-350.title: Gender and Sexuality in Renaissance Italy
ITAL-350.description: Interdisciplinary exploration of gender and sexuality in Italian renaissance literature and visual arts by male and female authors and artists from the fourteenth through the sixteenth century.

ITAL-360.title: Italian Cinema
ITAL-360.description: Survey of Italian cinema in its relation to social transformation, from the silent era to the present. Weekly screenings, lectures, and discussions. Conducted in English.

ITAL-374.title: Women Writers in Europe and America
ITAL-374.description: Introduction to works of major women writers from the Middle Ages to the 20th century in their literary, social and cultural contexts.

ITAL-490.title: Directed Research
ITAL-490.description: Individual research and readings. Not available for graduate credit.
ITAL-490.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Junior, Senior

JOUR-200.title: The Power and Responsibility of the Press
JOUR-200.description: Explores the role of journalism and social media in society - its influence on government, technology, business, national security, sports, science and entertainment.

JOUR-201.title: Culture of Journalism: Past, Present and Future
JOUR-201.description: Examines the social, cultural and political aspects of U.S. journalism over time and currently.

JOUR-205.title: Journalism Practicum
JOUR-205.description: Field experience in journalism, public relations, or related field.

JOUR-206.title: Reporting and Writing Practicum
JOUR-206.description: Experiential lab in which students report, write and produce digital journalism content and report and produce live radio/television broadcasts in a student-led newsroom.
JOUR-206.prereqText:
Prerequisite: JOUR 207
Major: open only to Journalism

JOUR-207.title: Reporting and Writing I
JOUR-207.description: Journalism fundamentals, including news judgment, finding and verifying information, and reporting and writing.

JOUR-210.title: Basics of News Production for Non-Majors
JOUR-210.description: Introduction to television, radio, and/or digital news production. Examination of issues in journalism.
JOUR-210.prereqText: Major: not open to Journalism, Public Relations and Advertising

JOUR-307.title: Reporting and Writing II
JOUR-307.description: Report, write, produce and distribute in-depth stories, including longer news and analysis pieces.
JOUR-307.prereqText:
Prerequisite: JOUR 207
Concurrent enrollment: JOUR 206
Major: open only to Journalism

JOUR-320.title: Introduction to Coding for Storytelling
JOUR-320.description: Introduction to basic web technologies; conceive, design, code and produce an advanced multimedia story package.

JOUR-321.title: Visual Journalism
JOUR-321.description: Basics of visual journalism, including video storytelling and photography.
JOUR-321.prereqText:
Prerequisite: JOUR 207
Concurrent enrollment: JOUR 206
Major: open only to Journalism

JOUR-322.title: Introduction to Investigative and Data Journalism
JOUR-322.description: Reportorial and analytical skills and techniques required for portraying and evaluating contemporary newsworthy events using basic data journalism techniques and tools for statistical analysis.
JOUR-322.prereqText:
Prerequisite: JOUR 307
Major: open only to Journalism

JOUR-330.title: Photojournalism
JOUR-330.description: Emphasis on fundamental skills necessary for photojournalism including camera techniques, story ideas and digital darkroom.

JOUR-340.title: Rewriting History: Reporting Rome
JOUR-340.description: Develop reporting skills by studying historical unsolved Italian crimes. Visit crime scenes, examine evidence, interview sources, analyze media reports and write articles for each crime.

JOUR-350.title: Introduction to Sports Media
JOUR-350.description: Highlight norms, routines of content, including print, broadcast, video. Focus on opportunities, constraints posed by roles of reporters, fans, players, publicists, agents, leagues, teams.

JOUR-372.title: Engaging Diverse Communities
JOUR-372.description: Covers strategies of community engagement and beat reporting.

JOUR-380.title: Sports, Business and Media in Today's Society
JOUR-380.description: An inside look at the important stories, topical issues, trends and historical developments related to the growing influence of business and media on college and professional sports; identifying the key components and meeting the influencers in class that help shape the business side of sports, while recognizing the role the media plays in providing daily coverage across multiple platforms.

JOUR-381.title: Entertainment, Business and Media in Today's Society
JOUR-381.description: An examination of the symbiotic relationship of the entertainment business and the media; press coverage of the entertainment industry; Hollywood's relationship with news media.

JOUR-392.title: Media and Migration in Times of European Crisis
JOUR-392.description: Investigates the implications of the perceptual process of mass media generated immigration discourse in Europe.
JOUR-392.prereqText: Major: open only to Communication, Journalism, Public Relations

JOUR-403.title: Television News and Sports Production
JOUR-403.description: Production of television news and sports programs while developing video, writing and communication skills and managing content in collaboration with others under deadline pressure.

JOUR-404.title: Produce and Host Sports Content in Studio A
JOUR-404.description: Interview, present and design sports segments for television/video in Studio A.

JOUR-405.title: Non-Fiction Television
JOUR-405.description: Presentation and selection in non-fiction television programs including documentaries, electronic magazines and news series; ethical problems, field research, reporting, interviewing, pre-production.

JOUR-406.title: Social Media Storytelling for Latinx Audiences
JOUR-406.description: Create native journalistic content for current social media and emerging platforms with an emphasis on engaging content for Latinx audiences and underrepresented communities.

JOUR-409.title: Audio Storytelling for Radio and Podcast
JOUR-409.description: Techniques for audio journalism, including effective use of sound, art of the interview, writing for the ear and crafting stories to engage listeners.

JOUR-412.title: Podcasting: Origin Stories
JOUR-412.description: A foundational understanding of the historic, cultural and theoretical underpinning of the podcast medium with an emphasis on critical listening.

JOUR-414.title: Advanced Digital Media Storytelling
JOUR-414.prereqText:
Prerequisite: JOUR 321; JOUR 322
Major: open only to Journalism

JOUR-430.title: Writing the Film Review
JOUR-430.description: Techniques of writing the film review; preparation and treatment of form and content; problems, responsibilities and ethics of film reviewing.

JOUR-432.title: Sports Commentary
JOUR-432.description: Techniques of reporting and writing sports columns and commentary for print, video, radio and Web-based media.

JOUR-441.title: Sports Reporting
JOUR-441.description: News and feature coverage of sporting events, including social and economic factors influencing sports in America.

JOUR-446.title: Entertainment Reporting
JOUR-446.description: Techniques of reporting and writing about the entertainment business, economics and finances. Analysis of the skills and background needed for reporters specializing in this area of the news.

JOUR-447.title: Arts Reporting
JOUR-447.description: Techniques of reporting and writing about the arts, including television, film, theatre, music, graphic arts, architecture and design.

JOUR-457.title: Food of Our Families
JOUR-457.description: Tell stories that explore food culture and culinary traditions, become familiar with cultural areas of Los Angeles and become immersed in global food and culture.

JOUR-462.title: Law of Mass Communication
JOUR-462.description: Covers the First Amendment and case law establishing journalists' freedoms and providing the framework for the practice of the craft.

JOUR-465.title: Latino News Media in the United States
JOUR-465.description: History and growing importance of Latino print and broadcast news media in covering immigration, discrimination, culture, social differences and other aspects of U.S. Latino life.

JOUR-467.title: Gender and the News Media
JOUR-467.description: Gender and news media evolving images of women and men in print and electronic media. Impact of gender in content and style of news, television and cinema. Open to non-majors.

JOUR-475.title: Print and Digital Design for 21st Century Storytelling
JOUR-475.description: Art, typography, and other graphic elements in publication design; traditional, contemporary, and advanced production methods, processes, and equipment; representative examples; practice in design.

JOUR-480.title: Sports and Media Technology
JOUR-480.description: Examine and analyze the ever-changing technology sector of the sports business and sports media worlds. Identify emerging technologies being developed in the sports industry and how they are being utilized to enhance the fan experience.

JOUR-490.title: Directed Research
JOUR-490.description: Individual research and readings. Not available for graduate credit.
JOUR-490.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Junior, Senior

JOUR-491.title: News Leadership
JOUR-491.description: Brutal economics, labor-management tensions, DEI, lawsuit threats -- learn how news leaders juggle all this and more while inspiring their staff to produce great journalism.

JOUR-522.title: Video Documentary Production
JOUR-522.description: Production of video documentary including research and reporting techniques, writing, interviewing, field work, editing, legal issues, economics, aesthetics, balanced presentation, ethics, diversity and production problems.
JOUR-522.prereqText:
Class standing: open only to Master Student
Major: open only to Journalism, Specialized Journalism, Specialized Journalism (The Arts)

JOUR-524.title: Advanced Video Reporting
JOUR-524.description: Reporting, production and writing for broadcast and other video platforms; practical experience; role of the video broadcast journalist; similarities and differences between media.
JOUR-524.prereqText:
Prerequisite: JOUR 528
Recommended preparation: JOUR 552
Class standing: open only to Master Student
Major: open only to Journalism, Specialized Journalism, Specialized Journalism (The Arts), Specialized Journalism (Arts and Culture)

JOUR-525.title: This California Life: Storytelling for Radio and Podcasting
JOUR-525.description: Advanced production techniques for public radio-style reports: writing, sound, editing, narrative voice. Techniques applicable for broadcast features or Web audio documentaries.
JOUR-525.prereqText:
Class standing: open only to Master Student
Major: open only to Journalism, Specialized Journalism, Specialized Journalism (The Arts)

JOUR-527.title: Advanced Disruption: Innovation with Emerging Technology
JOUR-527.description: Apply emerging technologies to tell innovative stories based on a production trip during spring break.

JOUR-542.title: Foreign Affairs Reporting
JOUR-542.description: News stories analyzed, researched, and critiqued for validity and background; projects to include editorials, news stories, magazine articles or broadcast reports.

JOUR-547.title: Navigating the Media Marketplace
JOUR-547.description: Explores the economics of the news industry and prepares students to navigate the journalism job market through practical exercises, practice interviews and cover letter-writing.
JOUR-547.prereqText:
Class standing: open only to Master Student
Major: open only to Journalism, Specialized Journalism, Specialized Journalism (The Arts), Specialized Journalism (Arts and Culture)

JOUR-557.title: Digital Investigations II: OSINT Reporting Lab
JOUR-557.description: Advanced techniques in open-source investigations and investigative reporting. Group research and publication of stories on important current topics grounded in digital investigations.

JOUR-569.title: The Art of (Macro) Food Journalism: A Global View
JOUR-569.description: Food is a powerful lens for thinking about cities, community, climate, technology, culture - even our relationship to other species. Focus is on the global.
JOUR-569.prereqText:
Class standing: open only to Master Student
Major: open only to Journalism, Specialized Journalism, Specialized Journalism (The Arts)

JOUR-572.title: Reporting on Entertainment and Popular Culture
JOUR-572.description: Reporting about entertainment, popular culture and their impact on American society; survey of past media coverage and current practices.

JOUR-579.title: Journalism Internship
JOUR-579.description: Field experience in journalism, public relations, or related field.

JOUR-585.title: Specialized Reporting: Religion
JOUR-585.description: Reporting and writing on religion; survey of world religion, religion and public life-including politics, gender and science.

JOUR-590.title: Directed Research
JOUR-590.description: Research leading to the Master's degree. Maximum units which may be applied to the degree to be determined by the department. Graded CR/NC.

JOUR-593.title: Arts Criticism and Commentary
JOUR-593.description: Writing workshops and independent fieldwork; development of critical skills to write socially valuable criticism and commentary about art, entertainment and culture.
JOUR-593.prereqText:
Class standing: open only to Master Student
Major: open only to Journalism, Specialized Journalism, Specialized Journalism (The Arts)

JOUR-598.title: Journalism Capstone Project
JOUR-598.description: Production of a journalism capstone project with multimedia elements for a master's degree. Projects can be single stand-alone pieces, or series of pieces.
JOUR-598.prereqText:
Prerequisite: JOUR 531
Class standing: open only to Master Student
Major: open only to Journalism, Specialized Journalism, Specialized Journalism (The Arts)

JS-100.title: Jewish History
JS-100.description: Major ideas, personalities, and movements in Jewish history from antiquity to the present in light of the interaction of the Jews with the general culture.

JS-150.title: Jewish Histories of the Modern Middle East
JS-150.description: Explores Jewish participation in the social, cultural, political and economic life of the modern Middle East.

JS-170.title: Exploring the Hebrew Bible
JS-170.description: Exploring the Hebrew Bible, the world in which it arose, and influential texts, including work from Ancient Egypt, Mesopotamia and the Southern Levant.

JS-180.title: Judaism
JS-180.description: Jewish beliefs, practices, and history from the biblical period to the present; Judaic contributions to Western civilization.

JS-211.title: The Holocaust
JS-211.description: Historical background and responses to the Holocaust, withspecial emphasis on ethical implications.

JS-310.title: The Eastern European Jewish Experience: Literature and Film
JS-310.description: Analyzes works by different artists -- writers, filmmakers, painters -- in order to understand the significant contribution that the Jewish experience in Eastern Europe has made to Jewish communities worldwide.

JS-315.title: Anti-Semitism, Racism and Other Hatreds
JS-315.description: History and contexts of anti-Semitism, racism and other discourses about difference examined through religious, national and cultural forms in Europe and in the US.

JS-370.title: Digs and Dispute: Religion and Archaeology in Israel
JS-370.description: Investigates contemporary conflicts in the discovery of the ancient world. Students will ask essential questions about the power of discovering and showcasing specific narratives.

JS-402.title: Jews, Judaism and Race
JS-402.description: Examine the history of race and racialization in Jewish life, culture and history across the world and the impact of race on Jewish tradition.

JS-415.title: The American Jewish Experience in Film
JS-415.description: A survey of American Jewish history through the medium of film, with particular emphasis on the experience of the post-war generation.

JS-490.title: Directed Research
JS-490.description: Individual research and readings. Not available for graduate credit.
JS-490.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Junior, Senior

JS-590.title: Directed Research
JS-590.description: Research leading to the master's degree. Maximum units which may be applied to the degree to be determined by the department. Graded CR/NC.

LAT-120.title: Latin I
LAT-120.description: Essentials of Latin grammar and vocabulary.

LAT-150.title: Latin II
LAT-150.description: Essentials of Latin grammar and vocabulary, continued. Basic reading skills.

LAT-222.title: Latin III
LAT-222.description: Reading Latin literature. Introduction to reading and translation of classical Latin prose and poetry. Extensive grammar review.

LAT-450.title: Readings in Latin Literature
LAT-450.description: Readings in various authors and genres of latin literature.

LAW-101.title: Law and the U.S. Constitution in Global History
LAW-101.description: By examining key constitutional moments involving race, rights, and revolutions, students will explore how legal meaning changes over time.

LAW-200.title: Law and Society
LAW-200.description: Sources and structure of law; history of Bill of Rights emphasizing effect on criminal justice system; limits of law in solving problems in American society.

LAW-201.title: Law and Politics
LAW-201.description: Examination of the rules and realities of American politics, and the role politics plays in American life and culture.

LAW-205.title: Introduction to Criminal Law
LAW-205.description: Provides a comprehensive analysis of the criminal justice system and an overview of the fundamentals of substantive criminal law.

LAW-210.title: Fundamentals of the U.S. Legal System
LAW-210.description: Introduces the U.S. legal system and its relationship to basic principles of the rule of law. Examines lawmaking institutions, judicial processes and contemporary legal issues.

LAW-211.title: Intellectual Property and Technology
LAW-211.description: Examines how American law protects and facilitates intellectual property and its modern utility. Provides a practical understanding of laws regulating patents, copyrights and trademarks.

LAW-212.title: Immigration Law for a New America
LAW-212.description: Examines current immigration law in America, the normative debates over immigration policies and the role the government plays in expanding or limiting immigration rights.

LAW-222.title: Interdisciplinary Perspectives on the Law
LAW-222.description: Examines law and the legal system from different disciplinary perspectives. It explores how various disciplines provide different insights to the legal regime.

LAW-223.title: Exploring Courthouses in Los Angeles
LAW-223.description: Gain hands-on experience by observing the inner workings of the criminal and civil law system through lectures and courtrooms visits.

LAW-225.title: Current Court Cases
LAW-225.description: Exposes students to the impact of legal decisions on society through analysis of pending and recent cases on the courts docket.

LAW-250.title: Children and the Law
LAW-250.description: Examines topics such as children's suggestibility, decision-making, and risk and resiliency all as they apply to legal settings.

LAW-300.title: Concepts in American Law
LAW-300.description: The main concepts and topics in American law, in the historical, economic and cultural contexts in which they have developed.

LAW-301.title: Voting Rights and the Law
LAW-301.description: Examines the basic themes surrounding the legal regulation of elections with a focus on voting rights.

LAW-310.title: Global Justice for Mass Atrocities and Genocide
LAW-310.description: Learn about international law and courts trying these cases, while also reflecting on whether criminal trials are the best response to bringing healing and reconciliation to affected societies.

LAW-311.title: Fundamentals of Entertainment Law
LAW-311.description: Examines key legal principles governing the entertainment industry by exploring legal challenges faced by professionals in music, film, sports, gaming and other areas of entertainment.

LAW-320.title: Law, Enslavement and Race
LAW-320.description: Studies how law, politics and culture interacted to shape the institution of enslavement and the development of modern conceptions of race.

LAW-324.title: Sports Law
LAW-324.description: Examines the relevance and application of legal structures to all participants in the sports enterprise by providing an overview of legal and ethical issues.

LAW-326.title: Law and the Modern Athlete
LAW-326.description: Covers legal frameworks that affect today's athletes and students working in sports: amateurism, negotiation, gambling, social media, agents and finding jobs in sports.

LAW-350.title: Law and Entrepreneurship
LAW-350.description: Examines areas of the law that impact entrepreneurs, starting, operating and financing businesses. Topics include: selection of business entities; securities laws and issues that arise in fundraising; employment law; contracts; torts; intellectual property; global expansion; mergers and acquisitions; and IPOs.

LAW-352.title: Introduction to Law and Economics
LAW-352.description: An exploration of core aspects of the US legal system (property, contracts, torts, criminal law, civil procedure) from the perspective of basic economics theory.

LAW-355.title: Law and Homelessness
LAW-355.description: Examines the current housing crisis by interweaving tenant/landlord law, local ordinances, historical exclusionary policies and reviewing current reporting and scholarship.

LAW-382.title: Refugee Law and Forced Migration
LAW-382.description: Examines international, regional, and U.S. refugee law, state obligations, implementation challenges, protection gaps, and contemporary displacement issues across the United States, Mexico, Canada, and European Union.

LAW-402.title: Psychology and Law
LAW-402.description: Explores issues of responsibility and credibility. Intentional and unintentional behavior. Clinical biases. Topics include witness credibility, confessions, cults, hostages, battered persons, and repressed memories.

LAW-403.title: Mental Health Law
LAW-403.description: Foundational legal and practice concepts at the intersection of law and psychology through three intersecting systems: the mental health, the criminal and the immigration systems.

LAW-406.title: Individual Rights in U.S. Constitutional Law
LAW-406.description: Explores the U.S. Bill of Rights and the limits that the Constitution imposes on the state majority's ability to impose its will on an individual.
LAW-406.prereqText: Class standing: not open to Freshman

LAW-407.title: Regulatory Law
LAW-407.description: Introduces legal and social ideas and issues surrounding regulatory law - how and why regulations are developed, along with the accountability and enforcement of regulations.

LAW-492.title: Undergraduate Law Review
LAW-492.description: Introduces students to the basics of legal writing and research, with a focus on legal scholarship and law review-type journal articles.

LAW-497.title: Legal Studies Capstone Project
LAW-497.description: A cumulative experience demonstrating a student's depth of knowledge in applying research and writing skills on examining the legal system.
LAW-497.prereqText:
Class standing: open only to Senior
Major: open only to Legal Studies
School: open only to Gould School of Law

LAW-498.title: Law Internship
LAW-498.description: Intensive law-related experience with a non-profit organization, public agency, government agency or private company.
LAW-498.prereqText: Recommended preparation: 8 units of LAW courses

LAW-499.title: Special Topics
LAW-499.description: Selected legal topics. Topics vary from semester to semester. May be repeated only if topic is different.

LAW-502.title: Procedure I
LAW-502.description: Consideration of the participants in litigation; private and public plaintiffs, defendants, and courts. Information exchange, process, outcomes, and costs of lawsuits.

LAW-503.title: Contracts
LAW-503.description: The interpretation and enforcement of promises and agreements.
LAW-503.prereqText: School: open only to Gould School of Law

LAW-504.title: Criminal Law
LAW-504.description: The crime problem and the legislative response to it through substantive criminal law; administration of criminal justice through police, prosecutorial, sentencing, and penological discretion.
LAW-504.prereqText: School: open only to Gould School of Law

LAW-505.title: Legal Profession
LAW-505.description: Functions of the lawyer in modern society; history and organization of the legal profession; the adversary system; equal access to justice; other problems of ethics and professional responsibility.
LAW-505.prereqText: School: open only to Gould School of Law

LAW-507.title: Property
LAW-507.description: The idea of property as understood through economic and philosophical concepts. Rights in land, water and other natural resources. Forms of shared ownership (e.g., landlord and tenant), and a survey of mechanisms for controlling land use.

LAW-508.title: Constitutional Law: Structure
LAW-508.description: Considers the delineation of spheres of responsibility between the judiciary and legislature, the nation and the state, and the government and the individual.
LAW-508.prereqText: School: open only to Gould School of Law

LAW-510.title: Legal Research
LAW-510.description: Examination of the basic sources of law for federal and California jurisdictions, utilizing a vast array of sources from books to computer-assisted research and analyzing research methodology and techniques. Graded CR/D/F.

LAW-511A.title: Legal Writing
LAW-511A.description: Two-semester course focusing on developing analytic and communication skills. Lawyers will analyze legal principles and incisively apply them to facts. Graded CR/D/F.
LAW-511A.prereqText: School: open only to Gould School of Law

LAW-513.title: Effective Writing for Professionals
LAW-513.description: Focuses on professional writing structure based on audience, tone, form and purpose.
LAW-513.prereqText: School: open only to Gould School of Law

LAW-516.title: Legal Research, Writing, and Advocacy II
LAW-516.description: Continuation of LAW 515. Development of legal research, writing, and advocacy skills. Emphasis on persuasive legal writing, including appellate briefs, and researching statutory and administrative law. Participation in a moot court program. Registration restricted to Law students.
LAW-516.prereqText:

LAW-520.description: The basic structure of government in the U.S., including the constitutionally mandated division of power in the federal government and the federal system of power sharing between state and federal systems. A comparative perspective on selected substantive and procedural matters, such as common law reasoning, jury trials, adversary process, and various aspects of civil procedure. Open to incoming LL.M. students only.

LAW-521.title: Topics in American Law
LAW-521.description: This course will provide LL.M. and M.C.L. students with a survey of various topics in American law including criminal law, evidence, family law, constitutional law, torts, wills and trusts, administrative law and property law. Open to LL.M. and M.C.L. students only.
LAW-521.prereqText: School: open only to Gould School of Law

LAW-523.title: Mass Torts
LAW-523.description: Examines how courts, lawyers, litigants, and financial institutions, respond when a single course of conduct allegedly injures hundreds, thousands, or millions of people.

LAW-531.prereqText: School: open only to Gould School of Law

LAW-532.prereqText: School: open only to Gould School of Law

LAW-550.title: Law for Business

LAW-550.prereqText: School: open only to Gould School of Law

LAW-553.description: Addresses evolving issues in using generative AI to produce commercial products and services relating to intellectual property rights such as copyright and trademark.
LAW-553.prereqText:
Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student, Master Student
School: open only to Gould School of Law

LAW-555.description: Explores the business of law, legal service delivery as it has traditionally been undertaken and its current transformation, and the primary drivers of change throughout the business of law ecosystem.
LAW-555.prereqText: School: open only to Gould School of Law

LAW-556.title: Artificial Intelligence: Law, Policy and Legal Practice
LAW-556.description: Explores how AI is transforming law and legal practice, how law governs AI, and how lawyers can use emerging technologies effectively, ethically, and with sound professional judgment.
LAW-556.prereqText:
Class standing: not open to Freshman, Sophomore, Junior, Senior, Senior (Fifth Year)
Major: open only to Law
School: open only to Gould School of Law

LAW-557.description: A philosophical inquiry into the nature, structure, and justification of rights. Legal rights feature prominently, but the perspective throughout is philosophical rather than doctrinal.
LAW-557.prereqText:

Major: open only to Law
School: open only to Gould School of Law

LAW-564.description: Explores the communication and presentation skills necessary for persuasive legal advocacy.
LAW-564.prereqText:

School: open only to Gould School of Law

LAW-566.title: Academic and Professional Skills for U.S. Law Studies II
LAW-566.description: Explores effective legal communication and professionalism skills.
LAW-566.prereqText:
Class standing: open only to Master Student
School: open only to Gould School of Law

LAW-579.title: Global Regulatory Compliance
LAW-579.description: Introduction to regimes that regulate business practices on a global level and compliance of such regimes, such as Foreign Corrupt Practices Act, OECD Anti-Bribery Convention, and other regulations.
LAW-579.prereqText: School: open only to Gould School of Law

LAW-600.title: Taxation
LAW-600.description: Federal tax statutes, technical issues and social problems involved in tax planning, tax litigation, and reform of the tax laws.
LAW-600.prereqText: School: open only to Gould School of Law

LAW-602.title: Criminal Procedure
LAW-602.description: Criminal procedure in the courts, and the regulation of lawenforcement by the courts through rules of evidence andinterpretation of the Bill of Rights.
LAW-602.prereqText: School: open only to Gould School of Law

LAW-603.description: Organization of economic activity especially the modern corporation as institutions of social power. The roles of managers, owners, and regulatory agencies in shaping processes ofdecision making.
LAW-603.prereqText: School: open only to Gould School of Law

LAW-607.description: Gratuitous transfer of wealth, especially the transmission of wealth from one generation to the next as a settlement of family affairs. Comparative analysis of the legal mechanisms of gifts, wills, and trusts. Introduction to problems of fiduciary administration.
LAW-607.prereqText: School: open only to Gould School of Law

LAW-608.title: Evidence
LAW-608.description: The purpose and character of trial. Problems of adversary presentation and the nature of proof. The basis for admission and exclusion of evidence in judicial proceedings.
LAW-608.prereqText: School: open only to Gould School of Law

LAW-612.title: California Civil Procedure
LAW-612.description: Examines the California rules of civil procedure. Emphasizes California law, with some discussion of the differences between state and federal procedure.
LAW-612.prereqText: School: open only to Gould School of Law

LAW-614.title: Accounting for Lawyers
LAW-614.description: The lawyer's skills needed to understand the financial affairs of a business client.
LAW-614.prereqText: School: open only to Gould School of Law

LAW-626.title: International Investment Law and Arbitration
LAW-626.description: Examine the protection offered to foreign investors through international investment agreements, which includes recourse to arbitration against the host states.
LAW-626.prereqText: School: open only to Gould School of Law

LAW-631.title: Mediation Clinic II
LAW-631.prereqText:
Prerequisite: LAW 630

LAW-632.title: Business for Lawyers
LAW-632.description: This course introduces law students to the tools, concept, and language of business. It is premised on the belief that to excel as a business lawyer, one must understand the business world from the perspective of the clients one counsels and assists. The course will cover, in compressed form, the basic subjects from the MBA program which are most useful to lawyers. Open only to law students.
LAW-632.prereqText: School: open only to Gould School of Law

LAW-636.title: Labor Law
LAW-636.description: The interrelation of labor, business, and government in collective bargaining, federal regulation of union and management practices and pressures, especially through the Taft-Hartley Act.
LAW-636.prereqText: School: open only to Gould School of Law

LAW-642.title: Secured Transactions
LAW-642.description: This is a course on Chattel paper and secured transactions involving personal property under Article 9 of the Uniform Commerical Code and some related bodies of law.
LAW-642.prereqText: School: open only to Gould School of Law

LAW-644.title: Corporate Taxation
LAW-644.description: Tax principles and practice applicable to business, especially problems of formation, liquidation, and reorganization.
LAW-644.prereqText:

LAW-645.title: Transactional Practice - The Syndicated Loan Agreement
LAW-645.description: Involves issues including loan restructuring; what loan agreements cover; how representations, covenants, default and financial and repayment terms interrelate; and how security documents fit in. Graded CR/D/F.
LAW-645.prereqText: School: open only to Gould School of Law

LAW-648.title: Topics in Entertainment Law
LAW-648.description: Contemporary topics in the field of entertainment law.
LAW-648.prereqText: School: open only to Gould School of Law

LAW-652.title: Computer Crime Law
LAW-652.description: Examines the legal and policy issues involved with the emergence of cyber crimes and cyber security issues, including government access and privacy issues.
LAW-652.prereqText: School: open only to Gould School of Law

LAW-653.title: Music Law in Practice
LAW-653.description: Focus on contract drafting and negotiation issues relevant to an artist's pursuit of a career in the music business.
LAW-653.prereqText: School: open only to Gould School of Law

LAW-654.title: Television and Digital Media
LAW-654.description: An in-depth study of television industry legal concepts, contracts, business structures and economic models.
LAW-654.prereqText: School: open only to Gould School of Law

LAW-658.title: Mergers and Acquisitions
LAW-658.description: Problems of integrating the corporate, securities, tax, business, antitrust, accounting and contractual aspects of corporate mergers and aquisitions.
LAW-658.prereqText:
Prerequisite: LAW 603
School: open only to Gould School of Law

LAW-659.title: Land use and Development Law
LAW-659.description: A practice-oriented introduction to various elements of land use and real estate development law.

MATH-108.title: Contemporary Precalculus
MATH-108.description: Equations and inequalities; functions; graphs; polynomial and rational functions; exponential, logarithmic, and trigonometric function; analytic geometry.

MATH-114.title: Foundations of Statistics
MATH-114.description: An introduction to the basic tools of statistics. Descriptive statistics; probability; expected value; normal approximation sampling; chance models; tests of significance.

MATH-125.title: Calculus I

MATH-126.title: Calculus II
MATH-126.description: A continuation of MATH 125: trigonometric functions; applications of integration; techniques of integration; indeterminate forms; infinite series; Taylor series; polar coordinates.

MATH-129.title: Calculus II for Engineers and Scientists

MATH-208.title: Elementary Probability and Statistics

MATH-225.title: Linear Algebra and Linear Differential Equations

MATH-225.prereqText:
Prerequisite: MATH 126 or MATH 127 or MATH 129
Duplicates credit: MATH 235

MATH-226.title: Calculus III
MATH-226.description: Vectors, vector valued functions; differential and integral calculus of functions of several variables; Green's theorem, Divergence theorem, Stoke's theorem.
MATH-226.prereqText: Prerequisite: MATH 126 or MATH 127 or MATH 129

MATH-229.title: Calculus III for Engineers and Scientists
MATH-229.description: A continuation of 129; vectors, vector valued functions; differential and integral calculus of functions of several variables; Greens theorem. Engineering and physics applications. Prerequisite: MATH 126, or MATH 127, or MATH 129.(Duplicates credit in MATH 226 and MATH 227)
MATH-229.prereqText: Prerequisite: MATH 126 or MATH 127 or MATH 129

MATH-235.title: Linear Algebra and Applications
MATH-235.description: Matrices, systems of linear equations, vector spaces, inner products and norms, linear transformations, eigenvalues, singular value decomposition. Applications such as image compression, graphs, networks or linear programming.
MATH-235.prereqText:
Prerequisite: MATH 125
Recommended preparation: Math 126 or any USC math course beyond Calculus 1

MATH-245.title: Mathematics of Physics and Engineering I
MATH-245.description: First-order differential equations; second-order linear differential equations; determinants and matrices; systems of linear differential equations; Laplace transforms.
MATH-245.prereqText: Prerequisite: MATH 226 or MATH 227 or MATH 229

MATH-290.title: Mathematical Reasoning and Problem Solving
MATH-290.description: Preparation for reading and writing proofs with applications from major branches of mathematics, focusing on axiomatic structures and transformations that preserve structure.
MATH-290.prereqText: Prerequisite: MATH 126 or MATH 127 or MATH 129

MATH-308.title: Statistical Inference and Data Analysis II
MATH-308.description: Confidence intervals, hypothesis testing, p-values, likelihood ratio, nonparametrics, descriptive statistics, regression, multiple linear regression, experimental design, analysis of variance, categorical data, chi-squared tests, Bayesian statistics.

MATH-395.title: Seminar in Problem Solving
MATH-395.description: Systematic approach to solving non-standard and competition level math problems on inequalities, infinite sums and products, combinatorics, number theory and games.
MATH-395.prereqText: Recommended preparation: MATH 126 or MATH 127 or MATH 129

MATH-407.title: Probability Theory
MATH-407.description: Probability spaces. Main families of discrete and continuous distributions and relations among them. Moments, characteristic functions, sequences of random variables, laws of large numbers, Central Limit Theorem.
MATH-407.prereqText: Prerequisite: MATH 226 or MATH 227 or MATH 229

MATH-408.title: Mathematical Statistics
MATH-408.description: Principles for testing hypotheses and estimation, confidence intervals, methods of moments, maximum likelihood, information inequality, likelihood ratio tests, goodness of fit and nonparametric methods.

MATH-410.title: Fundamental Concepts of Modern Algebra
MATH-410.description: Sets; relations; groups; homomorphisms; symmetric groups; Abelian groups; Sylow's theorems; introduction to rings and fields.
MATH-410.prereqText: Prerequisite: MATH 290 or MATH 430 or MATH 432

MATH-425A.title: Fundamental Concepts of Analysis
MATH-425A.description: The real number system, metric spaces, limits, continuity, derivatives and integrals, infinite series.
MATH-425A.prereqText: Prerequisite: MATH 290 or MATH 430 or MATH 432

MATH-425B.title: Fundamental Concepts of Analysis
MATH-425B.description: Implicit function theorems, Jacobians, transformations, multiple integrals, line integrals.
MATH-425B.prereqText:
Prerequisite: MATH 425A
Recommended preparation: one 400-level Mathematics course, excluding MATH 450

MATH-430.title: Theory of Numbers

MATH-430.prereqText: Prerequisite: MATH 225 or MATH 235 or MATH 245

MATH-432.title: Applied Combinatorics

MATH-432.prereqText: Prerequisite: MATH 225 or MATH 235 or MATH 245

MATH-435.title: Introduction to Differential Geometry

MATH-435.prereqText: Prerequisite: MATH 226 or MATH 227 or MATH 229; MATH 225 or MATH 235 or MATH 245

MATH-445.title: Mathematics of Physics and Engineering II
MATH-445.description: Vector field theory; theorems of Gauss, Green, and Stokes; Fourier series and integrals; complex variables; linear partial differential equations; series solutions of ordinary differential equations.
MATH-445.prereqText: Prerequisite: MATH 245 or MATH 225 and MATH 226 or MATH 225 and MATH 227 or MATH 225 and MATH 229

MATH-446.title: Data Science with Python

MATH-446.prereqText: Prerequisite: MATH 226 or MATH 227 or MATH 229; MATH 225 or MATH 235; MATH 308 or MATH 408; ITP 115 or ITP 116 or TAC 115 or TAC 116

MATH-447.title: Mathematics of Machine Learning
MATH-447.description: Mathematical aspects of Machine Learning. PAC Learning, VC-dimension and complexity. Linear predictors (regression, perceptron, SVM). Convex learning and gradient descent. Neural networks and backpropagation.
MATH-447.prereqText: Prerequisite: MATH 226 or MATH 227 or MATH 229; MATH 225 or MATH 235; MATH 307 or MATH 407

MATH-450.title: History of Mathematics
MATH-450.description: Evolution of mathematical ideas and techniques as seen through a study of the contributions of eminent mathematicians to the formulation and solution of celebrated problems. Recommended preparation: upper division MATH course.

MATH-454.title: Game Theory
MATH-454.description: Impartial games, partisan games, zero sum games, von Neumann Minimax Theorem, general sum games, Nash equilibrium, fixed point theorems, evolutionary game theory, signaling, coalitions, auctions, social choice theory.

MATH-458.title: Numerical Methods
MATH-458.description: Rounding errors in digital computation; solution of linear algebraic systems; Newton's method for nonlinear systems; matrix eigenvalues; polynomial approximation; numerical integration; numerical solution of ordinary differential equations.
MATH-458.prereqText:
Prerequisite: MATH 225 or MATH 235 or MATH 245
Recommended preparation: MATH 226 or MATH 227 or MATH 229

MATH-466.title: Dynamic Modeling
MATH-466.description: Formulation and study of models arising in population dynamics, growth of plankton, pollution in rivers, highway traffic, morphogenesis and tidal dynamics: stability, oscillations, bifurcations, chaos. The lab will consist of computer simulation of models using commercially available software.

MATH-471.title: Topics in Linear Algebra
MATH-471.description: Polynomial rings, vector spaces, linear transformations, canonical forms, inner product spaces.
MATH-471.prereqText:
Prerequisite: MATH 225 or MATH 235
Recommended preparation: MATH 410

MATH-475.title: Introduction to Theory of Complex Variables

MATH-475.prereqText: Prerequisite: MATH 226 or MATH 227 or MATH 229

MATH-501.description: Linear equations and matrices, Gauss elimination, error estimates, iteration techniques; contractive mappings, Newton's method; matrix eigenvalue problems; least-squares approximation, Newton-Cotes and Gaussian quadratures; finite difference methods. Prerequisite: linear algebra and calculus.

MATH-505B.title: Applied Probability
MATH-505B.description: Markov processes in discrete or continuous time; renewal processes; martingales; brownian motion and diffusion theory; random walks, inventory models, population growth, queuing models, shot noise.

MATH-507A.title: Theory of Probability
MATH-507A.description: Construction of probability spaces using measure theory; conditional expectation; properties of expectation; weak and strong laws of large numbers; characteristic functions; weak convergence.

MATH-510B.title: Algebra
MATH-510B.description: B: Commutative Algebra: Integrality, Hilbert Basis theorem, Hilbert Nullstellensatz; Modules: modules over PID's, chain conditions, tensor products; Noncommutative Rings: Jacobson radical, Artin-Wedderburn theorem, Maschke's theorem.

MATH-511A.title: Data Analysis
MATH-511A.description: Major parametric and non-parametric statistical tools used in biomedical research, computer packages including SAS. Includes laboratory. Lecture, 2 hours; laboratory, 2 hours.

MATH-511B.title: Data Analysis
MATH-511B.description: Statistical methods for analysis of categorical data including dichotomous, ordinal, multinomial and count data, using Stata package. Includes laboratory.

MATH-535A.title: Differential Geometry
