MUIN-272.description: Introductory survey of the music business. Topics include: copyright, record companies, contracts, music publishing, performance rights societies, managers, agents, and other artist team/income considerations. Not for major credit for Music Industry Majors. (Duplicates credit in former MUIN 372ax.)

MUIN-280.title: Communications in the Music Industry
MUIN-280.description: A comprehensive course on communications specific to the music industry with a focus on press and publicity for artists.

MUIN-360.title: Introduction to Music Law
MUIN-360.description: A study of entertainment law with a focus on the music industry.Areas of study include contracts, domestic practices,international practices, copyright protection, trademarks. Prerequisites: MUIN 270.

MUIN-370.title: Music Publishing and Licensing
MUIN-370.description: A contemporary survey of the methods used to monetize music through licensing/media placement, covering music publishing, songwriter agreements, performance rights and licenses for traditional/new media. Prerequisites: MUIN 270 or MUIN 272x.

MUIN-372.title: Business and Legal Aspects of the Music Industry
MUIN-372.description: An intermediate/advanced-level survey of music copyright law, artist contract analysis, infringement case studies as they affect modern/emerging business models and global music licensing.
MUIN-372.prereqText:
Prerequisite: MUIN 270 or MUIN 272
Duplicates credit: former MUIN 372b

MUIN-410.title: Marketing, Branding and Strategic Alliances in Music
MUIN-410.description: An in-depth study of music marketing, non-traditional revenue streams for artists, musicians, and labels including artist endorsements, artist tour sponsorships, digital music programs, music licensing, merchandise, and a primary focus on brand partnership deals in the music space. Prerequisites: MUIN 270 or MUIN 272x.

MUIN-420.title: DIY Music Marketing
MUIN-420.description: An exploration of the most current and effective marketing strategies and online branding tools for promoting, monetizing, and sustaining the career of the independent creative artist. Prerequisites: MUIN 270 or MUIN 272x.

MUIN-425.title: Live Music Production and Promotion
MUIN-425.description: A survey of the presentation of the live musical experience. Both classical and popular concert presentation will be examined including venue selection, promotion and security.

MUIN-430.title: Artist Management and Development
MUIN-430.description: A study of issues relating to the personal management of music artists including negotiating contracts, image, career development, agents, touring, merchandizing, fees and duties.

MUIN-450.title: Practicum in Music Industry Issues (Internship)
MUIN-450.description: Field application of music industry theories and practices; part-time employment. Project jointly defined by student, employer and professor.

MUIN-460.title: Streaming Economy in the Music Industry
MUIN-460.description: Focus on identifying the economic impact current music streaming models have on artists, record labels, publishing and consumers.

MUIN-461.title: Music Festival Design and Management
MUIN-461.description: Focus on planning, booking, marketing, promoting, ticketing and operating a festival in an ever-changing marketplace.

MUIN-462.title: Technology, Big Data and Marketing in the Music Industry
MUIN-462.description: Analyzing technologys relationship to the music industry. Use of data and analytics to develop successful strategies for new and existing artists.

MUIN-464.title: Public Assembly Venue Management
MUIN-464.description: Review and examination of the principles and practices associated with managing theaters, arenas, stadiums and all other public assembly venue types.

MUIN-465.title: Ethics in the Music Industry
MUIN-465.description: Focus on the intellectual/philosophical foundations of the modern interpretation and application of ethics within the music industry.

MUIN-467.title: DIY Touring
MUIN-467.description: A "hands-on" approach to learning the essential components of a successful small-market tour through the DO IT YOURSELF artist lens.

MUIN-475.title: Advanced Concert Management
MUIN-475.description: Application of theories, technologies, and practices of the live music industry. Focus on the business, management, marketing, promotion, and production of professional concert events.

MUIN-498A.title: Final Capstone Project
MUIN-498A.description: Culmination of the four-year course of study. Affords students the opportunity to experience guided work to meet the professional demands of the industry.

MUIN-498B.title: Final Capstone Project

MUIN-511.description: Focus on recorded musics sounds and innovators. Includes in-depth research, discussion, presentations and memorization for greater cultural context.

MUIN-520.title: Artist Management: Campaign Planning, Pitching, Partnerships
MUIN-520.description: Lecture and experiential learning focused on the role of an artists personal manager including developing their story, assets and strategy for various product release campaigns.

MUIN-521.title: Music Industry/Producers Forum
MUIN-521.description: Student-driven discussion, networking and Q&A; with guest industry leaders and role models, including producers, artists, music supervisors, concert promoters, agents, label executives, managers and attorneys.

MUIN-523.description: Focus on demystifying legalese" and music industry standards by assessing actual contract examples for context, including recording, songwriter, producer, media licensing, sponsorship and band partnerships.

MUIN-526.title: Music Supervision, Production and Creative Licensing
MUIN-526.description: A comprehensive look at contemporary music supervision for all visual media. Students will creatively apply guided lessons using real world example cases and projects.

MUSC-200.description: A uniquely American genre, the Broadway musical serves as a catalyst for inquiry into human diversity, cross-culturalism, and significant social and political issues.

NEUR-408.description: Sensory and motor systems to illustrate concepts regarding the functional organization of the brain, from microcircuitry of neural circuits to global processes such as perception. Prerequisite: BISC 421.

OT-648.description: Approaches to studying social contexts, structures, processes, discourses, practices and meanings of everyday life concerning people as occupational beings, emphasizing qualitative and mixed methods.

OT-660.description: Experiential learning through immersion in one or more externally funded research groups in the Division, enabling intense participation in multi-skilled research groups.

OT-670.title: Business Fundamentals for Healthcare  Professionals
OT-670.description: Development of foundational knowledge and practical skills required for occupational therapists and related healthcare professionals to create, pitch, and launch a comprehensive business/program plan.

OT-686.title: Residency
OT-686.description: Residency involving development, administration, evaluation, or policy formulation for occupation-centered programs in clinical or community settings. Development of portfolio for professional doctorate. Graded CR/NC.
OT-686.prereqText: Major: open only to Occupational Therapy

OT-710.description: Current professional issues related to fieldwork education; examination of best practices for teaching, learning and supervision; development of an envisioned future as a fieldwork educator.

OT-720.description: Fundamentals of teaching and learning in higher education in preparation for work in an academic setting; experiential learning in methods of course development and delivery.

OT-723.title: Doctoral Capstone Preparation: Seminar 2
OT-723.description: Collaboration with peers, Level II fieldwork and doctoral capstone experience site and faculty mentors to enhance the development of an evidence-based doctoral capstone program.

OT-725.title: Practice Scholar: Mobilizing Knowledge to Advance Practice
OT-725.description: Principles and practices of evaluation and knowledge mobilization skills to optimize outcomes, ensure stakeholder engagement and generate meaningful impact.

OT-729.description: Identification, analysis, critique and application of current occupational science research and themes to topic of relevance to post-professional occupational therapy education.

PAIN-401.description: An introduction to the physiological and psychological components of pain, and pharmacological and non-pharmacological management strategies. Cultural and social aspects of chronic pain are covered.

PAIN-707.title: Pain Neuroscience
PAIN-707.description: Anatomy of peripheral and central nociceptors, molecular mechanisms that underlie primary responses, neural networks, and neural mechanisms involved in hyperalgesia and allodynia.

PAIN-721.title: Advanced Therapeutics
PAIN-721.description: Patients who suffer from chronic pain often fail to respond to basic treatments. Therefore it is crucial for clinicians to be familiar with different treatment options.

PATH-551.description: Relationship between histopathological and clinical manifestations of disease and their underlying molecular mechanisms. Topics include inflammatory, developmental, environmental, degenerative, and neoplastic disease processes.

PATH-554.title: Emerging Trends and Methods in Molecular Pathology
PATH-554.description: Discuss emergent methodologies in molecular pathology with emphasis on applications important for genetics and epigenetics changes in various diseases, Sequencing Technologies, Data Analysis, Forensic Pathology.

PBHS-301.title: Science and Practice of Building Resilience
PBHS-301.description: Promotes learning principles and skills that enhance resilience to effectively navigate common stressors throughout a professional career through course lecture, group discussion, reflection and practice.

PBHS-305.title: The Science of Altruism
PBHS-305.description: Explores the science behind altruism, volunteerism, compassion and how helping others impacts individuals physically, psychologically and behaviorally through lectures, projects and experiential learning.

PBHS-306.title: Team-Based Care: Roles of Mental Health Professionals
PBHS-306.description: Explores evidence-based interdisciplinary team care in healthcare, focusing on roles of mental health professionals on these teams and communication amongst professionals in different disciplines.

PBHS-310.title: Identity Development of the Contemporary Male
PBHS-310.description: Exploration of identity development in terms of social, political and cultural constructs; examination of collegiate athletics and the contributions of men of color.

PCPA-506.title: Behavioral Sciences II
PCPA-506.description: Psychosocial issues in medical care such as death and dying, aging, and sexuality are addressed. Communication skills to multicultural patient populations are also explored. Open to Physician Assistant Practice majors only.

PCPA-546.description: Basic instruction in normal/abnormal states of organ systems in the study of human disease. The second of three courses that includes instruction in pathophysiology, pharmacology, diagnostic studies, and medicine. Open to Physician Assistant Practice majors only.

PCPA-583.title: Advanced Topics in PA Studies: Education
PCPA-583.description: Seminar format: students explore educational theories and methods used by PAs in variety of settings, including clinical practice, classroom and community. Open to Physician Assistant Practice majors only. Requires departmental approval.

PCPA-586.description: Seminar format: students receive an integrated experience in research methods including methodology, data collection, analysis and evaluation. Open to Physician Assistant Practice majors only. Requires departmental approval.

PCPA-589.description: Seminar format: studetns will explore current topics in medical care organization and physician assistant practice including administration, financing, changing organizational settings, and workforce issues. PEDO-701B.title: Seminar: Advanced Pediatric Dentistry
PEDO-701B.description: Discussion of literature related to specialty practice of pediatric dentistry. Biologic considerations in operative dentistry, odontogenesis, dental trauma, physiology of occlusion, pulpal biology. Graded CR/NC.

PEDO-703E.title: Interceptive Orthodontics
PEDO-703E.description: Recognition, evaluation, and treatment of developing orthodontic problems appropriate to the pediatric dentist; emphasis on diagnosis; laboratory experience included.

PEDO-705.title: Pediatric Diseases
PEDO-705.description: Discussion of medical conditions seen by the pediatric dentist in the hospital environment. Conditions include childhood cancer, HIV, heart disease, diabetes mellitus and blood dyscrasias. Graded CR/NC.

PEDO-707.title: Seminar: Cleft Palate Rehabilitation
PEDO-707.description: 3 Trimester Course Discussions and case conferences related to treatment of patients with oral and facial anomalies: includes interceptive and corrective orthodontics, preventive and restorative treatment, and selected oral surgery-prosthetic rehabilitative procedures. Seminar, 3 hours.

PEDO-708.title: Practice Management
PEDO-708.description: Discussion of issues related to the contemporary practice of pediatric dentistry (seminars and office visitations). Topics include: purchasing a practice, associateships, hospital affiliations, practice administration and marketing, computers, jurispudence and auxiliary utilization. Graded CR/NC.

PEDO-721.title: Pediatric Physical Evaluation
PEDO-721.description: Assessment of patient health status; evaluation and management of acute and chronic disease states which may be observed in the pediatric dental practice.

PEDO-772E.title: Clinic: Interceptive Orthodontics
PEDO-772E.description: Clinical application and treatment procedures for tooth guidance, stet and interceptive orthodontics.

PEDO-773.title: Hospital Pediatric Clinics
PEDO-773.description: Observation and participation in affiliated hospital clinics: anesthesiology, hematology, and genetic clinics; grand pediatric rounds andother conferences.

PEDO-774.title: Clinical Genetics in Pediatric Dentistry
PEDO-774.description: Genetic principles of oral, facial, and cranial malformations; technique and theory of clinical genetics, differential diagnosis, and treatment of disorders of the craniofacial complex.

PEDO-790A.title: Directed Research: Pediatric Dentistry
PEDO-790A.description: An examination and analysis of clinical and laboratory problems in dentistry for children leading to completion of an original research project. Graded CR/NC.

PEDO-790B.title: Directed Research: Pediatric Dentistry
PEDO-790B.description: An examination and analysis of clinical and laboratory problems in dentistry for children leading to completion of an original research project. Graded CR/NC.

PEDS-550.title: Pharmacoepidemiology
PEDS-550.description: Introduces pharmacoepidemiology and discusses key concepts and principles in the study of the utilization, safety and effectiveness of medications in large populations.
PEDS-550.prereqText:
Recommended preparation: PM 512 or Biostatistics course
Duplicates credit: former PHRD 550

PERI-701A.title: Seminar: Review of Current Periodontal Literature
PERI-701A.description: Review and critical evaluation of the current periodontal literature.

PERI-701B.title: Seminar: Review of Current Periodontal Literature
PERI-701B.description: Review and critical evaluation of the current periodontal literature.

PERI-702B.title: Seminar: Periodontal Treatment Procedures
PERI-702B.description: Presentation of various techniques in current periodontal treatment.

PERI-782E.title: Clinic: Implant Surgery
PERI-782E.description: Clinical procedures in dental implant surgery and site development for prosthodontic rehabilitation.
PERI-782E.prereqText:
Prerequisite: PERI 782D
Major: open only to Advanced Periodontology
School: open only to Ostrow School of Dentistry
Duplicates credit: REST 782e

PHBI-550.title: Seminar in Advanced Cellular, Molecular and Systemic Physiology
PHBI-550.description: Lectures and student presentations on advanced topics in molecular, cellular and systemic physiology. Open to Systems Biology and Disease, Physiology and Biophysics, and Pathobiology students only. Graded CR/NC.
PHBI-550.prereqText: Major: open only to Pathobiology, Physiology and Biophysics, Integrative Biology of Disease

PHED-102A.title: Weight Training
PHED-102A.description: Improvement of body shape, muscle endurance, and muscle strength; understanding of weight training and nutrition principles that can be utilized for future weight training development.

PHED-103.title: Personal Training
PHED-103.description: Science-based, client-centered personal training skills; applied exercise physiology and nutrition principles; individualized program design; movement analysis; results-driven programming; certification preparation.

PHED-104A.title: Self-Defense
PHED-104A.description: Basic instruction of self-defense for beginners; strategies for standing and ground fighting situations with and without weapons.

PHED-105.title: Principles of Self Defense and Personal Safety
PHED-105.description: Application of learned skills and strategies for identifying physical threats; increased situational awareness; understanding of when physical force may be required.

PHED-106A.title: Physical Conditioning
PHED-106A.description: a: Improvement in cardiorespiratory endurance, body composition, muscle endurance and flexibility; running, circuit training, resistance exercises; fitness principles and nutrition to develop individualized program.

PHED-110A.title: Swimming
PHED-110A.description: a: Instruction and practice of basic strokes for beginners and intermediate swimmers; elementary springboard diving; water safety techniques; endurance training as a fitness program.

PHED-115.title: Surfing
PHED-115.description: Fundamental instruction of surfing skills; water safety and wave etiquette; wave recognition and forecast interpretation; surf culture; board selection; surf related strengthening and conditioning.

PHED-117.title: Sustainability and Self-Care
PHED-117.description: Alternative ways to integrate sustainability practices into a daily routine; develop individual self-care modalities and connect to our planet; navigate climate anxiety.

PHED-118.title: Sleep for Peak Performance
PHED-118.description: Introduction to sleep as it relates to physical and mental performance; breathing and meditation modalities to support healthy sleep; study of sleep systems, disorders, strategies.

PHED-119.title: Introduction to Mindfulness
PHED-119.description: Introduction to the principles of mindfulness; application of learned techniques to enhance mind body awareness; cultivate strategies to improve physical and mental health.

PHED-120A.title: Yoga
PHED-120A.description: Introduction to meditation, breathing techniques and postures as a means towards relaxation; increase muscle flexibility, understanding of basic anatomy and nutritional guidelines.

PHED-122.title: Yoga and Meditation
PHED-122.description: Ancient yoga practice combining postures, meditation, breathing, mantras and focus techniques; designed to improve mind body awareness, balance, strength, flexibility, techniques and nervous system function.

PHED-123.title: Yoga Therapy
PHED-123.description: Holistic discipline combining traditional yoga techniques with a modern medicine approach to treating a variety of health conditions; includes physical, mental and breathing practice.

PHED-124.title: Walking for Fitness
PHED-124.description: Develop a strong fitness foundation through walking; fitness assessment and individualized programs; gait biomechanics and power walking; injury prevention; strategies for special populations.

PHED-126.title: AcroYoga
PHED-126.description: Groups work together to build strength, balance, coordination and communication skills, emphasizing dynamic movement of acrobatics, mindfulness of yoga, spotting and handstand training.

PHED-127.title: Principles of Yoga Through Community Outreach
PHED-127.description: Introduction and reinforcement of yoga postures, breathing techniques and meditation; sharing yoga principles and benefits with grade schools; teaching and community service opportunity.

PHED-129A.title: Cardio Group Fitness
PHED-129A.description: Group fitness instruction incorporating a variety of training methods such as cycling, HITT (high intensity interval training), step, circuits; nutritional guidelines.

PHED-132.title: Distance Running
PHED-132.description: Introduction to distance running while training for a 5k, 10k or half marathon; gait biomechanics and running efficiency; injury prevention; nutrition guidelines.

PHED-134.title: Hiking
PHED-134.description: Introduction to hiking; specific conditioning to develop muscle strength and endurance; equipment; various terrain, weather conditions, safety; environmental impact and trail etiquette.

PHED-135.title: Backpacking
PHED-135.description: Acquisition of backpacking knowledge and skills; conditioning plan; nutrition and equipment selection; ethics and environmental considerations; navigation, safety and wilderness first aid; trip planning.
PHED-135.prereqText: Recommended preparation: Students must be able to carry a weighted backpack through varied terrain for extended periods of time. Students must pass a fitness test given on the first day to be eligible

PHED-138.title: Beach Volleyball
PHED-138.description: Fundamental instruction of skills and tactics specific to sand volleyball and related physical conditioning; rules and strategies; history and culture.

PHED-139A.title: Volleyball
PHED-139A.description: a: Introduction to beginning and intermediate volleyball skills, rules, game tactics, and strategies. Emphasis on the development of: passing, setting, hitting, serving, blocking, and digging.

PHED-139B.title: Volleyball
PHED-139B.description: b: Advanced techniques; focus on offenses and defenses used in game situations.

PHED-140A.title: Tennis
PHED-140A.description: Fundamental instruction of basic strokes for beginners and intermediate players; rules, scoring, court etiquette, strategies; singles and doubles; practice and match play.

PHED-144.title: Pickleball
PHED-144.description: Introduction to pickleball; develop basic skills, techniques and fundamentals; rules, scoring, etiquette and strategies of play (singles/doubles play).

PHED-150A.title: Table Tennis
PHED-150A.description: Fundamental instruction of basic strokes for beginning and intermediate players; rules, scoring strategies; singles and doubles; practices and match play.

PHED-150B.title: Table Tennis
PHED-150B.description: Reinforcement of basic strokes for experienced players; development of advanced strokes including serves, use of spin, counter hits, footwork; drills and match play.
PHED-150B.prereqText:
Prerequisite: PHED 150A
Duplicates credit: former PHED 150

PHED-151A.title: Badminton
PHED-151A.description: Fundamental instruction of basic strokes for beginners and intermediate players; rules, scoring, strategies; footwork and court positioning; practical drills and games.

PHED-153.title: Futsal
PHED-153.description: Fundamental instruction of skills and tactics specific to Futsal; rules; strategies; elements of play that differ from soccer; conditioning, drills and games.

PHED-154A.title: Soccer
PHED-154A.description: Development of basic skills for beginners, intermediate and advanced players; rules, positioning elements of play, small group and team tactics; full field scrimmages.

PHED-155A.title: Golf
PHED-155A.description: Basic skills development and knowledge in stance, grip and swing mechanics; course strategy; use of woods, irons and putting; history rules and etiquette.

PHED-156A.title: Basketball
PHED-156A.description: a: Basic skill development in dribbling, passing, shooting, rebounding and defense; rules, history, and etiquette; drills and full court games.

PHED-159.title: Practice Planning for Motor Skill Acquisition
PHED-159.description: Apply fundamental principles and frameworks to different populations and people of all abilities in the learning of motor skills.

PHED-160.title: Stress Management for Healthy Living
PHED-160.description: Instruction on the effects of stress as it relates to work, sport and academics; coping strategies are discussed and applied through physical conditioning interventions.

PHED-161.title: First Aid
PHED-161.description: First aid safety education and infant, child, and adult CPR; demonstrated proficiency and successful completion of exam prepares students for Red Cross certification.

PHED-162.title: Principles of Athletic Coaching
PHED-162.description: Introduction to coaching strategies; team management; philosophy; ethics; leadership. Methodologies in sport specific training; skill progression; conditioning; athlete motivation; budgeting; fundraising.

PHED-163.title: Health Coaching
PHED-163.description: Skills and strategies of coaching principles promoting healthy lifestyle change. Motivational communication techniques; goal setting; designing safe, effective exercise program; health coach certification exam preparation.

PHED-164.title: Leadership Considerations in Sport, Health and Movement
PHED-164.description: Introduction to considerations for aspiring leaders. Learning to apply leadership principles and evaluate issues in a variety of contexts.

PHED-165.title: Varsity Athletics
PHED-165.description: Participation in the University's intercollegiate programs as sanctioned and governed by the PAC-10 conference and/or the NCAA. Graded CR/NC.

PHIL-100.title: Central Problems of Philosophy
PHIL-100.description: Explores questions about human beings and their place in nature, including questions about knowledge, mind and body, freedom and determinism, and the existence of God.

PHIL-101.title: Free People, Free Thought and Free Markets
PHIL-101.description: The philosophical foundations of modern political and economic thought, including economic rationality, neoclassical economics, free-market vs. socialist economies and behavioral economics.

PHIL-122A.title: Reasoning and Argument
PHIL-122A.description: Techniques for constructing good arguments and for assessing and criticizing the arguments of others. (Duplicates credit in former PHIL 250a)

PHIL-122B.title: Reasoning and Argument
PHIL-122B.description: Techniques for constructing good arguments and for assessing and criticizing the arguments of others. (Duplicates credit in former PHIL 250b)

PHIL-166.title: Current Moral and Social Issues
PHIL-166.description: Critical study of controversial social issues such as abortion, euthanasia, the death penalty, war and terrorism, sexual morality, affirmative action and economic justice.

PHIL-174.title: Freedom, Equality, and Social Justice
PHIL-174.description: Explores the nature of justice, and how apparently conflicting ideals, such as freedom and equality, are to be balanced within a just society.

PHIL-236.title: Issues in Space and Time
PHIL-236.description: What is time? What is the difference between past, present and future? Is time-travel possible? And what paradoxes might it give rise to?

PHIL-258.title: Probability and Rational Choice
PHIL-258.description: Explores formal tools for thinking about uncertainty. In an uncertain world, how is it rational to form our beliefs, make decisions, and interact with others?

PHIL-260.title: Ethical Theory and Practice
PHIL-260.description: Explores various conceptions of morality and what makes actions right or wrong, together with the implications of these views for concrete ethical issues.

PHIL-268.title: Philosophy of Sport
PHIL-268.description: The philosophy of sport, covering concepts, history, ethics and commercialization, with interdisciplinary perspectives from philosophers, historians and social psychologists.

PHIL-288.title: Love and its Representation in Western           Literature, Film, and Philosophy
PHIL-288.description: Key works that have shaped the European and American cultural inheritance, with a special focus on the nature of love.

PHIL-315.title: History of Western Philosophy: Ancient Period
PHIL-315.description: Major figures in the history of Western philosophical thought from the presocratics to the Hellenistic period; emphasis on Plato and Aristotle.

PHIL-317.title: History of Western Philosophy: Medieval Period
PHIL-317.description: Central themes in Jewish, Christian and Islamic philosophy from late antiquity through the scholastic period.

PHIL-337.title: Political Philosophy
PHIL-337.description: Analysis of some of the main political philosophies of the modern era; emphasis on the ethical and metaphysical foundations of political philosophy.

PHIL-339.title: Philosophy of Economics
PHIL-339.description: Central topics in the philosophy of economics, including models of economic rationality, the aggregation of preferences and the conditions in which markets yield undesirable outcomes.

PHIL-349.title: AI Ethics

PHRD-522.title: Integrated Science and Clinical Therapeutics II
PHRD-522.description: Covers endocrine disorders, including diabetes, thyroid disease, reproductive health and osteoporosis, integrating pathophysiology, pharmacology and clinical management for patient care applications.

PHRD-525.title: Integrated Science and Clinical Therapeutics V
PHRD-525.description: Expands on prior ISCT courses, covering pathophysiology, pharmacology, chemistry, pharmacokinetics and therapeutic management of disorders within patient care processes.

PHRD-526.title: Integrated Science and Clinical Therapeutics VI
PHRD-526.description: Expands on prior ISCT courses, covering pathophysiology, pharmacology, chemistry, pharmacokinetics and therapeutic management of disorders within patient care processes.

PHRD-613.title: Introductory Community Pharmacy Practice Experience
PHRD-613.description: The P1 Community IPPE provides 15 days of hands-on experience, introducing student pharmacists to community pharmacy operations and their role in patient care.

The P2 and P3 Elective IPPE provides the student with 80 hours of experiential learning to develop skills related to various aspects of the pharmacy profession in a variety of settings.

PHRD-628C.title: Longitudinal Interprofessional Collaboration Experience
PHRD-628C.description: The IPC experience provides student pharmacists with the specialized knowledge, skills, and experiences to provide team-based patient care through interprofessional collaboration (IPC). Lends expertise in the area of appropriate utilization of pharmaceuticals anchored in evidence-based medicine. The longitudinal IPC experience is designed to prepare students for optimizing team-based patient care through IPC.

PHRD-629B.title: Longitudinal Community Pharmacy Practice
PHRD-629B.description: For Year 2 pharmacy (P2) and Year 3 pharmacy (P3) students who are assigned to a Community Introductory Pharmacy Practice Experience (IPPE) after registering for PHRD 629a. The P2 and P3 Community IPPE provides the student with 80 hours of experiential learning to develop skills related to aspects of the pharmacy profession in the Community pharmacy setting.

PHRD-631B.title: Longitudinal Institutional Pharmacy Practice

PM-503.title: Practice of Public Health
PM-503.description: Introduction to the application of strategies and tools for practice in public health, including policy advocacy, leadership and management, program planning and evaluation, health communication.

PM-504.title: Quality in Health Care
PM-504.description: Examines quality assessment at different levels of the health care system including health plans, physicians, hospital and integrated system performance.

PM-508.title: Health Service Delivery in the U.S.
PM-508.description: Historical development of the American health care system; determinants of health care utilization; role of health care providers; health policy; public health services; and health care finance.

PM-510.title: Principles of Biostatistics
PM-510.description: Concepts of biostatistics; appropriate uses and common misuses of health statistics; practice in the application of statistical procedures; introduction to statistical software including EXCEL, SPSS, nQuery. Laboratory.

PM-511A.title: Data Analysis
PM-511A.description: Major parametric and non-parametric statistical tools used in biomedical research, computer packages including SAS. Includes laboratory. Lecture, 2 hours; laboratory, 2 hours.

PM-511B.title: Data Analysis
PM-511B.description: Statistical methods for analysis of categorical data including dichotomous, ordinal, multinomial and count data, using Stata package. Includes laboratory.

PM-512.title: Principles of Epidemiology
PM-512.description: Terminology/uses of epidemiology and demography; sources/uses of population data; types of epidemiologic studies; risk assessment; common sources of bias in population studies; principles of screening. Recommended preparation: algebra

PM-513.title: Experimental Designs
PM-513.description: Statistical methods for analysis of various experimental designs. Parametric analysis of variance (ANOVA), repeated measures methods, crossover designs, non-parametric ANOVA.

PM-516A.title: Biostatistical Consulting
PM-516A.description: An overview of the tools used by statisticians for solving statistical problems. Introduces students to the field of biostatistical consulting.

PM-516B.title: Biostatistical Consulting
PM-516B.description: Reinforce concepts in biostatistical consulting and will expose students to the practice of biostatistical consulting

PM-517B.title: Research Methods in Epidemiology
PM-517B.description: Overview of epidemiologic research in cancer. Selected cancer sites will be covered to highlight study design and conduct, exposure assessment, data analysis and interpretation.

PM-518A.title: Statistical Methods for Epidemiological Studies I, II
PM-518A.description: Principles and methods used in epidemiology for comparing disease frequencies between groups. Restricted to the analysis of binary outcome variables.

PM-519.title: Moving Toward Health Equity in the United States
PM-519.description: A thoughtful perspective on U.S. health services delivery while introducing students to social inequalities in health.

PM-520.title: Advanced Statistical Computing
PM-520.description: Techniques for the solution of statistical problems throughout intensive computing; iterative techniques, randomization tests, the bootstrap, Monte Carlo methods. Lecture and required laboratory.

PM-522B.title: Introduction to the Theory of Statistics
PM-522B.description: b: Theory of estimation and testing, inference, analysis of variance, theory of regression. Recommended Preparation: college-level calculus and linear algebra.

PM-523.title: Design of Clinical Studies
PM-523.description: Design, conduct, and interpretation of results of clinical trials; emphasis on principles affecting structure, size, duration of a trial, and the impact of ethical and practical considerations.

PM-525.title: Culture and Health: Global Perspectives
PM-525.description: International variations in health status with a focus on the impact of socioeconomic status, politics, environment, education and gender in etiology of illness, access to health care, progression of disease, and recovery.

PM-526.title: Communications in Public Health
PM-526.description: Application of communication theories and methods to community health problems. Includes background assessment, program design, evaluation, social marketing, media advocacy, review of major health campaigns.

PM-527.title: Epidemiology of Infectious Disease
PM-527.description: Survey of natural history of infectious disease, methods of disease control and outbreak investigation, and an overview of the epidemiology of injury. Prerequisite: PM-512.

PM-528.title: Program Design and Evaluation
PM-528.description: Core concepts, methods and values of public health program planning and evaluation, including community needs assessment, writing objectives, designing health promotion programs, process and outcome evaluation.

PM-542.title: Social Network Analysis
PM-542.description: Theory, methods and procedures of network analysis with emphasis on applications to public health programs.

PM-545.title: Introduction to Time Series
PM-545.description: Transfer function models; stationary, nonstationary processes; moving average, autoregressive models; spectral analysis; estimation of mean, autocorrelation, spectrum; seasonal time series.
PM-545.prereqText: Recommended preparation: Linear algebra, multivariable calculus, statistics

PM-547.title: Public Health Policy and Politics
PM-547.description: Examination of major policy issues in the U.S. health care delivery system to understand policy options in reforming health care and reducing health care disparities.

PM-559.title: Cancer Epidemiology
PM-559.description: Explores the fundamental concepts of cancer epidemiology, including the molecular basis, descriptive epidemiology, and historical and groundbreaking studies that have impacted the field.

PM-562.title: Intervention Approaches for Health Promotion and Disease Prevention
PM-562.description: Approaches for modifying health behavior in varioius settings and within diverse populations. Emphasis on practical considerations necessary to design and implement interventions with demonstrated effectiveness.

PM-564.title: Public Health Leadership and Management
PM-564.description: Introduction to leadership and management concepts, tools, and practices in the context of domestic and global public health and healthcare delivery settings.

PM-565.title: Introduction to Global Health
PM-565.description: Current public health issues and research topics relating to 21st century challenges and threats. Lessons learned and best practices to strengthen public health systems and enhance public health readiness and preparedness.

PM-576.title: Global Health Research and Programs
PM-576.description: Introduction to the core concepts and methods of planning and implementing health-related programs and research in resource-constrained settings.

PM-577.title: Global Health, Law and Human Rights: Concepts and Methods
PM-577.description: Highlights the complex interactions between global health, law and human rights, emphasizing the use of human rights in public health thinking and practice.
PM-577.prereqText:
Recommended preparation: MPH core course work
Duplicates credit: LAW 707

PM-586.title: Reproductive and Perinatal Epidemiology
PM-586.description: Introduction to reproductive health, from preconception to the neonatal and early period of human development. Heavy emphasis on the methods and public health implications.

PM-590.description: Research leading to the master's degree. Maximum units which may be applied to the degree to be determined by the department. Graded CR/NC.

PM-591.title: Machine Learning for the Health Sciences
PM-591.description: Introduces Masters and Ph.D. students in the Health Sciences to Machine Learning methods and their Biomedical applications.

PM-596.description: Applied practical experience through field placement in federal, state, and/or local public health agencies/organizations, including community-based organizations; research and school-based settings.
PM-596.prereqText: Recommended preparation: PM 502: Foundations of Public Health, PM 503: Practice of Public Health, and at least one MPH concentration core course

PM-605.description: Theoretical basis and practical approaches for identifying, summarizing and interpreting current bodies of scholarly information addressing a defined research question.

Covers the structure of NIH and other grantmaking agencies, the grant review process, tailoring ideas to the grantmaker's priorities, research design, development of training and mentoring plans, and budgeting.

POIR-622.description: Determinants, nature, and consequences of political attitudes and behavior exploring psychological-sociological models, political socialization and learning, and factors affecting trends in attitudes and behavior. POIR-644.description: Development of global state of affairs including foundations of political order and economic growth, formation of states in global perspective, survival of non-democracies and adopting inclusive institutions.

PORT-150.title: Portuguese II
PORT-150.description: For students with some language proficiency in Portuguese; increased emphasis on listening, comprehension, oral communication, reading, and writing. Students will be required to take a Portuguese placement exam in the Spanish and Portuguese Department. Prerequisite: PORT 120.

PORT-175.title: Accelerated Portuguese I
PORT-175.description: Encourages rapid acquisition through intensive exposure to Portuguese while following a proficiency-oriented approach. Recommended for students with a background in Spanish or another Romance language.

PORT-240.title: Portuguese IV
PORT-240.description: Four-skills course with review of grammar. Writing and reading intensive. Authentic materials related to Lusobrazilian culture and civilization.

PORT-250.title: Visions of Brazil
PORT-250.description: Comparative study of Brazil in the context of the Lusophone (Portuguese-speaking) world, especially Portugal's former colonies in Africa. Materials drawn from literature, visual culture, music and cultural theory.

POSC-110.title: Ideology and Political Conflict
POSC-110.description: Modern political ideologies; their assumptions, perceptions, and prescriptions regarding political stability and social injustice:anarchism, communism, socialism, liberalism, conservatism, and fascism.

POSC-120.title: Comparative Politics
POSC-120.description: Gateway to the major in political science. Comparative analysis of political institutions and processes in selected industrial, developing and socialist countries, in terms of contrasting ideologies, parties, elites, and economies.

POSC-130.title: Law, Politics and Public Policy
POSC-130.description: Interaction between law and politics; overview of the American legal system; value conflicts and public policy questions which arise within it.

POSC-201.title: Law and Politics
POSC-201.description: Examination of the rules and realities of American politics, and the role politics plays in American life and culture.

POSC-248.title: Human Rights
POSC-248.description: Overview of human rights controversies across the globe. Introduction to techniques of analysis for social issues, interdisciplinary research methods, and interpretation of complex political problems.

POSC-311.title: Political Analysis
POSC-311.description: Methodological and theoretical problems of micro-analytic studies in political science. Techniques of data collection and assimilation.

POSC-325.title: State Politics
POSC-325.description: American state politics from a comparative perspective. Examines political processes, differing policy outcomes and the impact of social change on system performance.

POSC-326.title: Case Studies in Modern Leadership
POSC-326.description: Study of a single leader or small set of leaders, including the strengths and weaknesses that distinguish them and the cultural forces that nurture them.

POSC-329.title: Korean American Politics
POSC-329.description: Exploration of critical issues in U.S. politics through the lens of Korean Americans.

POSC-335.title: Political Parties, Campaigns, and Elections
POSC-335.description: Organization and function of political parties, nominations and elections, strategy and tactics of campaigning, professional candidate management finance, political machines, voting behavior.

POSC-340.title: Constitutional Law
POSC-340.description: Development of constitutional law by the courts; leading cases bearing on major constitutional issues; the federal system; powers of government; civil liberties.

POSC-347.title: Environmental Law
POSC-347.description: Introduces students to central concepts and theories in environmental law and regulation; analyzes present environmental laws and regulations.

POSC-357.title: Urban Politics in the Global South
POSC-357.description: Examination of social and economic justice in the questions of urban governance facing cities in the developing world.

POSC-359.title: The Politics of Food
POSC-359.description: Use food as a lens to analyze the social and political world.

POSC-363.title: Cities and Regions in World Politics
POSC-363.description: Cities and the rise of states; globalization and localization; federalism and decentralization; comparative politics of urban regions in developed and developing countries. Recommended preparation: comparative or urban politics.

POSC-371.title: European Political Thought II
POSC-371.description: Western political thought since the French Revolution. Rise of Marxist socialism, communism, anarchism, fascism, National Socialism, other doctrines; the democratic tradition; new theories of the state.

POSC-395.title: Directed Governmental and Political Leadership Internship
POSC-395.description: Intensive experience in governmental and political offices. Minimum time requirement; evaluation by office and intern report required.

POSC-396.title: California Policy Research Internship
POSC-396.description: Conducting extensive research and analysis on a major public policy challenge facing California.

POSC-397.title: Field Research in Human Rights
POSC-397.description: Conducting human rights research and policy work in the field
POSC-397.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Sophomore, Junior, Senior

POSC-398.title: Trial Advocacy: Theory and Practice
POSC-398.description: Course covering substantive law, evidence, public speaking and use of societal mores in courtroom advocacy. Open only to Mock Trial team members.

POSC-438.title: How Washington Really Works
POSC-438.description: Provides students with a DC insider's understanding of American politics, campaigning and elections.
POSC-438.prereqText: Class standing: not open to Freshman

POSC-439.title: Critical Issues in American Politics
POSC-439.description: Intensive examination of critical issues of particular interest in the field of American politics.

POSC-442.title: The Politics of Human Differences: Diversity and Discriminat
POSC-442.description: A comparative perspective on social and cultural forces that affect American laws and policies concerning discrimination on the basis of race or ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation, age, and disability.

POSC-443.title: Law in Film
POSC-443.description: Analysis of the depiction of law in film; use of film to explore topics in jurisprudence and the politics of law and courts. Recommended preparation: POSC 130

POSC-444.title: Civil and Political Rights and Liberties
POSC-444.description: An examination of debates and controversies surrounding the nature and scope of civil rights and civil liberties.

POSC-447.title: Global Justice: Interdisciplinary Perspectives
POSC-447.description: Classical and contemporary theories of justice, from an interdisciplinary perspective.

POSC-449.title: Political Psychology
POSC-449.description: Psychological forces shaping politics and persons, processes and interactions; emphasis on political socialization and cognitive and effective orientations to politics.

POSC-452.title: Critical Issues in Law and Public Policy
POSC-452.description: Intensive examination of special topics in the field of law and public policy.

POSC-456.title: Women in International Development
POSC-456.description: How various developmental theories analyze the role of women as producers and how Third World women are increasing their role in development.

POSC-469.title: Critical Issues in Comparative Politics
POSC-469.description: Intensive examination of critical issues of particular interest in the field of comparative politics.

POSC-490.title: Directed Research
POSC-490.description: Individual research and readings. Not available for graduate credit.
POSC-490.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Junior, Senior

PPD-225.title: Solving Public Problems
PPD-225.description: Develops a framework for understanding public policy and its role in solving current complex issues. Theories, processes and institutions that shape policymaking and professional development for policymaking. Course sections may vary in policy subject emphasis.

PPD-240.title: Citizenship and Public Ethics
PPD-240.description: Review of legal and ethical traditions of citizenship withemphasis on the latter; consideration of implications for currentpractice of public policy-making and management.

PPD-245.title: The Urban Context
PPD-245.description: The urban context for planning and policy decisions. Socioeconomic, physical and spatial structure of cities; and the underlying demographic, economic and social processes that drive their ongoing transformation.

PPD-300.title: Social Justice Issues in Public Policy and Urban Planning
PPD-300.description: Social justice issues through the lens of public policy and urban planning with main focus on Los Angeles; critical thinking skills about the fields and their relevance to social justice.

PPD-301.title: PPD Practices: Internship Seminar
PPD-301.description: Policy, planning, and development skills for practice; internship seminar; leadership, group dynamics and presentation skills; application of management; organizational diversity; reflection on experiences.

PPD-303.title: Statistics for Policy, Planning, and Development
PPD-303.description: Statistical applications applied to the real world; techniques including probability, sampling; hypothesis formation and testing; correlation, and linear regression.

PPD-314.title: Public Policy and Law
PPD-314.description: Institutional foundations and analysis of public policy issues; policy formulation and implementation; application of theories; case analyses.

PPD-315.title: Analytic Foundations for Public Policy
PPD-315.description: Qualitative methods of analysis; ethical and political implications of policy choices; issue diagnosis and policy design skills; critical reasoning and ethics; policy leadership.

PPD-321.title: Behavioral Insights for Policy Makers
PPD-321.description: Climate change, public health, and other societal issues require behavior change. Learn how to design communications and behavior-change interventions, and how to evaluate their effectiveness.

PPD-325.title: Fundamentals of Health Policy and Management
PPD-325.description: Learning the institutions of health care delivery and financing; evaluating key health policy issues; understanding and using economic, statistical and mathematical tools as ways to inform health policy issues.

PPD-330.title: Introduction to Health Care Systems
PPD-330.description: Concepts and determinants of health and illness; health care delivery organizations and programs; the role of the administrator; issues in health care financing and access; quality evaluation; future trends.

PPD-345.title: AI and Urban Planning
PPD-345.description: Exploration of the core concepts and use of AI in urban planning; developments in the field; urban applications; assessment of AI's ethics, equity and impact

PPD-357.title: Government and Business
PPD-357.description: Interrelated roles of business and public institutions; effects of public policies and laws on business sector; incorporates public and business perspectives.

PPD-363.title: Mapping Urban Data for Social Change
PPD-363.description: Examines the power of maps to catalyze action for social change or disenfranchise populations and operationalize racism. Experiments with GIS and Adobe for critical cartography.

PPD-371.title: The Nonprofit Sector and the Public Interest
PPD-371.description: Theories of the voluntary nonprofit sector in society and its relationship to government and business; public policies toward the sector.

PPD-400.title: Topics in Public Policy and Urban Studies
PPD-400.description: Seminar in cross cutting topics in public policy and urban studies that engages students with faculty and scholars in interdisciplinary research and analysis of key problems and issues in the fields.
PPD-400.prereqText:
Major: open only to Public Policy, Urban Studies and Planning
School: open only to Sol Price School of Public Policy

PPD-402.title: Management of Public and Nonprofit Organizations
PPD-402.description: Contemporary management theory; the nature of complex organizations' organizational and intergovernmental arrangements; roles and responsibilities of managers; managerial and organizational effectiveness; organizational structure and dynamics.

PPD-407.title: Financial Management of Public and Nonprofit Organizations
PPD-407.description: Time value of money, risk, government bonds and tax-exempt financing, cost of capital, budgeting, financial statement analysis, and working capital management.

PPD-410.title: Comparative Urban Development
PPD-410.description: Urbanization and urban development and growth through an international scope; globalizing cities.

PPD-412.title: Geodesign Practicum
PPD-412.description: Application of design concepts, planning protocols and spatial analysis skills to a complex planning or design problem sponsored by a local public, private or not-for-profit client in a studio setting.
PPD-412.prereqText:
Prerequisite: ARCH 403 or RED 425
Corequisite: SSCI 381 or SSCI 382
Class standing: open only to Senior
Major: open only to Geodesign

PPD-414.title: Community Health Policy and Planning
PPD-414.description: Historical perspectives on and the contemporary practice of community health planning; impact of culture, socioeconomics, and environment; policy dimensions; urban plannings role in enhancing and sustaining health.

PPD-415.title: Health Policy
PPD-415.description: Health policy analysis and challenges; price of health; structure of major sectors in health care; role of insurance in policy debates; trade-offs with policy decisions.

PPD-422.title: Transportation Data and Automation
PPD-422.description: Introduction of the role that technology will play in facilitating shared mobility, disrupting transportation markets, and reshaping multi-modal urban transportation systems; analyses of governance issues; the interaction between private markets and regulators; changes in the nature of infrastructure and urban planning that will be required to accommodate the wired future of transportation.

PPD-427.title: Geographic Information Systems and Planning      Applications
PPD-427.description: Basic GIS concepts, ArcView and other GIS software, planning applications and databases, basic cartography; students select, research and prepare a planning GIS analysis project.

PPD-431.title: Undergraduate Policy, Planning, and Development Studio
PPD-431.description: Application of methods in the exploration of a specific project, policy, or organization from the multiple perspectives of the five tracks in the undergraduate program.
PPD-431.prereqText:
Class standing: open only to Junior, Senior
Major: open only to Public Policy, Real Estate Development, Urban Studies and Planning

PSYC-100.title: Introduction to Psychology
PSYC-100.description: Introduction to psychological science, including historical and contemporary approaches. Behavior examined from biological, cognitive, social, developmental, and personality perspectives. Disorders and treatments.

PSYC-165.title: Drugs, Behavior, and Society
PSYC-165.description: An integrative systems perspective of drugs; including their historical, economic, and cultural importance, psychopharmacology, addiction, relationship to crime, and therapeutic use in treating psychological disorders.

PSYC-215.title: Music, Mind and the Brain
PSYC-215.description: An interdisciplinary approach to music, mind and brain. Explores music as an object with its own properties and as a form of human behavior.

PSYC-240.title: Scientific Inquiry and Reasoning in Health Care
PSYC-240.description: Critical analysis and reasoning skills required to solve scientific problems in human behavior, including presentation of data, logic of research design, statistics, and research ethics. Not for major credit for Psychology majors.

PSYC-250.title: Natural and Artificial Intelligence
PSYC-250.description: Introduces core ideas in artificial intelligence (AI) as emerging from a dialogue between psychology, neuroscience, and computer science with an emphasis on quantitative reasoning.

PSYC-274.title: Statistics
PSYC-274.description: Introduction to the use of statistics in psychology: basic ideas in measurement; frequency distributions; descriptive statistics; concepts and procedures in statistical inference.

PSYC-301.title: Cognitive Processes
PSYC-301.description: Experimental and theoretical aspects of human memory, perception, thinking, and language. Lectures, demonstrations, and individual experiments. Prerequisite: 100g or departmental approval.

PSYC-304.title: Sensation and Perception
PSYC-304.description: Receptor processes and stimulus organization; traditional topics in the perception of objects, space, time. Laboratory demonstrations and exercises.

PSYC-305.title: Learning and Memory
PSYC-305.description: Principles involved in classical and operant conditioning. Concentration on basic causes of behavior; consideration of the relevance of simple behavioral laws to complicated human behavior.

PSYC-314.title: Experimental Research Methods
PSYC-314.description: Experimental research methods in psychology; nature and concepts of scientific method.

PSYC-316.title: Non-Experimental Research Methods
PSYC-316.description: Non-experimental research methods in psychology. Observational, survey and data analysis exercises

PSYC-326.title: Behavioral Neuroscience
PSYC-326.description: Neural bases of behavior. Concentration on sensory and motor processes and the interaction of neural, chemical, and hormonal systems.

PSYC-336.title: Developmental Psychology
PSYC-336.description: Child and adolescent behavior and associated theories; exploration of the continuity between child and adult behavior. Laboratory projects.

PSYC-339.title: Origins of the Mind
PSYC-339.description: Exploration of ancient philosophical questions concerning the origins of human knowledge through empirical studies of infants, animals, and adults from diverse cultures.

PSYC-353.title: Close Relationships
PSYC-353.description: Scientific perspective of close relationships: intimate relationships, friendships and others, evolutionary and biological bases of attraction and love, historical, social , cultural influences. Prerequisite: PSYC 100. (Duplicates credit in PSYC 359)

PSYC-355.title: Social Psychology
PSYC-355.description: Theoretical and experimental analysis of human behavior. Social processes involved in attitudes, conformity, compliance, interpersonal perception, liking, affiliation, aggression, altruism, and group dynamics.

PSYC-360.title: Psychological Disorders
PSYC-360.description: The commonly diagnosed behavior pathologies; biological, social, cultural and developmental antecedents of abnormal behavior; principles of learning, perception and motivation, as they relate to psychopathology.

PSYC-361.title: Introduction to Clinical Psychology
PSYC-361.description: Introduction to the scientist-practitioner model of clinical psychology, including research methods, psychological assessment and diagnosis, psychotherapeutic interventions, and treatment of special populations.

PSYC-365.title: Introduction to Forensic Psychology
PSYC-365.description: Survey of current topics, technologies and techniques. Students acquire a basic understanding of how forensic psychologists contribute their unique expertise to the American legal system. Prerequisites: PSYC 100. Duplicates credit in former PSYC 465.

PSYC-367.title: Stress, Health, and the Mind-Body Connection
PSYC-367.description: Introduction to psychological, biological and behavioral processes affecting physical health, including stress, coping with disease, health behaviors and socioeconomic and cultural influences on health.
PSYC-367.prereqText:
Prerequisite: PSYC 100
Major: open only to Health and the Human Sciences, Psychology, Social Sciences (Psychology)

PSYC-372.title: Human Sexuality
PSYC-372.description: Psychological and physiological base of sexuality; gender identity, childbearing, birth control, venereal diseases; dysfunctions and treatments.

PSYC-380.title: Junior Honors Seminar
PSYC-380.description: Advanced study of scientific inquiry in psychology with in-depth analysis of current research by faculty in the Psychology Department. Preparation for senior honors thesis research. Prerequisite: acceptance in Psychology Undergraduate Honors Program and consent of instructor.
PSYC-380.prereqText:
Corequisite: PSYC 314
Class standing: open only to Junior, Senior

PSYC-424.title: Neuropsychology
PSYC-424.description: Effects of brain damage on human behavior and abilities, particularly language, memory, and emotion.
PSYC-424.prereqText:
Prerequisite: PSYC 100
Class standing: open only to Junior, Senior, Senior (Fifth Year)

PSYC-426.title: Motivated Behaviors and Addiction
PSYC-426.description: Social, environmental, and physiological influences on behaviors associated with aggression, eating, reproduction, and sleep. Will focus on behavioral disorders such as addiction.
PSYC-426.prereqText:
Prerequisite: PSYC 314
Recommended preparation: Junior or Senior Standing

PSYC-427.title: Neuropsychopharmacology
PSYC-427.description: Pharmo-chemical nature of the brain; diseases of the brain and drug treatments. Recommended Preparation: background in biological psychology, biology and/or neuroscience.
PSYC-427.prereqText:
Prerequisite: PSYC 100
Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student, Master Student, Junior, Senior

PSYC-430.title: Social Development of Infants, Children and Adolescents
PSYC-430.description: An analysis of selected topics and issues in child social development. Recommended preparation: PSYC 274, PSYC 314, PSYC 336.

PSYC-432.title: From Eugenics to Neurodiversity: History of DisAbility
PSYC-432.description: An introductory overview of the primary historical issues, questions, concerns and developments that directly impact our current thought and action around disability and inclusion of disabled people in society.

PSYC-433.title: Children's Learning and Cognitive Development
PSYC-433.description: Principles of learning and cognitive development from infancy through adolescence. Prerequisite 336.

PSYC-437.title: Adolescent Development
PSYC-437.description: The adolescent years from both an applied and a research-oriented perspective. Topics include physical, cognitive, and moral development; socialization; and sexual and sex-role development.

PSYC-439.title: Science of Yoga and Meditation
PSYC-439.description: Reviews intersection between modern science and ancient contemplative practices of yoga and meditation. Explores mind-body-spirit connection through personal practice, review of contemplative texts and empirical research.

PSYC-440.title: Foundations of  Cognitive Neuroscience
PSYC-440.description: Introduction to the major components of cognition (perception, memory, intelligence) in terms of the neural coding characteristic of the relevant brain areas.

PSYC-452.title: Social Neuroscience
PSYC-452.description: Overview of principles and research in social neuroscience, which uses neuroscience approaches to inform social processes including empathy, inter-group relations, emotion, morality and social decision-making.

PSYC-454.title: Social Cognition
PSYC-454.description: Theory and research on cognitive processes in social behavior, to include social inference, cognition and emotion, the Self, social categorization, person memory, and attribution processes. Recommended preparation: PSYC-355.

PSYC-455.title: Cognitive Behavior Therapy
PSYC-455.description: The philosophical, ethical, historical, theoretical and procedural aspects of cognitive behavior therapy (CBT), including how theory guides practice and how practice informs theory.

PSYC-464.title: Psychology of Marriage and the Family
PSYC-464.description: Theories and research on family relationships across the life span, including research methods, cultural and developmental perspectives, communication, conflict, attachment, individual psychopathology, and family violence.

PSYC-467.title: Introduction to Autism Spectrum Disorder
PSYC-467.description: A comprehensive overview of the assessment, diagnosis and treatment of individuals diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder.

PSYC-468.title: Happiness:  Research in Neuroscience and Positive Psychology
PSYC-468.description: Neuroscientific and psychological perspectives that investigate the basis of happiness and well-being.

PSYC-470.title: Health and Mental Health Research in Mauritius
PSYC-470.description: Explores research design, existing health and mental health studies and research programs in Mauritius, unique challenges of conducting international research and ethical considerations in human subjects research.

PSYC-480.title: Senior Honors Seminar
PSYC-480.description: Advanced study of empirical approaches in psychology. Progress presentations and evaluations of Senior Honors Thesis research. In-depth exploration of issues in science. Not available for graduate credit.
PSYC-480.prereqText:
Class standing: open only to Senior
Major: open only to Psychology

PSYC-490.title: Directed Research
PSYC-490.description: Individual research and readings. Not available for graduate credit.
PSYC-490.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Junior, Senior

PSYC-499.title: Special Topics
PSYC-499.description: Selected topics in the various specialty areas within psychology. Topic will vary from semester to semester.

PSYC-503.title: Regression and the General Linear Model
PSYC-503.description: Multiple regression as a tool in experimental and non-experimental data; analysis of variance and covariance as regression on coded variables. Computer applications. Laboratory exercises.

PSYC-505.title: Research Methods in Applied Social Psychology
PSYC-505.description: Various research techniques that are useful in a variety of different real world settings, such as business, governmental agencies and charities. Open only to M.S., Applied Psychology students.
PSYC-505.prereqText:
Class standing: open only to Master Student
Major: open only to Applied Psychology

PSYC-509.title: Qualitative Research Methods in Applied Psychology
PSYC-509.description: Examines qualitative research in applied settings. Learn to design, execute and report qualitative research in response to stakeholder needs.
PSYC-509.prereqText:
Corequisite: PSYC 505
Class standing: open only to Master Student
Major: open only to Applied Psychology

PSYC-517.title: Group Dynamics and Leadership
PSYC-517.description: Theory and research on effective teams and characteristics of strong leaders. Negotiation, morale-building, managing expectancies, utilization of cultural diversity as a strength. Open only to M.S., Applied Psychology students.
PSYC-517.prereqText:
Class standing: open only to Master Student
Major: open only to Applied Psychology

PSYC-521.title: Cross Cultural Psychology in Applied Settings
PSYC-521.description: Examination of major theoretical frameworks mapping worldwide cultures and values with a focus on applying thatknowledge in organizations. Open only to master students in Applied Psychology.
PSYC-521.prereqText:
Class standing: open only to Master Student
Major: open only to Applied Psychology

PSYC-523.title: User Experience (UX) Research
PSYC-523.description: Provides a broad introduction to the social science methods UX researchers most commonly use, including qualitative approaches, and quantitative approaches.
PSYC-523.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Master Student

PSYC-535.title: Research Methods in Behavior Analysis
PSYC-535.description: Survey of methods for measuring behavior. Examines theoretical background for single subject research methods, practical application of research methods to treatment evaluation, and analyzes strengths and limitations of single subject research methods.

PSYC-536.title: Behavioral Interventions
PSYC-536.description: Examines empirically supported behavioral interventions across a range of socially relevant behavioral excesses, skill deficits, disorders, and age ranges. Focuses on least-intrusive, person-centered approaches.

PSYC-537.title: Organizational Behavior Management
PSYC-537.description: Surveys evidence-based practices in the application of behavioral principles of learning and motivation to assessing and supporting organizational behavior change.

PSYC-539.title: Behavioral Approaches to Skill Acquisition
PSYC-539.description: Examines contemporary research on behavioral procedures for teaching complex skills to individuals of a variety ages and populations, including language, social, cognitive, vocational, and independent living skills.

PSYC-541.title: Experimental Analysis of Behavior
PSYC-541.description: Examines a collection of experimental procedures and findings within the experimental analysis of behavior (EAB); basic principles of operant and respondent learning and motivation; translate findings of basic research to the development of applied sciences of behavior change.
PSYC-541.prereqText:
Class standing: open only to Master Student
Major: open only to Applied Behavior Analysis
School: open only to Dana and David Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences

PSYC-550A.title: Proseminar in Human Behavior
PSYC-550A.description: The nature of the human mind, social interactions, conflicts, cooperative behavior, mutual influence and effectiveness. Application of psychological principles to the dynamics of commercial entities. Open only to M.S., Applied Psychology students.
PSYC-550A.prereqText:
Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student, Master Student
Major: open only to Applied Psychology

PSYC-550B.title: Proseminar in Human Behavior
PSYC-550B.description: Application of psychological principles to the dynamics of commercial entities. Develop practical skills with a focus on professional development.

Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student, Master Student
Major: open only to Applied Psychology

PSYC-552.title: Principles of Consumer Psychology
PSYC-552.description: Examination of the attitudes and decisions of consumers, and how to effectively reach consumers by using persuasion and proper positioning in the marketplace. Open only to M.S., Applied Psychology students.

Class standing: open only to Master Student
Major: open only to Applied Psychology

PSYC-555.title: Introduction to Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging
PSYC-555.description: The physical and physiological bases of MRI and fMRI. Design and analysis of fMRI experiments. Operation of a magnetic resonance imaging system.

PSYC-556.title: Psychology of Interactive Media
PSYC-556.description: Examination of the diverse methods of communicating with a target audience with a special emphasis on the newest computer-based tools for providing information and influence.
PSYC-556.prereqText:

PSYC-565.title: Organizational Psychology

PSYC-565.prereqText:
Class standing: open only to Master Student
Major: open only to Applied Psychology

PSYC-566.title: The Psychology of Employee Selection and Assessment
PSYC-566.description: Develop an understanding of recruitment and selection practices, processes, and approaches into the strategic role that recruitment and selection plays in organizational success.
PSYC-566.prereqText:
Prerequisite: PSYC 565
Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student, Master Student
Major: open only to Applied Psychology

PSYC-570.title: Organizational Program Design and Evaluation
PSYC-570.description: Consulting-focused course on program design and evaluation: diagnose needs, benchmarking, build logic models, define program components, plan implementation, design measurement, evaluate impact, deliver client-ready recommendations.

PSYC-577.title: Analysis of Covariance Structures
PSYC-577.description: Multivariate analysis of non-experimental data, including structural equation modeling, path analysis, and confirmatory factor analysis. Computer applications using variety of optimization routines and purpose-written software.

PSYC-578.title: Workshop in Quantitative Methods
PSYC-578.description: Practical, hands-on experience in the application of selected quantitative methods to empirical data. Includes training in the use of relevant computer software.

PSYC-580.title: Applied Research Design
PSYC-580.description: Supports students on their capstone treatise, allowing them to consider topics, ideate on research design, develop a proposal and draft a treatise protocol.

PSYC-587.title: Practicum in Applied Behavior Analysis
PSYC-587.description: Provides supervised practical experience in implementing behavior analytic assessment and treatment services. Meets supervision requirements for the Board Certified Behavior Analyst exam. Students meet with course instructor to present and discuss cases for two hours per week every semester, including one summer session. Practicum hours in the field vary from 18-20 hours per week during the academic year to 30 hours per week during the summer.

PSYC-588.title: Capstone Project in Behavior Analysis
PSYC-588.description: Supervision for completing independent project, consisting of practical treatment evaluation, program development, or literature review.

PSYC-589.title: Interprofessional Education and Collaboration for Geriatrics
PSYC-589.description: Students from multiple health professions learn about aging and collaborative team care through a combination of didactic and experiential learning working in a community-based setting.

PSYC-597.description: Part-time or full-time, practical work experience in the students field of study. The internship must be located at an off-campus facility. PSYC-612.title: Seminar in Advanced Social Psychology
PSYC-612.description: An intensive consideration of selected concepts, theories, and research problems in social psychology.

PSYC-619.title: Psychological Intervention
PSYC-619.description: Study of clinical psychological treatment: Research and theory about major psychological approaches to intervention. (One of 4 clinical psychology core courses: PSYC 514, PSYC 515, PSYC 619, PSYC 620.)

PSYC-627.title: Machine Cognition
PSYC-627.description: Explores Machine Cognition, tracing AI's history from symbolic systems to LLMs, analyzing emergent capabilities and the philosophical questions of artificial minds.
PSYC-627.prereqText: Recommended preparation: For Non-Engineering majors: Psych 625 or a similar course, for Engineering students: CSCI 544 or a similar course.

PSYC-691B.title: Internship in Clinical Psychology
PSYC-691B.description: Supervised clinical work in an approved mental health setting. Graded CR/NC. Prerequisite: Good standing in clinical program and departmental approval.

PSYC-695.title: Advanced Practicum in Clinical Psychology
PSYC-695.description: Didactic practicum combining theory and research on psychological intervention with clinical practice in assessment and treatment, focused on particular client groups or disorders. Graded CR/NC.

PSYC-696.description: Externship for Practical Training is for clinical-related training experience in the students fieldof study. Students are individually supervised at their site.

PT-529.description: Introduction to sensorimotor systems, overview of current perspectives in motor control from fetus through late adulthood, and clinical tests of motor proficiency.

PT-530A.title: Therapeutic Exercise
PT-530A.description: Theoretical and practical principles for evaluation of exercise need and prescription of exercise programs. Emphasis on approaches for patients with musculoskeletal deficits.
PT-530A.prereqText:
Prerequisite: PT 509; PT 514; PT 521
Duplicates credit: former PT 530

PT-546.title: Neuropathology
PT-546.description: Pathology in the central and peripheral nervous systems that alter motor and sensory performance. Emphasis on loss of motion, excessive and involuntary movement disorders.
PT-546.prereqText:

Corequisite: PT 529; PT 569; PT 581

PT-554.title: Analytical Anatomy
PT-554.description: Detailed kinesiologic analysis of axial, spine, head, neck, face and bulbar muscles. Lecture, laboratory and clinical demonstration.

PT-561B.title: Evidence for Physical Therapist Practice
PT-561B.description: Introduction to acquiring, appraising and integrating research evidence.

PT-561D.title: Evidence for Physical Therapist Practice
PT-561D.description: Advanced integration of patient values as influenced by culture, ethnicity, lifestyles, gender, and age into patient-centered clinical decision making.

PT-566.title: Disorders of the Musculoskeletal System
PT-566.description: Regional description of pathology and pathophysiological mechanisms of disorders of bone, connective tissue, and joints. Lecture, demonstration.

PT-569.title: Fundamentals of Neuroscience
PT-569.description: Detailed analysis of neurophysiologic mechanisms underlying normal and abnormal motor and sensory function.

PT-574.title: Clinical Biomechanics
PT-574.description: Introduction to the principles of biomechanics (statics, dynamics) as they apply to physical therapy practice. Emphasis on tissue mechanics, joint function and gait.

PT-581.title: Clinical Management of the Patient with Neurological Dysfunc
PT-581.description: Physical therapy theory and methods for intervention in neurological dysfunction.
PT-581.prereqText:

Corequisite: PT 529; PT 546; PT 569

PT-583.title: Clinical Electrophysiology
PT-583.description: Use of electrical currents to evaluate and treat musculoskeletal, neurological and wound disorders. Theory and practice.

PT-600A.description: Practical experience in two- or six-week physical therapy manual skills, decision making and professional behaviors.

PT-621.title: Clinical Management of the Patient with Musculoskeletal Dysfunction
PT-621.description: Physical therapy theory and methods of evaluation and treatment of orthopedic dysfunction. Lecture, demonstration, laboratory. Dissection lab available.

PT-630.description: Advanced evaluation and management of patients with movement dysfunction spanning all diagnoses seen by physical therapists.

PT-632.description: Integration of physical therapy management of complicated patients with concurrent musculoskeletal, cardiopulmonary and/or neurologic disorders.

PT-640B.description: Advanced evaluation and management of patients with movement dysfunction spanning all diagnoses seen by physical therapists (musculoskeletal conditions focus on lower quarter body regions).

PT-642B.description: Integration of physical therapy management of complicated patients with concurrent musculoskeletal (concentrating on lower quarter body regions), cardiopulmonary and/or neurologic disorders.

PT-660.description: A 16-week clerkship consisting of a minimum of 24 hours per week in a part-time setting. Emphasis on the care of orthopedic, neurologic, pediatric or complicated medical conditions.

PT-670B.description: A 13-week clerkship consisting of a minimum of 36 hours per week in a full-time setting. Emphasis on care of orthopedic, neurologic, pediatric or complicated medical conditions.
