PTE-520.description: Understanding deep learning: for students in engineering, physical and life sciences and computer science with mathematical background.

PTE-533.title: Drilling, Completion, and Production Engineering
PTE-533.description: Theory and practice of well drilling and completion technologies. Includes physical properties of rocks and fluids, artificial lift methods, decline analysis, fracturing, and well stimulation.

SOWK-536.description: A study of the complex and interconnecting systems of policy, programs and communities that directly and indirectly impact Social Workers' clients lives. (Duplicates credit in SOWK 534)

SOWK-546.title: Science of Social Work
SOWK-546.description: Introduction to the role of scientific inquiry in advancing social work goals. Inspires students to include science in their social work identity and professional decision-making. (Duplicates credit in SOWK 562)

SOWK-591.title: Applied Learning in Practicum Education I
SOWK-591.description: Practicum seminar and placement for developing foundational skills in integrative social work practice with individuals, families, groups, communities and/or organizations.
SOWK-591.prereqText:
Concurrent enrollment: SOWK 523
Duplicates credit: SOWK 589a

SOWK-593.title: Applied Learning in Practicum Education II
SOWK-593.description: Practicum seminar and placement for developing foundational skills in integrative social work practice with individuals, families, groups, communities and/or organizations.
SOWK-593.prereqText:
Concurrent enrollment: SOWK 525
Duplicates credit: SOWK 589b

SOWK-603.title: The Transforming Power of Social Work and Sports
SOWK-603.description: The power of social work and sports to promote well-being, inclusivity and personal growth. This dynamic partnership fosters positive change within individuals, communities and society.

SOWK-608.title: Research and Evaluation in Integrative Social Work Practice
SOWK-608.description: Critical analysis and application of empirical evidence and research methods to assess client strengths and needs and to evaluate and improve integrative social work practice.

SOWK-609.title: Advanced ISW Practice II: Schools and Educational Settings
SOWK-609.description: Critical application of theory, evidence and professional standards for integrative and culturally responsive assessment and intervention, highlighting practice contexts involving schools and educational settings
SOWK-609.prereqText: Prerequisite: SOWK 614 or SOWK 627 or SOWK 643 or SOWK 686

SOWK-612.title: Assessment and Diagnosis of Mental Disorders
SOWK-612.description: Assessment of mental disorders, and the rationale and organization of the system for diagnosis. Emphasis is on developing differential diagnostic skills.

SOWK-614.title: Advanced ISW Practice I: Schools and Educational Settings
SOWK-614.description: Advanced policy analysis, engagement strategies and human rights advocacy in integrative social work, highlighting practice contexts involving schools and educational settings
SOWK-614.prereqText: Recommended preparation: Introductory coursework in integrative social work or comparable preparation as determined by the program

SOWK-615.title: Brief Therapy and Crisis Intervention
SOWK-615.description: Theory and multimodal approaches for brief therapy and crisis intervention with a broad spectrum of clients in a range of mental health and health settings.

SOWK-617.title: Substance Related and Behavioral Addictive Disorders and Rec
SOWK-617.description: Causal exploration of substance related and behavioral addictive disorders. Evidence-based and practice informed treatment models for vulnerable individuals, groups and families.

SOWK-627.title: Advanced ISW Practice I: Children, Youth and Families
SOWK-627.description: Advanced policy analysis, engagement strategies and human rights advocacy in integrative social work, highlighting practice contexts involving children, youth and families.

SOWK-630.title: Self-Awareness and Intercultural Humility in  Social Work
SOWK-630.description: Critical exploration of sociocultural context and one's own values/assumptions/biases to enhance intercultural humility in social work.

SOWK-642.title: Advanced ISW Practice II: Children, Youth and Families
SOWK-642.description: Critical application of theory, evidence and professional standards for integrative and culturally responsive assessment and intervention, highlighting practice contexts involving children, youth and families.
SOWK-642.prereqText: Prerequisite: SOWK 614 or SOWK 627 or SOWK 643 or SOWK 686

SOWK-643.title: Advanced ISW Practice I: Adult Mental Health and Wellness
SOWK-643.description: Advanced policy analysis, engagement strategies and human rights advocacy in integrative social work, highlighting practice contexts involving adult mental health and wellness.

SOWK-647.title: Advanced ISW Practice II: Adult Mental Health and Wellness
SOWK-647.description: Critical application of theory, evidence and professional standards for integrative and culturally responsive assessment and intervention, highlighting practice contexts involving adult mental health and wellness.

SOWK-651.title: Clinical Psychopharmacology for Social Workers
SOWK-651.description: Understanding major psychoactive drugs used in treatment of psychological and behavioral disorders in behavioral and primary care medical settings. Theoretical/practical approaches to treatment are examined.
SOWK-651.prereqText:
Prerequisite: SOWK 506
Class standing: open only to Master Student
School: open only to Suzanne Dworak-Peck School of Social Work

SOWK-656.title: National Military Immersion in Washington, DC: Military and
SOWK-656.description: A short study at the campus, online, and in Washington, DC addressing policies and programs for military members, veterans, and their families.

SOWK-665.title: Grant Writing and Program Development for Social Workers
SOWK-665.description: Grant writing and program development that are generalized to any settings and relevant to direct and macro social work practice expertise.
SOWK-665.prereqText:
Prerequisite: SOWK 503 or SOWK 506; SOWK 505 or SOWK 506; SOWK 534 or SOWK 536; SOWK 535 or SOWK 536
Class standing: open only to Master Student
School: open only to Suzanne Dworak-Peck School of Social Work

SOWK-677.title: Mental Health Assessment and Diagnosis of Children and Adole
SOWK-677.description: Mental health assessment and diagnosis of children and adolescents. Course includes relevant diagnoses and the systematic or societal challenges that impact mental health of youth.

SOWK-686.title: Advanced ISW Practice I: Military and Veteran Social Work
SOWK-686.description: Advanced policy analysis, engagement strategies and human rights advocacy in integrative social work, highlighting practice contexts involving military and veteran social work.

SOWK-689.title: Advanced ISW Practice II: Military and Veteran Social Work
SOWK-689.description: Critical application of theory, evidence and professional standards for integrative and culturally responsive assessment, and intervention highlighting practice contexts involving military and veteran social work.
SOWK-689.prereqText: Prerequisite: SOWK 614 or SOWK 627 or SOWK 643 or SOWK 686

SOWK-691.title: Applied Learning In Practicum Education III
SOWK-691.description: Practicum seminar and placement for developing advanced skills in integrative social work practice with individuals, families, groups, communities and/or organizations.

SOWK-693.title: Applied Learning in Practicum Education IV
SOWK-693.description: Practicum seminar and placement for developing advanced skills in integrative social work practice with individuals, families, groups, communities and/or organizations.

SOWK-697.title: Advanced Clinical Social Work Practice Certificate Lab
SOWK-697.description: Clinical practice lab designed to strengthen clinical social work practice skills grounded in professional values and ethics.

SOWK-704.title: Complex Social Problems
SOWK-704.description: Emphasizes leadership in addressing systemic social challenges.

SOWK-705.title: Leadership and Strategic Communication for Stakeholder Engag
SOWK-705.description: Leading public discourse for the purposes of increasing civic engagement and public participation, building broad based public support and enabling competencies.

SOWK-706.title: Leadership for Intervention Implementation in Complex System
SOWK-706.description: Examining large scale national, state and local intervention programs as well as modeling potential organizational redesign to improve service delivery strategies.

SOWK-707.title: Financial Management for Social Change
SOWK-707.description: Senior financial management and planning in human service organizations, emphasizing fiscal approaches that focus on strategy, including how to maximize revenue, control costs, allocate resources, improve decision-making and support successful social programs and disruptive social change.
SOWK-707.prereqText:
Prerequisite: SOWK 704; SOWK 706
Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student
Major: open only to Social Work
School: open only to Suzanne Dworak-Peck School of Social Work

SOWK-711.title: Design Laboratory for Social Innovation I
SOWK-711.description: Incorporates leadership in intervention design, stakeholder engagement, and evidence-based practices.

SOWK-713.title: Research Methods for Intervention Design and Evaluation
SOWK-713.description: Introduction to doctoral-level applied research and evaluation methods, emphasizing the selection, design and application of methods for intervention design and evaluation in complex social contexts.

SOWK-714.title: Executive Leadership: Leaders as Maestros
SOWK-714.description: The Leader/Maestro Concept enlarges the student from a virtuoso perspective - individual performance - to include an organizational performance in leading, creating and measuring change.
SOWK-714.prereqText:
Prerequisite: SOWK 704; SOWK 706
Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student
Major: open only to Social Work
School: open only to Suzanne Dworak-Peck School of Social Work

SOWK-716.title: Leadership in Complex Social Problem Identification
SOWK-716.description: Develops advanced skills to define complex social problems through interdisciplinary, systems, and evidence-based analysis, identifying root causes, gaps, and implications that guide capstone solution design.

SOWK-717.title: Stakeholder Engagement and Solutions
SOWK-717.description: Prepares students to lead stakeholder-informed inquiry and identify feasible, values-aligned solutions to complex social problems by deepening understanding of problem and solution landscapes.
SOWK-717.prereqText:
Recommended preparation: Completion of introductory coursework in the Social Work doctoral programs (SOWK 716 for DSW program students), or comparable preparation as determined by the program
Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student

SOWK-720.title: Leadership Communication for Social Impact
SOWK-720.description: Mastering communication for social impact. Students will learn the power of listening, consensus-based facilitation, storytelling for social change and communicating with brevity.

SOWK-721.title: Data Driven Decision Making in Social Services
SOWK-721.description: Practical introduction to using quantitative administrative data to identify trends, track performance, evaluate programs and drive decision making.
SOWK-721.prereqText:
Prerequisite: SOWK 704; SOWK 706
Class standing: open only to Doctoral Student
Major: open only to Social Work

SOWK-723.title: Design Laboratory for Social Innovation II
SOWK-723.description: Emphasizes leadership in developing responsive interventions to address complex social problems.

SOWK-725A.description: Design and develop an innovative, feasible, and defensible Capstone Project focusing on a selected Grand Challenge for Social Work.

SOWK-725B.description: Refine a fully implementable, innovatively designed Grand Challenge Capstone Project. Future-focused on garnering support, piloting and launching students' capstone prototype.

SOWK-725C.description: Complete a fully implementable, innovatively designed Grand Challenge Capstone Project. Future-focused on garnering support, piloting and launching students' capstone project.
SOWK-725C.prereqText:
Prerequisite: SOWK 725B

SOWK-733.title: Policy Analysis and Advocacy in a Comparative Social Policy Context
SOWK-733.description: Examination of the evolution of American and other welfare states in selected nations. Analysis of global welfare institutions. Engaging in policy analysis in a comparative context.

SOWK-743.title: Applying Theory in Intervention Research
SOWK-743.description: Doctoral seminar on applying behavioral theory across research stages, from conceptualization to implementation, with focus on intervention design, and real-world application in social work.

SOWK-763.title: Social Work Research Methods II: Issues in Research for Soci
SOWK-763.description: Building on SOWK 762, deepens students' knowledge of social work research methods and strengthens their ability to develop original and rigorous research proposals.

SOWK-764.title: Statistics in Social Work II: Categorical Data Analysis
SOWK-764.description: Introduction to single equation statistical modeling using limited dependent variables, including dichotomous, ordered categorical and other outcome forms. Methods are drawn from statistics and econometrics.

SOWK-765.title: Writing Successful Dissertation Research Grants
SOWK-765.description: Prepares doctoral students to write and submit applications to obtain extramural funding to support their dissertation research. Students will learn about opportunities and eligibility requirements for federal and foundation supported dissertation research grants, how grants are reviewed and scored once submitted, and how to write successful proposals. Recommended preparation: Completion of a qualitative or mixed methods course is preferred.
SOWK-765.prereqText: Recommended preparation: Completion of a qualitative or mixed methods course is preferred

SOWK-783.title: Doctoral Seminar II: Independent Scholarly Trajectories
SOWK-783.description: Enhance students scholarly skills that are critical for becoming an independent scholar. Prepare students for their qualifying exam.
SOWK-783.prereqText: Recommended preparation: Completion of introductory doctoral seminar coursework in the social work doctoral programs, or comparable preparation as determined by the program and  instructor

SOWK-784.title: Teaching Foundations in Social Work: Pedagogy  and Reflection
SOWK-784.description: Teaching practices for future Social Work educators. Topics include teaching philosophy, lesson planning, and addressing common classroom challenges.
SOWK-784.prereqText: Recommended preparation: USC Center for Excellence in Teaching (CET) Future Faculty Institute

SOWK-790.title: Research
SOWK-790.description: Research leading to the doctorate. Maximum units which may be applied to the degree to be determined by the department. Graded CR/NC.

SPAN-120.title: Spanish I
SPAN-120.description: For students with limited proficiency in Spanish. Practice in listening comprehension, oral communication, elementary reading and writing.

SPAN-150.title: Spanish II
SPAN-150.description: Continuation of Spanish 110 or 120; increased emphasis on listening comprehension, oral expression, reading and writing.

SPAN-220.title: Spanish III
SPAN-220.description: Continuation of SPAN 150; intensive work in listening comprehension, oral communication, reading, and writing with emphasis on free expression; readings related to Hispanic culture and civilization. Prereq: SPAN 150 or equivalent.

SPAN-240.title: Spanish IV
SPAN-240.description: Intensive review of Spanish grammar with emphasis on four skills. Audio-visual materials and readings related to Hispanic culture and civilization.

SPAN-260.title: Advanced Spanish: Arts and Sciences
SPAN-260.description: Development of students' oral and writing skills using literary and scientific materials; grammar review. Duplicates credit in the former SPAN 266.

SPAN-270.title: Spanish for Heritage Speakers
SPAN-270.description: Culture-based course designed for Spanish speakers not formally trained in the language. Review language and grammar and hone presentational skills.
SPAN-270.prereqText:
Prerequisite: SPAN 220
Recommended preparation: Heritage profile
Duplicates credit: SPAN 260

SPAN-280.title: Conversational Spanish
SPAN-280.description: Discussions of short films, cultural and literary texts and other activities designed to improve conversational skills. Prerequisite: SPAN 220. Not for credit for Spanish majors.

SPAN-295.title: Gender and Sexuality in Latin American and Spanish Cinema
SPAN-295.description: Examines the representation of gender and sexual discourses and the intersection with wider social, political and theoretical issues in Latin American and Spanish cinema. Taught in English.

SPAN-301.title: Introduction to Literature and Film
SPAN-301.description: Introduction to critical reading and interpretation of poetry, narrative fiction, drama and film from Spain and Latin America.

SPAN-304.title: The Art of Fiction
SPAN-304.description: A survey of Spanish and Latin American fiction from the Middle Ages to the present, acquainting students with various critical and theoretical approaches to narrative. Conducted in Spanish.
SPAN-304.prereqText:
Prerequisite: SPAN 260 or SPAN 270
Recommended preparation: SPAN 301

SPAN-315.title: Advanced Grammar and Translation
SPAN-315.description: Contrastive study of Spanish and English structures designed to explore the similarities and differences between the two languages and to familiarize students with translation techniques. Emphasis on a variety of text types with the aim of increasing linguistic and cultural appreciation of the Spanish language.

SPAN-316.title: Spanish for the Professions
SPAN-316.description: The language and culture of a particular area of study or profession, such as medicine and healthcare, political and social sciences, business and the law. Limited to 4 units for major or minor credit.

SPAN-321.title: Sounds, Images, Objects
SPAN-321.description: Introduction to the study of Iberian and Latin American cultural forms through readings on the visual arts, cinema, architecture and music. Conducted in Spanish.
SPAN-321.prereqText:
Prerequisite: SPAN 260 or SPAN 270
Duplicates credit: former SPAN 360 and former SPAN 370

SPAN-380.title: Literature of Mexico
SPAN-380.description: Principal writers and their works from Colonial times to the present. Non-majors may write assignments in English. Recommended preparation: advanced comprehension of oral and written Spanish.

SPAN-385.title: The Culture of Food in Hispanic Los Angeles
SPAN-385.description: Experiential learning and project-based course designed to familiarize students with the food culture of Hispanic Los Angeles. Students create Spanish language blogs about their experiences.

SPAN-483.title: Gender and Sexuality
SPAN-483.description: An examination of gender, sexuality, and power in Iberian and Latin American literatures and cultures. Conducted in Spanish.
SPAN-483.prereqText: Recommended preparation: SPAN 304 or SPAN 306 or SPAN 308

SPAN-490.title: Directed Research
SPAN-490.description: Individual research and readings. Not available for graduate credit.
SPAN-490.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Junior, Senior

SPAN-501.title: Cultural Narratives of Spain and Latin America
SPAN-501.description: Theoretical and methodological approaches to cultural narratives in Spanish and Latin American literary and cultural studies.

SPAN-602.title: Seminar in Spanish and Latin American Critical Theory
SPAN-602.description: Major developments in literary criticism in Spain and Latin America from the early modern period to the present.

SSCI-135.title: Maps in the Digital World
SSCI-135.description: The role of formal reasoning, abstract representation and empirical analysis in building maps for sharing knowledge across the physical, life and social sciences and humanities.

SSCI-165.title: Sustainability Science in the City
SSCI-165.description: The influence of sustainability science on public policy and vice versa in the context of social/ethical theories, analytical methods and solutions.

SSCI-175.title: Food, Health and Place
SSCI-175.description: The role of food systems in human nutrition and environmental health, and system transformations needed to achieve good health, equity and sustainability.

SSCI-201.title: Principles of Geodesign
SSCI-201.description: Foundations of geodesign combining place-making, design, collective action, and the science of location-based information to improve human interaction with the functioning of the Earth.

SSCI-214.title: Human Populations and Natural Hazards
SSCI-214.description: Introduction to the complex relationship between human development and natural hazards, which are increasingly causing damage and displacement to human populations throughout the world.

SSCI-265.title: The Water Planet
SSCI-265.description: An exploration of earth's water, ranging from water properties, chemistry, and pollution, to groundwater dynamics, watershed processes, and oceanic-atmospheric circulation. Implications for past and future societies. Lecture and laboratory.

SSCI-301.title: Maps and Spatial Reasoning
SSCI-301.description: Role of maps and spatial reasoning in the production and use of geographic information for representing and analyzing human and environmental activities and events.

SSCI-315.title: 3D GIS and Geodesign
SSCI-315.description: Integrated 3D GIS, CAD, and BIM workflows for geodesign, spatial analytics, and digital twins to support data-driven urban and environmental decision-making.
SSCI-315.prereqText: Recommended preparation: ARCH 203, ARCH 303, PPD 227, SSCI 201, SSCI 301L

SSCI-350.title: International Geodesign
SSCI-350.description: Intensive living-learning research and field experience in Los Angeles and abroad; application of geodesign strategies to local societal challenges.

SSCI-382.title: Geographic Information Science: Spatial Analytics
SSCI-382.description: The various ways in which geography can be used to acquire, represent, organize, analyze, model and visualize information. Laboratories are organized around ArcGIS software suite.

SSCI-383.title: Geographic Information Science: Geospatial Modeling and Cust
SSCI-383.description: Fundamentals of spatial modeling and remote sensing and how to use GIS customization and programming to streamline complex spatial analysis and modeling workflows.

SSCI-397.title: Spatial Sciences Internship
SSCI-397.description: Intensive experience in local public agency, private firm, or nonprofit agency engaged in applied geospatial analysis, modeling and mapping work.

SSCI-412.title: Geodesign Practicum
SSCI-412.description: Application of design concepts, planning protocols and spatial analysis skills to a complex planning or design problem sponsored by a local public, private or not-for-profit client in a studio setting.
SSCI-412.prereqText:
Prerequisite: ARCH 403 or RED 425
Corequisite: SSCI 381 or SSCI 382
Class standing: open only to Senior
Major: open only to Geodesign

SSCI-420.title: Human Security and Geospatial Intelligence Practicum
SSCI-420.description: Create conceptual solutions for a real-world human security and geospatial intelligence issue by developing a problem set and recommended solution to the same.

SSCI-490.title: Directed Research
SSCI-490.description: Individual research and readings. Open only to juniors and seniors. Not available for graduate credit.
SSCI-490.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Junior, Senior

SSCI-575.title: Spatial Data Science
SSCI-575.description: Introduce the spatial data scientific approach to issues and present a holistic generalizable analysis pipeline.

SSCI-576.title: Geospatial Artificial Intelligence
SSCI-576.description: A review of mainstream geospatial artificial intelligence methods and their ability to find actionable insights in geo-enriched data spanning multiple application domains.

SSCI-579.title: Geospatial Intelligence Tradecraft
SSCI-579.description: Typical geospatial intelligence tasks and their use in military operations, national and homeland security, international relief work and disaster management. Recommended preparation: SSCI-581.

SSCI-581.title: Concepts for Spatial Thinking
SSCI-581.description: The unique characteristics and importance of spatial information as they relate to the evolving science, technology, and applications of Geographic Information Systems.

SSCI-582.title: Spatial Databases
SSCI-582.description: Design, implementation, and interrogation of relational, object-oriented and other types of geospatial databases. Recommended preparation: SSCI 581.

SSCI-583.title: Spatial Analysis and Modeling
SSCI-583.description: Provides the knowledge and skills necessary to investigate the spatial patterns which result from social and physical processes operating at or near the Earth's surface.
SSCI-583.prereqText:
Recommended preparation: SSCI 581
Duplicates credit: former GEOG 583

SSCI-585.title: Geospatial Technology Project Management
SSCI-585.description: Concepts, principles, and use of project management tools and the people issues encountered running GIS projects. Recommended preparation: SSCI 581.

SSCI-586.title: GIS Programming and Customization
SSCI-586.description: Design, coding, and implementation of GIS-based software and models using the Python programming language. Recommended preparation: SSCI 582. Duplicates credit in former GEOG 586.

SSCI-587.title: Spatial Data Acquisition
SSCI-587.description: Role of global positioning systems, maps, geocoding, and other kinds of sensors as geospatial data sources. Includes field data acquisition excursion on Catalina Island. Recommended preparation: SSCI-581. Duplicates credit in former GEOG 587.

SSCI-589.title: Cartography and Visualization
SSCI-589.description: Principles of visual perception, spatial cognition and cartographic design and their contributions to the maps, animations, virtual reality and multimedia displays produced with modern GIS. Recommended preparation: SSCI 581.

SSCI-590.title: Directed Research
SSCI-590.description: Research leading to the master's degree in cognate fields. Maximum units which may be applied to the degree to be determined by the department. Graded CR/NC.

SSCI-594A.title: Master's Thesis
SSCI-594A.description: Credit on acceptance of thesis. Graded CR/NC.

SSCI-594B.title: Master's Thesis
SSCI-594B.description: Credit on acceptance of thesis. Graded CR/NC.

SSCI-594Z.title: Master's Thesis
SSCI-594Z.description: Credit on acceptance of thesis. Graded CR/NC.

SSCI-595.title: Applied Geospatial Intelligence Problem Solving
SSCI-595.description: Provides hands-on problem solving opportunity that requires knowledge and GEOINT skills to provide an informed recommendation involving a variety of human security settings.

SSCI-596.title: Internship in Spatial Sciences
SSCI-596.description: Part-time or full-time practical work experience in the student's field of study at an off-campus facility under faculty direction.

SSCI-680.title: Advanced Spatial Computing
SSCI-680.description: The role of spatial computing in understanding the world, in knowing and communicating our relationships to specific places, and for navigating through those places.

SSCI-683.title: Principles of Spatial Data Analysis
SSCI-683.description: The theoretical foundations and techniques of spatial analysis and the ways in which they have been used to identify spatial processes and patterns. Recommended preparation: Enrollment in a USC PhD Program.

SSCI-684.title: Spatial Modeling with GIS
SSCI-684.description: An introduction to spatial models identifying the key issues influencing the success of these models in simulating key social and environmental processes and health exposures.

SSCI-790.description: Research leading to the doctoral degree. Maximum units which may be applied to the degree to be determined by the department. Open only to doctoral students.

SWMS-105.title: Identity Development of the Contemporary Female
SWMS-105.description: Exploration of identity development in terms of social, political, and cultural constructs; examination of collegiate athletics and the contributions of women of color.

SWMS-212.title: Introduction to Gender and Sexuality: American Perspectives
SWMS-212.description: Examination of how gender and sexuality have been constructed, experienced and legislated.

SWMS-219.title: Introduction to Feminist Theory
SWMS-219.description: Emergence of feminist thought from the Enlightenment to the present; historical development of female subjectivity; advancement of womens rights; feminisms from alternative ideological perspectives.

SWMS-221.title: Introduction to Queer Theory
SWMS-221.description: Genealogies of queer theory, from psychoanalytic theories to feminism and post-structuralism; evolving concepts of gender; relation to social justice, resistance and power.

SWMS-306.title: Contemporary Issues in LGBTQ Studies
SWMS-306.description: Interdisciplinary analysis of LGBTQ issues; examination of the intersections of gender and sexuality with social class, race, religion and nationality.
SWMS-306.prereqText: Prerequisite: SWMS 210 or SWMS 212 or SWMS 215 or SWMS 221

SWMS-310.title: Gender and Social Justice
SWMS-310.description: Exploration of the ways in which developments and policies, including neoliberalism, the carceral state, and economic precarity, are connected and gendered.
SWMS-310.prereqText: Prerequisite: SWMS 210 or SWMS 212 or SWMS 215 or SWMS 219 or SWMS 221

SWMS-311.title: Gender and Sexuality Studies: Internship
SWMS-311.description: Intensive experience with gender-focused community organizations; analysis of relationships between organizations and feminist and queer theory.
SWMS-311.prereqText: School: open only to Dana and David Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences

SWMS-344.title: Sexual/Textual Diversity
SWMS-344.description: Questions of gay and lesbian identity, expression and experience in a variety of literary and cultural forms; emphasis on sexual politics, equality and difference.

SWMS-350.title: Gender and Sexuality in Renaissance Italy
SWMS-350.description: Interdisciplinary exploration of gender and sexuality in Italian renaissance literature and visual arts by male and female authors and artists from the fourteenth through the sixteenth century.

SWMS-355.title: Transgender Studies
SWMS-355.description: Analysis of transgender behaviors, from androgyny and transvestism to transexuality. Discussion of changing laws, representations, medical standards, and social attitudes towards transgender and intersex people.
SWMS-355.prereqText: Prerequisite: SWMS 210 or SWMS 212 or SWMS 215 or SWMS 219 or SWMS 221

SWMS-372.title: Human Sexuality
SWMS-372.description: Psychological and physiological base of sexuality; gender identity, childbearing, birth control, venereal diseases; dysfunctions and treatments.

SWMS-374.title: Women Writers in Europe and America
SWMS-374.description: Introduction to works of major women writers from the Middle Ages to the 20th century in their literary, social and cultural contexts.

SWMS-378.title: Gender and Sexuality in Literary Theory
SWMS-378.description: Literary representations and theories of gender difference. Examines questions of gendered voice in writing and the cultural construction of gender in various periods and cultures.

SWMS-392.title: Junior Seminar in Gender and Sexuality Studies
SWMS-392.description: Research methods in gender and sexuality studies scholarship; study of feminist, queer and post-colonial epistemologies.
SWMS-392.prereqText: Prerequisite: SWMS 210 or SWMS 212 or SWMS 215 or SWMS 219 or SWMS 221 or SWMS 308

SWMS-395.title: Gender, Media and Communication
SWMS-395.description: Issues of gender in communication, including: mediarepresentations of femininity and masculinity; and gender's rolein communication at the interpersonal, public, and cultural levels.

SWMS-412.title: Gender, Sexuality and Media
SWMS-412.description: Examines how gender and sexuality are figured in cinema and television with an emphasis on the development of feminist media theory.

SWMS-434.title: Women and Aging: Psychological, Social, and      Political Implications
SWMS-434.description: Problems and resources of the middle-aged and older woman in a changing society; including discrimination, stereotypes, employment, social interaction, etc.

SWMS-456.title: Women in International Development
SWMS-456.description: How various developmental theories analyze the role of women as producers and how Third World women are increasing their role in development.

SWMS-467.title: Gender and the News Media
SWMS-467.description: Gender and news media evolving images of women and men in print and electronic media. Impact of gender in content and style of news, television and cinema. Open to non-majors.

SWMS-490.title: Directed Research
SWMS-490.description: Independent research and readings. Not available for graduate credit.
SWMS-490.prereqText: Class standing: open only to Junior, Senior

SWMS-492.title: Gender and Sexuality Studies: Honors Thesis
SWMS-492.description: Writing of the honors thesis; for students in the Gender and Sexuality Studies Honors Program.
SWMS-492.prereqText:
Recommended preparation: SWMS 410
Major: open only to Gender and Sexuality Studies

SWMS-560.title: Feminist Theory
SWMS-560.description: History of feminist theory and major perspectives of current feminist theory: liberal feminism, socialist/Marxist feminism, radical feminism, psychological feminism, spiritual feminism, and ecological feminism.

SWMS-590.title: Directed Research
SWMS-590.description: Research leading to the master's degree in cognate fields. Maximum units which may be applied to the degree to be determined by the department. Graded CR/NC.

TAC-100.title: Enhanced Productivity with AI
TAC-100.description: Enhance how you think, work, and create by mastering AI tools that amplify focus, creativity, and personal productivity.

TAC-101.title: Business Tools and Digital Fluency
TAC-101.description: An introduction to the software and technologies used in modern business environments and practices required to effectively function in online environments.

TAC-104.title: Web Development
TAC-104.description: Core HTML and CSS for building functional, custom websites. Includes responsive design, modern frameworks and AI-assisted tools.

TAC-115.title: Programming in Python
TAC-115.description: Introduction to Python; intended for students without prior programming experience.
TAC-115.prereqText: Duplicates credit: TAC 116 and former ITP 116

TAC-116.title: Accelerated Programming in Python
TAC-116.description: Accelerated introduction to Python; intended for students with prior programming experience.
TAC-116.prereqText:
Recommended preparation: Prior programming experience
Duplicates credit: TAC 115 and former ITP 115

TAC-125.title: Hackers to CEOs: Intro to Cyber Security in the AI Era
TAC-125.description: Cyber security, threats, intrusions, controls and countermeasures. Hacking computers and humans. Cyber and AI risk. Phishing, social engineering and other human hacking techniques.

TAC-165.title: Introduction to C++ Programming
TAC-165.description: Introduction to programming using C++, including variables, operators, conditionals, loops, arrays, vectors, strings, functions, files, structs, pointers, dynamic allocation and an introduction to classes.

TAC-168.title: Introduction to MATLAB
TAC-168.description: Fundamentals of MATLAB: a high-performance numeric computation and visualization environment. Overview of linear algebra and matrix manipulation; using 2-D and 3-D plotting routines; programming in MATLAB; basic numerical analysis.
TAC-168.prereqText:
Recommended preparation: MATH 118 or MATH 125
Duplicates credit: former ITP 168

TAC-181.title: Video Game QA Management
TAC-181.description: Survey of game software development through quality assurance and in-depth analysis of the development cycle with a focus on bug testing systems, methodologies and QA Management.
TAC-181.prereqText:
Recommended preparation: former ITP 180 or TAC 180
Duplicates credit: former ITP 181 and former ITP 230 and TAC 230

TAC-190.title: Digital Graphics and UI Design Tools
TAC-190.description: Learn tools for digital graphics and visual communication using Photoshop, with fundamentals supporting social media, print, presentations and UI design.
TAC-190.prereqText: Duplicates credit: former ITP 090 and former ITP 190

TAC-215.title: Introduction to 3D Modeling, Animation and Visual Effects
TAC-215.description: An applied introduction to the techniques used for modeling, animating, texturing, lighting, rendering, and creating 3D content for games, cinematics, visual effects, animation and visualizations.
TAC-215.prereqText:
Recommended preparation: knowledge of any 2D paint, drawing or CAD program
Duplicates credit: former ITP 215

TAC-216.title: Applied Python
TAC-216.description: Development of practical Python programming skills through project-based applications; "Pythonic" ways of solving problems in modern computational domains.
TAC-216.prereqText:
Prerequisite: TAC 115 or TAC 116 or ITP 115 or ITP 116
Duplicates credit: former ITP 216

TAC-228.title: Computer-Aided Modeling and Rapid Fabrication
TAC-228.description: Computer-aided modeling techniques for rapid fabrication. Conceptualize, design, fabricate, assemble and test 3D printed prototypes.

TAC-249.title: Introduction to Data Analytics
TAC-249.description: Introduction to data analytics. Basics of databases, applied statistics, data visualization. Leverage data to make critical business decisions.
TAC-249.prereqText: Duplicates credit: former ITP 249 and former ITP 250 and former ITP 251

TAC-259.title: Basics of Artificial Intelligence
TAC-259.description: Concepts and techniques in artificial intelligence; approaches in artificial narrow intelligence; applications of AI that are already changing society; ethical and social questions in AI.
TAC-259.prereqText:
Prerequisite: TAC 216 or ITP 216 or CSCI 113
Duplicates credit: former ITP 259

TAC-265.title: Software Design with Object-Oriented Programming
TAC-265.description: Learn to design and build software systems using object-oriented programming, with a focus on modular thinking, problem solving and real-world applications across disciplines.
TAC-265.prereqText:
Prerequisite: TAC 115 or TAC 116 or TAC 165 or ITP 115 or ITP 116 or ITP 165
Duplicates credit: former ITP 265

TAC-298.title: Special Topics
TAC-298.description: Selected topics in Technology and Applied Computing.

TAC-301.title: Front-End Web Development
TAC-301.description: Covers programming fundamentals, client-side programming, dynamic UI manipulation, modern frameworks and libraries and the use of AI-assisted tools in front-end development.
TAC-301.prereqText:
Prerequisite: TAC 104 or ITP 104 or IML 300 or JOUR 320
Duplicates credit: IDSN 531 and former ITP 301

TAC-303.title: Full-Stack Web Development
TAC-303.description: Modern web development techniques for building web applications from the ground up. Front-end and back-end development, including databases, JavaScript libraries and web application frameworks.
TAC-303.prereqText:
Prerequisite: TAC 265 or ITP 265 or CSCI 103
Duplicates credit: former ITP 303

TAC-308.title: Computer-Aided Design for Bio-Mechanical Systems
TAC-308.description: Concepts of computer-aided design in 2-dimensions and 3-dimensions. Creating advanced parts using extrusions, surfaces, and equation driven sketches. Forming assemblies and sub-assemblies, for motion analysis
TAC-308.prereqText:
Recommended preparation: MATH 245, strength of materials knowledge
Duplicates credit: former ITP 308

TAC-310.title: Design for User Experience
TAC-310.description: Fundamental concepts, techniques, practices, workflows and tools associated with the practice of user experience and interaction design in web and mobile applications.
TAC-310.prereqText: Duplicates credit: former ITP 140 and former 310

TAC-325.title: Ethical Hacking
TAC-325.description: Ethical hacking; penetration testing; vulnerability assessment; red teams; hacker environments, infrastructure and frameworks; lateral movement and data exfiltration techniques; evasion and anti-forensics.
TAC-325.prereqText:
Prerequisite: ITP 125 or TAC 125
Duplicates credit: former ITP 325

TAC-342.title: iOS App Development
TAC-342.description: Introduction to the Swift programming language, various frameworks, and design patterns needed to develop applications for iOS mobile devices such as iPhones and iPads.
TAC-342.prereqText:
Prerequisite: TAC 265 or ITP 265 or CSCI 103
Duplicates credit: former ITP 342

TAC-348.title: Making Smart Devices: Introduction to Electronics/Wearables
TAC-348.description: Design of electronic devices that interact with the physical world; electronic interfaces; development of software algorithms; micro-controller implementation.
TAC-348.prereqText:
Prerequisite: TAC 115 or ITP 115 or TAC 116 or ITP 116 or TAC 165 or ITP 165 or TAC 168 or ITP 168 or BME 210
Recommended preparation: Students should have completed a course in object-oriented programming
Major: not open to Electrical and Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering
Duplicates credit: former ITP 148 and former ITP 348

TAC-349.title: Enterprise Data Analytics
TAC-349.description: Methodology to store, organize, cleanse, harmonize and stage enterprise data for analytics. Report, visualize, slice and dice, forecast and predict trends.
TAC-349.prereqText:
Prerequisite: TAC 249 or TAC 320 or ITP 249 or ITP 320 or DSCI 351
Duplicates credit: former ITP 487 and former ITP 349

TAC-357.title: Enterprise Networks: Design and Architecture
TAC-357.description: Network technologies. Routers and managed switches. Integrated operating systems (IOS). Strategies for endpoint management. Subnets and securing subnetworks. Reliability with networks and network infrastructure.
TAC-357.prereqText:
Prerequisite: TAC 125 or ITP 125
Duplicates credit: former ITP 357

TAC-359.title: Applied Neural Networks
TAC-359.description: Design, build, and train applied neural networks to solve real-world problems; implement neural networks for machine vision, image recognition and object detection and tracking.
TAC-359.prereqText:
Prerequisite: TAC 259 or ITP 259 or DSCI 352
Duplicates credit: former ITP 359

TAC-361.title: Character Rigging for Games
TAC-361.description: Fundamentals of character rigging for video game production and development; optimization of character design, skeleton and mass properties for effective rigging; virtual rigs.
TAC-361.prereqText:
Prerequisite: TAC 215 or ITP 215 or CTAN 452
Recommended preparation: Any experience with 3D character rigs
Duplicates credit: former ITP 361

TAC-368.title: Cross-Platform App Development with Flutter
TAC-368.description: Programming applications with dynamic graphical user interfaces. Topics include events, controls, resources, data bindings, styles and user experience.
TAC-368.prereqText:
Prerequisite: TAC 265 or ITP 265 or CSCI 103
Duplicates credit: former ITP 368

TAC-370.title: Cybersecurity Management and Operations
TAC-370.description: Cybersecurity project design. Incident response. Teambuilding, management and communications for cybersecurity. Scalable approaches for implementation of Information Security Management Systems.
TAC-370.prereqText:
Prerequisite: TAC 125 or ITP 125
Duplicates credit: former ITP 370

TAC-375.title: Digital Forensics and Cybersecurity Investigations
TAC-375.description: Forensic science techniques. Digital evidence preservation. Processes and methodologies for digital examinations. Cyber crime investigations. Windows file system analysis. Real case scenario analysis and reporting
TAC-375.prereqText:
Prerequisite: TAC 125 or ITP 125
Duplicates credit: former ITP 375

TAC-380.title: Video Game Programming
TAC-380.description: Underlying concepts and principles required for programming video games (topics include vectors, transformations, 3-D math, geometric primitives, matrices).
TAC-380.prereqText:
Prerequisite: CSCI 104 or TAC 365 or ITP 365
Duplicates credit: former ITP 380

TAC-383.title: Database Systems: Storage and Retrieval using SQL
TAC-383.description: Data models for industry applications. Modeling and designing robust databases. Implementing and querying databases with SQL. Innovations in database applications.

TAC-388.title: Developing Smart Devices
TAC-388.description: From prototype to PCB to funding pitch: building internet-connected smart devices. Design, fabricate, assemble and test a smart device of your own conceptualization.
TAC-388.prereqText:
Major: not open to Electrical and Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering
Duplicates credit: former ITP 388

TAC-393.title: Video Game Project Management
TAC-393.description: Production and project management of video games from concept to release and beyond.
TAC-393.prereqText:
Prerequisite: TAC 180 or ITP 180
Duplicates credit: former ITP 393

TAC-405.title: Advanced Back-End Web Development
TAC-405.description: Advanced back-end web development frameworks and practices for creating scalable web applications and APIs. AI-powered tools to enhance development workflows, streamline testing, and boost productivity.

TAC-425.title: Web Application Security
TAC-425.description: Examine web applications from an offensive security standpoint. Topics include information gathering, vulnerability discovery and validation, exploitation and privilege escalation techniques.
TAC-425.prereqText:
Prerequisite: TAC 301 or ITP 301 or TAC 325 or ITP 325 or ACAD 275
Duplicates credit: former ITP 425

TAC-435.title: Professional C++
TAC-435.description: Applications of advanced concepts in C++ including lambda expressions, templates, secure coding, parallel programming, writing performant code, CMake and continuous integration.
TAC-435.prereqText:
Prerequisite: CSCI 104 or TAC 365 or ITP 365
Duplicates credit: former ITP 435

TAC-443.title: Malware Analysis and Reverse Engineering
TAC-443.description: Reverse engineering concepts for malware analysis; debuggers and decompilers; static and dynamic analysis of malicious scripts and binaries; focused on Windows and Windows APls.
TAC-443.prereqText:
Prerequisite: TAC 325; TAC 375
Recommended preparation: Familiarity with the modern Windows operating system and Windows APIs.

TAC-447.title: Mobile Device Forensics and Security
TAC-447.description: Digital forensics, evidence extraction and analysis of mobile devices (Android, iOS and Blackberry), Cellular networks, IoT devices and legacy mobile and hand-held devices.
TAC-447.prereqText:
Prerequisite: TAC 375 or ITP 375
Duplicates credit: former ITP 447

TAC-449.title: Applications of Machine Learning
TAC-449.description: Hands-on approach to fundamental modeling techniques and machine learning algorithms that enable students to build robust predictive models from real-world data and test their validity.
TAC-449.prereqText:
Prerequisite: TAC 216 or ITP 216 or CSCI 113
Duplicates credit: former ITP 449

TAC-450.title: High Performance Computing in Applied Machine Learning
TAC-450.description: Theoretical and practical high performance computing approaches to various computational methods in applied machine learning.
TAC-450.prereqText:
Prerequisite: TAC 449 or ITP 449 or DSCI 352 or MATH 446 or BUAD 425 or BUAD 427 or CSCI 467
Recommended preparation: Python programming on the level of TAC 115 or TAC 116
Duplicates credit: former ITP 450

TAC-459.title: Applied Natural Language Processing and Generative AI
TAC-459.description: Generative AI and NLP fundamentals through hands-on work with GPT/BERT, covering prompt engineering, RAG, fine-tuning, retrieval, sentiment analysis, QA and machine translation for product building.
TAC-459.prereqText:
Prerequisite: ITP 359 or TAC 359 or CSCI 467 or EE 460
Duplicates credit: former ITP 459

TAC-460.title: Web Application Project
TAC-460.description: Team-based projects using Agile methodology, Git workflow, product design and AI-assisted tools; plan, build and launch fully functional web applications.
TAC-460.prereqText:
Prerequisite: ITP 303 or TAC 303 or ITP 304 or TAC 304 or ACAD 276
Duplicates credit: former ITP 460

TAC-466.title: Building the High Tech Startup
TAC-466.description: Startup creation: idea and team development, market strategy, business models, financial planning, go-to-market approaches, product development, agile methods and core organizational building skills.
TAC-466.prereqText:
Prerequisite: BUAD 301 or ACAD 181
Duplicates credit: former ITP 466

TAC-470.title: Technology and Applied Computing Practicum
TAC-470.description: Independent technology project related to specific topics under the direction of a faculty member.
TAC-470.prereqText:
Recommended preparation: appropriate 300-level course work to topic of study
Duplicates credit: former ITP 470

TAC-479.title: Cyber Law and Privacy
TAC-479.description: Cyber legal issues, search and seizure, 4th amendment and digital evidence, warrants, private searches, wiretaps, tracking devices, workplace privacy.

TAC-480.title: Technology and Applied Computing Internship
TAC-480.description: Practical experience in applying information technology skills in real-world settings. Supervised internship at companies and start-ups. Balancing academic rigor with corporate challenges and deadlines.
TAC-480.prereqText:
Recommended preparation: knowledge of chosen function area
Class standing: not open to Doctoral Student, Master Student
Duplicates credit: former ITP 480

TAC-485.title: Programming Game Engines
TAC-485.description: Building the core components of a modern 3D game engine including shaders, animation, collision detection, artificial intelligence algorithms, multithreading and profiling.

TAC-499.title: Special Topics
TAC-499.description: Recent developments in computers and data processing.

THTE-107.title: Foundations of Vocal Performance
THTE-107.description: Exploration of the foundations of vocal technique in a group setting, with an emphasis on musical theatre repertoire.

THTE-201A.title: Acting for Musical Theatre
THTE-201A.description: Analysis and investigation of role interpretation and character development by working on two or more scenes from the same play. Introduction of techniques to unlock objectives based on the text.
THTE-201A.prereqText: Major: open only to Dramatic Arts (Musical Theatre), Musical Theatre

THTE-206B.title: Movement for Musical Theatre
THTE-206B.description: Introduction to foundational skills for musical theatre movement, including safe alignment and a movement vocabulary.
THTE-206B.prereqText:
Prerequisite: THTE 206A
School: open only to School of Dramatic Arts

THTE-208.title: Musicianship for Musical Theatre Actors II
THTE-208.description: Continued development of the foundations of musicianship necessary for a career in musical theatre.
THTE-208.prereqText:
Prerequisite: THTE 107
School: open only to School of Dramatic Arts

THTE-226.title: The History of Content Creation
THTE-226.description: An exploration of the evolution of content creation spanning from the ancient multicultural oral traditions to the digital age. Discover how storytellers and story-sellers have always been influencers in the realms of entertainment, activism and commerce.

THTE-300.title: Script and Score
THTE-300.description: Introduction and development of techniques needed to transition from the script to score. Beginning with an exploration of Broadway's "Golden Age" and the examination of Sondheim and his contemporaries.

THTE-340.title: Musical Theatre Integration Workshop I
THTE-340.description: Introduction to the synthesis of emotional life, voice and movement skills as the foundation for an authentic musical theatre performance.
THTE-340.prereqText:
Prerequisite: THTE 306
School: open only to School of Dramatic Arts

THTE-350B.title: Musical Theatre Integration Workshop II
THTE-350B.description: Continuation of the techniques developed in THTE 350aL to heighten dramatic text for musical theatre.
THTE-350B.prereqText:
Prerequisite: THTE 350A
School: open only to School of Dramatic Arts

THTE-354.title: Musical Theatre Individual Instruction
THTE-354.description: Introduction to foundational healthy vocal performance/singing skills needed to sustain a career in the musical theatre.
THTE-354.prereqText: School: open only to School of Dramatic Arts

THTE-450B.title: Musical Theatre Integration Workshop III
THTE-450B.description: The investigation of various musical theatre roles in preparation for entering the entertainment industry.
THTE-450B.prereqText:
Prerequisite: THTE 450A
School: open only to School of Dramatic Arts

THTR-101.title: Introduction to Acting
THTR-101.description: Study of diverse genres and disciplines of acting; fundamental techniques necessary for performance; scene study from contemporary text.

THTR-105.title: Introduction to Screen Acting
THTR-105.description: Introduction to the theoretical and foundational practices, techniques and strategies specific to screen acting in relation to the basic dynamics of acting for the stage.

THTR-120B.title: Acting I
THTR-120B.description: Basic principles and techniques of acting through theatre games and improvisation. Introduction to contemporary texts, basic characterization and cold reading techniques.

THTR-122.title: Improvisation and Theatre Games
THTR-122.description: Individual and group exercises to free the actor physically and emotionally and to stimulate creativity, imagination, and self-expression.

THTR-130.title: Introduction to Theatrical Production
THTR-130.description: Introduction to the non-performance areas of theatrical production(administrative, design, and technical fields) through hands-onparticipation in USC productions.

THTR-131B.title: Advanced Theatrical Production
THTR-131B.description: Advanced understanding of non-performance areas of theatrical production (administrative, design, and technical fields) through hands-on participation in USC productions.

THTR-132B.title: Art of Theatrical Design
THTR-132B.description: Development of the artistic process and theatrical design vocabulary of the individual within the environment of collaborative storytelling.

THTR-141.title: Beginning Voice
THTR-141.description: Physiological mechanism of voice: breath control, phonation, resonance, articulation of language for the stage; expressive use of stress, intonation and rhythm.

THTR-152.title: Introduction to Scene Study: Contemporary Plays
THTR-152.description: Application and consolidation of the skills, knowledge and techniques acquired in the study of fundamentals of acting encountered in THTR 101.

THTR-192.title: History of Stand-Up Comedy
THTR-192.description: A comprehensive overview and understanding of how stand-up evolved in the United States, from the mid-1800's to the current touring performers.

THTR-197.title: Comedy and Performance
THTR-197.description: Comedy and Performance traces the history of comedy in performance from its earliest incarnations to the present day.

THTR-202.title: The Fundamentals of Comedy
THTR-202.description: Introduction to the fundamental elements of comedy and how to apply those elements to create short, original pieces of comedy in performance and writing.

THTR-213.title: Corset Construction
THTR-213.description: Design and construct period corsets, along with the materials and terminology needed to sew (machine and hand) corsets.

THTR-214B.title: The Actor's Instrument: Voice and Body
THTR-214B.description: A comprehensive exploration of voice, speech and acting to strengthen the actors physical instrument.

THTR-216.title: Movement for Actors
THTR-216.description: Training and practice in the coordination of the physical apparatus of the actor utilizing various movement techniques through improvisation.

THTR-220B.title: Intermediate Acting I
THTR-220B.description: Continuing development of imagination leading to an increased range of dramatic expression through the formalized text of William Shakespeare.

THTR-225.title: Theatre Across History and Cultures
THTR-225.description: The analysis of a range of plays from different times and cultures with a consideration of the roles of actor, director, dramaturg and designer.

THTR-230.title: Theatrical Design as Poetic Realism
THTR-230.description: The visualization and communication of design ideas through free-hand and mechanical drawing, as well as advanced dramaturgical storytelling and the creative collaborative process.

THTR-232.title: Introduction to Theatrical Lighting
THTR-232.description: Theory and practice of theatrical lighting design including electricity, radiant energy, refraction, reflection, absorption, chromatic variation and electronic controls.

THTR-241.title: Methods and Materials
THTR-241.description: Cutting-edge and traditional methods and materials that enhance both the planning stages and realization of the theatrical design.

THTR-250.title: Camera and Improvisation
THTR-250.description: Understanding on-camera acting and improvisation by creating original material both in front and behind the camera.

THTR-252A.title: Intermediate Acting I: Drama/Comedy
THTR-252A.description: Polishing the actor's skills through analysis and performance applied to the arc of a character. The 'a' section of the course will cover drama and the 'b' section will focus on comedy.

THTR-252B.title: Intermediate Acting I: Drama/Comedy
THTR-252B.description: Polishing the actor's skills through analysis and performance applied to the arc of a character. The 'a' section of the course will cover drama and the 'b' section will focus on comedy.

THTR-295.title: Theatre in Los Angeles
THTR-295.description: Current state of American theatre, through a study of acting, playwriting, criticism, stage design, lighting, and dramatic styles.

THTR-302.title: Shakespeare in His World
THTR-302.description: The plays and theatre of Shakespeare, the influences on his work and his contemporary world. Recommended preparation: THTR 201, THTR 310, THTR 311

THTR-303.title: Projection Design I
THTR-303.description: Investigation of the projection design process, equipment, multi-media, digital technology concepts and related documentation.

THTR-305A.title: Directing
THTR-305A.description: Examination of basic directorial principles. Pre-production analysis and rehearsal procedures; relationship of the director to actor; integration of technical aspects of production.

THTR-305B.title: Directing
THTR-305B.description: Examination of basic directorial principles. Pre-production analysis and rehearsal procedures; relationship of the director to actor; integration of technical aspects of production.

THTR-306.title: Audio-Drama
THTR-306.description: Develop a basic understanding of the skills required to effectively develop, create, record, edit and market an audio drama.

THTR-308.title: Lighting Programming for Live Events
THTR-308.description: Strategies and principles in computerized programming for theatrical lighting, emphasizing its applied use in creating kinetic, responsive environments.

THTR-320B.title: Intermediate Acting II
THTR-320B.description: Further development of range and breadth of performance skills with emphasis on texts of heightened language and style.

THTR-322.title: Improv 2: Advanced Improv
THTR-322.description: An in depth study of improvised comedy scene work. An exploration of the primary tools and structure for creating improvised scenes and developing characters for stage and screen.

THTR-325.title: Casting for Stage and Screen
THTR-325.description: Introduction of the casting principles and practices for four of the mediums that dominate entertainment: theatre, film, television and commercials.

THTR-336.title: Sound Design I
THTR-336.description: The art and techniques of theatrical sound design. The use of music and ambient sound in theatrical presentations. Design elements as metaphor.

THTR-339B.title: The Actor's Instrument: Voice and Body II
THTR-339B.description: Continued training in the areas of breath awareness, physical awareness, voice, speech work and movement training.
THTR-339B.prereqText:
Prerequisite: THTR 339A
School: open only to School of Dramatic Arts

THTR-342A.title: Basic Voice
THTR-342A.description: a: Examination of the individual voice centering on resonance, tone, flexibility, and support through dramatic selections for transmitting meaning and emotion of character.

THTR-342B.title: Basic Voice
THTR-342B.description: Examination of the individual voice centering on resonance, tone, flexibility, and support through dramatic selections for transmitting meaning and emotion of character. Continuation of 342a.

THTR-343.title: Musical Theatre Audition
THTR-343.description: Designed to give students confidence and integrity for auditions in musical theatre. Choosing appropriate material and preparation for the audition and performance. Audition required.

THTR-346.title: Musical Theatre Sound Reinforcement
THTR-346.description: A hands-on course in the use of microphones and music theory skills to reinforce all instrument sections in a typical musical theatre pit.

THTR-352B.title: Intermediate Acting II
THTR-352B.description: Building and sustaining character with special focus on stylized realism, subtext and heightened language. Multi-cultural text and methodologies.

THTR-354.title: Acting Shakespeare
THTR-354.description: Basic approach to the acting and analysis of the highly formalized texts of William Shakespeare.

THTR-355.title: Acting for Sitcoms
THTR-355.description: Provide an understanding as to how to work in half-hour television and streaming media.

THTR-365.title: Playwriting I
THTR-365.description: Essential elements of playwriting through weekly assignments, students' initiative, occasional productions of scenes, and extensive classroom analysis.

THTR-366.title: Playwriting II
THTR-366.description: Continuation of the work begun in 365.

THTR-395.title: Drama as Human Relations
THTR-395.description: A focus on American ethnic and multicultural diversity from the perspectives of gender, race, and myth as revealed in plays, film, and other performance media.

THTR-397.title: Theatre Practicum
THTR-397.description: Substantive participation in a production sponsored by the School and supervised by the faculty.

THTR-401.title: Contemporary Theatre in a Changing World
THTR-401.description: Explores the bold approaches that characterize the best of contemporary theatre, as well as the artists who are groundbreakers in a changing world.

THTR-404.title: Acting Theory
THTR-404.description: Examination of the theoretical foundations of acting as an art form through the reading of primary historical texts.

THTR-405.title: Performing Identities
THTR-405.description: This course explores the live performance medium as a creative means of social redress and personal expression. Duplicates credit in the former THTR 393m.

THTR-406.title: Theatre on the Edge
THTR-406.description: An exploration of the art of theatre at the edge of possibilities.

THTR-407B.title: Drawing and Rendering for the Theater
THTR-407B.description: Drawing and rendering techniques appropriate for theater designers. Drawing and drawing theory.

18523.notes:
Making The Live Sports Talk Show
Step into the studio and produce a live sports talk show from the ground up, covering the biggest stories in college and professional sports. YouUll rotate through real production roles: operating cameras, directing from the control room, producing original segments, running graphics, and learning how every piece of a live broadcast comes together. By the end of the semester, youUll know what it takes to create and produce a live television show while building hands-on experience you can add to your reel and resume.

18524.notes:
Making The Podcast Series
Have an idea worth hearing? Turn it into a show. Develop, record, and produce your own original podcast from the ground up. Building the concept, finding your voice, creating compelling episodes, and leaving the semester with a polished pilot you can call your own.

18526.notes:
Making the Dating Show
Ready to create the next great USC love story...or total dating disaster? Develop an original dating show from the ground up, then bring it to life through casting, challenges, set design, graphics, producing, and live studio production as you shoot multiple episodes throughout the semester.

18527.notes:
Making The Game Show
Develop an original game show from scratch, pitch your idea, and help turn the winning format into a fully produced series. You will build the games, cast contestants, create graphics, design the set, build the games, cast contestants, create graphics, design the set, and shoot multiple episodes throughout the semester, culminating in a big-screen premiere at USC's IMAX theater.

18528.notes:
Making the Sports Documentary
Go beyond the scoreboard and tell the story that deserves to be seen. Find a story, follow real athletes, and direct or produce your own five-minute sports documentary from first idea to final cut. Then premiere your film on the big screen in front of friends, family, athletes, and the USC community.

18530.notes:
The Morning Brew
Turn the latest entertainment, pop culture, and campus life into a fast-paced live morning show produced entirely by you, the students. Create original segments, shoot field packages, operate studio cameras, work in the control room, and learn how a weekly entertainment show goes from an idea to live television.

18531.notes:
Making The Trojan Tank
Step into the tank, or the Colosseum, and develop an original concept inspired by entrepreneurial TV shows, build your pitch, and learn how to sell your vision as you compete, collaborate, and bring your idea to life in this one-of-a-kind, hands-on class.

33501.notes:
Super 8 and the Handmade Collage Film
This course is a studio class for analog and hand-painted film post the digital revolution in an art context. Students shoot Super 8 film and learn to hand-paint, etch and collage 16mm filmstrips. The class screens historical and contemporary works utilizing analog film processes, read relevant essays for discussion, and learn about the film community. Workshops, demonstrations and a field trip to the film lab push students to experiment with shooting on Super 8 film, using found footage and the unique processes of drawing, painting, staining, scratching and collage directly on filmstrips as well as experimental film processing. Students learn to project their work on film projectors while also transferring their work to digital formats for editing and digital projection. The creative projects, lectures, discussions, works screened, field trips and readings will lead to an understanding of experimental analog film in a digital world.

33599.notes: Students work with distinguished faculty and visiting design professionals through a series of private studio meetings. Visits typically occur weekly, but may occur more or less frequently, as determined by the students' needs and faculty advisors.

33868.notes:
Riot Grrrl: Music, Art, Zines and Video of the 90s to the Present
This class examines the influence of the Riot Grrrl movement of the 1990's to the present and its intersection with music, art, video, film, zines and DIY culture. The class places equal importance on women's voices in Hip-Hop, Punk and other simultaneous and historical movements of the 90's. The movements used music, art and zines to produce a platform for empowerment. Students make zines and a research based project in response to the class.

64715.notes:
Education and Intellectual Development
This thematic will promote the development of college-level writing and critical reading skills in the context of sustainable development, a contemporary movement that melds together concerns having to do with the environment, the economy, and social justice. In class workshops and through formal and informal writing assignments, students will have the opportunity to pursue individuated investigations into sustainability issues such as global warming, biodiversity, resource depletion, and the appropriate balance of economic and environmental requirements.

64984.notes:
Globalization Current Issues & Cross-Cultural Perspectives
This Writing 150 thematic will promote the development of strong writing and critical reasoning skills by providing students an opportunity to examine those values, belief systems, and ideologies that affect every dimension of our lives, whether personal, social, professional, or civic. We will approach writing as a recursive process of engaged reading, invention, arrangement, revision, and editing. The texts we produce will demonstrate respect for the needs of readers and will exemplify the kind of ethical rhetoric that has the potential to engage with and influence the worlds values and belief systems in positive ways.

64995.notes:
Inside-Out Writing Workshop
This course is being offered in conjunction with the USC Dornsife Prison Education Project. This class aims to create opportunities for USC and students in-custody to learn from each other in a rigorous and collaborative environment. This course will focus on autobiography, and each week, students will be tasked with drafting a new chapter of their life stories. We will try to understand ourselves and our society through reading, writing, with an emphasis on writing as a process. Work between USC and students in-custody will be exchanged via electronic correspondence or in person, dependent upon the facility. For D-clearance please email Professor DeDominic at dedomini@usc.edu.

65500.notes:
Writing in Practical Contexts
For information on this course, please email Professor Antonio Elefano at elefano@usc.edu. Please note that students must have completed (or currently be enrolled in) either WRIT 340 or CORE 112 as a prerequisite for this course. This course examines how being humorous allows authors and comics to tackle subjects in their work that might otherwise seem taboo, and how this freedom provides a unique opportunity for social commentary and critique. One particular emphasis is understanding how comedic authors balance the need to entertain an audience with their efforts to provide insight on controversial issues. Throughout the semester students will explore aspects of writing and argumentation by analyzing a range of comedic texts, and will have the opportunity to produce original work in a variety of comedic genres (rants; scripts; stand-up routines; sketches; etc.).

65994.notes:
AI Writing Lab
AI Intensive.This project-based course emphasizes experimentation and reflection. Each week, instructors will challenge students to put a diverse range of AI tools - including agentic AI - to the test. Activities and assignments will interrogate foundational assumptions about AI, knowledge generation, language, rhetoric, and the potential for humanistic inquiry. By working both with and against AI, students will hone their writing and critical-thinking skills while reflecting deeply on their engagement with these tools.
